Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
I was really hyped to play this game because of the extraordinary ratings. And in the end I was quite disappointed with this 97/100 „masterpiece“.
Good things first: Until the sequel came out this game was the biggest Zelda game ever made: Biggest open world, best combat system, first voices overs, character customization (armor, weapons), crafting/cooking system, weather/climate system etc… those are all the reasons why this game is nothing less than spectacular. Futhermore this was the best open world game on any handheld console at the time (2017).
At first I was no fan of the breakable weapons because you would use your good weapons on enemy camps to find worse weapons afterwards. So in the end I kind of found myself ignoring a lot of those camps because of the bad loot that came with them… I would have loved some kind of „The Witcher 3“ system where you just repair often used weapons. But in the end that‘s ok…
The things that bothered me the most (light spoilers regarding boss fights):
- The shrines are too many and get really repetitive. Just because there is a reward (heart/stamina containers) doesn‘t make them fun.
- Exploration is almost only rewarded with korok seeds. It speaks for itself that they had to include 1000 of them so the world wouldn‘t feel empty. I would have loved more diversity there. More interesting side quests or loot in the open world would have been nice. But every time I‘m climbing a mountain to discover what‘s up there it‘s a korok seed 99% of the time. And the same with korok seeds: Doesn’t make them fun just because there is a reward for them (inventory space).
- No memorable boss fights/Missing dungeons. The devine beasts play almost the same every time. The boss fights in those are the most forgettable in Zelda games period. All four kind of look the same just with different elements to them. The Ganondorf fight was one of the worst as well in my opinion…
- Then the story was one of the weakest Zelda stories for me as well. I didn‘t like the delivery and the pacing. I lost interest in the game after the 3rd devine beast and finished the game just because I didn‘t want to leave it unfinished.
- Soundtrack/Score was definitely one of the worst in any Zelda game ever…
All those points are the reason why for me it doesn’t deserve the praise it gets. But I mean Mario Odyssey got a 97/100 as well. Which is crazy considering it has the same score as Mario Galaxy 2. Since the Switch era Metascores are getting stupid…

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
I wanted to like this game more. I really, really did. Breath of the Wild has of the best aesthetics, some of the most charming characters, and maybe the most impressive vision I’ve ever seen for a game… but these positives don’t make up for the game’s sins. Especially the cardinal sin of games: Breath of the Wild is a *boring* video game.

- A needlessly frustrating weapon-breaking system designed to “encourage versatility” that only serves to force players into certain behaviors in combat (in stark contrast to the game’s approach to exploration, where fine-tuned physics really do encourage and reward creativity in a way seldom done better). Good weapons essentially become the Ethers of BotW, rare resources which you stockpile in your inventory and never use, because nothing seems important enough to risk your most precious gear on, even in the final climb up Hyrule Castle. You will never, ever convince me that a knight’s sword **** into a thousand pieces after twenty-something swings is either realistic OR fun.

- The physics-based gameplay, which an absolute revelation for exploration, makes most puzzles meaningless. There are clear intended solutions for most brain-teasers scattered across the game, as the puzzles in Breath of the Wild are kept fairly simple by the franchise’s standards, but it’s equally easy in most cases to disregard what the game wants you to do in favor of just breaking the puzzle by brute-forcing your way to the reward using the game’s physics. Figuring out the solution to a particularly tough Zelda puzzle and getting over that mound and progressing after pounding your head against the game again and again is one of the most rewarding experiences in the gaming canon, and Breath of the Wild just doesn’t have that. 

- A vast, expansive and immersive open world with not nearly enough stuff to do in it. Fitting to the post-apocalyptic setting of this new Hyrule, sure, but that doesn’t make those long stretches of empty travel time any less boring. Putting nine hundred Koroks across your world (most of which are hidden behind those brute-forceable physics puzzles, might I add) doesn’t make it an engaging environment. Empty worlds *can* be done in an interesting and engaging way—Fallout built an entire franchise around this idea—but this reimagining of Hyrule is simply too quiet.

- An outright disregard for the established source material and timeline. I *really* want to like this game’s story, because a lot of it is just so well-written, and I understand that the Zelda timeline can be confusing and tricky to write around. But choosing to cherry pick names and concepts while throwing out decades of established continuity in favor of something “fresh” is like taking clippings of your baby’s hair before throwing them out with the bath water. It was, at least to my way of thinking, the wrong move.

I’ve played this game front-to-back, and I’ve sunk my teeth more deeply into the lore than I care to admit. And my biggest takeaway from this game is… I’m really, really gonna miss classic Zelda now that it’s gone.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Released on Nintendo Wii U and Nintendo Switch, The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is THE game that revolutionized the openworld genre.

Link, who has no memories, awakens in the ruined Hyrule Kingdom 100 years after a great battle in the Great Plateau. He must free the four divine creatures (machines created by the Sheikahs) in order to fight and eradicate the Calamity, while trying to remember his past with the Prodigies, the blossoming nation of the kingdom and Princess Zelda (who begins to appreciate him following the failure of the assassination of the latter by the Yigas, servants of Ganon.

The environment is perfect: mountains, lakes, rivers, forests, desert, jungle, everything is well put together to offer us a world full of secrets.

The characters are extremely well developed (special mention to Revali who has the hero complex), unlike the dungeons (original but which are too short and therefore not enough puzzles) and the bosses (except Ganon) which are too similar (this will fortunately be corrected in Tears of the Kingdom).

The music varies: it can be simplistic (very naturalistic, it feels good) or even epic (thanks to the orchestra, the fights or the memories or the themes of each character or even the game are excellent).

An 8 out of 10 seems to reflect a game that was released on March 3, 2017 (more than 7 years ago when this review was written). Let's hope that in the future, around 2027-2028, we will have a game that mixes open world and tradition with dungeons (a little linearity).

I have played Breath of the Wild more than four times now and I still haven't been able to capture what I felt when I first played it.

Breath of the Wild is fun for a first time playthrough but the open world aspect dies out the moment you explore each corner of the map and realize it's just another Korok or just another shrine. The Divine Beast boss battles were fun and the Blight Ganons were different. And heck even I liked the DLC but those things don't make a Zelda experience, do they?

And look I'm all down for customizable link and open world and all that. But come on if your going to plaster Zelda's name on it at least make it feel somewhat like Zelda. This new format has something, but it needs to be seriously refined.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Breath of the Wild is, quite simply, one of the most beautiful games every made. The "tutorial" is probably the best in the history of Zelda, and the feeling of traversing the open world is unmatched in modern games. If Skyrim set the standard for a modern open-world game, then Zelda took it to the next level by allowing Link to climb everything. Going back and playing games like Skyrim will make you wish you could climb. Having said that, not everything was positive to me. 

There is no feeling of progression. The augments you get at the beginning are the same augments you have at the end, more or less. Although some may praise this, I really missed the items of previous Zeldas. I like the feeling of past Zeldas where you get items that help you traverse through the world piece by piece as you progress. The only items to speak of are sword/bow and sword/bow adjacent weapons, which have weapon stamina. While I understand why weapon stamina is important given the survivalist feel **** like this, I was pretty tired of the mechanic even early on. It's just no fun to have your awesome weapon be unusable anymore.  The only progression here is to grind more shrines so you get more stamina, so on and so on.

Speaking of the shrines, a lot of them were underwhelming. There were a lot that featured the game sword-and-shield type enemy over and over again with different hit points. Only a few shrines were genuinely interesting and really made me feel any sense of accomplishment from beating them. This ****, because when I started the game I expected to a completionist run where I did every shrine, but the thought of doing that is pretty unappealing after actually playing through so many of them organically. 

As for story, there is none. Some will say that is the point and that it is supposed to be Link communicating with nature or something, but I felt they could have done more. The story that exists is just a bare-bones placeholder, and makes no sense. I know the stories in these games are not exactly "Crime and Punishment," but I felt a pang of nostalgia for games like Majora's Mask that felt like they had moreof a narrative element.

My other big gripe with the game is how empty Hyrule feels. The first time you play it it's amazing and overwhelming, but subsequent playthroughs emphasize just how few people are actually in this world. If Ganon is really contained in the castle, why aren't there most towns? I would love to see a really big, ambitious Zelda city crop up in a game at some point.

Overall, the game overcomes these deficits and is still incredible, but I feel it is outdone but some other Zelda offerings in certain respects.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Nothing short of overrated. As a lifelong Zelda fan, I had high hopes for this "revolutionary" game, yet as I progressed through the game looking for clues as to why the general public continually endorses this game, all I seemed to find was disappointment. 

Not only is the story minimal, it is mostly locked behind "lost memories" scattered across the map, which wouldn't be that bad if it weren't for the fact it doesn't add anything of value to the divine beast flashbacks or the intro, effectively making the whole ordeal of chasing these memories down completely and utterly useless.

On to the so-called 'incredible' combat, you have the choice between 3 different weapons varying in styles allowing for additional damage and/or durability, and that's pretty much it. Hit, hit, and block makes for boring combat against overleved monsters that drop useless loot, making fighting unsatisfyingly pointless, unless you're a fan of breaking your weapons for no reason (oh and they do break fast).

Puzzles are a recurrent element in Zelda games and most certainly make a comeback in Breath of the Wild in the form of Divine Beasts and numerous shrines. The beasts felt tedious, all over the place, and more so frustrating than challenging. The shrines on the other hand often felt too easy, a clear imbalance. 

As far as the overworld goes, this is a complete disaster. While the game looks promising at first, it soon comes to light upon further inspection that it is completely bland and devoid of life. Clearly aiming for quantity over quality, the vast green lands are clearly just here to limit test the Switch. For the game's purposes? Clearly no power and no point. 

On top of that, the game reeks of confusing and hidden elements. As someone who's played his fair share of videogames, my gamesense is developed enough for me to get a grasp **** basic features in a quick manner. However, BOTW hides gameplay elements so far behind walkthrough guides, I finished the game skipping over a ton of elements (none that would have enhanced my experience however). Not to mention, the iconic master sword and hylian shield are not even major story elements (if even minor ones) this time around so have fun with you bokoblin club I suppose.

TL;DR: In no way is this game revolutionary when other clearly superior games of the same genre exist. Clearly a proof of concept for the sequel, TOTK, or a game targeting kids (green and inexperienced).  Not worth the time nor the hype.

SKIP

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
I really don't understand the hype about this game...  I'm a huge Zelda fan, I have LoZ tattoos... And it took me years and multiple tries to even get through this game.  Every time I tried, it slid off me like greased goose ****.
For reference, my favorite LoZ game is Ocarina of Time, but Link to the Past will always have a special place in my heard.  Twilight Princess was fun and I like some of the art choices.  Even Wind Waker was great, though repetitive and slow in places... but recent games, starting with Skyward Sword just feel dull to me.
Breath of the Wild combined two of my least favorite things you could do to a LoZ game.  
First, it eliminated the dungeons, and dungeon bosses that are perhaps some of the most iconic pieces of Zelda games.  I don't understand how someone could make that decision.  The puzzle shrines were nice, I guess... Maybe sick a dozen of them together, focusing on different ways to use a new item/ability and theme it around a particular terrain motif, culminating in a boss fight?
Second, the destructible weapons/shields felt jarring to me.  Zelda has always been a series about gaining powers, items, ect, on your quest.  Turning into a veritable Swiss Army Knife of abilities to solve puzzle, with combat being another puzzle to solve.  The idea that you could find something cool and powerful, but have the game rob you of it once you use it a couple times feels like something out of a different game.
The world and art are beautiful, and returning to the open world exploration roots of Zelda could be very interesting, but the story was so thin, and the challenges presented were so generic and formless that I felt like I was grinding through the game to get it over with, rather than going on a journey in a new take on a beloved world.
Also, the voice acting was terrible, particularly for Zelda...

The constant "die and try again" may be appealing to some, but not to me, especially when done for dozens of hours on end.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: If you know about the Legend of Zelda series then you should know that the most recent installment of the series is The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom which takes place in the newest timeline and map. Although you may also know that Tears of the Kingdom is a sequel and the story begins with The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. Queue the title theme from Ocarina of Time if you would.	The Legend of Zelda is an incredible franchise with huge success all the way to the first game in 1986. All these games have had a similar play style but always manage to produce new mechanics, a 2D almost dungeon runner as a hero. In 1998 they released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. This was a large leap with it now being a 3d game and it seemed to be very popular as it is to this day considered to be in the top 10 greatest video games of all time with a 10/10 on IGN and a 99/100 in Metacritic. Ocarina of Time inspired many games to come including another game that happened to slip into the top 10 as well and that is 2017’s The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. This is my personal favorite and I'm sure I'm not alone. Breath of the Wild decided to take a large leap in the Zelda franchise and became the first 3D Open-World RPG Zelda game. From personal experience, 300+ hours, I would have to rate it a 10/10 game. Everything from the gameplay to the storytelling to the atmosphere is incredible, and the music is just perfect. It portrays so much emotion whether it's joy or sorrow and always fits perfectly. Hell, I'm listening to it as I write this. I know it sounds cheesy but is genuinely hard to describe. It's the first game in the Zelda series where you have complete freedom and where every single moment is its own. Sure, there is a written story and a suggested path but it's just that, a suggestion. You could skip the whole story and just go straight to the final boss if you really wanted to. Yes, there are games like GTA or any others but as a zelda it feels so different. You will have such intense moments and then the most beautiful and peaceful ones right after, almost like a reward. It's a game that teaches you that when you fail, you keep trying until you succeed because when you do it feels incredible. It's a game that taught me how much small things can make you happy. By mid-2018 I had beat the game, but it wasn't over. There was so much more to do with hundreds of side quests and 999 of these things called Koroks, tiny tree folk hidden around the map, to find. By 2019 I had 100% completed the game and after doing everything the game had to offer my judgment from the beginning never changed, 10/10, even though some sessions felt like they lasted years. Another thing happened in the E3 of 2019. A sneak peek of the sequel to Breath of the Wild was revealed. After many delays and Nintendo saying “It's worth it” it was finally released on May 16th, 2023. I had it pre-ordered and the day it was released I downloaded it and opened it. The bar was high but they rocketed past it in seconds. Within the first few minutes of play I was already fan-girling. It had the same things that made Breath of the Wild so good just now with so many new mechanics, music, map, and story. If I could rate it higher than a 10/10 I would. Many times the game brought me to tears. Chills would go through my body every 3 minutes. The new atmosphere, the new music, and even the old music continued to hit me just right. There are moments of music and atmosphere that make you feel like you can do anything, until the boss shows up and you're humbled. Now I have not 100%’d the game, meaning I have not done all that it has to offer, but honestly, to give a full review it's not necessary because it's that good. These two games had a huge impact on who I am, especially Breath of the Wild as I was much younger. It made me appreciate the things I didn't even think to notice. It's made me more aware of the smaller details. It's even led me to want to play instruments due to its immaculate soundtracks. I can definitely see now that if I hadn't played that game I would be who I am today.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
8.0
BotW is an open world game with minimal structure. The player roams the wide, diverse and beautiful world, going on their own adventure. At times, you will meet npcs or even find a village. However the vast majority of the world is wilderness. There are three things to find: shrines, korok seeds, and treasure chests. Treasure chests often contain low value items and are often guarded by monsters. Since the monsters and treasures are very repetitive, these are usually not sought after actively. Korok seeds are also repetitive but at least have some practical value and give a sense of progress .Shrines are the main attraction. They symbolize you conquering the wilderness after all you can always travel to their, this part of the wild is now yours. Also, they are often quite fun.Personally, I like the side quests quite a bit. They make the player connect with other characters in a world that can feel very solitary. And some quests are pretty good!

All in all, the game does what it does very well, with some flaws. I enjoyed the main quest quite a lot. But the main quest is only a small part of the game. I also like exploring the world and reveling in its beauty. However, the game does feel a bit to empty and lonely to me. 
When I play, I enjoy the meditative aspects of exploring a beautiful world of solitude. But the reward density is too low to keep my interest for longer than 30-60 minutes every couple of days. I miss the typical Zelda songs and the feeling of living in a world with other beings.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: Ah, where do I even begin with The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild? It's like trying to juggle flamingos while riding a unicycle made of bubblegum, all the while reciting Shakespeare backwards in a room filled with upside-down pineapples. This game is a surreal masterpiece, a cacophony of pixelated dreams woven together with threads of cosmic spaghetti. Playing it is akin to sipping moonlight from a teacup made of **** while tap-dancing on the rings of Saturn. The open world is as vast as the universe itself, filled with more mysteries than a riddle wrapped in an enigma and deep-fried in perplexity.Combat? It's like engaging in a sword fight with a rubber chicken while wearing socks made of marshmallows. The enemies, oh, the enemies! They're as diverse as a collection of mismatched socks in a laundromat run by interdimensional goblins. And the storyline? It's as convoluted as a labyrinth designed by a sentient crossword puzzle. You'll find yourself questioning the very fabric of reality, pondering the meaning of life, the universe, and why chickens always seem to have a bone to pick with you.Comparing this game to other titles is like comparing a supernova to a jellybean, or a symphony to a kazoo solo performed by a sloth. In the grand tapestry of gaming, Breath of the Wild is a neon-colored giraffe in a sea of monochrome ****, my dear readers, I bestow upon this masterpiece a solid 9 out of 10. Why not a perfect 10, you ask? Well, perfection is overrated, like trying to catch moonbeams in a fishing net or explaining the concept of time to a caffeinated squirrel. Embrace the chaos, revel in the absurdity, and let Link guide you through this wonderfully bewildering adventure.

Review: It might not be the console seller reviewers will let you believe it is, but it's an decent open world game. What it makes up for a non-existent story, sloppy combat, some frustrating sections and annoying puzzles is incredible exploration and creative ways of tackling any obstacle or problem. There is no one way of doing something if you're creative enough, which is something a lot of modern games fail to implement. However, some aspects in this game are so poorly designed that it makes you repeat annoying chunks of the game, killing the pacing in the process. Some enemies hit way too hard, the lock-on system is straight up broken, the camera is wonky and some game mechanics are not explained to the player properly. As much as I hate to say it, this game is overrated, and while the traversal and mechanics are pretty good, the downsides overweigh the upsides by a lot.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: I want to make this clear to whoever is reading this review right now. This game is not perfect, but that’s ok because no game will ever be. What this game has accomplished is simply amazing. Nintendo finally took a shot at an open world game, with the genre being as popular as it is, and blew us away with their first go. (Spoilers from here on out) PROS- Traveling throughout the world in Breath of the Wild (BOTW) is the most fantastic part of the game. You have so many options as you are traveling. You can surf down massive cliffs and snow mountains for a blistering way to get to places. Climb up mountains anywhere to get a good view on the landscape, plan where to go next and paraglide over their. If you want to get to an area quickly you can take a horse, or if you completed the DLC a motorcycle. If your in the desert you can use a seal to take you across it quickly. This game provides options when traveling throughout the world witch plays in part why it’s so fun to explore. The other reason this game is so enticing is their is something around every corner. Their are 4 divine beast, 120 shrines, 900 korok seeds, and many side quest and mini games. So while the world is massive their is always something to see or do. The world is most enjoyed when you take your time with the game. Both me and one of my friend got the game around the same time as each other my friend tried to collect everything in the game before beating Calamity Ganon, including all 900 korok seeds. By the end of the game he had put just about 300 hours in to it. He was completely burned out and hated the game for it. This is not the game where completing it 100% completion will be fun in a short period of time. I have had the game for about 1.5 years now and still play it because I don’t do the little at at once. I beat the game a couple months after I got it and completed all the main stuff along with it like, freed all dive beast, got the master sword, found all the memories, and beat the DLC. After I defeated Ganon I still wanted to explore the world and see what I could find. I still only have about 250 korok seeds and finally finished all the shrines but I’m till even to this day having fun exploring the world. I constantly come back and find new things. I stumbled upon a beautiful dragon for the first time and was blown away. Found full towns after beating Ganon and still have fun finding korok’s around every corner. Some of the best moments I have ever had in gaming are from stumbling into stuff naturally from this game. BOTW does this better than any game I have played yet. Cons- It’s interesting because what this game achieves so well make the shortcomings seem like more of a misstep than it normally would be. The voice acting in many ways is just average, which really surprised me since this is the first time there are voice actors in a Zelda game that both Nintendo and the voice actors didn’t go for perfection. In many of the cutscene it seemed like they were took only a couple times. The Divine Beast are very interesting and unique concept the first couple you do but later on I realized they were extremely short and boring compared to past Zelda dungeons. They also have exactly the same boring interior look for each dungeon and shrine. Again, previous Zelda dungeons where much more creative and interesting than these and if one thing gets changed in the sequel I hope it would be this. Most of the other problem I had were small. The music in this game is perfect for what the game is supposed to be, but for a more personal problem I miss the bombastic Hyrule Field music or the optimistic Great Sea theme. Again this is not a problem for the game but a personal one. The durability system is almost great for the ability to keep you on your toes at all times but I would like if you got a couple more hits out of each weapon, so instead that would make players be more aggressive instead of being cautious about breaking weapons. The menu system works ok but I still often find myself stumbling around in it. Also I didn’t like how you can only hold 5 items at a time; I would like to be able to hold more. In conclusion, this game is fantastic and I would recommend it to anyone who has any interest in it. This is probably my favorite game of all time, mainly because I have had so many memorable moments from it and I can call my adventures in the game my own. This game got me back into video games and I really appreciate it for that. Yes, the game does have flaws just like every other game ever will, but here hoping the recently announced direct sequel can fix some of those problem, retain what’s great about this game, and come up with creative ideas and story to make it unique from its predecessor.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: Breath of the Wild, I will admit is a very fun entry to the Zelda franchise but if the most fun you have in your game is doing things that are not the story that says something about the game and this game is one of those games. The most fun I had with this game was messing around in the overworld doing non story and optional material. It feels more like a sandbox game then a Zelda game at least to me. Im all for games in a series trying something new and experimenting with different features and such but when the bad features stick out more that is not a good sign. The sheika slate does a bit of both with aspects of it like the camera and having to take pictures being a sore spot. On the other hand I found being able to freeze water and stop time on objects to be some of the most fun new gameplay mechanics. The shrines have some interesting puzzles and feel more like a classic dungeon in the Zelda sense. Sadly the great shrines are far to short and the not so great ones feel like they drag on. The guardians before getting ancient weapons are a scary thing to encounter but once you can defeat them with ease its satisfying. The Devine Beasts I think were a neat idea but do drag on and have some rather confusing puzzles in them but were an interesting way to try and shake things up. Cooking is one of the sore spots. I do admit I like the idea but the execution was a bit rocky with just having to throw things in the pot and hope it works with no real direction. I must now mention the worst thing WEAPON DURABILITY. Why in the heck can the master sword the most powerful sword break like who's idea was this. It takes the fun out of combat when a weapon you love using breaks mid fight. There are some positives for this game as well, this is the biggest and best looking Hyrule has ever been. I know many other switch games graphics are compared to this one and this has taken a world and made it very real and full of life from horses running to even just sitting and watching the monsters interact with bombs when you drop then is just a joy to take in all the little details that bring the world to life. Just like all Zelda games the music is beautiful making the world have this sense of charm and at some times dread. This is the best looks Link and Zelda have ever had in the series and there moments of interaction to me are just so wholesome and wonderful full of emotion and character from there eyes and interactions without even a word having to be said. The growth of there relationship is a highlight of the game for me personally. Overall well this game does have some detractors it is still a wonderful game for any Zelda fan to play. Well it is not top 3 for me it is still a game every fan of the series should play at least once

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
The game I bought the Switch for.

Bad stuff:
- this game feels like playing World of Warcraft in Legion without a guild. Essentially the same cycle of activities, but with dramatically worse music.
- there's no story here at all. I've gotten so used to AAA games being sweeping, emotional narratives, with engaging characters, wading into this quiet sandbox was disorienting. I havent played a Zelda game since Ocarina of Time, so it might have been a misunderstanding on my part of what I was getting into, but this story is shallow to the point of tedium.
- Almost everything is extremely easy - and then some random things are so absurdly difficult as to seem like you've started playing a different game. Not my favorite phenomena.
- Just make the frigging horse magic. Just let me summon the horse wherever. I shouldnt have to buy a DLC to have basic transportation be fun and easy when the game covers such impossible distances. Everything about the horses is cool, except the sheer impossibility of using them with any regularity. In a game that wants me to treat my horse like a trusted companion, I ended up swapping them out like cars in GTA. Dreadful design.
- Cooking is extremely endearing until it is agonizing. Terrible interface for something you have to do so much of, and while the noise they came up with for it is very good, there are limits - if a method of bulk cooking had been included, I suspect I never would have tired of the cooking music. Dreadful design.
- No fishing pole. What on earth possessed them to not include a fishing pole?
- The DLCs are just stuff they left out of the game. Nothing new, it's all stuff that genuinely should have been in the game, that already cost 70 dollars. Nasty business.

Good stuff:
- The puzzles, and the tools and interface for those puzzles, are magical. I never, ever wanted the shrines to end. Dazzling, imaginative work, Im only sad they werent more difficult, and more plentiful. Not worth 70 dollars, bc there simply isnt enough of them, but definitely the thing that best recommends the game.
- the slate abilities, even outside the puzzles, are wonderfully good fun, and feel fresh and engaging long after everything else has faded.
- It's a very pretty place to spend time.
- Some really terrific set-pieces; the four big 'dungeons' felt great.
-  A quality of wonder and scale that is hard to overstate.

I think if I hadnt kept playing WoW after my core group of friends moved on, and thus suffered the resource grind cycle of that game for so many hours, this one wouldnt have bothered me so much. But I did. And some design choices feel, even now, however many hours through, completely inexplicable - made worse when they rectified a number of them, but wanted me to pay to get them. Terrible cost to joy ratio when considered against most big titles.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
I've always loved Zelda. It took me 6 years to finally play BOTW, because I didn't love the console catalog and was really worried about some criticism I heard about the game. I enjoyed the game, but most of that criticism isn't only right but also pretty bland.

The four divine beasts are the only places in the game that resemble the classic dungeons, and aren't even good ones. The first two (Zoras' and Ritos') were annoyingly easy. I was kinda surprised because the shrines felt like very little bits of prepararion for the five big dungeons (beasts + the castle) but those also had pretty lazy designs. The two remaining were more interesting but also pretty lacking when compared to any previous 3D Zelda. But the worse part was the castle, which feels like an amusement park with a bunch of completely optional paths to get some cool gear but absolutely zero puzzles or challenges to reach the final boss.

But what really me off are the shrines. A bunch of them are almost running in a straight line to the goal and the combat ones just put an enemy in front of you and that's it. I'm also enormously surprised about the so spammed guardians. They only stand in front of you and shoot you a laser you can parry with any shield. That's it.

I'm really tired of "professional" reviews. Those reviewers have no guts. They just read the hype and unless the game is an absolute catastrophe or are strong leaks with bad news about a game, they just give the readers the news they want to hear.

BotW is a good game. It's fun, it gives a lot of hours of content, and it kind of brings Zelda to the physics era of gaming, which bloomed around 2004, when Half Life 2 really instrumentalized physics into the gameplay, both in combat and puzzles. But it's not the masterpiece the press says. If you haven't played it yet, temper your expectations and enjoy this good mix of the modern sandbox and Zelda.

Review:
It is not an easy task to get an open-world game right on the first try, but Nintendo somehow did it.

What we got was the Kingdom of Hyrule, an area 60% bigger than Skyrim. The world is filled with landmarks and points of interests to explore with an insane ammount of detail. The freedom you have in this game is incredible. After finishing the great plateau, you can do *everything*. You could go to Kakariko and start the main quest, but you could also go to the final boss around 45 minutes into the game.

The story is dramatic, yet the game is very calm and quiet, with ambient music playing at just the right moments. Exploration is also combined with survival. Many people hate the durability of weapons or *rain at inconvenient times*, but I don't mind it.

What I do mind is the fact that there is no post-game since it is impossible to complete all the main quests. When you beat the game it brings you back to the title screen. When you return to your save file, you are back in Hyrule Castle. Why?

Shrines are generally very easy. They were rarely good and required little to no brain to complete. Same can be said for the „dungeons“.

Side quests have no depth and don't feel rewarding. I would like to have some side stories in side quests like Skyrim has. 

I give it 97%.

Review: This game changed my life, really. It changed my view on all video games, and I am strongly convinced that this is objectively the best game of all time. Best Switch game, best console game, best game. I have not been able to find a single other game that could out-do this, other than its sequel, Tears of the Kingdom, which takes everything that BotW has done and makes it better. The feeling of being overwhelmed mixed with the feeling of pure curiosity when you look out from the peak outside of the Shrine of Resurrection on the Great Plateau is just incredible. This game has so much for you to do, and half of it, you don't even need to do. You can just run to the final boss as soon as you've left the Great Plateau if you want to, as speedrunners have proved by beating this in only 20 minutes. Or, you can take the completely opposite route, and beat every dungeon, find every Korok seed, do every shrine, find every treasure chest, and beat every side quest. Even then, you probably still haven't done all there is to do. The equipment in this game as well, oh my God. There is just so much to find and use. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Honestly the game is more of a 8.5/10 for me, but unable to give that score on this system. I finished this game like two years ago, but wanted to write a quick review since im currently playing through TOTK and will write a review for that once i finished that game.

I'm going to list the negatives first,
-Weapon breaking although it didn't bother me too much, it was annoying at first when you get a cool weapon and then it breaks.... i don't really understand why the bows break either. I think what they should of done for this game is make it where some weapons break easily, and then have a few more weapons that don't break at all. Because there's no reasons why the weapons break fast (totk provides reasons why at least in the story). Don't hate the overall mechanic, and it's more improved in TOTK
-Enemy variety- This in my opinion is the weakest part of the game, the boss fights are all the same type of enemy. there's very few different minion types.
Music- The music in the game is fine, it's just weaker compared to other games in the series.

Positives
- Combat is fun, fast, and fluid. Controls are responsive. So many different ways to approach fights
- art direction/style is amazing, and I'm glad to say they carried that over to TOTK.
-lots of characters in the game that can provide some comic relief at times
-overall solid story, I like how you don't really know what's going on at first but slowly learn what exactly happened in the past, and what's going on currently. I love the final boss battles as it's very cinematic and symbolic.
-I like the puzzles in the game, most of the puzzles were fair and it's fun using your special abilities to solve most of them.
-The different environments are well designed.
-Several hours of gameplay easily provided

Overall, as an open world game it perfectly gives this vibe of "oh today I'm going to explore this part of hyrule," and spend like a good two hours doing that. It's an easy game to jump in and out of, and just have fun. I would set a goal of what I wanted to accomplish in my gaming session (usually about two-three hours at most), and then go have fun. It was fun just exploring the map. To those that complain about the game being open world, you do realize that a lot of zelda games are open world???, from wind waker, twilight princess, OOT, and many more focuses on the exploration. I can understand the complaints about wanting a more traditional game though like OOT, but idk if they are going to do that anymore. TOTK is more breath of the wild, and it's going to be years before a new zelda game since TOTK was just released a few months ago. What is clear is that these games sell very well, and I get why TOTK is very similar to this game. Maybe in the future games we'll get a different setting.

It's pretty simple though, if u like this game then you'll like TOTK.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
This has by far been one of the greatest open world games I’ve ever laid my hands on. There is literally so much to do in this special world, that I simply don’t have a large enough character limit list them all. The attention to detail in this game is absurd. The climate gauge is a great example of this. Hiding in the shade or going up in altitude decreases the surrounding temperature, standing in direct sunlight increases it. The desert in this game acts exactly the same as in real life, days are hot and nights are cold. Another fantastic example would be the equipment. Metal shields, bows, and swords can conduct electricity and you can literally get struck by lightning in a thunderstorm. Wood shields, bows, swords, and basic arrows catch on fire when exposed to level 3 heat. Those fires can be extinguished when going into water.

This entire game is built around exploration, and it heavily encourages you to explore. Completing shrine puzzles can permanently increase your maximum health or stamina, scaling tall towers updates your map. Encountering groups of enemies and defeating them is rewarded with a chest. Finding Korok seeds can increase your equipment slots.

Exploration is also encourage via resource gathering.  The cooking system is built around buying or gathering food, which allows you to create food that can buff your defense, attack power, or movement speed. It can temporarily increase your maximum stamina and hearts too, or you could make food that buffs resistances to heat, cold, and electricity, or even increase your stealth. If cooking isn’t your thing, you can create elixirs that essentially provide the same effects that cooking can. Mob drops aren’t useless in this game, as most of them are used in upgrading your clothing. Ancient materials can be used to upgrade runes.  The puzzles in this game are sometimes simplistic at best, and mind intensive at worst. But all of them are fun and enjoyable. The best puzzles that really force you to think are found in the Divine Beasts, often requiring the Beast to be moved in certain ways to complete certain things. Locations in Breath of the Wild are vast and extremely different. Ranging from a hot volcano to the icy tundra. Each one of them requires different clothing or resistances to explore. You can only find certain resources in specific biomes, and this also applies to animals and monsters too! The boss fights were unique and varied, each requiring their own strategy. Now to the story. The beginning fills you with questions. Why did Link wake up in a cave? Why is ancient technology littering the landscape? You explore this world and piece by piece you begin the assemble the missing information like a puzzle. In the end game, you’ll completely understand what happened before you went into your 100 year slumber. This game literally turns you into Link. You must find your old memories and piece together who you once were. The silent protagonist really shines here, putting the player into their boots.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
this game was a disappointment for me. after everyone talked about how "excellent" and "revolutionary" this game was, i decided to pick it up in 2020 for the sweet sweet price of "it's still €60 3 years later", and after leaving the Great Plateau (where you start your adventure), the biggest issue of this game became obvious: the empty open world. as cool as it was to finally get an open world in a Zelda game (albeit a throwback to the first game), the magic of it quickly wore off: there's nothing to do there besides beating the 100+ identical shrines in terms of design, attacking identical groups of enemies and finding Korok seeds (which there are over 900...). what's great in an open world like GTA isn't just the vastness of the world, but also the ability to go off the beaten track and create your own fun outside of the main story. Breath of the Wild severely lacks that. heck, even Ocarina of Time, a game from 1998, has more stuff to do outside of the main game, with more interesting fetch quests in my opinion (and OOT isn't even my favorite Zelda game).

the controls aren't perfect, and they had to kind of grow on me. i absolutely hated them at first, but now i think they're fine. the weapon breaking mechanic, although criticized by many, is really interesting in my opinion, as it forces you to improvise and make the most out of the limited resources you get. same goes for cooking. and i don't mind the soundtrack (or mostly lack thereof), as it perfectly fits in with the atmosphere of the game

anyway, if the open world was more fleshed out, i think this game would be deserving of its 97 average score, and in my opinion, user reviews of this game severely lack nuance by overlooking the pros or cons of this game to give it a 0 or a 10, the latter being the most common. i'm kind of tired of seeing everyone praise this game like it has no flaws and call it "perfect" (and spoiler alert: making a perfect game is literally impossible)

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Open World: The Game
This game is simply dreadful and encompasses all the things I hate about open world games, while adding a few other game mechanics that only make the game worse. The game started out okay but once I got out of the tutorial area things went downhill quickly. Any attempts to further progress the story was met with a swift end by any number of enemies that will one shot you and you will randomly encounter these enemies just trying to get from point A to point B. Getting more hearts and stamina in this game is a chore. You have to complete a trial which you have to find first just out in the wild with no real easy way to locate them. Then you have to complete 4 of them to get 1 more heart or a minimal increase to links stamina wheel. I lost my patience doing these trials really quickly. Link needs stamina to pretty much do anything running, swimming and climbing all consume stamina and Link has so very little of it that trying to get anywhere takes so long that I would just rather turn the game off. There is cooking in this game because of course. Cooking is also an activity that takes forever. You first have to find a cooking pot and ingredients again randomly out in the wild. You then have to navigate some menus before adding ingredients one at a time to links hands before tossing the ingredients in the cooking pot which the ingredients will dance around for a bit before you get the meal you cooked. The meal you cook typically gives you health or stamina and thats pretty much it. It all just wastes your time everything in this game is just a waste of your time. There is a weapon durability system that is awful makes me not even really want to fight anything. The only thing enemies drop are monster parts that can be used in cooking to make elixirs that give you buffs. No recovery hearts. No rupees. No anything that I play The Legend of Zelda games for. There are certain areas that you cant go to without appropriate clothing or food buffs because the areas are to hot or to cold. Just a very unfun game. I tried doing some sidequests but the only rewards I got were weapons and shields. Since these shatter like glass anytime I try to use them I just didnt bother anymore. Returned the game for a refund after playing for roughly 8 hours and the only reason I'm not giving the game a 0/10 is because the game works and the graphics are actually pretty nice. Everything else about Breath of the Wild is terrible.

Review:
Zelda: BotW from 2023 perspective
Just got myself a new Switch OLED Zelda TotK edition because of how beautiful it is. The last time I played Nintendo games was in prime of Nintendo DS.
There were 3 reasons for buying Switch - BotW, Mario Odyssey and TotK. And now the 1st one is completed.
I play only major GOTY-type games. No Assassins creeds-like sandboxes and other trash they publish each and every year. Don’t have time for worst.
I enjoy powerful stories. That’s why I like GoW and The Last of Us diologies. Both parts of Red Dead Redemption, Disco Elysium, Control, Guardians of the Galaxy, It Takes Two and so on. So I had my expectations high, considering this game is the best one on Switch.
Yes, I’ve heard that story wise BotW is weak. Not that it’s weak - there’s just almost no story. Nothing interesting in both - the main story and side-quests. Graphics - I’ll be quick. It still has style, I’ve enjoyed it in handheld mode - never had an urge to play on TV. Had a glimpse once and never repeated that mistake - low res PS2 level textures and certain “squareness” is what you will get.
Gameplay. I’ll call Zelda game an open world puzzle game. That’s what it is. Temples - puzzles, main 4 objectives in the whole game - puzzles. Battles are primitive and I’ve tried to avoid them mostly. Bosses are easier than some above the average enemies. Interaction with the world and temples - physics based puzzles. Fire, gravity, magnetism etc. And, listen up, the main and most important game feature is that…you can climb everything. Yeah - that’s satisfying. And lots of travelling. Unfortunately, after RDR2 most of games’ worlds feel dead and empty. The same with BotW. Yeah, there were some animals here and there, I’ve met a few NPCs. Still world felt mostly as a huge dead territory. Beautiful, colourful and dead.
Conclusion. Do ability to climb everything (except in Temples) and lots of puzzles make Zelda one of the best games ever created? Certainly not. It was my impression that people, who still put this game on the pedestal, play mostly Nintendo games and/or missed all the major titles since 2017. However in 2017, I suppose, it was pretty above average. Right now the 60+ hours experience from BotW haven’t convinced me to play TotK and Mario Odyssey and just to sell the Switch. Maybe I could just check those later on Deck or…^^

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Zelda: Breath of the Wild presenta algunos puntos adicionales que podrían influir en tu decisión de no adquirir el juego:

1. Falta de dirección clara: Si prefieres juegos con una estructura lineal y una narrativa guiada, Breath of the Wild puede resultar desorientador. El enfoque en la exploración libre y la falta de dirección clara pueden hacer que te sientas perdido y sin un propósito claro, lo que podría generar aburrimiento y desconexión con la historia.

2. Dificultad de navegación: El vasto mundo abierto de Breath of the Wild puede resultar desafiante cuando se trata de orientarse y moverse de un lugar a otro. La falta de puntos de referencia claros y un sistema de navegación menos intuitivo pueden dificultar la exploración y provocar que pierdas tiempo y te sientas frustrado al tratar de llegar a tu destino.

3. Durabilidad de los objetos: Además de las armas, otros objetos en Breath of the Wild, como escudos y arcos, también tienen una durabilidad limitada. Esto significa que tendrás que estar atento a su desgaste y reemplazarlos con frecuencia, lo que puede ser una tarea tediosa y que distrae de la inmersión en el juego.

4. Interfaz de usuario poco intuitiva: Algunos jugadores han criticado la interfaz de usuario de Breath of the Wild por ser confusa y poco intuitiva. La gestión de inventario y la navegación por los menús pueden resultar incómodas y complicadas de usar, lo que puede generar frustración y afectar la experiencia general del juego.

5. Contenido repetitivo: Aunque el mundo abierto de Breath of the Wild es vasto y diverso, algunos jugadores han señalado que ciertos elementos y actividades en el juego pueden volverse repetitivos con el tiempo. Las misiones secundarias y las actividades adicionales pueden carecer de variedad y ofrecer poca recompensa, lo que puede hacer que te sientas desmotivado y aburrido después de un tiempo.

Estas críticas son subjetivas y pueden variar según las preferencias y experiencias individuales. Aunque Breath of the Wild ha sido ampliamente elogiado por su innovación y su mundo abierto, es importante considerar estos aspectos negativos adicionales para tomar una decisión informada sobre si el juego se ajusta a tus gustos y preferencias.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Breath of the Wild is the single-handed-ly best video-game I have ever played. This game is a bit of a mix, some elements are a bit disappointing but here are the pros and cons:

Pros:

Gameplay

Replayability

Memorable characters

Exploration

Glitches

Hours you get out of

Story

Cons:

Music

Combat

Dungeons

So, starting with the pros:

The Gameplay is some of the best I have seen. Flying from Rito village to shield surfing down a mountain is just satisfying, the number of things to do and ways to play the game is amazing, the best I have ever seen.

The replayability in this game is amazing, I have played through this game over and over and I am still discovering new things and finding new locations. You could play through game repeatedly and still not find so many things, The hours though...

There are many memorable characters, the way Nintendo does this is great, from Ravioli’s **** to Zelda’s Love is crazy compared to other games.

Exploration is crazy, Breath of the Wild changed the Idea of open world, letting the player do as much of they want and getting to do finish the game when they feel like it, the world is massive compared to anything else at the time and revolutionized open world.

The glitches in the game do not look good... But! For an open world game, it does not have many glitches compared to games like Cyberpunk, and the community only discovered the game-breaking glitches a couple of years after the game came out, if you look at them now, it does not look great but looking further it is great.

The hours you get out of it might seem like a con to some, put a big pro to others, this game is the most addicting I have ever played, and I have hundreds of hours on it, and like I mentioned before, there is way too much to do.

The story is good, not much compared to other Zelda games but it is overall good, the game focuses on the backstory and history of the world, being slightly barebone in the current time, but overall, solid.

Now onto the Cons:

The Music is horrible compared to other Zelda games, they are masterpieces, while this is just a guy playing some keyboard notes every few seconds and is boring. I really think Nintendo could have done better but they did not put the effort in.

The combat in this game is barebones, if you use glitches this is the opposite, but the normal combat BORING. The only things you can do are normal attacks and spin attacks, that’s it. There are 3 types of weapons being Swords, Two-handed Swords, and spears, all with different fighting styles, but the combat is still boring.

The dungeons in this game are a bit disappointing coming from Zelda, the game series is all about them. The dungeons are not Horrible, but you get 120, yes 120 bite-sized dungeons that take 5-10 minutes + 4 Big dungeons that take about 20-30 Minutes, this is disappointing for Zelda.

Overall this is a masterpiece, end of story.

What perhaps was not emphasized enough is this game manages to impress even after many years (I play it since March 2023) and it never appears as a six years old game... especially after playing such and horrible and low-quality game as Scarlet and Violet.

About this game I enjoyed the ability to insert the player, from the beginning, in a vast and wild nature that you don't feel is yours, but in which you have to know how to live and feed. BOTW, is for this reason, in the first place, a huge survival experience. You know there is a story to carry on but what there is between two points of the plot is something of the highest quality and fun beyond imagination.

But not all that glitters is gold: I must to point out that I didn't fully appreciate the final part of the plot. The entire game, as many have emphasized, maintains a "low profile" plot because its focus is on the "wild" game play, but I do not think that this aspect could be a sufficient justification.

The finale is too fast and is not able to create solid memories in the player.

Review:
BOTW is a game you play through gritted teeth.

The combat is basic and link has very few avoidance mechanics, leaving him standing there, dumbly unable to get out of the way of an instakill swipe from a early-game bokoblins. You are beset by mobs and then skeletons spawn from the ground to make it worst, you are then backed into a corner as the camera is pushed, dark-souls-like, into the back of link's head as he auto attaches to the wall, leaving you wondering why you can't do anything as an enemy kills you in one strike. The starting stamina is atrocious and is too slow to come back. Link doesn't simply move to where you want him to, but he does a little semi-circle circuitous move that punts you off of cliffs and makes it impossible to get onto ladders. All of this stuff came from skyward sword - the worst Zelda game.

I used to think that they could improve all of this for the next Zelda game. I now know different. Screw you, Nintendo!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Although now in many ways this game is completely outclassed by Tears of the Kingdom, this game was a revolution for its time, and Tears isn't. This game crafted a brand new physics and chemistry system and a ginormous world to explore. And the exploration and sense of freedom this game brings is what makes it so great. It is a remarkable achievement in the context of its time.

However, it is also a hugely flawed experience. The Divine Beasts are deeply underwhelming, the story is terrible, and the game is much too far removed from what made Zelda great in many respects. And now, the banality of the sidequests is laid bare by how excellent Tears's side adventures are. Tears would go on to address other flaws too, but not all of them and not always with great success.

This game's biggest asset is the huge, brand new world you explore. In this way, it wipes the floor with Tears' re-used map and somewhat underwhelming underworld. Whether you rate this game better than Tears depends on whether you consider the surrounding context: everything in this game is new, whereas a huge amount of Tears is re-used.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Many like me struggled to enjoy the first few hours (example: low stamina to climb walls or slipping druing rain, no proper cloithing to endure the cold, having to get used to weapons breaking). Soon after however, you really begin to enjoy and discover the open world and appreciate the effort developers put into this. BUT, eventually it begins to feel like a chore and you start to burn out. It becomes tiring to search for temples, tiring to collect additional heart and stamina containers, or increase inventory space, or replace weapons, or changing armour for weather or enemy type, or upgrading clothes or weapons. I found myself collecting all these for the sake of doing it, not for the fun of it.

I would have rated this game a 6 for the first 3 hours, and then a 10 for the next 20 hours, and eventually settle at 8 overall for what should be called Zelda Chores in the Wild.
Would be great to have voice overs instead of reading what felt like impossibly dry senseless dialogue accompanied by bizarre grunting noises. I had to lower the TV volume for fear my neighbours thinkinbg I'm watching porn (no joke).

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Gran juego en todos los aspectos.

Gameplay: Evolucionó la saga en todos los aspectos. Es por excelencia uno de los juegos que da sensación completa de libertad e infinidad de opciones. Para el desarrollo de los santuarios, alcanzar objetivos o completar misiones secundarias se pueden lograr de múltiples maneras. Esto otorga gran control al jugador.

Banda Sonora: sublime, espectacular y acorde a la historia. Se siente en todo momento el contacto con la naturaleza, con la soledad y con el inminente enemigo al asecho.

Gráficos: el estilo gráfico me costó en un momento asimilarlo pero cada Zelda tiene un estilo gráfico, ¡Y este ha marcado tendencia! Se puede observar en cuantos otros juegos "se inspiraron" en su apartado gráfico.

Historia: Debido al gran mapa de Hyrule se puede percibir que no hay historia, pero la historia la construimos nosotros. Están las memorias, el jefe final, las bestias divinas, misiones secundarias y aún así tu decides cómo quieres desarrollarlo y si deseas hacerlo completo.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Incredible game. One of the best-designed open worlds I have ever seen. It's crazy how if you can see an area, you can go there. You can climb basically everywhere. Gliding makes it even crazier. I love that there are different communities and biomes within the world. I loved exploring every one of them one by one.

The shrines are impressive. They are amusing to solve, and also very rewarding. Increasing the stamina wheel incentivizes more exploring, leading to more shrines. It's a loop I couldn't escape. It feels very rewarding when you solve the puzzle. It makes you feel like you are the only one who could do it, as it doesn't give you any instructions. That is very satisfying.

The combat feels great. I like that weapons break. It forces you to try new weapons which present a variety and breaks monotony. I also like the food system.

There are some things that hold me off from giving this game a perfect score. Firstly, I didn't enjoy the majority of side missions. They are repetitive and dull. Also, the main story wasn't anything special. The final boss was extremely easy and disappointing. In addition, although the open world is amazing, there wasn't much to do in between the shrines.

Still, a breathtaking game.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
An Artistic Masterpiece.
Breath of the Wild has the most enjoyable Open World I've ever explored in a videogame, I've played the game for hundreds of hours and I enjoyed every single second of it.

It's a very rewarding experience, and the world is absolutely massive with so many secrets and details, everything works as intended, which results in a masterfully crafted world full of life.

Finding shrines, doing puzzles, clearing camps and endlessly exploring the lands always feels fresh, there's a good amount of content within this game, and despite its repetitive nature, the game never actually gets repetitive.

As for the combat, it's decent, it might feel clunky at first but everything gets better once you get used to the controls. Also, the weapon durability can get in the way, it's a little bit annoying in the beginning, but it's not really an issue later on, there are so many ways to approach combat, to the point where using weapons isn't even necessary.

Weirdly enough, the physics play a huge role in the gameplay and I have to say... wow, the way every little thing coexists and interacts with each other is absolutely insane, and the attention to detail is groundbreaking.

There are so many things you can do, so many ways to interact with the world, use the environment as a tool or a weapon, solve puzzles in very creative ways and so much more. This game makes you think outside of the game, it treats the player as a smart person and gives you time to think before you act.

Breath of the Wild is a revolutionary game, and it changed the Open World formula forever, which inspired many other games to follow its steps.

Final Rating: "Masterpiece" ~ 10/10.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Let me be clear, this game is flawed. From its overall lacking story, to the absence of major dungeons, to its lack of enemy variety, to its occasional poor performance issues, it would be impossible to say that Breath of the Wild is a perfect game. I don't care, this is my favorite game ever created. The world itself is alive with so much to see and do, I've never experienced a game where the world itself begs the player to explore and simply discovering new places is so intrinsically rewarding. When I think of beauty in videogames I think of Breath of the Wild. When I think of the essence of discovery in videogames I think of Breath of the Wild. When I think of what it means to experience child-like wonder I think of Breath of the Wild. This is the single player game I have the most time in, with over 250 hours and multiple game completions, yet I still haven't experienced everything this game has to offer, and I probably never will. I can only hope that BOTW 2 comes within a mile of this masterpiece.

EDIT: BOTW is a worse game than TOTK, so I would recommend TOTK over this if you are choosing between the two. Still very much a worthwhile game to play though.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Okay, I'm just going to start by saying that this game is absolutely phenomenal. I consider The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild to be my number 1 favorite video game of all time. What I like most about it is its combat mechanics. Combat in this game is incredibly fun, and I like how a good chunk of it fundamentally boils down to timing. The game isn't that picky with the timing, but just picky enough to the point where it is not underwhemingly easy. Its story, while not the best, is still fairly interesting, and is the most common complaint about this game, at least that I hear. I also love how the map is never short of things to discover. From shrines, to sheikah towers, to labyrinths, to the farious villages and towns scattered across the map. I will, admit, that I do not have a good attention span, and I find it difficult to sit and play the same game, or do the same activity, for any more than one-and-a-half hours without taking breaks. This game however, is one of the few exceptions, one where I am able to get immersed so well to where I end up spending upwards of five hours in one sitting (which, for me, is a lot) only interrupted by the occasional food break and bathroom break. This game is also very replayable. After finiahing it, I started up another save file, just so I could experience it again. Although, the second time isn't as fun because I already knew what to expect, but that problem is unavoidable with any game. The controls don't make it feel like my hands are holding the controller, it feels like my hands ARE the controllers. My only real complaint about this game is a pretty minor one, but it's over the fact that after finishing the main story quest, the adventure log does not say you finished it, and the game just acts as if you never finished it, regardless of how many times you actually do finish the story.

TLDR: Graphics: 9.5/10
Gameplay: 10/10
World immersion 10/10
Story: 8/10
Replayability: 10/10
Controls: 10/10
Overall: 10/10

But I do believe video game developers should quit trying making Hollywood soundtracks and go back to the good old melodies. It feels very bland and impersonal. There is something frustrating in this. Like "give me that vibe". But it’s not coming, except a few short instants.

More enemy variety would have been better.
Weapons breaking like glass, too fast.
Climbing in the rain.
Hyrule castle, so fade. As a conclusion, it was interesting. I respect the work. But just overall bland. Without relief and magic. Sorry.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
The last couple of weeks I played Breath of the Wild extensively and I was living and breathing (pun intended) Zelda until I finally saved the land of Hyrule. This is a landmark in gaming history, a masterpiece and when people say this is the best game of the last decade I'm inclined to believe them. For me however it has become a unique journey in an immersive world, but as it sometimes goes with journeys, not everything goes as smoothly as you like. I'm not going to discuss the spectacular open world, fantastic physics engine, the inventive puzzles in the shrines or the amazing Divine Beasts. Plenty of people have already done that and probably in a better way I ever could. Instead I want to discuss - and what I've rarely seen in other reviews - is the experience curve. Because Breath of the Wild is an experience I've never experienced before, both in a good way, but also with a plethora of inconveniences.

The game is truly open world and the masked tutorial in the beginning is somewhat friendly for the player, but after this part the world of Hyrule can become a very scary place. Every enemy is a potential death threat and enemies will find you. With a scarcity in resources the game resembles Resident Evil in more ways than one. When Nintendo said they have rethought what a Zelda game is they weren't kidding. The questionable mechanic that weapons break in an instant makes the game hard, but for all the wrong reasons. The first few hours in the game were not enjoyable for me and probably neither for the majority of other players I guess. It's only when I have resolved a number of shines, have collected a respectable number of weapons, increased my heart count and possess a number of potions that the game really shines.

And shine it does! Exploring this seemingless organic world is maybe the greatest strength of this game. I have visited several outskirts on earth and Breath of the World equals that experience. I've never thought this was possible in a game. The game really unveils itself when I start to visit the different peoples and Divine Beasts. The moment I visit Zora's Domain is a magical moment where everything comes together and you only encounter a handful of times in your gaming career. And Breath of the Wild is the proud owner of such a moment. It's on this moment that euphory starts to kick in and in my brain I already have concluded this is the best game ever. However, the more I explore this imaginative world of Hyrule I'm starting to discover the game mechanics, the somewhat repetitive structure of shrines and Divine Beasts and the game loses its magical touch.

The plenty of minor inconveniences that are available in the game start to annoy me. Not able to climb when it rains is a nuisance, the swimming is way too slow, the voice acting is sometimes of a questionable level and the slow commutes between locations can be a hassle. I'm no longer in love with this game. As in each relationship the biochemistry of love doesn't last forever, but here the feeling of routine comes sooner than expected. The unanymous appreciation of an open world Zelda causes the gameplay to be unbalanced. Say what you want about the more linear adventures of Link, but they never felt unbalanced. Here it does. The beginning is maybe a tad too difficult, but after dozens of hours into the game the mainquest becomes too easy. The final battle with Ganon is a piece of cake compared to taking down a Lynel. I think the diversive Twilight Princess is the best Zelda game to this date because of the ingenious design of its dungeons and Breath of the Wild doesn't replace that experience. It's a very nice addition to that game, but no replacement.

There is plenty to talk about this game and that is what the internet still is doing. After four years major gaming websites such as IGN and Gamespot are still releasing articles and movies about this game. It's a testimony to the impact, power and greatness of this game. While I think this game is unbalanced, has a somewhat skewed experience curve and possesses plenty of minor inconveniences, it all pales in comparison in what this game has to offer. An unrivaled open world experience that is unique for every player that has set a new defintion not only for this genre, but gaming in general. Imitation is the sincerest form of flattery and a few games have already copied the structure of Breath of the Wild. This game is after four years still the darling of the games industry and I don't see this changing anytime soon.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is an absolute masterpiece **** that completely redefines what an open-world adventure game can be. From the moment you first step out into the vast world of Hyrule, you are presented with a breathtakingly beautiful landscape that is filled with wonder and adventure.

The game features a vast array of diverse environments, ranging from lush forests to snow-capped mountains to scorching deserts, each with its own unique creatures and challenges to overcome. The attention to detail is simply astounding, and it's clear that the developers put a tremendous amount of care and effort into creating a world that feels truly alive.

One of the most impressive aspects of Breath of the Wild is its sense of freedom and exploration. Rather than holding your hand and leading you down a linear path, the game allows you to approach its challenges in any way you see fit. You are free to climb any mountain, swim across any river, and explore any nook and cranny you come across. This sense of freedom is incredibly empowering and makes the game feel like a true adventure.

Another standout feature of the game is its combat system. Battles are intense, strategic affairs that require you to think on your feet and make use of a wide variety of weapons and abilities. Whether you prefer to sneak around and take out enemies from afar or charge headfirst into battle with a sword and shield, there are countless ways to approach each encounter.

Overall, The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is a truly exceptional game that deserves all the praise it has received. Its vast open world, attention to detail, sense of freedom, and engaging combat system all come together to create an unforgettable gaming experience that is sure to leave you breathless. If you're a fan of adventure games, or simply looking for an unforgettable gaming experience, then this game is an absolute must-play.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
In a single sentence: the games feels tedious, repetitive and unfinished.

Pros:
1. The game's esthetic: beautiful open world, comic-like character design, lighting, as well as the esthetic of the remnants of an ancient technologically advanced civilisation
2. Dungeons inside giant moving robots with 3D maps!
3. The overall plot line is cool and credible
4. The ability to glide is very satisfying
5. The sound effects are pleasant

Cons:
1. The world might be beautiful, but it is completely empty. No big cities, just a handful of small settlements, practically no inhabitants. It feels ver strange.
2. No monster variety. You find the same few monsters in pretty much all zones.
3. Disappointing local story lines. The overall plot might be great (Calamity Ganon reappearing regularly throughout history, an ancient civilization building robots to help bring him down, Zelda keeping Ganon busy for 100 years), but the local storylines Link encounters when travelling are completely underwhelming (e.g. the elephant robot is making it rain too much in the Zora domain...)
4. Shrines are too repetitive: there are too many shrines and the puzzles are too similar. I get it that shrines are an excuse to travel the world but it's just far too much.
5. Too little dungeon variety. In previous games each dungeon had its own unique esthetic and music, but in BotW there are only 4 dungeons (excluding the shrines, which are also lacking in variety) and they are very similar.
6. Weapons breaking: you don't create an attachment to your weapons because they will end up breaking, therefore no weapon feels valuable. This adds to the feeling of repetitiveness.
7. The sheikah tablet: it's basically an all-can-do smartphone that takes away the medieval feel of Zelda games. Also, the fact that Link's powers are granted by the tablet is not credible and disappointing.
8. Princess Zelda is incredibly annoying.
9. There is too little esthetic emphasis on the triforce versus too much emphasis on the sheikah eye for a Zelda game.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Breath of the Wild is an incredible game that encourages creativity in its large open world with diverse landscapes. It encourages player choice in its fun combat, creating a good risk and reward system for players to interact with. For example, a player can go up against a strong enemy and get good rewards for it, or they could fight low level enemies and get other, less valuable rewards. While this is a great game, it is not without its flaws. The game has a lack of guidance, which can be discouraging for some players. It also has a weapon breaking system which, while it encourages creativity, it also can take away strong weapons that the player has grown attached to. The game also lacks a deep story, it gives a background to the game and a vague description of the events that unfolded before the game and is built upon very little, if not at all. Certain areas can also have poor performance, but this is limited to only a couple areas.

Pros:
- Fun combat
- Large filled open world
- Good risk-reward

Cons:
- Lack of guidance
- Weapon breaking can take away weapons you grow attached to
- Lack of a deep story

Overall, this is a very impressive game and I cannot wait for the sequel to come out.
