Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Points positifs :
- Le jeu est fourni, il est difficile de s'ennuyer.
- L'histoire est prenante, voire touchante. Pour une fois, les quatres élus sont vivant. Les gens nous connaissent (et pas que les vieux zoras).
- Les nombreux pouvoirs permettent de libérer sa créativité de toutes les manières, et les nombreuses solutions aux énigmes nous font nous sentir plus malins que le jeu.
- Un tas de nouveaux plats, de nouvelles tenues, de nouveaux ingrédients, de nouvelles fonctionnalités.
- Une véritable amélioration, des détails qui font toute la différence.
- La plupart de PNJ sont retravaillés. Alors qu'on avait jusque là que trois âges (enfant, adulte, personne âgée), un quatrième a fait son apparition (adolescent).

Points négatifs :
- Un jeu beaucoup trop bazar. On est submergés par des quêtes, des grottes, des puits, des korogus et des monstres.
- Un total oubli du jeu précédent. Toute la technologie archéonique a disparu, les château d'Hyrule a perdu toute sa saveur. Pas de nouveaux secrets sur les vestiges anciens.
- La nouvelle technologie magique n'est pas belle. Du vert brillant, de la "glue", une batterie...? Et surtout, la technologie magique ne semble pas exister dans l'histoire. Dans Botw, l'histoire était centrée sur les gardiens, les sheikas, les créatures divines. Là, hormis Ganondorf et sa magie, on n'entend jamais les personnages s'en sortir grâce à la technologie, qui est pourtant le centre du jeu.
- Pas d'ajouts. Pas de nouveaux peuples, de nouveaux villages, alors que la taille de la map a triplé ! À croire que les développeurs n'ont créé ces nouveaux lieux que pour "stocker" du matériel...

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Este juego, puesto simplemente, es el mejor juego que jugué en mi vida. Las habilidades que se presentan podrían ser, cada una, revolucionarias e increíbles por sí solas. Pero no, acá están las 4 juntas. Ya a nivel mecánico, este juego es una locura nunca antes vista. La forma en la que se puede manipular todo el entorno, y a su vez usar las diversas habilidades a la ves para hacer lo que te dé la gana es una genialidad. Por ejemplo (muy simple), quiero llegar a un lugar alto, entonces agarro una tabla de madera, la alzo, luego la dejo caer y retrocedo el tiempo para infiltrarme. Por más tonto que parezca, esto es una completa locura solo a nivel jugable si no que en programación. Y para agregar más, se agregaron las islas en el cielo, un subsuelo igual de grande que el mapa original, y una red cientos de cuevas y cientos de pozos en el mapa original. Las físicas, a su vez, complementan a las habilidades y el mapa, siendo extremadamente detalladas y retroactivas. Hay tantas cosas para decir sobre este juego, pero intenté resumirlo en un párrafo. Simplemente alucinante en todos los aspectos (incluso la música y la dirección de arte por dios!), y uno de los mejores, sino el mejor juego de la historia. 15/10

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Basically, it's Breath of the Wild, but a lot better. There's so much more to do in TotK. Two brand new areas to explore, on top of the original map being made a new experience again. The side quests are more fun as well. Combat has quality of life improvements. The hand abilities are a lot better than BotW's shekiah slate powers. Ultrahand lets me mess around in all kinds of new ways, like driving across large stretches of land, and kill monsters in new ways. Fuse fixed the weapon durability problem. There is one weakness in gameplay: the sage abilities are more gimmicky and less practical (exception being the wind one). The story is an improvement over BotW (mainly due to the tear memories, rather than Link's own quest) but still a bit lacking. The dungeons are decent, with proper elemental themes returning, as well as unique bosses (rather than the boring Blight Ganons in BotW). The finale is pure greatness, and Ganondorf has had his best showing to date.

Review: 一进游戏就立马勾起了荒野之息的回忆，果不其然还是一如既往的好玩上瘾。比起前作本作在文本故事性做足了功课，主线结局实在是震撼且有共鸣。另外各种支线的小故事也颇为有趣，有种走进海拉鲁人民生活的感觉。说到开放世界，空岛部分十分好玩；但地表部分基本上就和前作一致了，略显重复；地下就不说了，过于阴间且无聊，虽说和地表反过来的设计颇为有巧思。几大神殿和前作一样保持了极高水准的设计水平，尤其是风之神殿，我用俯冲头槌破boss，完全是一种前所未见的游戏体验。最后说一下造高达，确实是神来之笔，然而不作弊的情况下升级电池和收集材料都过于痛苦，只能说更适合云多一点。

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Since the release of BOTW, we never thought it could be beaten, never mind matched. However, Tears Of The Kingdom undoubtedly improves on virtually every single aspect of the game, from the core gameplay its self, to minor details within the game, truly defining it as the greatest game OF ALL TIME. 

Firstly, Tears of the Kingdom drastically improves upon the dungeons seem within Breath Of The Wild. Although the divine beasts were very good, they felt repetitive, and each one felt like a slight reskin of the other. However, in Tears Of The Kingdom we see a more traditional and unique style to the temples, each fitting their respective areas. The lightning temple, a prime example of how great the temples are, feels much more like a traditional dungeon with rooms throughout the dungeon connecting to each other to form a sensational sequence of puzzles to finish the temple. Furthermore, the journey to the temple itself is sensational, truly setting up the marvel of the temple to come. To further improve upon BOTW, the bosses are drastically improved. The fights are thrilling, entertaining and truly enhance the dungeon further. They are completely unique which makes it feel all the more special. 

Secondly, the new abilities introduced truly enhance the gaming experience. Firstly, fuse is essential to fixing the durability problem. Instead of looking for the weapons themselves, fuse allows us to create our own weapons which mean that we are focused upon the materials not the weapons. Ascend allows us to efficiently ascend through ceilings, hills, caves in order to reach another place, almost like revali’s gale. Recall is just out-right amazing. And ultra hand completely revolutionises Tears Of The Kingdom. It allows us to create and tackle the game in what ever way we want, eradication the linear aspect to any puzzle and the game in general. It brings the players imagination to life and truly changes the gameplay experience, making it better than ever. 

Thirdly, the story of TOTK is more in-depth and meaningful than before. Characters like Zelda are more developed and truly feel essential to the plot. It is all a mystery at first, and engages the reader as we slowly unveil the mystery. And, of course, the introduction of Ganondorf is genius, adding a deceitful, thrilling and powerful antagonist to the plot and giving us the greatest Zelda boss fight ever, and the greatest cinematic ending to a game in history. 

Finally, the introduction of the sky Islands and The Depths eradicate the emptiness of breath of the Wild and give us a more jam packed Hyrule. Everywhere you go, there is always a new puzzle, challenge or mystery to the game, perfecting the open world genre. 

Tears Of The Kingdom doesn’t revolutionise open world gaming, but perfects it and improves upon one the greatest games of all time. It is truly a masterpiece and a must get for any player of any console.

I have a lot of flaws with this game. There's too much dialogue, the UI ****, the sky islands are barren, the cutscenes for the dungeons are boring, etc. etc. etc. But all these flaws completely fail to ruin my experience with the game. 

This game gave me an emotion that no other game could have given me. I don't want to do a spoiler review but I can write so much about it. Some of my favorite moments in not only Zelda but gaming history, come from this game and it took me 150 hours to finally decide to fight Ganon. And the ending was... simply fantastic.

Maybe I'm biased or my love for the franchise blinds me to its flaws, but I have not had this much fun with a game since Mario Odyssey nor Celeste.

I don't want to write more. Just know, there are critiques one could give the game, but the highest of highs remain here and I wouldn't trade this experience for anything.

I wondered before what Breath of the Wild was missing when I played that game. It wasn't the weaker abilities; it wasn't the lackluster ending; it wasn't the empty Hyrule. It was one thing: a heart. The charisma and wit of Ocarina of Time, Majora's Mask, Wind Waker, Twilight Princess, and Skyward Sword were missing in Breath of the Wild. This game has it.

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom... has it all. If they just tweaked a few more things and I'd give this a perfect rating

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Esse jogo é talvez o melhor que já joguei e já vi na vida, com um mundo imenso e uma história maravilhosa, Zelda totk é a mistura perfeita de um jogo mundo aberto e linear. Zelda totk é uma melhora em todos o sentidos quanto ao botw, agora com a adição das profundezas e das ilhas no céu, o poder de exploração e a sensação de descobrimento está ainda maior, sem falar que o mapa principal (a superfície) não é exatamente igual a do jogo anterior, mesmo que em teoria fosse o mesmo. Além da exploração, a resolução de problemas e das shrines estão bem melhores, podendo ter diversas soluções para apenas um problema, e muitas vezes necessitando muita criatividade para passar por eles. E por último mas não menos importante, a história de Tears of the Kingdom está espetacular e muito mais imersiva do que nunca, com trechos emocionantes, de deixar qualquer um na ponta da cadeira. Claro que esse jogo não é perfeito, algumas críticas que tenho quanto a ele é de que se repete alguns erros de seu antecessor, não o suficiente para estragar sua jogatina mas ainda assim são meio chatinhos, os problemas mais graves que encontrei são quanto a performance do jogo, onde muitas vezes o fps cai ou para renderizar o mapa e alguns lugares o jogo tem telas de loading maiores do que o ideal, onde muitas vezes me vi pegando o celular enquanto carrega, algo que com certeza não é bom, outro ponto negativo são as profundezas, eu particularmente gostei bastante de explorar, porém preciso admitir que pode sim ser repetitivo e um problema para a maioria das pessoas. No geral The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom é um jogo espetacular e uma obra de arte, e definitivamente um dos melhores jogos de todos os tempos, como disse antes, não é perfeito, mas não acho que suas imperfeições impactam de forma muito negativa a experiência do jogador, e mesmo com esses problemas não muda a grandiosidade deste jogo incrível, e com certeza um jogo que todos que gostam de mundo aberto e uma história fenomenal devem jogar algum dia.

All the Chests you get, have useless stuff in them, just another batch of bow/sword/shield... put them to the 50 other ones in your inventory. Having to walk to my next destination scared me more than Ganondorf and his lackeys and you know whats worse? now you get the same empty useless world in the sky and in the depths.
The Whole game felt like a chore to play. Just finished it at around 65h, not gonna continue or play the sidequests.

Pro:
- Crafting variety is huge, some ppl will love to build machines etc. (not me)
- gameplay is nice, swordplay and bow etc. is great
-love the coloring of the game
- interesting characters including both mcs and villain

con:
- cant call your horse from more than 20 meters. not gonna buy any dlc for that tbh, nintendo has to learn to build in quality of life features (they are probably scared that it would cut the playtime short if you were on horseback all the time)
- weapon durability
- weapons overall,  mastersword is probably the biggest joke ever.
the only good weapons in the game are either limited or have big debuffs... is that supposed to be fun?

- the game is trying too hard to be mysterious .. i dont want to explore everything, give me a clear line, show me where i have to go, where i can find the caves etc., the world is too big and everything looks similar so i dont wanna go to most of those places and explore them

i enjoyed the game but it had moments where i absolutely hated it.
i am glad that i played it, but i will def not preorder the next zelda title thankts to this game

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: It irons out almost all of BotW's weaknesses. GOOD: - Gigantic open world with lots of secrets and unique caves. - A comprehensible story with an epic climax, albeit very predictable. - GANONDORF IS BACK! The final battle is epic, but simple. This is probably the way to pick up casuals and veterans alike. - The skills! Weaponfuse as well as building vehicles is great! Crafting weapons in particular is great fun. There aren't too many special fusions in the end, but it solves the problem that BotW still had. Battles are motivating. You are well rewarded and make noticeable progress without a level system. AVERAGE: - Timeback Skill - is very helpful, but also necessary in places to rewind the far-flying parts that didn't land where you physically expected them to. - Bosses - they're still not as good as they were in previous Zelda instalments, but better than the Ganon fights in BotW. Not good: - Enemy Variation. BotW already had few enemies, but TotK simply has too few enemies for a game in 2023. Only a handful of new ones have been added. I would have liked more creative enemies here, especially because of Weaponfuse. - Dungeons. Some say that the great dungeons of the good Zelda days have returned. I can't confirm that. The 4 story dungeons are even worse than the Divine Beasts. The fire and water temples in particular are just areas stuck together with no depth. The worst dungeons Zelda has ever had. - Sky Islands: Of all things, the main focus of the marketing is the weakest area in the entire game. It's more a question of how you get up there. Once you're up there, one of three copy-paste patterns awaits the player. Boring. On top of that, there is a pathetic variety of enemies up here. There are really only the small robots and maybe the occasional flying enemy. - Underground. Provides strong kicks for the first 3 hours. Then it becomes just as trivially boring as the Sky Islands. Absolutly NO GO: - There's nothing worse for an open world than copying the world from the previous instalment and barely reworking it. There are caves, which are the best innovation on the surface. Everything else in the familiar open world is a bitter disappointment. Exploration is no fun. Worse still: where there was nothing in BotW, there is often nothing to be found in TotK either. So the open world degenerates even more into an Ubisoft junk world. TLDR: A potentiel masterpiece that fails due to its open world formula and doesn't make the most of its cool game design ideas.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
While the game functions fine technically, I don't have much else positive to say. TotK is everything BotW was not, it's unrewarding, grindy, immersion-breaking, poorly written, trend-chasing, un-interactive, and, frankly, stupid. 

The core gameplay loop of exploration doesn't work without a world designed for that exploration, that the player has not experienced and does not fully understand. That was BotW innovation. TotK fails to understand this on a fundamental level to such a degree that we might even start to think BotW was a fluke. 

Beyond that, TotK's new mechanics actually negatively impact BotW's other major innovation: world interaction. Because, you no longer have to think about the terrain when you can just Ascend past it all or build a flying machine to bypass it all. It's kind of amazing how little they considered BotW when making this game.

Then, there's the story, which tries to pretend all other Zelda games never existed. BotW included, despite being a sequel. Never seen anything like it before, but it's awful.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Many people have their own criticisms of this game - the reused map, the weird storytelling, the weapon durability, the objectively empty depths, and objectively repetitive sky islands, which soured the gameplay experience for some. 

However, dropping into Hyrule for the first time in 6 years, what you are met by, are a plethora of questions - What happened to Zelda? What happened to the 4 races of hyrule? What changed? As you explore the surface of Hyrule, you never run out of questions to ask. The depths, and the sky islands, nurture this constant sense of curiosity, drawing your eyes to them, perhaps not acting as second and third maps, but rather like additional locations on the original map, fueling your imagination and curiosity. While the rewards at the end of the trail these questions lead you on may not necessarily be the best or most useful, what is fulfilling is the journey, the act of travelling, the anticipation, and the discovery along the way itself. Along with the constant discovery and exploration, there were some of the highest highlights along the way. This game is the king of setting the mood. The sounds, the atmosphere, and the visuals of the Lightning Temple, Wind Temple and Fire Temple set the mood in the best way possible, getting you ready to take on the puzzles, enemies and bosses.

This game nails the *feeling* of exploration, wonder, and curiosity, enhanced by the gorgeous artstyle and mood setting. This, is what sets this game apart, and this is what makes this game a 10/10 for me, despite all its other shortcomings.

They can manipulate where (and even when) objects are to solve puzzles as well as jumping through ceilings as a brilliant display of vertical traversal. Breath of the Wild was already one of the greatest games ever made, and if this game is just that but improved and on a bigger scale with a brand new mechanic that completely re-invents the wheel, then what's not to love? The game has its flaws not because it isn't like Ocarina of Time in how it does its dungeons or story structure, instead I think ToTK's approach to dungeons are extremely valid and well-made, but it has its flaws due to some repetition in its world and poor writing in its story. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: This was the single greatest gaming experience I have ever had. The opening sequence immediately captured me and left me wanting more. once we gained full control, learning the new mechanics of the game was absolutely delightful. ultrahand especially was the most fun i've ever had learning. The moment the great sky island is finished, the game allows you complete freedom to explore and do whatever you wish. I loved visiting locations that were present in Breath Of the Wild and seeing how the developers changed it. My love for exploration also made traveling the depths one of the most fun parts of the game. there were a ton of mines where i dug up zonaite to upgrade my batteries and every now and then, my exploration would be rewarded with a side quest, or a neat piece of armor that referenced the older zelda games. I smiled from ear to ear upon finding my first piece of the twilight princess set. And the temples for the sages were all so much fun to play through. Especially the wind temple. The atmosphere, music, and dungeon puzzles in that dungeon made me realize that this game was everything I wanted it to be. It's also insane how you can try almost anything with ultrahand and things just work. I don't know how the hell the zelda team pulled off making a game like this work for the switch in just 6 years. the parallels the drew between Zelda and Ganondorf as determined individuals willing to sacrifice everything for their goal, as well as the connection between king Rauru's ideal of what it means to be a king compared to Ganondorf's were executed masterfully. This game was an emotional roller coaster.  Absolutely my favorite game of all time and a must play for anyone who calls themselves a gamer. Not to throw shade at any of the fantastic games that are nominated for GOTY 2023 but after playing them all it feels absolutely impossible that any game other than tears of the kingdom wins. Excellent work Hidemaro Fujibayashi and the rest of your team.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Tears of the kingdom is one of the best games not only from Nintendo, but also in general, its mechanics such as ultra-hand or combination, are fun and easy to understand, which makes it unique, its open world despite being the same, it still feels fresh Thanks to the new sanctuaries, caves and the representation of the underground, the only thing that is not very good at all are the celestial islands, these are few, small and become repetitive, from then on it has a Quite a broad and fun exploration for which you don't know where to start.

Its story seemed somewhat simple and not very elaborate to me, it was what I had the most expectations for, the best part of the story is Zelda's sacrifice to repair the master sword for more than 10,000 years by becoming a dragon, the idea of ​​memories is not bad, it's just that it is not well captured because they were able to put an order to the memories and make them last longer, I also lack context for certain things such as a representation of the underground, how the zonnan became extinct (not counting rauru and mineru), these if we see his **** ending is excellent, it feels epic and magical, even though all the bosses are easy, the dialogues and scenes never cease to amaze, such as Ganondorf, the battle against the black dragon is beautiful, the soundtrack is wonderful and as it is In the Zelda saga, burying the master sword in the dragon to destroy the tear that started it all, making Ganondorf powerful. Breath of the Wild had a sad ending due to the death of the champions but in Tears of the Kingdom despite the death of Mineru's spirit, the post-credits scene conveys joy and peace, defeating Ganondorf, his draconic form and saving to Zelda saving her from the fall and making her Hylian again.

In conclusion, Tears of the Kingdom surpassed its predecessor in many aspects, making it a totally unique open-world video game.

The new areas and building on the old map is awesome, but occasionally some areas feel empty. The machine building and weapon crafting is fun as well, but the controls feel a little clunky. There's a tad bit too much when it comes to shrines and collectables, but those quests are mostly skipable if you don't want to do them  The item durability is less of an issue this time around, which was appreciated! I will say the story is amazing from start to finish. If you love Zelda, and if you adored BotW, this is a must play.

Nintendo has put even more effort into creating the Sandox experience, with unbelievable mechanics that beg the question of how they managed to create this game on the Nintendo Switch. The world's size and richness have nearly tripled, and the gameplay of the basic map has also been significantly altered. The player can navigate to a substantial number of sky islands and a massive subterranean area without encountering any loading screens. In conclusion, Nintendo has succeeded in producing a game that both matched and surpassed its expectations.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
En clair The Legend of Zelda : Tears of the Kingdom est un excellent jeu avec un travail de fou sur des éléments comme les pouvoirs qui offre tellement de possibilité que les développeurs ont prévu/laissé. Mais tout en réussissant à ce qu’il ne soient pas destructeur de l’expérience en cassant totalement le jeu. Un jeu qui vient corriger quelques soucis de son prédécesseur notamment sur les temples et leurs boss qui possède plus d’identité. Qui propose une histoire plus intéressante, des musiques toujours aussi bien travaillé comme son univers. Bien que la formule soit conservée et toujours au top on ressent trop que c’est une suite directe. Avec trop de nombreux manques d’ambition sur certains aspects, surtout avec 7 ans de développement derrière, soit plus qu’entre Skyward Sword et Breath of the Wild. Un bestiaire trop inchangé, des îles et souterrains sous exploité ou encore des boss qui manque de puissance.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
So much busy work. So. Much. Time. Wasting. 
How many times do I need to see the same temple cut scene? I don't care about the poor dialogue from unmemorable NPCs. 
To make it worse, for a hand-held console game, the button mapping is a nightmare. It tries to do so much and we're given so little, an octopus would have a hard time trying to juggle all the different controls you need to remember and execute simultaneously. Why is "send a giant annoying opaque rock monster flying, exploding everything in its path" the same freaking button as "pick up this exploding plant" This only get more annoying with the ever expanding crowd of opaque **** crowding Link doing nothing but block his view and slightly improve the meaningless busy-work that needs to be done. 
All in all it's a collection of colourful fetch quests in large open spaces by Nintendo. Play it on a plane.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Simply put- the best game ever made. It’s so good that its flaws become irrelevant. Exploration and creativity have never been better applied to a video game. It takes everything BOTW was and tops it. 

Ultrahand is the greatest gaming mechanic ever made. It adds an unprecedented level of creativity and interactivity. There’s nothing more fun or engaging than designing a machine, device, or item to accomplish or reach something. It along with fuse lead the list that adds up to the best set of abilities Zelda has ever had. 

It’s almost inconceivable that arguably the most massive open world game ever made was pulled off on such obsolete hardware with so little compromises. The graphics are somehow immersive and fantastic as a result of Nintendo’s doctorate in cartoon worlds and knowing what makes graphics look good and bad. With that said, I’d still love to see what Nintendo could do with identical hardware to PS5 and Series X. 

I spent over 700 hours on this game because I didn’t want it to end and because there’s that much to do in it. 

My only real complaints are that the coordinates should’ve had a movable reticle that shows it’s locations rather than yours, the hero’s quest tracker was too short and should’ve been limitless, that the game could have had a more organized and extensive tracking of true 100% completion and central hub featuring several hundred categories (you can add hundreds of hours to a game by simply creating more to complete), the lack of a meter that shows a weapon’s or shield’s degradation, and the main dungeons should’ve been self contained and lengthier. All that said, as I noted above it’s so good it makes these complaints completely irrelevant. 

At the end of the day, like BOTW it’s as good as gaming gets and further proof Nintendo is untouchable when it comes to game design. I just hate that there’s such an extensive wait in between titles. If only gaming had the same delivery time as TV shows. Imagine a world where we get one Zelda per year or every other year.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: I really wanted to love TOTK. While the game is wonderful and nostalgic on its own, I cannot shake the feeling of general disappointment. The incredible draw and magic of BOTW lies in a world undiscovered, the melancholic yet absolutely liberating feeling that you're one with the wild, seeing what's beyond every hill, lake, cliffside, spark in the distance. TOTK doesn't have that feeling anymore because the main map has already been explored in the previous game, and both the sky islands and the depths are not real worlds with complex biomes, objectives, and stories for you to want to explore. They're just filler environments, stretched for the sake of expanding the worlds. They're not that rewarding or exciting to discover as a whole. The memory aspect also doesn't fit with TOTK, and the story line falls under the same formula as BOTW, which does not work in the context of TOTK. Although the weapons, combat, runes, gameplay elements are new and exciting and innovative, the core meat of the game (story, world exploring), are just not enough to make this game great. In summary, TOTK doesn't capture the magic and awe that BOTW has in its open world concept , doesn't have elements from previous zelda games that make up for it (story is weak, dungeons are weaker), and the innovative aspects of the game (building, interesting runes), are just not nearly enough to make this game a truly spectacular standalone zelda game.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Strong proposition from Nintendo who doubles down on the Breath of the wild recipe, with added mechanics but overall same game structure in almost every aspect (shrines, 4 abilities, 4 main temples, … the list goes on).I have to praise how innovative Nintendo developers have been while using the same basics. The player will experience again the joys of discovering abilities and find fun and exciting ways to use and mix them to solve puzzles.A good thing is the emphasis on the story structure, which was not really the case with the previous game (pretty lackluster in that regard). The map is also more filled with caves, wells, enemies, things to build with abilities etc… Some stuff feels dispensable to be honest.Given the fact that there are skies and souterrains now, I would even say that the game feels a bit bloated but this gives gamers a lot of hours to enjoy their game (only if they like to do the same thing again and again …).What bugs me the most in that game is not related to its content or structure. It has to do with the techinical capabilities of the console.I find it concerning that this game is so strongly hindered by Nintendo’s unwilingness to provide a console on par with the ambitions of the developers. The framerate, the resolution are just horrible for a 2023 game and although I enjoy the game, I find it too bad that it is not able to express its qualities, merely because the hardware on which it is delivered is way passed obsolete. This struck me as soon as I played the prologue, as I found the eery autumnal ambience and tone particularly well done, if not burdened by slobbery textures and unsteady framerate. But this initial impression stuck with me for the total duration of my playthrough. And it even got worse as you get companions later on, which makes the Switch struggle like hell.A videogame, albeit very good at its core, can not be good when it is not playable, sorry. Please update your hardware and respect your franchise with a console able to support it.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: This is the most innovative game I have ever played. I missed out on Breath of the Wild until a year after its release, so I didn't get that magic of exploring Hyrule completely blind without any spoilers. After having played Tears of the Kingdom completely blind, I now understand what the big deal was. Except now, you have so much more freedom in movement and altitude, which makes exploring all the more fun. Things like farming dragon parts were made so much easier, because of the freedom of the sky the game gives you. Also, I like how they developed the story and the relationship between Link and Zelda. Breath of the wild was lauded as one of the greatest games ever(rightfully so), but Tears of the Kingdom takes it to a whole other level.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: It's effectively just Breath of the Wild but better in every way. Better side quests, better visuals, better abilities, better story, better shrines, better enemy variety, a better world, and more content to sink your teeth into if you're a completionist. However, two things hold the game back. The first one is the UI, which is extremely clunky when doing things like fighting alongside sages or attaching items to your bow. The second major issue is that the game is on the Nintendo Switch. I love the Switch, but it can barely handle this game and its innovative mechanics. Frame drops are the norm and not being able to experience this game in 4k 60fps means part of the world's beauty is lost. Despite that though, the new mechanics alone could warrant buying the game since they are unbelievably fun to mess around with for hours.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The Legend Of Zelda Tears of the Kingdom SIGNIFICANTLY improves all aspects of the previous entry and continues to bring what made BOTW a great game with it’s story mechanics and voice acting. However in this entry with the nearly 7 year old system that is powering the game, the mechanics sometimes struggle to truly live up to modern day games. The game suffers performance issues that modern day gaming would find atrocious and absurd. Combat in the game has not improved much for the entry and the enemies are mostly familiar. It’s quite unreasonable the charge that Nintendo is offering for the game. What this game really delivers on in the other hand no pun intended is ultra hand, this new ability can stick almost anything together. Players have created such monstrosity’s like mechs to cars. This is an unusual mechanic to this series however the way it’s used and the endless possibilities are truly what make this game shine including a world that has tripled.

VERDICT: The Legend of Zelda Tears of The Kingdom is full of fun surprises in a familiar place. The game is full of tech issues, however with the addition of Ultrahand brings a whole new light to this game.
Due to the Nintendo consoles lack of performance the game remains a last gen experience that may not be suitable for most gamers, Nintendo Switch Fans will find this possibly the greatest Switch Game of All Time.

7.5/10 Great!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Review in Portuguese.
Tears of the Kingdom parece viver à sombra do seu predecessor, trazendo inovações que, embora interessantes, não justificam completamente o preço integral do jogo. Entre as novidades, os novos poderes e a mecânica de construção são os pontos altos, sendo implementados de maneira criativa e eficaz. No entanto, outras adições deixam a desejar. 
O novo mapa, chamado Depths, é notavelmente vazio e repetitivo, dando a impressão de ter sido incluído apenas para justificar a existência de uma nova área no jogo. As ilhas no céu também são escassas e, em grande parte, se assemelham umas às outras, o que diminui a sensação de variedade e exploração. 
A trama é envolvente, mas não traz nada de realmente inovador, seguindo uma estrutura de missões semelhante ao jogo anterior. Para um título desse porte, esperava-se uma abordagem mais inovadora e cativante.
Em relação aos gráficos, o jogo mantém o belo estilo de arte do seu antecessor, mas, em algumas ocasiões, parece até pior, o que é decepcionante, especialmente considerando que o jogo foi lançado para o Nintendo Switch. A escolha de um console limitado pela própria Nintendo não justifica totalmente esse retrocesso visual.
A trilha sonora é um ponto forte, com composições fantásticas e emocionantes, embora uma parte significativa delas seja reaproveitada do jogo anterior. 
Em resumo, Tears of the Kingdom é um jogo competente, mas é difícil ignorar a falta de inovação em muitos aspectos. É decepcionante ver um título tão esperado reciclar elementos sem trazer melhorias significativas. Ainda assim, ele oferece uma experiência sólida para os fãs da série, mesmo que deixe a sensação de que poderia ter sido muito mais do que é.

GOTY 2023.
Zelda TOTK superou minhas expectativas e se tornou o melhor jogo que eu ja joguei na vida. Todas as criticas envolvendo o BOTW ficam extremamente irrelevantes quando se trata de TOTK. Esse jogo não somente superou o seu antecessor como também impulsionou e transformou positivamente tudo o que conheci em BOTW. Zelda TOTK aprimora o combate, revoluciona a exploração e os puzzles (que são incríveis), e, acima de tudo, contém uma lore magnífica e muito bem roteirizada. A historia de TOTK esta em outro nível! Eu realmente fiquei impressionado com a diferença entre os games, porque em BOTW o mundo era vasto mas ao mesmo tempo era vazio, a historia era boa, mas ao mesmo tempo era comum, enquanto em TOTK o mundo ganha vida. As sky islands, o underground, a exploração da superfície, a utilização de tudo que está em sua volta para solucionar as dificuldades de exploração... tudo está extremamente bem feito e bem planejado. Os novos poderes: ultra hand, fuse, ascend, recall... TODOS são incríveis. Tudo em Zelda TOTK é incrível, surpreendente, completo, magnífico, e, acima de tudo, MONUMENTAL. Acima de GOTY, esse jogo é o melhor de todos os tempos. ZELDA TEARS OF THE KINGDOM É MONUMENTAL.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
It's a great, fun and beautiful sandbox action game, but I long for the days when Nintendo valued story and lore. I think there's been a Mario-fication of the Zelda series and the developers have even stated that the story isn't critical to Zelda games, but I'd argue that the story is what has always driven interest in it. Look at any Zelda fan forum or site and they're overflowing with analyses of the story and the lore.

TOTK's gameplay is undoubtedly great, but I found the main story once again left a lot to be desired. I found much more joy in the side quests (like Lurelin village) and general exploration. My advice is to avoid the main story as much as possible and explore the game. The end of the game felt rushed and like an afterthought, unlike the beginning, so don't hurry to the end.

Are we ever going to have instruments and great music in Zelda games again? I sure hope so. TOTK is a wonderful game, and it sounds like it's the formula that Nintendo is going to use going forward, but I pray for a better story and music in the next one. I don't know how Nintendo can look at the success of Elden Ring, a brand new IP, and keep saying that story isn't important for the Zelda series.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Yes, they reused BOTW map, but they changed, added so much to it: underworld, sky islands, and tons of caves (filled with materials). The new mechanisms (fuse, zonai builds) adds so much variety in the way to handle battles and at times exploration. Along with the new items' usage, these new features overall extends greatly over BOTW the number of methods at disposal to solve problems. Creativity runs wild thanks to Zonai builds allowing for almost unlimited possibilities. As a result, some shrines can be solved in multiple ways. The fantastic physics unique to this game will be talked about years and years after. You might surprise yourself when trying to build a cutomized machine, not knowing if your machine is built properly and is working as intended. You get sometimes this "Aha" moment when you find out it actually works or how it should work. Then you go wild testing and destroying any moving living things (no I didn't say Koroks, though I could...).

The final boss fight might be one of the most memorable fighting moments I have ever witnessed.

On the downside, the sky islands are sometimes a bit empty and there are repeat locations in the depth (e.g., Yiga hideout and monster mining camp) but there are also tons of good surprises in the skies (dungeons, starview, zonaite forge) and in the depth (bosses, coliseums, labyrinths, spirits, abandoned mines, all the areas surrounding fire temple).

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
People are going too soft on this game since it got review-bombed with 10s at the start and they're probably afraid of offending people. It's not just - "Im too old for this!" (Thats an excuse to calm the internet). As a 26-year-old, I can still enjoy many other games with more intensive puzzle mechanics/building. A game where I have to watch a youtube video to make every contraption I need to make is a bad game. I get absolutely no reward for tediously gluing parts together for hours so to complete this slog I just ended up climbing and using stamina potions just like the last game. Call me an idiot, but I don't have time to keep failing, and failing just to save another Korok and get two pieces of poop. I've been a Zelda fan for decades and played and enjoyed every title thus far (even BOTW! Though I enjoyed it less than many others). TOTK is "fun" in the sense that sometimes I feel like I get to do something interesting, but lets face it - for the most part this game is a puzzle/engineering sim THEMED with Zelda. And if you dont like spending hours upon hours doing literal work for minor rewards, this game isn't for you. We watched people playing it online - tons of videos with robots shooting lasers from their nether regions and thought haha! That looks fun. But the strangest thing happened. My partner and I get the game, played for an afternoon, and then moved on with our lives. Then I went to plug in my Wii and play Twilight Princess again ;) When the hype clears and your depression over the world's events has its upturn - which game do you return to? Probably not TOTK.
Also where's this metacritic score coming from? 96? Really? That is hilarious. Nice job lining your pockets with Nintendo money.

Review: If you compare TOTK to BOTW, then yes TOTK beats BOTW overall. But TOTK feels like a very solid expansion pack of the previous game. Exploration has been ramped up, story expanded in a very satisfying way and core gameplay loop remains the same. Biggest milestone is the new feature of utilizing your surroundings to merge weapons and create various tools for transport and destruction. A fantastic addition to the general gameplay. And exploring the various levels was a blast. While the game definitely amazed me, it lacked for me the same WOW factor I experienced with BOTW. In some sense its suffering from its own previous success. I hope they continue with this format of Zelda games, but if they do so completely different map.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: This game is a milestone for the Zelda franchise as a whole, as it builds on the environment already established in Breath of the Wild, but also incorporates elements of older Zelda games within it. Tears of the Kindgom’s story is also unbelievable in its own right. Although it retains the same format of storytelling from Breath of the Wild, that being explaining the narrative through events that occur in the past, it subverted my expectations with its intriguing ideas. Furthermore, the gameplay is outstanding, for it allows the player to make the game as creative and fun as they want it to be. Instead of making a set of rules that the player must follow to accomplish tasks, they said, “Here,  YOU figure out YOU want to solve this problem.” Overall, Tears of the Kingdom fixes most of Breath of the Wild’s problems, and outshines it in many ways. I strongly recommend this game if you haven’t played it already.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Clairement le meilleur Zelda auquel j’ai pu jouer. Cependant, cela est sûr et certain que les personnes ayant déjà été sceptiques sur le nouveau format que le dernier opus avait apporté le resteront. Oui le jeu est une extension de Breath Of The Wild étant une suite DIRECTE de ce dernier, cela ne veut en rien dire que le jeu lui est une copie sans ajout de contenus. AU CONTRAIRE.
Ce jeu, c’est Breath Of The Wild, avec les **** soucis en moins et un contenu MONSTRE.
Les sanctuaires sont pour certains plus faciles pour d’autres plus difficiles, ce qui est sûr, c’est que la possibilité de faire chaque énigme de la façon dont on le souhaite est fabuleuse.
De plus le marketing de Nintendo en ne montrant que l’espace céleste était réellement réussi, quelle était ma surprise lors de ma découverte des profondeurs qui font la taille de la map entière de BOTW avec une ambiance étonnamment étrange, sombre voire même horrifique.
Pour les amateurs de musique de jeux vidéo là aussi pour moi, c’est un carton plein, que dire tout est bien géré, autant dans le réarrangement de musique des précédents opus que dans les nouvelles productions alors merci à Koji Kondo et à son équipe de compositeur.
L’histoire, elle, a été étoffée surtout comparée à son désormais petit frère BOTW, même si on aimerait en avoir plus sous les dents, mais finalement les histoires des Zelda ne sont pas si remplies que ça, et je trouve ça bien dommage.
Bref.
C’est un excellent jeu, j’ai réussi à retrouver la surprise et l’émerveillement que Breath Of The Wild m’avait apporté.
J’ai adoré ce virage qu’a pris l’équipe Zelda avec ce format. Je suis d’autant plus heureux qu’ils aient choisi de sortir un BOTW 2.
En résumé, foncez si vous avez adoré Breath Of The Wild, essayez si vous n’avez pas joué à BOTW et je vous déconseille si vous avez détesté Breath Of The Wild car force est de constater que c’est une suite.

Review:
ToTK It's basically Breath Of The Wild, but enhanced, not just in the game mechanics, but also in the performance, gameplay, art and so on.

For me, it's an incredible game, I had very good times with it and I even finished it with the 70% of the total content done. But the waiting for the game release have been long and, unfortunatelly, for me it doesn't really deserve it.

I must be from that group of people that they don't like the new creative tools, but what can I say! I didn't really use the tools for displacements or other purposes, because at the end of the day I use the same 2-3 ways to explore, combat or move.

And it's cool that now people have new ways for being creative, but I feel like we didn't need so much 'freedom'. Also, the world is bigger, but the space between every 'content area' stills big too. I know that there are hardware limitations, but you can make more with less space.

Tears of The Kingdom It's an awesome adventure and I'm excited to see what's next but, for me, doesn't deserve the GOTY.

Review:
Es un excelente juego, mejora en todos los aspectos a breath of the wild, si bien el mundo ciertamente es el mismo, es mucho más grande, tenemos el cielo con sus islas flotantes, y el subsuelo que sigue siendo una gran extensión de tierra para explorar, gráficamente tiene una ligera mejora respecto a breath of the wild, sobre todo en la iluminación, la banda sonora a mi parecer también mejoro, al explorar tenemos temas un poco más variados que solo las 3 notas de piano del juego pasado.
Jugablemente ni que decir, es mucho más superior que breath of the wild, nos permite explorar el mundo de mil maneras diferentes, y con respecto a la dificultad, tuvo un aumento, no monstruoso al grado de decir que es un dark souls, pero ciertamente es algo más difícil que breath of the wild y eso se agradece, los enemigos son más fuertes, hay más variedad de ellos y podría jurar que la inteligencia artificial fue mejorada.
Solo le veo 2 detalles, uno de estos "detalles" entre comillas, es que la estructura en si, es prácticamente la misma que el juego pasado, partimos de una zona delimitada en la que hay que completar varios santuarios para obtener acceso al mundo abierto, y al llegar a el partimos de la premisa de que hay que visitar las 4 regiones que ya vimos en el juego pasado, si bien en mi opinión esto no es un problema muy grande, ya que hablamos que es su secuela directa, si que podría resultar repetitivo para algunos.
Y el último detalle que si considero un problema, es el rendimiento, dios, en general es bueno, casi siempre se mantienen los 30fps, pero hay momentos donde puede llegar a caer a los 20, y ni siquiera son momentos donde hay mucha acción, por ejemplo en la aldea kakariko, el juego en ocasiones baja de esos 30 fps, o en zonas abiertas donde usamos la ultramano también llega a bajar en ocasiones, y no se si sea cuestión de mi switch, pero por momentos hace bastante ruido, solo en el modo tv, no al punto de oirse como turbina de avión pero si te acercas es notorio, la switch es una gran consola y ha tenido ports muy buenos, pero con tears of the kingdom, me parece que ya pide su jubilación a gritos.
Es un excelente juego, probablemente Goty, pero el rendimiento si deja bastante que desear.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The Legend of Zelda series has always been a beacon of innovation and storytelling in the gaming world. With "Tears of the Kingdom," the franchise has once again outdone itself, proving that there's always room for growth and evolution, even in a series as storied as this one.

Compared to its predecessor, "Tears of the Kingdom" is a treasure trove of depth and richness. The main quest itself is a sprawling epic, filled with intricate narratives, challenging puzzles, and memorable characters. But where the game truly shines is in its side adventures and dungeons. In the previous installment, many felt that there was a noticeable lack of these elements, which are quintessential to the Zelda experience. Thankfully, the developers took this feedback to heart. The new dungeons are not only numerous but also varied, each offering a unique challenge and story. The side quests, meanwhile, are as engaging as the main storyline, often intertwining with it in unexpected ways.

Exploration in "Tears of the Kingdom" is unparalleled. The vast, open world is brimming with secrets waiting to be discovered, from hidden villages to ancient ruins. Every nook and cranny feels purposeful, and the sense of wonder never diminishes, no matter how many hours you pour into the game.

One of the standout features of this installment is the introduction of new gameplay mechanics. These fresh additions breathe new life into the series, ensuring that even long-time fans will find something novel to enjoy. Without giving away any spoilers, players can expect to be pleasantly surprised and challenged in new ways.

In conclusion, "The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom" is a masterclass in game design and storytelling. While it pays homage to its roots, it's not afraid to chart new territories. With its deep quests, expansive world, and innovative gameplay, it's no wonder it has earned a well-deserved 9 out of 10. Whether you're a seasoned Zelda veteran or a newcomer to the series, this game is a must-play.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I can't remember the a time I complained about a game nearly the entire time I played it, yet left the experience loving it so much, but The Legend of Zelda Tears of the Kingdom currently has the honor of being that experience for me. Everything about this game is familiar to it's predecessor Breath of the Wild, but harder. The enemies hurt more, the weapons are weaker, the guidance is vaguer, the side quests are more convoluted, and everything about it reminds me how much I love the first game more... And yet somehow, that made this title stand out in a way that made it so unique. It's so different as a successor with so many new and unique mechanics that changed up the gameplay experience, and that created a new level of fun in it's own right (and plenty of frustration, but still lots of fun).

Breath of the Wild had a clear focus on exploration, and a world to explore and secrets to uncover. That charm is missing here, with the same world as the first game and a more desolate one at that. Instead where the charm of Tears of the Kingdom comes in is expanding on that world. Revisiting characters from the first game was an honest joy that made me happy to see some old favorites again, which was the case both in main quests as well as the side adventures that all tell their own charming stories. Story is the clear focus of this game, reusing old favorites like Zelda, Purah and the friends Link made in each regions, but also adding new characters to deepen the lore like Rauru, Sonia, and of course Ganondorf. How this game expanded on it's world and characters was done not by giving us new things to see, but more to do in the places we've already seen. Apart of me almost wishes you started the game with the surface map unlocked for this very reason. This game is the true definition of a sequel in every sense of the word.

I could go on for paragraphs over what makes Tears of the Kingdom so special, but honestly it has a magic that has to be found on it's own. This game can be punishing, even grueling at times. Full completion feels nearly impossible, and with such a well done story, you may find yourself just wanting to cross the finish line rather than stop to smell the roses. But for every complaint I could have, I could go on about something I loved about the experience. Tears of the Kingdom may not be a perfect game, but it was an amazing one that I will never forget, and would happily revisit again.

The experience is here.

Even worse they completely diminished Ganondorfs character.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
A great adventure game, but a completionists nightmare

Tears of the Kingdom is a fantastic game if you're looking for a 60-hour experience, but if you set yourself completionist goals, for example discovering all shrines, the flaws of this game weigh in heavily, since the game then easily reaches the 200-hour mark.

These being:
- The horrible controls (not remappable)
- The recycled and way too small soundtrack
- The grind; 100,000 rupees to upgrade all armor sets while a quest rewards an average of 20- Enemy Sponges
- The repetitive weapon fusing- The Ultrahand vehicle puzzles

I recommend this game to any fan of exploration games, but do not plan to complete it to 100%.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Zelda Tears of the Kingdom is a masterpiece! So much so Xbox, Sony and people from Steam had to congratulate Nintendo publicly for it. It again does what systems that boas of power and technology marvel can’t even do.      Link is exploring Hyrule again but it’s not the same as last time! There is now sky portions and also the depths (beneath the ground) portion! I explained it to a friend and he was like. “Oh shoot! So you go to hell?!” I cracked up so hard!!! I told him no you don’t go to hell but you’re deep underground and becasue there is lava in certain parts it’s kind of like hell. lol!      Not only that but there are new sages of the elements to help Link and not just with a little measly attack like the last ones. There aren’t any divine beats this time but you can take avatars of those elemental sages with you all at once in Hyrule!      Yes that’s right you can literally go around with your own mob and mob on the moblins and other monsters for a change! This was a breath of fresh air for me to see Link not alone all the time. There are the usual weapons and items you can collect on your own or buy from vendors.      There is so much to do and I know I didn’t do everything, but the dungeons are absolutely amazing!      They all have a theme song but the theme changes depending on what stage of the dungeon you’re at. So basically every dungeon actually has about 5 different songs to it. There are 4 main dungeons so that’s 20 songs. They way they blend it with the story is incredible and it’s so fitting not intruding on the gameplay at all like many AAA games seem to like to do.      No area is off limits and you aren’t penalized for going out of bounds or some other silly crap like that. If anyone wants to make any game open world or not, you should definitely take notes from Zelda TOTK.      Wherever you see you can go. One of the new features this time around are the being below and going above through the earth. This power is great and definitely makes scaling certain areas they you may remember in Zelda Breath of the Wild much more easy now. The upheaval happened and due to that there are more caves than ever in Hyrule. Use that to your advantage!      The depths are great for finding a new raw mineral called Zoneite. This is integral if you want to use the newly descovered ancient tech.     To top it all off you know who is the last boss. The big bad! He’s back in full force this time not just as some ethereal mad being but as the man the myth and the legend that is Ganon/Ganondorf! He’s everything you’d expect from a top tier villain, and depending on how you played the game it can be more or less challenging leading up to him.      Nintendo once again outdoes themselves and pushes the hardware to the max with this one, continuing to set the standard for games anywhere and  everywhere.      I give Zelda TOTK a 11/10, and it greatly exceeds my expectations so much! It’s packed with content! An absolute must buy! I recommend it to everyone! Love and peace! happy gaming everyone!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Tears of the Kingdom is an excellent if imperfect game that doubles down on the Breath of the Wild formula instead of reinventing it. It pushes and expands it as far as it can go on the Switch, stuffing open world Hyrule with a Lego universe of movable and buildable objects, adding a new dimension of sky islands and underground labyrinths, and creating more complex bosses and temples than BotW. When the game fires on all cylinders, it really fires: Some of the set-piece boss encounters, especially the epic finale with Ganondorf, are superb. And the new building powers are tastefully handled, coaxing you into using them at your leisure rather than forcing you into anything (apart from one pretty painful robot mission). But overall there are fewer moments of wonder and more busywork than in BotW. And there was less reason to hang around up in the sky or explore the depths than I’d hoped. More of the same is no bad thing when it’s Zelda, and overall this is a worthy sequel. But when the credits rolled I felt ready to move on from this chapter of Hyrule.

Review:
I think my score gets extra points because i didn't play botw. For me, the exploration was a new thing in Zelda games, i don't know if it felt the same for players who played both totk and botw. Overall this game is awesome, but has a few major let downs. 
 
The dungeons are really boring compared to older Zelda titles. In totk all dungeons are based on one idea, go to four or five different places and then fight the boss. At least the last dungeon has more character.
 
Also the story doesn't go anywhere while you complete the main four dungeons around Hyrule. After each dungeon you get almost exactly the same cut scene every time, about the imprisoning war. It is one of the most boring ways for a game to tell a story.

This review turned out to be way more negative then i wanted. I still love the game. The ending is really epic and overall i think the game was best after the four temples.

The gameplay and exploration is really fun, sometimes i played the game for like 5 hours without noticing. The abilities were really fun and creative. My favourite has to be ascend. It makes coming out from caves so much easier. The Zonai devices was a really cool addition as well. Building vehicles was fun and a really easy way of exploring the depths.

My score still remains a 9 even though the game has it's flaws. It might not be my favourite Zelda game, but it still was an epic and fun journey!

It's a bunch of padding designed to waste as much time as possible to block you from getting to the better content. The main overworld map is copy-pasted from BOTW. The underworld map is copy-pasted from the overworld map. The sky islands are just frustrating to navigate, in general. Review:
If you played BotW, don’t get this game because you’ve already played it. This game has its origins as BotW DLC and it shows - it’s messed right up that they charge a whopping $70 for 4 extra gigs of poor game design. If you didn’t play BotW, you’re clear.

While I’m not going to pretend that I didn’t have a good time with this game, I’m also not going to pretend I didn’t have a good time because it was Breath of the Wild again. The two heavily and maliciously advertised regions in the game are either complete gimmicks or just straight up boring and a slog to get through. The dungeons are on average much better than the Divine Beasts except for the water dungeon because of the cognitive dissonance of it being in the sky and the last dungeon in the game (not the final area) is straight up just a tech demo. The story is just a slightly altered repeat of its predecessor with a whole new cast you’re never going to meet. The gameplay is “better” especially since it fixes the main issue with weapons that people had in the last game. The game however shamelessly lies to you in order to make ends meet. No like seriously. In the numbers and the world itself. I have a whole 13.3 MB documents of me going on a rant about this game I can share if requested.

I’m saying this as a diehard fan of this franchise and it infuriates me that this is what we got. Can’t in good faith recommend this to any Zelda veteran. If it was in the $30 -$40 price range this game would be an well deserved 9-10 /10 but if you’re going to list yourself as a higher than average AAA game at $70 you better have the bite to back up that bark and this game just doesn’t have that.

Es una estafa. Es un DLC de BOTW. Es exactamente igual. Tenes que buscar a Zelda y ayudar a las 4 tribus, vaya casualidad... igual que BOTW. Encima los 4 templos son EXACTAMENTE IGUALES. A veces se torna insoportablemente lento (aldea onana por decir un ejemplo). El clan Yiga, una vez que tenes la primera pelea, despues va a ser el resto igual... vas al lugar donde esta, peleas, se escapa y lo tenes que seguir al siguiente lugar...
Aparecen nuevas mecanicas, se utilizan mas los materiales (sarcasmo) reemplazaron habilidades por otras simplemente: Antes tenias bombas? ahora podes acoplar armas a piedras para romper paredes, pero adivina que... vas a tener que ocupar espacio en armas que su unico fin es romper piedras (y que encima se suelen romper antes de que te abras camino, por lo que tenes que cargar muchas). Podes hacer mas fuertes las armas? es exactamente igual que BOTW solo que ahora estan oxidadas las armas y es NECESARIO usar materiales para mejorarlas (SUPER FORZADO). Las camaras del juego dejan mucho que desear (lentas de moverse, muchas veces dificultan lo que queres hacer, sobre todo con el iman), los acompañantes en los templos son insufribles y te ocupan espacio de camara todo el tiempo (sobre todo el goron... dios mio, tuve que googlear como hacer el templo de fuego rapido porque no lo soportaba mas de acompañante).

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Warning: Minor Spoilers

Not only has Tears Of The Kingdom surpassed its predecessor, but, in my eyes, it has surpassed every other game in history regarding its quality in practically every aspect of the game.

First and foremost the gameplay is incredible, there is a real sense of immersive and engaging exploration no matter where you find yourself in Hyrule. Many criticise the fact that it reuses the map from Botw, however to call it a reused map is harsh at best. Not only are there many additions to the bulk of Hyrule (such as the temples, new enemies with new fortresses and a multitude of caves) but there are two new unique sections; the depths and the sky islands. Although both can at times become a bit repetitive, the vast amount of new and mysterious locations, alongside the diversity of new monsters makes both a pleasure to explore. The combat, while unchanged, is nonetheless thrilling, and is refreshed by the addition of new enemies such as the Gleeok and Froxes. Alongside this, one of the most hated aspects of Botw combat has been somewhat mended, and of course I am referring to weapon durability. The ability of fuse, while not completely solving breaking weapons, still allows new and powerful weapons to be remade fairly easily and adds a creative aspect to Link’s weapon stash. Furthermore, the addition of ultra hand has been praised by many for adding further creativity to the game, and giving the player more freedom to explore Hyrule as they wish.

Secondly, I highly praise Nintendo for the enthralling story provided. Throughout the entirety of the game I found myself constantly looking forward to encountering a Geoglyph, as practically every time I was treated with a captivating or thrilling scene regarding Hyrule’s past. The addition of new characters such as Rauru, Mineru and Sonia, alongside the return of our favourite characters such as Link, Zelda and the man the myth the Legend Sidon, has added a both familiar and emotional side to the story. I must take a moment to talk about the return of the Demon King himself: Ganondorf. My hat goes off to Nintendo for the addition of such a menacing, intimidating and epic character. He is the driving force for the entire story and the final boss battle against him is inconceivably incredible, by far the best boss battle I have ever done. I do recognise that there are some convenient tying up of loose ends post game, however the ending is ultimately wholesome and rewarding.

Finally, the progression of the game is also very well executed. While some argue that they fall short of the quality of old Zelda dungeons, the 5 (technically 6) temples are all a blast to complete. They all have a much needed uniqueness about them and there are a couple of brilliant boss battles, but ultimately they are a nice change from the reparative nature of Botw’s divine beasts.

I apologise for the lengthy review, however I just wanted to reveal and reiterate what an incredible game this is. If you haven’t already picked it up I highly suggest that you do. 

Easily the best game I have ever played: 

10/10

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Tears of the Kingdom is a really fun game. It's new mechanics, bosses, and parts of it's story are really cool, fun and entertaining. It does have it's downsides however. For one, the sage's powers are not as good as the champion's from Breath of the Wild. 

A good example of this is Riju's power, where a lightning bolt strikes wherever an arrow hits. This does work well on paper, but when they executed it, it was difficult to activate not only because of the other sages, but also because Riju used melee combat only. So to use a range move with a melee fighter who always runs towards the enemy make things pretty annoying. 

Another thing that annoys me is the lack of connection between BotW and Totk. While playing the game, I only really got some references to Mipha, but not to the others. And sure, I can get their weapons, but I'm not sure that 100% counts. What also annoyed me is how there's no way to transfer items from Breath of the Wild to Tears of the Kingdom. It would've been cool if we had some way of doing so, like going into the house at Hateno Village and finding them.

The final thing I wanna mention that annoys me are the droprates of certain items. I spent at least 3 days hunting Ice-Breath Lizafros because I needed their tails in order to upgrade my Desert Voe Trousers, and out of the 39 (Yes I counted them) Ice-Breath Lizafros that I could find, only 6 of them actually dropped a tail.

However looking past those small annoyances, I did enjoy the game. Weapons when fused last longer than normal weapons in Breath of the Wild, which is incredible because it actually feels like I'm using a weapon for more than 5 seconds. Back in Breath of the Wild, a normal Lynel fight use to take at least 3-5 of my weapons. In Tears of the Kingdom, not so much. Sure, sometimes my weapons break during those fights, but it's not as short as it is in Breath of the Wild.

Overall, I do love this game. I recommend you try it.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This game is great, but it kind of annoys me to see so many reviewers call it a masterpiece. It does have plenty of flaws.
The good:
-Fun, interesting, unique gameplay. The mechanics are almost the same as Breath of the Wild and that's okay, it was a great game too. The main new mechanic is the building of zonai devices. It felt out of place to and it can be really janky, but it is fun once you get the hang of it.
-The story is a bit more cohesive and interesting and a less generic than your typical Zelda game.
-Exploration is top notch. There's so much to do and look at. So much interesting stuff happening. If you see something unusual in the distance, there's a 90% chance something worth checking out awaits.
-Copy and paste most of what was great about Breath of the Wild.
The bad:
-The starting price of $70.
-Enemies are overpowered. Most enemies can kill you in two or three hits. As you gain more hearts and better armor, the smaller enemies will take a little longer to kill you, but the large enemies still kill you in two or three hits. The exception is the bosses. They're actually pretty easy.
-The unskippable and partly skippable cutscenes you have to watch over and over again. Nintendo, STOP IT.
-The unskippable and slowly scrolling dialog. Nintendo STOP IT!
-Platforming. Zelda games need to fix the way Link jumps or stop having platforming. It is tedious and its not fun. He jumps much like you would in real life. Not very high, not very far, and forward without any ability to correct in midair. That's fine except in real life you're not jumping across 5,000 foot high chasms and you're not controlling your movement with an analog stick.
-The companions are awful. They get in the way, they sabotage you, their powers are either underwhelming or useless.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I completed the game last week after playing for 3 weeks nonstop, got all shrines and sidequests complete (but not seeds/armors upgrades/photos), just like I did with BOTW.

I'm a huge Zelda fan and completed all games in the series, I had the same opinion as I often read about BOTW, it's an amazing open world game filled with content, but a very poor Zelda game. I hate how people praised the "you can do anything in any order" part, that's exactly what makes it stray away from the formula. You are supposed to unlock unique items in a specific order to gain abilities and unlock harder sections of the map, that's what makes a Zelda game a Zelda game. I also hated like most the weapon destruction, and the stamina/climbing that while it helped with locomotion, it was painfully slow and long and padded the playtime with annoying moments doing nothing but waiting. Nevertheless, I enjoyed pretty much everything else.

Come TOTK, I initially got a bad first impression when they showcased it with a construction aspect. I hate construction games, if I wanted to do so I would play Sim Cities or Minecraft or online survival games, not a single player Action RPG. But fortunately, it ended up being not bad at all. The fact that pieces are limited and break after a while restrict it to smaller sets and mostly to get past a simple puzzle, so I actually liked it.

The new paragliding mechanic is great for faster locomotion too, but completely rendered the horses useless (never used one in the whole game except for quests). It also brings the same negative aspect as climbing that half of the gameplay time is spent teleporting to a tower, launching up and gliding toward the objective point, which get long and repetitively annoying with nothing happening.

As far as the rest of gameplay elements go, there's absolutely nothing else, it's a complete copy/paste of the same game with no redeeming qualities that can explain the long development time, same engine, same graphics, same combats, same quest structure. I think they trolled us by making the weapons "decayed" and even easier to break. Instead of making longer more complex shrines, they just added even more!

The depths seemed cool at first, and I loved the Yoga questline in there, but after it was done I realized it was just an empty mess. It's 10x bigger than it should have been and there's absolutely no reward for lighting it up, it seems like a big afterthought they didn't complete. "Just make the players run along in the dark for hours with no goal".

But the part that disappointed me the most are the side quests. In every previous Zelda games, including BOTW, they were at least interesting to complete, always with some funny or clever aspects. In TOTK, they are just fillers, they are boring collectible or just going back and forth to places. I feel like they forced themselves to place references to every character of other games, even if it didn't fit in the story and the world, they put them there as an afterthought to fill in a checklist of references.

That said, I still loved my time playing it, but I absolutely cannot agree with people saying it's the game of the year, it's just a downgrade to this marvelous series. I seriously hope Nintendo scraps the concept and reboots anew again for the next title.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I had a pretty well thought out review prepared for TotK to justify giving it such a middling score, but through the power of the internet and Error 403, that review has, much like my hopes for this game, been cast into the pits of despair, consigned to endless oblivion.

In short, as I've already wasted enough time talking about a game I can't seem to get myself to enjoy:

-Ultrahand is a novelty that quickly becomes tedious and jerks me out of any immersion I may have felt regarding the exploration and story elements.

-The same can be said for weapon durabilty and the new "feature" of using Link's power of "Gorilla Glue" to attach random bits and bobs to a stick, turning it into a new-and-improved stick. I didn't have a problem with this in BotW, though it was annoying at times; the new mechanic just means I'm forced to spend hours of my finite existence attaching things to other things; it's like I'm trapped in a nightmare where I'm forced to make children's crafts and then go out into the wide-open (and sort of boring, to be honest) world and beat something to death with them.

-I can't comment on the story, as I haven't been able to force myself to endure the water-boarding that is the new "Super Zelda Maker" building mechanic long enough to get to anything approaching an interesting story hook. Notwithstanding this, I've received mixed signals on the story from other reviews: some swear it's the best thing since sliced bread; others say it's boring and full of contrivances and retconning of lore from other games. I sincerely hope the latter isn't true, but given i've already been spoiled on a few major plot points and was pretty unimpressed with them, I don't have high hopes.

All in all, this game might be acceptable if it didn't have the Legend of Zelda or Breath of the Wild names attached to it, with all of the expectations that entails. But as a Zelda game, it's not at all what I expected, and sets a precedent for the series that I have no interest in. Here's hoping this is an anomaly and not a guidepost for how the games are going to be moving forward. The saying goes that a bad craftsman blames his tools. But I came here to go on an adventure and save a princess, not build 500 rafts and bridges.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
A continuação direta de The Legend of Zelda: Breath of The Wild de 2017, teve seu retorno de forma conturbada, Link e Zelda se depararam com uma entidade antiga, denominada Demon King (Rei Demônio) no subsolo do Castelo de Hyrule, e após um confronto direto dos nossos heróis com o inimigo, o destino de Link e de Hyrule se tornaram caóticos.

Sobre o jogo em si, foi reaproveitado da versão de 2017, tanto em gráficos, quanto em jogabilidade e inimigos, porém, a Nintendo aprimorou a forma em que lutamos contra os nossos inimigos com as novas habilidades adquiridas por Link com o seu novo braço concedido por Rauru (Primeiro Rei de Hyrule).

Com estas novas habilidades, o jogo ficou totalmente mais intuitivo para os jogadores atingirem seus objetivos, quer antingir o topo de uma montanha? ao invés de subir por completo e demorar minutos até chegar ao topo, monte uma construção que possa levá-lo em segundos, isso foi uma sacada genial por parte da Nintendo.

A história por outro lado, foi na minha visão muito mais bem construida que o jogo de 2017, apresentando figuras mais conhecidas da franquia The Legend of Zelda, como por exemplo o Ganondorf.

De forma geral, o jogo teve tudo de superior ao Breath of The Wild, usando a criatividade do jogador a todo momento, porém ao meu ver, foi uma construção mais fácil de se fazer e menos inovadora por reaproveitar grande parte dos recursos do jogo anterior.

Nota final: 9/10

Recomendado!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Improves on Breath of the Wild in every way. Nintendo managed to re-use BOTW's map and still made the game and world feel fresh and exciting.

The new powers (that replace BOTW's) are all fun to use, and can provide a huge variety of ways to finish the game's various shrines and other puzzles. There's so much to discover, as well as rediscover from BOTW. The dungeon design is a big step up over BOTW, enemies and bosses are more varied, and the overall game is such a blast to get absolutely lost in.

This is what open world games should aspire to be.
