Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This game does everything that Botw did, but better. The open world is even bigger, while at the same time being more interesting. Classic Zelda dungeons are finally back and offer creative and fun puzzles just like in OoT or Majora's Mask.
Many of Botw weaknesses, like the weapon system or climbing mechanics got improved and actually turned into major strengths, making it easier and more rewarding to explore Hyrule and challenge all kinds of enemies.
The 4 new main abilities of Link manage to replace the old ones perfectly. They also create many new ways for players to solve puzzles, with most of the shrines being solvable in a much more creative manner than the intended one.
While the base game had some performance issues, the day-one patch fixed them and so far I have not experienced any frame drops that impacted my gameplay.
Because of all of this, I think that the game overcame the predictions of just being a Botw DLC by a lot. It offers way more content than its predecessor, probably more than twice as much and discovering this content makes more fun than ever before. This game is undoubtedly a contender for being one of the best games of all time.

Review:
The best Open World game just got 100% better, 100% bigger, and like 1000% more vertical… don’t play TotK if you are scared of heights xD

For everyone else, yeah of course this game is an absolute masterpiece and a great sequel. I didn’t expect Nintendo to add this much new stuff. This isn’t like Horizon or GoW where they added a few new things and the rest of the game was more or less the same.

Endless possibilities, endless skies, the only limit is your own creativity. Fantastic exploration in the best Open World to date. The best physics system in the industry. TotKs gameplay makes other games look like a tech demo.

Best looking Switch game. What they achieved on this small machine is mind blowing. Great image quality, great attention to detail, and probably the best use of LOD in a video game ever so you can look across the whole gigantic map all the time at a stable performance and without any noticeable pop-ins. TotK is a technical masterpiece.

Nintendo has done it again. They made the best Open World game with BotW and now with TotK. 10/10 and it raises the bar even higher.

Review: Having just recently played botw going directly into Tears of the Kingdom, I was at first sceptical of the reusing of the same world but not anymore. Nintendo not only expanded upon the lore of the world but made it feel so different and alive that its exciting. The game feels fresh and new and caters to both old and new fans alike. With the day 1 patch, the fps has been very good and pretty smooth with minor dips in heavily populated areas but doesn't detract from the experience. The new mechanics are exciting and really open up on what you can do and how you traverse the world. I think the most surprising is the traversal between sky, to the land of Hyrule and even to the underground is seamless with no loading screens between. You can dive from the sky islands straight into a chasm leading to the underground without any issues. Its pretty impressive and it shows how much polish and thought the developers put into the game. They've redone the music and sound system, providing a better experience and adding awesome musical scores that really add to the experience. Overall, this is game of the the year material. I highly recommend everyone pick this up and play.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
What an banger! Nintendo did it once again, a game that truely supprise on every corner. Tears of the Kingdom is Breath of the Wild on steroides, more like that. It makes many points better than the predecessor. More Story-Driven-Gameplay, Dungeons, more Quality of Live features. And the exploration part is even more heavier than it was on Breath of the Wild. You now have the Sky above Hyrule, the Ground and the Underground to explore, with tons of new things, that will attract your attention. The "ground" overworld itself is even changed enough not to bore experienced players of the predecessor.

The build mechanic is very fresh and is very much used for puzzles and for exploration. The Fuze mechanic make the weapon break system no longer bad.

Conclusion: If you even loved the predecessor, this game is a must have! If you missed story and dungeons in the predecessor its very likely that you maybe like this game. If you absolutely hate Open World games or the way that Zelda went with BotW you maybe shouldnt buy it.
For me a 10/10, one of the best videogames Ive ever played.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: The Legend of Zelda: tears of the kingdom is a game that truly lives up to the hype. It's a sprawling, open-world adventure that encourages exploration and rewards players for their curiosity. The graphics are stunning, with a vibrant art style that's both beautiful and immersive. The game's mechanics are innovative and intuitive, making it easy to pick up and play, but with enough depth to keep players engaged for hours on end. The puzzles are challenging, but always fair, and the combat is satisfyingly strategic. What really sets totk apart, however, is its sense of freedom. Players can tackle the game's challenges in any order they choose, and the game never feels restrictive or linear. With so much to discover and explore, Totk" is a game that will keep players coming back for more, long after the initial playthrough is complete.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
An instant classic - this game is better than BOTW. It takes its predecessor and puts it on steroids. Everything is bigger, better and more refined; the world, the story, the mechanics, the enemies, the freedom, the combat, the music, the puzzles, the atmosphere.

This is an advert for the world of gaming, and shows what an incredibly talented group of people can do if they put their mind to it. Very few things being made in this day and age can compare to this game, and it should serve as an inspiration to other game creators with the example it sets.

I think the people who are complaining about performance have lost their way a bit in gaming... gaming is about enjoying a fantastically made game, not complaining about graphics this and framerate that. Besides - I have had no problems with performance, and the art style is stunning (played in docked mode so far). The magic that Nintendo has pulled out of the bag is timeless, and will go down as another one of the greats - to the envy of other studios!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: I am not sure why this game is receiving so many positive reviews. Is it marketing and hype or just reviews from gamers who have no idea what the Zelda names means? In all fairness, if this game was called Adventure Island instead, it would be a hit. However, Nintendo opted to go with the franchise name, Zelda. How is this a Zelda game? There is no tri-force, no dungeons that store special items that help progress the adventure. Heck, where is the adventure at all honestly? You will find yourself walking around an empty world absent of color or life while you cook random things and fuse random objects together like this was an incredible machine. You will be swinging tree branches or shoot arrows with items that break after a few uses. Constantly fighting camera angles and wondering to yourself, what am I doing and why? Better than Breath of the Wild - Yes. A true successor to the Zelda Franchise - Not even close. Nintendo could of make this the most amazing Zelda adventure to date with their open world, but fell flat on their face. Maybe they assume gamers today are not capable of going on adventures where you must locate hidden dungeons that hold secrets, maybe they do need huge stars on minimaps that say GO HERE. None the less, for those who do enjoy cooking and fusing stuff together, fighting the same 8 monsters, defeating shrine after mindless shrine or just like to play games with no failure, then go for it, you will like it. However, for those older fans who remember what Zelda really stood for and the epic adventures that came before us, do not waste your time or money. I'd like to say Nintendo will get it right eventually, but lets be honest, they are done. We will never see another great Zelda game, so lets just hope they port Windwaker over to Switch sometime soon. RIP Zelda.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Like BOTW, but removes the fun abilities and replaces them with a lot of time wasted with clunky controls and menus.
'I found a new weapon - great now I have to fuse it with something to make it viable. Let's go through my fusion items.. ah who cares, it's gonna break in 5 minutes anyway, let's just choose a random one. Select it, drop it on the floor, change ability to fuse, aim, fuse it'. One minute wasted for no reason. Why must something that should take 2 seconds within the menu itself take 30 seconds of awkward repetitive motions? Baffling. You can tell Miyamoto is not involved in the development of Nintendo games and busy with theme parks and movies these days, something like this would have never gotten past him.

After a few hours, after the same repetitive enemy camp, the same cave with a million useless trinkets to collect, and yet another minute wasted attaching some piece of junk to a rusted sword, I dropped the game. I already work all week, playing a game that feels like work is not a fun way to pass the free time.

No doubt this game can offer moments of absolute emergent brilliance, I'm just not willing to wade through hours of tedium to get to them.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I just don't understand all the hype for this game; not only does it heavily inconvenience the player with fragile weapons and limited stamina (just like BotW), but it's also incredibly grindy when it comes to resources and Zonai devices, not to mention bringing back the downright-awful Korok Seeds. It also neglects to give the player a sense of direction, by deliberately leaving out developer-placed map markers, meaning if you can't see something you would have no idea something is even there; not great, for a huge open-world game with multiple layers.
This game is a 6/10 at most, not 9, and definitely not a 10 - it's way too flawed for that.

If weapons and shields were significantly more durable, and there were ways to repair damaged equipment, then that wouldn't be as much of an issue - just look at Minecraft, which is also an open-world game with stamina, breakable equipment, and zero direction given (even less than BotW/TotK), but wisely gives its equipment more than a hundred uses each, and even then has the Unbreaking enchantment to reduce the chance of durability loss, the Mending enchantment to auto-repair the equipment piece with it by absorbing EXP, and multiple ways to straight-up repair equipment (combine the same two tools in the 4x4 inventory grid, at the cost of all enchantments, or the Anvil to repair with the same type of resource [iron armour requires iron ingots, for example] or combine the same two equipment pieces and keep enchantments).
That's way more player-friendly than what BotW and TotK offer, where every weapon and shield you find just feels like disposable trash that WILL break after a mere handful of uses, **** the excitement out of earning powerful gear from defeating tough foes, or making your way to secret areas.

As for stamina...face it, the game would work _just as well_ without this unnecessary green wheel. Sure, it can be upgraded to last longer, but that's just delaying how long you have before you're forced to slow down and wait for it to refill. This makes exploring this huge, multi-layered land even more tedious, for no benefit.
It's telling when other open-world games, such as Assassin's Creed and Ghost of Tsushima, don't even bother with stamina, allowing the player to rush around their large worlds however they damn well please with no need to slow down and wait.

Open-world games are already massive time-sinks; this one didn't need to be artificially lengthened further by forcing the player to grind rare resources, or wander this massive multi-layered world without an adequate number of map markers to guide them. That's just needless padding for padding's sake, and serves as a major turn-off for time-poor players (which is a large proportion of the adult customer base, and likely a large number of children too these days) as well as players without much patience.

Due to all of this, TotK just doesn't deserve 9s or 10s when it's far from perfect or ideal; at the most, it's 6/10 and easily skippable. If you've already trudged and suffered through BotW, this is largely more of the same tedious crap.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
No one's here to read a college thesis, so I'll knock this one out, good/bad/ugly style (ugly being things that I wasn't a fan of but that don't affect the overall score).

The Good:
-if you liked BOTW, you'll be happy to know all of its mechanics have essentially returned.
-the new runes are mostly pretty good and shake up exploration in inventive ways.
-the remixed overworld isn't perfect, but I am willing to admit they did more than I expected them to.
-the new areas are pretty cool. Spelunking is really fun.
-the dungeons, as the game calls them, are generally a big improvement on the Divine Beasts.

The Bad:
-if there were aspects of BOTW you didn't like, you'll be disappointed to know that every single core mechanic has returned.
-using Ultrahand for building (it has other uses, which are fine) ****. Stray from what the game *wants* you to make and it will rarely ever work. Just make bridges. They're funny and they actually work.
-while it doesn't come into play often, there are parts of the world where it's very clear the game wasn't built with your toolset in mind. (hint: because it was built for BOTW's toolset)
-the story is almost laughably bad. Same minimalistic approach as BOTW but with a far worse script. Ganondorf deserved better.

The Ugly:
-no matter what the game calls them, these still aren't dungeons as Zelda fans know them. The Divine Beasts weren't terrible, but they left me feeling hungry for something better. Dungeons in this game are basically the Divine Beasts without the control mechanism. They are generally better, though.
-they took whistle-sprinting out. While it was a glitch and did need to be removed, it was really handy for getting around quickly. Having nothing replace it is really unfortunate.

Overall a fun game, but six years and $70 is a big ask for what we ultimately ended up getting, which largely does play like an DLC rather than a proper sequel. Not in terms of scope (the game definitely has scope), but in terms of what the game actually is.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
M y score is a 7.5 .  This is a Great game that is sadly deeply flawed like botw and doesnt quite live up to much of its potential.

From a technical standpoint this game is very impressive with how everything looks and runs. The artstlye isnt my cup of Tee but its unique.

This games brings back shrines and they are much like in botw. Most of them are  great  and fun but there is one gigantic flaw with them. They all look the same. Something as simple has giving us different shrine themes in different Regions would have really helped from them eventually feeling stale.

Sadly this games biggest flaw is enemy veriety . They added maybe 4 new enemys and 3 new minibosses. Its baffling that for a game this gigantic it has so few enemys. Becouse of this flaw , combat get stale after a while when youre only fighting the same enemys over and over again. This is a gigantic flaw and makes me take away 1 and a half points.

The caves in this game  are really well designed and funt to play but yet again they suffer from little veriety. they all have the same enemys and goals. finding satori frogs and finding shrines.  It would have been so much more exciting exploring the caves if there were unexpected minibosses or enemys or the shrines themselves had unique different themes.

Overall the Overworld of hyrule just feels too samy  to botw  with exeptions of caves.  Age of calamity showed the potential of how they could change the map like having rebuilt ruins or a rebuilt hyrule castle but much of the game just feels like they only aded sky dabree.

Speaking of the sky , what a disapointment. The opening Skypllateu is amazing   but otherwise there is very little to do in the sky. The skyislands feel like an afterthought that they mostly used for marketing.  The underground in this game is just as big as the base botw map but is very empty. Its frustrating becouse it has an extremely cool astetic  and atmosphere  and the Idea of that you cant see anything and constantly need seeds and checkpoints too light up the map is really cool... but  most of the time thats the only thing youre doing. There is a really cool lengthy side adventure in the underground  but other then that most of the underground is just walking around and sometimes finde patents or costumes.

The dungeons in this game are a big mixed bag. On the one hand they fixed botw biggest issue with the dungeons having destinct themes this time around. on the other the dungeons design itselft just isnt as good as in the old 3 zelda games. I think the five terminal sytem really limits the potential of these dungens and that you can solve the puzzles in any order you want. The puzzles are fun but easy. Now the gameplay segment leading up to these dungeons are fantastic and really fun. They give me my zelda dngeons fix but not they just dont reach the highs of the dungeons in twighlight princess , Skyward Sword , Oot.  The bosses on the other hand are fantastic and this game has some of the best and most creative bosses in the franchise. And this game has arguably the best ending and final boss in the entire series so  thats a humongus step up from botw.

The story in this game is frustrating. This game has imo the best opening and ending to any zelda game however just like in botw the story is told through memorys and it just cuts any tention the story could have had because its not really relevant to what you are doing at the present moments. The cutscenes are fantastic and add alot to the zelda lore but it would have been so much more effective if it would have been told in the present and in a linear fassion.

The new fuse mechanic is incredible but it feels like Nintendo spent much more  development time on the new mechanics then everything else. I feel like the game would have felt alot better if it came out 3  or 4 years after botw but after  6 years  it feels like this game has so much wasted potential. My biggest fear was that this game just eels like dlc and sadly atleast for me , it does just feel like really big dlc most of the time.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Desde 2011, na apresentação da Tech Demo de Zelda na apresentação do Wii U ficávamos imaginando o quão épico seria um novo Zelda em HD. Mal sabíamos que The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild era uma Tech Demo para The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.


Tinha receio de como seria uma continuação do melhor jogo que já joguei. As poucas imagens e trailers divulgadas me deixaram curioso, varias perguntas para saber como seria a história, gameplay, visual. De qualquer forma, eu só queria jogar. 


E desde o primeiro toque no jogo não parei de jogar. Estava totalmente imerso ao jogo. As novas mecânicas, a história do jogo e a mesma sensação de liberdade que senti em Breath of the Wild.


Desde o início do jogo somos jogados a imensidão de Hyrule, porém dessa vez Hyrule está maior. É o mesmo mapa, porém, conseguimos observar no horizonte mais e mais lugares para explorar. Incrível a sensação de exploração e querer saber o que tem em cada canto do mapa, e conversar com os NPCs e ver como eles estão após Breath of the Wild e também, conhecer novos habitantes de Hyrule. 


É sensacional como o jogo recria e exercita sua criatividade. O que você constrói deixa você maravilhado pelo jogo. Me via jogando e parando para construir algo que me dava na cabeça, um carro para ir mais rápido a outro local, subir uma montanha gigante sem ser escalando ou apenas construir algo sem sentido.


Assim como Zelda: Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom é gigantesco, grandioso, excessivo e imenso. Pega todas as qualidades de Breath of the Wild e soma, multiplica e potencializa o mundo de Hyrule. E isso vale para tudo no jogo; o mapa que foi expansível verticalmente, os velhos e novos inimigos, os novos itens, novas comidas, novos pratos, novas armas, novos NPCs e muito mais. É tudo tão novo e o mesmo tempo tão ligado a Breath of the Wild, que parece que você esta visitando uma cidade 6 anos depois de uma primeira visita que te marcou muito.


Da mesma forma que, Breath of the Wild mudou a fórmula de mundo aberto, Tears of the Kingdom mudou a fórmula de Breath of the Wild. Portanto, eu vejo como o Game Of The Year de 2023, e não é uma continuação qualquer, uma sequência que decepciona, é um jogo totalmente novo, um jogo que prende do início ao fim para saber, criar, explorar e descobrir.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: The Legend of Zelda Tears of the Kingdom is an amazing game that adds a lot of new mechanics and a whole new story. You can attach things together in order to build litterally anything, like a simple bridge or even more complex constructions like a flying car that can shoot the enemies. The new Fuse ability lets you combine weapons with every material you can see; trees, rocks, machines, and even other weapons! The variety is incredible and that makes battle a lot better: in the previous game you were likely not going to engage a battle if you could because that would have consumed your weapons, but with fuse you are pretty much always rewarded for killing an enemy, you can in fact you can use the drop to repair your weapons. The ascend ability makes you able to pass through ceiling and floors, which is very usefull to quickly climb mountains if there is a cave in it or to surprise the enemies in their own bases. Lastly there is the recall ability. Recall works as a rewind that sends an object back in time, retracing its movements and returning it to the state and place it was some seconds before. The story is beautyfull and a lot better than the previous game. The world is HUGE and filled with things to do, you can really feel the care for the details. It is almost 3 times bigger than the Hyrule of The Legend of Zelda Breath of the wild. The game is full of things to do and i really loved the freedom the player has, if you like adventure games and the use of creativity this is a must play.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Zelda is an iconic video game franchise that has been entertaining gamers for decades. With its rich storytelling, captivating gameplay, and memorable characters, it is no wonder that Zelda is beloved by so many.

One of the standout features of Zelda is its immersive world-building. From the sprawling fields of Hyrule to the treacherous dungeons and mysterious temples, every corner of the Zelda universe feels alive and full of adventure. Players are encouraged to explore every nook and cranny, uncovering secrets and discovering new challenges along the way.

But it's not just the world that makes Zelda so special. The series is also known for its memorable characters, from the heroic Link to the devious Ganon, and the various races and creatures that inhabit the world. Each character has their own unique personality and backstory, making them feel like real people rather than just game characters.

The gameplay in Zelda is also top-notch, with a perfect balance of action, puzzle-solving, and exploration. Players are challenged to use their wits and skills to overcome obstacles and defeat enemies, but the game never feels frustrating or unfair.

Overall, Zelda is a must-play for any gamer. With its timeless storytelling, unforgettable characters, and engaging gameplay, it is sure to provide hours of entertainment and leave a lasting impression on anyone who plays it.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The fact that this low-budget rehased garbage got a 96 proves there are double standards and hypocrisy among these critics. Let's all be honest with ourselves. Forget the PS5/XSX and $70 price tag, If this were just a PS4/X1 game for $60 without the Legend of Zelda title, the narrative would've been so different. There is no way it would've scored higher than a 75 average. This game would be crucified by critics for low-budget graphics, poor draw distance, bad lip syncing, low unstable FPS and lack of innovation. Gamers would be roasting it by calling it a PS2 game. And then these game journalists have the audacity to rant and virtue signal over studios crunching, even though they are the main reason why crunch even exists in the first place, because every studio has to work at least 100 times harder than Nintendo to get a 90 overall Metacritic score. Playstation Studios had to crunch hard to become a critic darling with those graphics and over-produced cutscenes, but Zelda devs can make copy/paste shovelware and get treated like the Messiahs of gaming. I don't even want to hear about the Switch being underpowered. They are charging a premium next-gen price of $70, so I expect the same level of quality as PS5 and XSX. Not my fault these greedy cheapskates at Nintendo refuse to release next-gen hardware. There are hundreds, or maybe even thousands of indie games with higher quality than this trash for a cheaper price, yet get much lower scores from critics.

There is no multiplayer. So once you beat the story, there is literally not a reason to touch this game again. Charging $70 for a game with no replay value is a cash grab. Nintendo, you can make all the indie quality games you want. But when I get a $70 game with no guaranteed online multiplayer, that is where I absolutely draw the line. How dare you give me half of the game for $70. I might've actually had fun if it had online. That's the least they could do after increasing the price for this low budget game. It's funny when Zelda fans make fun of COD for being the same game every year. At least there are new maps and graphics every year, while Zelda is the same map and graphics in 6 years. It's mind boggling that this game gets universal acclaim for indie quality at $70, when others work much harder and get panned by critics and gamers. I don't recommend this game at all, unless you want to support laziness.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Once, I dreamed ****. A fantasy game where you explore an open world, do side quests and fight various enemies. For some time, I thought that that game doesn't exist. And then, I bought a switch to play mainly Mario games. When I looked up what other good games are there, I saw everyone saying BotW. I played it. It was that game, it was incredible, the best game I've ever played. And then, this game comes out. I said: as long as it doesn't make BotW worse, it will be my favourite game. This game has our favourite hyrule with two more maps added, new dungeons, new allies, new story, new enemies, new items, new side quests, new skills, and more possibilities. This game does have the same map, (even though there are two more new maps) but everything else is different. This game shows all the reasons why - even with joycon drift - we are nintendo fans.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: It's an easy 10 so far.  I'm 15-20 hours into the game and haven't even completed the second major area I've visited (hell, I probably have only completed 50-60% of the first major area).  It's less overwhelming than BOTW because they give you a bit more guidance of where to go, and a lot more clear objectives once you get there.  But where this game shines is the exploration.  If one is game to step into the world like a virtual reality and make the most of it, there is a nearly endless supply of moments it can offer you.  As of this writing, I think it may be superior to BOTW but no need to make such large statements so early.  There's also a possibility it's one of the best games of all time, but also---why make such a claim so early.  For now, just enjoy the game!

Review:
I have played a bunch of Zelda games over the years, and going in blind to BOTW was truly the pinnacle of it all. For those first few moments, and throughout the rest of the game, it was an absolute gem of an experience, a Diamond being the gem. It’s the standard games SHOULD value, take time to make a game to its absolute best potential. Granted, I see pros AND cons. Dungeons were lackluster, bosses exactly the same, and the world did feel a bit more empty. But it was one of the cases where, hype aside, the good outweighed the bad in such a tremendous and spectacular way. Climbing up that hill to see all of Hyrule still hits me even to this day.

Tears of the Kingdom is, to me, an INCREDIBLE successor!! Taking the criticisms of BOTW, and following up on that exponentially. Dungeons, while small, ARE present, and the Allies mechanic is a treat! New abilities to help world traversal, the vehicles being so expansive on what you can and can’t do. It’s truly imagination beyond itself, and the way they somehow made hyrule feel fresh (while still being familiar), is astounding. Granted, a LOT of people here complain about the graphics, YES we get it the hardware is not next Gen. But the $70 was NOT for a graphical upgrade, but rather an expanded experience. I’ve only just began and I’m already at like 18 hours, and I’ve yet to scratch a tiny bit of the surface. Beat a dungeon and boss, all that good stuff.

Point is, BOTW was Nintendo running an experiment, and Tears of the Kingdom was Nintendo being fully confident in what they could produce!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
My main concern prior to playing was that Tears would feel more like an expansion or DLC than a true sequel. The pre-existing overworld remained, and the visuals appeared mostly unaltered.

These fears were (mostly) dispelled after a few hours of playtime. The game encourages you to think and improvise in a way that few others have done before, including BoTW. The world is truly vast, probably twice the size of the original and the sense of freedom is intoxicating. You won’t get more than a few minutes into a task or journey before becoming distracted with something new, and yet somehow the game never feels overwhelming.

The Sky Islands are beautiful and awe-inspiring, The Depths are vast, despite having a repetitive procedurally-generated feel about them.
Some of the new concept mechanics are ingenious in a way that only Nintendo could conceive, and must be experienced first-hand to fully appreciate their brilliance.

I would point out however that the game has failed in doing what all great sequels are in fact required to do: and that is to address its predecessor’s shortcomings:-

The clunky and banal combat system, the tedious cooking routine, overly brittle weapons, feeble voice acting and occasional FPS issues are a few examples of drawbacks which remain unrectified.

It’s a very fun and inventive game, easily a top 5 Zelda title without question, but in my opinion has failed to show sufficient separation from an already imperfect first title to be considered an all-time great.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This game is a huge steaming pile of garbage. The greedy developers are charging $70 for a mobile game. It doesn't even have the AAA quality to justify the $70 price tag. Just when I thought Nintendo has done the greediest thing imaginable, something even greedier comes up. They are charging a $70 next-gen price for a game that isn't even on a next-gen console. Are you freaking kidding me? This game can barely runs at 30fps 720p and dips to 20fps in combat. When I pay $70, I expect a performance and fidelity mode. The graphics are a joke. This whole cel shading stuff is just an excuse for developers to be cheap and lazy. The textures are pukeworthy. The physics are beyond horrible. The combat is boring and repetitive. The story is terrible. Cringeworthy running animations. It's the exact same game as the last, even the map is the freaking same. It's just new missions, cutscenes and attaching things. It's literally $70 DLC. When it comes to voice acting, Nintendo are extremely cheap. $70 only to get "oh ah uh hmm" voice acting during in-game dialogue. That's pathetic. Lack of enemy variety and laughable boss fights.

There is nothing to do in the open world. It's just a boring empty landscape of plants, trees, rocks, water and mountains. It's the same map as BOTW. All the lazy developers did was edit the map a bit with the creator tools and called it a day. And no, the map under the world and the sky islands don't count as new maps. GTA 5 Online has gotten new places under the map through updates and players can create sky maps with the Content Creator, so that makes it a different map, right? Wrong, it's still the same map. Not to mention the sky islands in TOTK are copied and pasted. It's embarrassing that a smaller studio like Coffee Stain North can give me a new map for Goat Sim 3 at $30, while TOTK is the same map with worse FPS and graphics for $70. Speaking of which, you can now build cars like you can in a Goat Sim 3 quest, but the cars are much slower. Maybe if they went fast enough, I might've had fun doing stunts off the empty boring mountains. Obviously the developers made it slow so it wouldn't expose a framerate nightmare. When I axed a tree, it **** like glass and magically went under the ground.

The fact that this low-budget rehased garbage got a 96 proves there are double standards and hypocrisy among these critics. Let's all be honest with ourselves. Forget the PS5/XSX and $70 price tag, If this were just a PS4/X1 game for $60 without the Legend of Zelda title, the narrative would've been so different. There is no way it would've scored higher than a 75 average. This game would be crucified by critics for low-budget graphics, poor draw distance, bad lip syncing, low unstable FPS and lack of innovation. Gamers would be roasting it by calling it a PS2 game. And then these game journalists have the audacity to rant and virtue signal over studios crunching, even though they are the main reason why crunch even exists in the first place, because every studio has to work at least 100 times harder than Nintendo to get a 90 overall Metacritic score. Playstation Studios had to crunch hard to become a critic darling with those graphics and over-produced cutscenes, but Zelda devs can make copy/paste shovelware and get treated like the Messiahs of gaming. I don't even want to hear about the Switch being underpowered. They are charging a premium next-gen price of $70, so I expect the same level of quality as PS5 and XSX. Not my fault these greedy cheapskates at Nintendo refuse to release next-gen hardware. There are hundreds, or maybe even thousands of indie games with higher quality than this trash for a cheaper price, yet get much lower scores from critics.

There is no multiplayer. So once you beat the story, there is literally not a reason to touch this game again. Charging $70 for a game with no replay value is a cash grab. Nintendo, you can make all the indie quality games you want. But when I get a $70 game with no guaranteed online multiplayer, that is where I absolutely draw the line. How dare you give me half of the game for $70. I might've actually had fun if it had online. That's the least they could do after increasing the price for this low budget game. It's funny when Zelda fans make fun of COD for being the same game every year. At least there are new maps and graphics every year, while Zelda is the same map and graphics in 6 years. It's mind boggling that this game gets universal acclaim for indie quality at $70, when others work much harder and get panned by critics and gamers. I don't recommend this game at all, unless you want to support laziness.

La música no se queda atrás pero aún más destaco los sonidos pequeños que son icónicos y muy reconocibles como por ejemplo abrir un baúl, usar las herramientas, el menú, las voces de aliados al usar los especiales, los enemigos... El juego no se queda corto, tiene varios objetivos sin contar los secundarios que lo vuelven interesante: Los santuarios que ayudan a teletransportarte, las torres para completar el mapa, las bestias divinas que serían la previa del enemigo principal y un excelente castillo enorme para ambientar el final. 
Comenzando por los santuarios, los note creativos e interesantes, tienen cierta dificultad pero lamentablemente a mi percepción personal no son lo suficientemente desafiantes en cuanto a lo mental, llevan su tiempo y de hecho tienen diferentes soluciones pero pudieron ser mejor, si cumplen porque entretienen bastante y hacen muy llevadero el juego. 
Las torres son más difícil encontrarlas que subirse a ellas, no tienen una dificultad real pero si tienen ese añadido perfecto que junto a los santuarios como ya mencioné, hacen las horas del juego muy llevaderas con una mecánica de progreso visible. 
En cuanto a las bestias divinas puedo decir que son enemigos con una dificultad bastante mediocre salvo por ira del rayo quien de hecho hasta me pareció más difícil que el propio Ganon. Entrar en cada bestia tiene una previa bastante interesante, luego dentro empieza lo mejor incluso superior a su final que sería enfrentarse a los enemigos físicamente: Completar los puzles dentro de cada bestia, se siente increíble el poder mover la máquina y se nota que es más difícil y hasta lleva si tiempo, acá sí que no me parece algo mediocre porque es bastante divertido, pero volvemos a caer en lo mismo como todos los santuarios:
-Es largo, no difícil 
Pero repito, eso no quita que deja una buena sensación al completar cada bestia. ¿Se hace repetitivo? Realmente si se hace repetitivo el cómo se enfrenta a cada bestia, pero a mi parecer todo eso no tiene importancia porque como dije, completar un puzle así de gigante es muy satisfactorio. En cuanto a las armas me parece que es razonable la queja de que se desgastan, pero solo con las más importantes, de hecho, este problema se agiganta aún peor en el final... Castillo hermoso, indiscutiblemente hecho a medida para dar esa sensación de "Este es el final, la princesa está en apuros y vos tenes que salvarla", esa sensación que solo se encuentra en obras como películas de gran calidad, no irónicamente es algo parecido al final de Shrek 2, obviamente hablo de sensaciones no de que es igual. Uno se siente el héroe no solo por donde esta entrando si no que la música es simplemente magnifica sobre todo al final. Ganon es por lejos el villano con mejor estilo artístico y transmite miedo, pero lamentablemente su dificultad si bien no es fácil no me pareció ultra difícil. Uno puede decir que el juego es así y esta bien pero cuando ve que los mismos minotauros son más difíciles que Ganon, o enfrentarse a dos guardianes... 
Y acá viene mi crítica más letal y la razón de porque no puedo subirle la nota más allá de un 9: El juego pierde algo muy importante, la capacidad de gratificación...
Perder las armas valiosas es una cosa, pero no obtener un final donde Hyrule este salvado y poder jugar en él incluso sin poder hacer mucho más que misiones secundarias, o al menos poder ver más de Zelda con Link. De hecho, esto me hace plantearme si debería ser un 9 o un 8.9 pero no darle un 9 sería muy exigente y ridículo porque simplemente el juego esta bien diseñado en cada aspecto, los biomas y el mundo es espectacular, el frío de las montañas... el calor del desierto... Montar a caballo bajo la lluvia temiendo de los rayos... También para ser sinceros si transmite sensaciones de progreso a lo largo del juego cuando uno revisita el mapa y se da cuenta que ya no es el jugador indefenso del principio...

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild starts off medium‑fast: it doesn’t throw you into the open world immediately, but it does a great job teaching the basics. The tutorial island is tight, clear, and never feels like a boring checklist. By the time you leave the starting point, the game truly opens itself and becomes a reactive, fun, and interesting experience that keeps you engaged from minute one to final credits. A world that wants to be messed with. The sheer amount of things you can interact with is insane.•	You can set fires, cook, craft, experiment with weapons, and watch the world react: rain puts out flames, wind spreads fire, metal conducts electricity, and climbing works everywhere.•	There are tons of recipes, enemy types, sword types, and shields, so you never feel like you’re repeating the same loop.•	Every town and region has its own lore, vibe, and mini‑story, and the side quests are actual stories, not just “kill 10 monsters” spam.•	Easy‑minded enemies throw rocks at you, gang up if there are more of them, and try to flank you.•	Bigger enemies later on are even better, they’ll cover their weakness once you hit them, reposition, and force you to adapt. The characters are interesting and lovely, the towns look great, and the overall story is engaging enough to keep you invested, even when you’re off doing random side stuff. The enemies actually react how you fight them, which makes combat feel smart instead of just mindless.  There are many, many more little tweaks like this, and they make every fight feel like a tiny puzzle instead of a button‑mash. The game has:•	Cold sensor / heat sensor for different biomes,•	Noise sensor where a clanking weapon on your back makes your sneaking louder; unequip that loud sword and suddenly you’re way stealthier. These aren’t just “flavour” details: they’re real gameplay incentives to think about your gear, position, and timing. Want to take out multiple enemies?•	Shoot some fire arrows around them, make them panic, and then clean up the mess.•	The skeleton animations are hilarious! I’m not spoiling it; you just have to experience it yourself. Puzzles that actually feel like Zelda. I’m usually bad at puzzles, but the ones in Breath of the Wild make sense.•	They’re canon‑adjacent, not just “time‑waste” filler.•	They feel like real puzzles, not random busywork, and they’re actually fun to solve.  Resident Evil games could really learn from this: puzzles that match the world and don’t feel like homework. Loot, loot, and more loot The game is packed with loot:•	Weapons to pick up,•	Shields to experiment with,•	Food to cook,•	Items to trade,•	Side quests that feel meaningful. Even after you finish the main story, there’s a ton of content to keep you going. You can keep exploring, crafting, cooking, and doing side quests, and it still feels like you’re discovering something new. Final verdict: 10/10.  This is a fantastic f***king game and truly one of the best games ever. AFTER Beating the game: The game can be very hard, but very balanced if you use everything the game gives you.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: 2017 REVISITED: A REVOLUTION IN FREEDOM: Looking back at 2017, it’s hard to overstate how much this game changed the industry. While other open-world games were obsessed with checklists and map markers, Breath of the Wild gave us a paraglider and told us to "go." The true greatness of this game lies in its physics-based chemistry system. Whether you were using a metal sword to attract lightning during a storm or freezing a boulder to launch it at a camp, the game rewarded curiosity in a way that felt truly revolutionary at the time. TECHNICAL PERFORMANCE: AGING WITH GRACE: Does it show its age? Yes. When played today, you’ll notice the 30 FPS cap (granted, there is a switch 2 edition, but it costs money) and the occasional frame dips in dense areas like Korok Forest. However, the art style is so strong that it masks the technical limitations of the original Switch hardware. The painterly, watercolor aesthetic ensures that Hyrule still feels vast and inviting, rather than "outdated." It’s a testament to the art direction that a game from 2017 can still stand side-by-side with modern Switch 2 titles without feeling out of place. THE WORLD: A RELEVANT MASTERPIECE: The most surprising thing about playing this today is how relevant it remains. Many games have tried to copy the "Zelda formula," but few capture the same sense of lonely, quiet exploration. The lack of a constant music track—replaced by the sounds of wind and grass—makes the world feel alive and "lived-in." Even with its sequel out in the world, the original journey of Link waking up in the Shrine of Resurrection still carries a weight and a simplicity that is unmatched. THE DURABILITY DILEMMA: If there is one thing that frustrates me the most in this game, it’s definitely the weapon durability system. While it encourages you to try new gear, it can still feel frustrating to have a legendary weapon shatter after a single encounter. It creates a "hoarding" mentality that sometimes clashes with the game’s otherwise perfect sense of freedom. PROS: Unrivaled sense of exploration and freedom. Timeless art style that still looks beautiful today. The "Chemistry Engine" allows for insane player creativity. CONS: Divisive weapon durability system.Occasional frame rate stutters in busy environments. THE FINAL VERDICT: 9/10: In 2017, this game was a 10/10. Today, it remains a near-perfect 9/10. It is a technical marvel of its time that has aged with incredible grace. Even with newer titles pushing hardware further, the original "Breath" remains an essential, quiet, and breathtaking journey that every gamer should experience at least once.

At first I was a bit bored from this game. The starting area is a bit tedious. The combat is descent. I like how you can get better by learning to parry and flurry rush, but it can get repetitive a bit boring after like 50 hoursm but exploring is the thing that makes the game a masterpiece so it isn't a problem. Plus there are many different weapons with different natural abilities (fire, ice...) that make it more interesting.

The story is intriguing and you help figure stuff out by finding memories (which you access by playing like geoguessr which is fun). The characters can be a bit goofy and have intereseting things to say.

The quest are ok I guess. Some are very hard to figure out so you will probably need to look them up on youtube.

The only thing I genuinely don't like is that there isn't a big variety in enemies. There are only 3-4 enemy types in the different zones and it does get a bit dull, but as I said combat is not the main part of the game (it does play a hue big, but exploration is number 1).

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Jeśli ktoś szuka sandboxa na ponad 100h, must have!
Jeśli ktoś nie lubi eksploracji i sandboxowych otwartych światów, to raczej się odbije...

Kontekst: Zelda w klimacie post-apo, dostajemy duży otwarty świat który po przejściu dobrze tłumaczącego mechaniki prologu (nie prowadzi za rączkę jak typowe AAA) praktycznie cały stoi przed nami otworem, fabuła jest tylko tłem ale dobrze nakreśla cel i daje motywację do gry.
Gameplay: gra nie wprowadza niczego całkowicie nowego, ale łączy w idealny sposób wiele znanych mechanik. Eksploracja jest genialnie zrealizowana, jeśli tylko pozwoli nam na to poziom staminy i nasze umiejętności jesteśmy w stanie dostać się wszędzie gdzie tylko zechcemy, świat jest wystarczający duży żeby móc na spokojnie eksplorować i poczuć klimat podróży, ale jednocześnie nie jest pusty, jeśli coś przykuje naszą uwagę, to najprawdopodobniej coś ciekawego tam znajdziemy. System walki jest prosty, ale satysfakcjonujący, a przez mnogość sposobów na eliminowanie przeciwników nie nudzi nawet pod koniec gry, tak na prawdę najgorsze walki to te z bossami, bo tam mamy ograniczoną przestrzeń i często wymuszony sposób walki. Mamy tu system niszczenia się broni, który wymusza na nas ciągłe zmienianie naszego rynsztunku i szukanie nowych broni, dzięki temu nawet jeśli znajdziemy na początku gry silny miecz, nie przejdziemy nim całej gry. Gra oferuje też wiele pomniejszych mechanik, takich jak jedzenie, temperatura, wspinaczka, latanie na lotni, moce które dostajemy w prologu, czy wierzchowce. 
Grafika i dźwięk: styl artystyczny doprze pasuje do gry, buduje klimat, udźwiękowienie też jest na najwyższym poziomie, z jedną wadą... praktycznie w grze nie uświadczymy dubbingu. Muzyka jak chyba w każdej zeldzie jest na bardzo wysokim poziomie i świetnie wpasowuje się w to gdzie jesteśmy i co aktualnie dzieje się na ekranie. Nie ma co ukrywać że gra momentami nie zachwyca szczegółowością tekstur czy rozdzielczością, ale to kwestia przestarzałej konsoli i na szczęście wersja na switch 2 eliminuje wszystkie te niedociągnięcia.
Wydajność/optymalizacja: Gra jest świetnie zoptymalizowana, wyciska z pierwszego pstryczka 100%, momentami zdarzają się chrupnięcia, czasy ładowania na pierwszym switch'u też nie są najkrótsze, ale nadal gra się przyjemnie, a nawet lekkie ścinki nie zaburzają gry i nie irytują, jest to na prawdę solidny port z WII'U. 
Najważniejsze + i -
+ Eksploracja!
+ Brak prowadzenia za rączkę
+ Ogrom aktywności w świecie gry
- Walki z bossami
- brak dubbingu...
Podsumowując, jest to gra która na pewno nie trafi do każdego, stawia na kreatywność gracza, eksploracje i sandboxowość, jeśli ktoś nie lubi takich sandboxowych otwartych światów i po prostu chce przebiec przez fabułę, jasne, można, ale w takim wypadku raczej nie polecam, ale dla graczy takich jak ja, którzy szukają dużego otwartego sandboxa nie prowadzącego za rączkę jest to tytuł obowiązkowy, obiektywnie gra ma niedociągnięcia, braki i nie jest idealna, więc na pewno nie zasługuje na 10/10, a raczej na solidne 8,5/10, ale dla mnie osobiście, to aktualnie najlepsza gra w jaką kiedykolwiek grałem!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
“Open your eyes.”——《塞尔达传说：旷野之息》通关测评

自《塞尔达传说：旷野之息》发售后，开放世界游戏如雨后春笋般诞生。这是游戏史上的里程碑，开放世界游戏的常青树，也是青沼英二献给全天下玩家的情书。

画面9/10
在Nintendo Switch上的运行表现中规中矩，在2017年已经是较为优秀的画面处理了。但部分场景例如克洛格森林掉帧严重，噪点明显。游戏整体没有华而不实的设计和多余的特效，设计得十分简洁。我依稀记得，即便在画质受限的掌机上运行，拔出大师之剑的那个场景抵得过所有游戏。

战斗系统10/10
本作的战斗系统极具深度，只要玩家发挥想象力，没有什么事情是做不到的。从时间停止到遥控炸弹，从“林克时间”到“风弹”，这是任天堂独有的游戏设计理念——“留白”。这不是什么高深的理论，只是单纯地让玩家决定游戏该如何“玩”。

地图设计10/10
从踏出复苏神庙的那一刻起，任天堂就展现了一个“活”的世界，一个所见即所得的海拉鲁大陆。这里有雪山和湖泊，有丘陵和洞穴，还有火山和沙漠。本作几乎没有引导玩家如何探索，脑海中驱动我的只有“那座山的背后是什么，我想去看看”。

剧情&人物塑造8.5/10
较为平淡的剧情和人物塑造。没有惊人的反转也没有可怕的真相，保持着任天堂的传统作风，一个拯救公主的故事。我认为林克的作用只是任天堂让玩家体验这个世界的媒介。林克是“哑巴”的原因，在我看来，是设计团队认为过多的对于操控角色的塑造会影响玩家对于林克的代入感，而林克便是每位玩家自己，这又是一处“留白”。

配音/配乐9.5/10
一切都那么美好，一切都那么平静。在如今的2026年，找到“呀哈哈”的音乐还在被人使用。走出神庙，俯瞰整个世界时的背景音乐彷佛还在我耳边环绕。那些音乐是属于海拉鲁大陆的“呼吸”，这便是“旷野之息”了。

综评97/100
优点：极高的自由度；有活力的开放世界；极具开发性的战斗系统；精心设计的地图。

缺点：极其微弱的游戏引导，导致部分玩家难以沉浸；画面质量有待提高，噪点/掉帧在某些场景严重。

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: This game is a really good open world experience, the adventurous energy in this game is unbeatable. Let's talk about the story, the whole vibe with Calamity Ganon bringing Hyrule down to it's knees and Princess Zelda having to seal him away is amazing, and then Link get's put to sleep and he has to venture through the destroyed Hyrule to build up his strength in order to fight Calamity Ganon. That's all I'm going to tell you about the story so let's talk about some other things. Techniques such as flurry-rush and bullet-time were added to the combat and I find them to be really fun additions. Along with that, there's a weapon durability system that encourages you to use the game's different weapons in a way that I really like. Now we need to talk about how fun it is to explore this game's interpretation of Hyrule. There is a tonne of chests to be opened and there is something so fun about finding a random Bokoblin base in the middle of a field. Many people complain about the dungeons in this game but I don't mind them, even if they take away the charm that was the original Zelda dungeons. Now I want to talk about the boss fights. They're all unique in their own ways and they can be really challenging sometimes. I believe I died more than 10 times fighting Thunderblight Ganon, so good luck fighting him! Also the visuals are stunning, especially considering it's running on the Nintendo Switch. I just want to finish off by saying, please buy this game, it's definitely worth it for anyone who owns a Switch. But if you don't want it, there's always other games to buy, so why not check out some of my other reviews to see if you're interested in any of the those games.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Um novo lindo Mundo Aberto

​Não é apenas mais um Zelda, é um novo padrão para a indústria. A Nintendo honrou o DNA da franquia enquanto reinventou completamente a liberdade nos videogames.

​Exploração Orgânica: O mapa é sua tela. Sem ícones poluídos, a curiosidade é o que guia o jogador. O sentimento de que você pode alcançar qualquer ponto no horizonte é genuíno e recompensador.

​Dinâmica e Criatividade: O uso da física e a gestão de armas transformam cada combate em um quebra-cabeça único. 
As Shrines e missões secundárias são perfeitamente integradas ao ambiente.

​Dificuldade e Atmosfera: O desafio é justo e respeita a inteligência do jogador. 
A trilha sonora minimalista e a arte melancólica criam uma imersão poética sem igual.

​Como muitos ressaltam, o trunfo aqui é a ausência de "mãos dadas". Cada descoberta é um mérito seu, tornando a jornada verdadeiramente épica.
​
Uma obra-prima indispensável que dita as regras para o futuro dos jogos.

Review:
Um dos melhores games que já joguei em toda a minha vida. Não diria que é o jogo perfeito, porque não acredito que exista tal tipo de game, por isso não dou nota máxima. Mesmo após anos do seu lançamento, o jogo segue sendo um destaque até nos dias atuais. Mundo gigante que te permite explorar e viver de forma intensa, porém, senti falta de uma maior diversidade dos inimigos e em escalar um pouco mais no quesito dificuldade, a história é interessante mas não chega a ser um grande destaque desse game, e as missões da história principal ficam repetitivas, porque é basicamente ir atrás das feras, conversar com algum NPC que vai se mostrar importante para a história, desativar a fera divina, entrar e eliminar o boss. O chefão final, Ganon, também não me pareceu desafiador. Tanto é que o venci de primeira sem nenhuma dificuldade. E o pós game, após derrotar o chefão principal, não me pareceu tão atraente e acabei desistindo de prosseguir a minha jogada (com 65h de gameplay).
Apesar das limitações gráficas a Nintendo fez um excelente trabalho com a arte gráfica do game, porque é lindo, a parte de áudio também é um espetáculo a parte e traz uma paz gigante ao jogador quando explora esse universo. Com certeza o jogo possui os seus defeitos mas é uma baita experiência e com toda certeza foi uma inspiração para um outro grande jogo: Elden Ring.
Apesar do jogo ser considerado velho, recomendo demais a experiência e que ao jogar, possa viver e explorar ao máximo o universo prque com toda a certeza isso agrega muito valor ao jogador. JOGAÇO!!!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Overall, Breath of the Wild is an amazing game with freedom, exploration, and creativity at its core. However, there are a few areas where I think the design could have been improved:


1. Ganon’s Difficulty: 
For a player who has tamed all the Divine Beasts and prepared thoroughly, Ganon feels too easy. A scaling system where he becomes faster or deals more damage depending on your exploration and completion in Hyrule would have made the final battle far more satisfying. This issue alone drops the game by a point in my personal rating. 


2. Weapon Durability: 
Weapons break frequently, which interrupts the flow of combat and exploration. While it encourages creativity, it often feels more frustrating than strategic. 


3. Champion Ability Cooldowns: 
Champion abilities only recharge after all charges are used. This requires intentionally wasting abilities before entering tough fights just to reset the cooldown, which is unintuitive and disrupts gameplay. 


4. Master Sword Recharging:
This is basically the same problem as the Champion Ability Cooldowns


5. Limited Inventory Space: 
Starting with few weapon slots and having to hunt Koroks for expansions can feel tedious. Players who want to experiment with a variety of gear are forced into repetitive side content, which reduces the sense of freedom early on.


6. No way of keeping track of the recipes you have already found or  the recipes of the food you have already made:
I would recommend having food as a tab in the Hyrule Compendium where you can see the recipes, default pictures or pictures you take yourself of the food and the names of the food.


7. No dedicated UI section to drop items in your inventory when opening chests while you have a full inventory:
This is annoying because you have to close the chest, drop an item and then open the chest again to get your item.


8. Limited stamp variety:
The small selection of map stamps forces players to reuse symbols for unrelated purposes, such as marking shrines with treasure chest icons or using cooking pots to mark Link’s house.


9. 
No option to store an image in the Hyrule Compendium without it saving in the album:
There is no option to save an image directly to the Hyrule Compendium without also storing it in the album. This requires players to manually delete photos afterward, which is inconvenient and unintuitive.

10. Dinraal, Naydra and Farosh being in the Monsters category in the Hyrule Compendium:
Their description in the Hyrule Compendiun literally says that they bear no ill will toward people.


11. No text that says what you're sorting for in the inventory
I never knew how the sorting worked even after beating the game.

RATING: 8/10

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: So yeah, I’ve probably spent way too many hours in Hyrule, but honestly, Breath of the Wild is just one of those games that you can’t ever really stop thinking about once you’ve experienced it. It’s not just a game, it’s like this weird, beautiful, lonely, and yet totally chaotic world that just lets you be whoever you want to be. I remember the first time I stepped out of the Shrine of Resurrection—that pan over the Great Plateau? Absolute cinema. It’s a masterclass in game design because it doesn’t give you a checklist or a map full of annoying icons. It just says, "Hey, see that mountain? You can climb it. See that weird glow in the distance? Go figure it out." And you do. You just wander. You get distracted by a butterfly, then a group of Bokoblins, then you find a shrine, and suddenly four hours have passed and you haven’t even touched the main quest. That kind of freedom is rare. Most games talk about being open world, but then they hit you with invisible walls or level-gating. BotW doesn't care about any of that. If you’re smart enough (or crazy enough), you can go straight to the final boss from the start. That’s just insane to me.I love **** let’s talk about the gear for a sec because, man, the items in this game are actually legendary once you figure out how to use them. I’m a huge horse guy in games, and the way they handled the horses here feels so grounded. But the real game-changer is when you get your hands on the Ancient Saddle and Bridle. Before those, your horse was kinda just... there. You’d leave it behind because you climbed a cliff and it couldn't follow you. But with that Ancient set? You whistle and boom, teleportation. It makes the bond with your horse feel so much more useful and, honestly, it adds to that cinematic feeling when you’re galloping through a field at night and you can just summon your ride whenever you need to make a quick getaway from a Guardian. It’s those little things, the quality of life stuff mixed with the "Chemistry Engine" where fire actually burns things and lightning is attracted to your metal shield, that makes the world feel like a real place rather than just a digital **** thing that really got to me, and I know I’m a total **** for this kind of stuff, is the whole tragic, romantic undertone of the story, especially involving Mipha. I’m a big fan of those cinematic, slightly heartbreaking backstories, and hers just hits differently. It’s not forced down your throat, it’s just there in the memories and the way the Zora people talk about her. The fact that she made that Zora Armor specifically for Link as a proposal... and then she died before she could even give it to him or tell him how she felt? That’s some heavy stuff. Every time I see her spirit on Vah Ruta, or use Mipha’s Grace to save my skin in a fight, it feels like this lingering, protective love that survived a hundred years of darkness. It gives the whole "save the world" thing a lot more weight because it’s not just about a kingdom, it’s about the people who loved you and aren't there anymore. It’s subtle, it’s romantic in a very sad way, and it makes the quiet moments of the game feel so much **** music, man... it's just perfect. Some people wanted a big, bombastic theme playing 24/7, but they’re wrong. The silence is what makes the music work. You're wandering through the ruins of a village, and you just hear these sparse, lonely piano notes that feel like they're mourning the world with you. But then, when things get real, the soundtrack absolutely **** final push toward Hyrule Castle is probably the most "epic" feeling I’ve ever had in a Zelda game. The way the music shifts from the outdoor theme to that heavy, orchestral march as you get closer to the sanctum is incredible. And that final fight with Calamity Ganon? It’s pure spectacle. When the Divine Beasts fire their lasers and the Champions' spirits are there with you, it feels like this massive culmination of everything you’ve suffered through. The second phase out on the field, with the sun low on the horizon and Zelda calling out to you while the music swells... that’s the kind of stuff I play games for. It’s grand, it’s emotional, and it feels like a true ending to a century-old tragedy. You’re not just hitting a boss; you’re ending a nightmare. It’s the perfect mix of gameplay and pure cinematic storytelling.Seriously, if you haven't played this yet, I don't know what to tell you. It’s a masterpiece. The weapons break, the rain makes you slide off cliffs, and you’ll probably die a hundred times to lightning or falling rocks, but that’s the charm. It’s a raw, beautiful experience that respects the player’s intelligence and emotions.I still go back just to ride my horse through the fields sometimes. It's just that good.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is not just a game, it is a revolution. A true masterpiece that redefines the very idea of the open world, it doesn’t simply invite exploration; it demands it. From the very first moments, the player is driven by pure curiosity, by the irresistible urge to wander, to climb, to look beyond the next hill just to see what lies there. Exploration is never forced or guided,it feels natural, organic, and deeply personal.What truly sets Breath of the Wild apart is its extraordinary artistic direction and attention to detail. Every landscape feels hand-crafted, every ruin tells a silent story, and every sunrise over Hyrule is a moment worth stopping for. The game’s physics system is nothing short of astonishing: fire spreads with the wind, metal conducts electricity, and the environment reacts intelligently to the player’s actions. This level of systemic depth makes experimentation endlessly rewarding and turns even simple encounters into memorable experiences.Most of all, Breath of the Wild is profoundly immersive. It creates a version of Hyrule that feels alive, vast, and breathtakingly beautiful,a world you never want to leave. Hours pass unnoticed as the game constantly fuels your desire to explore just a little more, to uncover one more secret, to lose yourself completely. It is a game that reshapes expectations, sets a new standard for open-world design, and remains unforgettable long after the console is turned off. Simply one of the best game of all time, or perhaps the greatest.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild redefines what an open-world adventure can be. 

It’s a breathtaking reinvention of a beloved franchise, blending freedom, discovery, and artistry in a way few games have ever achieved. From the moment Link awakens on the Great Plateau, every hill, forest, and distant shrine feels like an invitation to explore—a living world that rewards curiosity rather than handholds the **** gameplay is a triumph of systemic design. 
Every mechanic—from weapon durability to environmental interaction—plays a role in shaping a unique adventure with every session. Whether cooking meals for survival, mastering combat physics, or finding clever ways to scale impossible cliffs, Breath of the Wild empowers players to think, experiment, and create their own stories.

Visually, the game is stunning in its simplicity. The cel-shaded art style and painterly lighting elevate Hyrule to something timeless, while the soundtrack alternates between serene piano whispers and grand, emotional swells. Performance on the Nintendo Switch isn’t flawless, with occasional frame dips in dense environments, but it never detracts from the sense of **** there’s one minor drawback, it’s the lack of traditional dungeons that once defined Zelda’s legacy. Still, that trade-off enables a breathtaking scale of freedom and emotional immersion. 

Breath of the Wild isn’t just one of Zelda’s best—it’s one of gaming’s greatest achievements.

Review:
Este juego simplemente es una obra de arte. He estado viendo reseñas negativas, que directamente no tienen sentido, por ejemplo:
- (No se siente como un zelda) Los que dicen esto no saben lo que es la innovación, si todos los zeldas fueran iguales, decaeria la franquicia.
- (No hay nada que hacer) Eso es mentira, es un mundo abierto muy vivo con muchas misiones principales, secundarias, secretos, mazmorras, templos, acertijos, puzles, desafíos, etc...
- (El juego va mal) Este juego va a 30 fps si lo juegas en swicht, pero es culpa de la consola. También puedes jugarlo en swicht 2 o pc para que vaya mejor.
- (El juego se ve mal) Completamente falso, puedes ver en YouTube como el juego tiene una dirección artística muy bonita y original.
- (Poca variedad de enemigos) Estas criticas no entienden el sistema de enemigos del juego. Basicamente, hay una variedad base de enemigos, y a lo largo de tu progesión, estos sufren cambios que los van haciendo más fuertes, por lo que en total hay mucha variedad. Ademas que el mapa está llena de bosses originales por todos lados.

Conclusión: pruébalo, es un gran juego, un mundo abierto increíble, un combate divertido. Las cosas malas que tiene este producto son ínfimas, en mi opinión el inventario puede ser un poco lioso y las armas se rompen rápido, pero son detalles sin importancia. Quien lo haya jugado y pasado, te podrá decir que es de los mejores juegos de la historia.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
旷野之息的开放世界是设计得很精妙、让人很有好奇心和探索欲的，你总是会被一些别的地方的兴趣点所吸引。同时，你的探索欲也会收到回报，可能是装备、道具、神庙、新的谜题、呀哈哈、稀有矿床、优美的风景或者是莱尼尔……
游戏的机制简单但很有意思，炸弹、磁力、静止器、制冰、冰火电元素互动，就能造就很丰富的可能性和游玩趣味。
如果说有什么我觉得有点遗憾或者是不足的话，就是：故事性的缺乏。总的来说，它只提供了一个主线故事（或许加上DLC给每位英杰补充的一点点叙事），几乎没有任何支线故事（每个支线任务的情节都简单得很难称得上是个完整的故事），很多看似该有着迷人故事的地方或者景点（比如遗忘神殿，德伊布朗遗迹，长得像盘蜷的蛇的一个半岛，最东部那几个被木桥连接的耸立的岛屿……），提供的都是“谜题”或“试炼”，或只是单纯的奇特的风景，而没有“故事”。这会让我在探索的后期感到孤独，以及感受不到海拉鲁大地的生命力。
总的来说，它在我心中，离十全十美仅仅只差了一些。

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: Oh yes, Breath of the Wild. After taking a break from video games for about 15 years, this game brought me back when I tried it on my sister’s Switch, and I’m grateful for that. At first, I was skeptical about an open world where you’re not told what to do next. But that’s exactly what made it so special in the end. I just wanted to explore every corner out of sheer curiosity, wondering what was behind the next mountain or waiting at its summit. I know it’s been said a thousand times already, but it’s just so true for me. This was also encouraged by the fact that you can climb anywhere and then fly to your desired destination with the kite. It never stopped being fun and incredibly satisfying. So, the game completely pulled me in. Just being in this world was an incredible experience, thanks to the atmosphere, the “breath of the wild” with its changing weather, rain, sunrise, twilight, all captured so beautifully. The graphics may be technically outdated, but the art style is timeless, and the world feels alive. Add to that the unique gameplay mechanics and puzzles, and the result is pure fun. The absence of classic Zelda-style dungeons didn’t bother me (and I also love the classic Zeldas!), because I liked the concept of the shrines. And while the divine beasts could have been a little bit better, that’s only a minor drawback considering everything else the game offers. The soundtrack is wonderful too - it supports the atmosphere instead of dominating it, and emphasizes emotional highlights in subtle ways. Some people dislike the lack of voice acting, but I enjoyed the charming written dialogue. It even allows for humor in ways that voice acting can’t. The weapon durability system is also a common complaint. I can understand that partly, but for me it added a layer of strategy and resource management that made the experience even more engaging. It also forces you to try out different types of weapons and be inventive in combat. All in all, an unforgettable masterpiece. I called it the best game of all time (for me!) - until Tears of the Kingdom came along. ;)

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
Even though this game is not my first love among its genre, even though some of its content no longer feels fresh to me, even though its price can be daunting for someone who doesn’t own a Nintendo Switch, and even though it has long been overpraised—I would still give it the highest evaluation.Because the gameplay it presents is unparalleled. It once again redefined the open-world genre and laid a tremendous foundation for those that followed. What it wants is for players to play the game, rather than for the game to play the **** the main storyline, I am Link, the knight who rescues the princess. But in the vast open world, wandering around freely is me—the “old rascal.” The game does not rely on explicit numerical progression, so the one who truly grows throughout the journey is not the knight Link, but the **** gameplay is remarkably free, which also highlights the importance of using intelligence and strategy. In this kind of game, what I can never forget is climbing to the top of a mountain and, from its peak, watching the arrival of dusk or sunrise—that moment filled with overwhelming emotion from deep within.Perhaps that is the true meaning of games…
即使此游戏在这类游戏里并非是我的初恋，即使部分内容已经对我来说没有了新鲜感，即使它贵的让一个不接触ns的人来说望而生畏，即使这个游戏早已被吹烂——但我仍会给它至高评价，因为它展现出来的游戏性是无法比拟的，它再一次的定义了开放世界，为后者奠定了莫大的基础，它想要的是让玩家去玩游戏而不是游戏去玩玩家。在主线剧情中我是拯救公主的骑士林克，而在开放的世界中乱逛的是我这个“老流氓”，这个游戏并没有明确的数字化表现，所以在游戏中成长并非骑士林克而是玩家自己。游戏的玩法也是相当的自由，这也侧面说明了智取的重要性。在这类游戏中我任然忘不了的是每当我翻上一座大山，在大山之上欣赏黄昏和日出的到来的那一幕，那来自内心的感慨万千。也许这正是游戏的意义......

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review:
To be fair to this game, I played it nearly 7 years after its release on Nintendo Switch, so keep that in mind while reading this review. The most fun I had playing this game was while doing the dungeons, shrines, and while hunting for Korok seeds/cooking ingredients. The interaction of elements and the physics of this game were the absolute coolest part of the game. It felt so good to try something random to solve a puzzle and have it actually work, that by itself makes the game worth playing. I think scope is probably one of the biggest problems this game has, it has so many ambitious things it does, but on hardware that doesn’t support these grand ideas. 
The art style is pretty good, but it looks so fuzzy that it really ruins the visuals of the game when you’re playing. Sacrificing visual fidelity wouldn’t be that bad if you got the tradeoff of having good performance (60 fps), but the frame rate isn’t good either, often feeling like you’re lucky if you get 30 fps. Combat is okay, but it isn’t something I enjoyed doing in this game. It mostly felt like I fought the same few enemies in the same way over and over. This isn’t because you don’t have a diversity of combat options, you can actually be quite creative in the way you approach combat, but because of the homogeneity of the enemy design there is no real incentive for you to experiment in combat. You pretty much find what works and stick with that, there are no mechanics that force you to try out different systems. This might be a positive for many players who want the freedom to express themselves in combat, I am not a creative person so if the game doesn’t force me to change how I think about a situation then I generally don’t experiment. My biggest issue with the combat though is weapon durability; I understand why they did it so that you can’t just go grab a strong weapon early and make the game easy mode, but that flies in the face of the rest of the design choices in this game: go anywhere and do whatever you want in whatever order you choose. If I want to get a strong weapon and use that for the entirety of the game, that should be an option. Instead, I have to mark camps on the map where there are weapons that I like and then wait multiple in-game hours for a blood moon to respawn camps so that I can farm multiple instances of the stronger weapons that I want for combat. At the very least, make it so that I can force the camps the respawn rather than having to wait for my game to refresh its memory, it’s anti-fun. Lastly, the story was garbage and basically non-existent, but whatever that isn’t a big deal, you can just skip that stuff. All in all, I had fun and this is a great game, but considering the hype and reverence I have heard for many years about how this is the greatest game ever made, I had much higher expectations and was disappointed in the game when I finished it.

But once I got into the core of the game, it quickly became underwhelming. The open world, while visually appealing, feels mostly empty. I was hoping for diverse areas packed with interesting content, but what I found instead were large stretches of space populated by the same handful of copy-pasted enemies. Exploration didn’t feel rewarding—it felt repetitive. Combat is decent. I can see why some players enjoy it. There’s a certain charm in the way battles play out, but the poor weapon durability system really drags it down.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is an ambitious open-world game that impresses in some areas but falls short in others. The sense of exploration is its greatest strength, with a vast, beautiful world that encourages curiosity and discovery. Unfortunately, that world often feels empty, with repetitive shrines and copy-paste enemy encounters that wear thin over time. The story is minimal and lacks the emotional weight seen in other Zelda titles, leaving little incentive to push forward beyond pure exploration. Weapon durability adds unnecessary frustration rather than meaningful challenge. There are undeniable moments of wonder, but they come buried under a lot of filler. It is a good game, but far from the flawless masterpiece some make it out to be.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: Un excellent passage au monde ouvert. Le monde ouvert est grand et bien rempli. Des thèmes musicaux très réussis, des personnages très bien écrits et une histoire intéressante, bien que assez courte et que je n'ai pas vraiment aimé le fait qu'on nous la raconte par l'intermédiaire de souvenirs. On déplorera cependant la manque de personnalité du «level design» des 4 créatures divine ainsi que du design des boss. De plus, le boss final (1ère partie) ne fait que reprendre les «paterns» des 4 fléaux et la 2e partie du combat est une vaste blague tant elle est d'une facilité indécente. La perte des objets ainsi que le remplacement des mythiques donjons par des sanctuaires en quantité industrielle (mais de très courte durée) est un choix que je n'apprécie pas à titre personnel, mais je conçois également que d'autres personnes apprécient. La mécanique d'armes cassables est assez frustrante aussi. Pas que ce soit une mauvaise chose que les armes soient cassables, mais à ce point, oui. En résumé, Zelda Breath of the Wild est un excellent jeu qui brise la formule qu'on avait depuis Link To The Past, mais il y a plusieurs points qui manquent pour le considérer comme plus qu'un excellent jeu.

Review:
BoTW is one addictive, amazing game. I spent a lot of time exploring and challenging myself until I was able to defeat enemies that seemed impossibleat the beginning. But the best bit is the vast world and its secrets, the post-apocalyptical atmosphere, the hidden secrets that you find everywhere. Controlling the character is easy and fun. You have lots of different activities you can do in the game. My only issue with it was that I didn't get to see a post-Ganon world rebuilding, characters acknowledging the change and Hyrule becoming whole again.
The ending seemed so swift compared to the many hours I put in that I felt I've been robbed of closure. But I understand it's a necessary mechanic so that people can come back and fine tune their skills or finish doing whatever they left out. Other than that, it's really a wonderful game that I'll always cherish.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild
Review: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild... where do I even start?The gameplay is incredible. Scavenging for weapons and supplies makes every upgrade feel earned, and while most weapons break, that just pushes you to think creatively and adapt — which fits perfectly with the game’s vibe. It’s like if you think something should work, it usually does. Want to roast an apple? Hold a torch under it — just try not to burn the forest down.There’s so much freedom and possibility, I could spend hours just listing cool stuff you can do. But what surprised me most was the story. Most games lose me halfway through, but this one had me locked in the whole time. I actually cared about the characters, the world, and what happened **** you’re looking for a game to get completely lost in, something to turn your summer into a legendary adventure — this is it. Breath of the Wild isn’t just hype. It’s history. Trust me when I say that it's genuinely fun to play.
