Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Tears of the Kingdom is a masterclass in game design. It takes the foundation of Breath of the Wild and expands it in ways I didn't think were possible on the Switch. The new building mechanics (Ultrahand and Fuse) are a literal game-changer—they turn every puzzle and combat encounter into a playground for your own **** verticality is breathtaking. Diving from a sky island all the way down into the depths feels seamless and epic every single time. Hyrule feels more alive than ever, packed with secrets, meaningful side quests, and a much more engaging main story this time **** only reason I’m giving it a 9 instead of a 10 is the performance. The hardware is clearly struggling to keep up with the game's ambition, and the frame rate drops can be distracting during heavy action. Also, navigating some of the menus can feel a bit clunky after dozens of hours.Overall, it's a monumental achievement. If you own a Switch, you owe it to yourself to play this.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
My favorite series' second major blunder. 

I want to preface this by stating, TOTK is not a bad game. I know a lot of people will look at a 7 and loose their minds but stay with me here. 

Every time a Zelda game gets announced the hype is electric, everyone is on board. When that first TOTK teaser dropped in 2019/20 (don't remember exactly when) the one where Link and Zelda descend beneath the castle to find the mummified corpse of Ganon I was hooked. I thought we were going to get another darker LoZ game, like twilight princess but in a world beyond Hyrule. 

Imagine my immense disappointment when I learned it was the same world again with sky islands and essentially a giant cave system underground. 

I love Breath of the Wild, the game was unique in its minimalist approach and it works so well, but outside of the story change up and new crafting techniques available to link, it really felt like being shown the same game twice. 

Now there are improvements, very welcome improvements such as traditional dungeons, weapon creativity, a stronger story in my opinion and if you played on the switch 2; a playable framerate. However, they don't do enough to make me feel like this is a brand new Zelda game and not BOTW 70$ DLC. 

I want to love this game, and there are times I had fun playing it. But I don't have the urge to explore like I did the first time which is a shame, there are probably cool things hidden in the world but I genuinely can't be bothered to walk through the same areas for the 100th time in the hopes of finding a new shiny temporary weapon or shrine. 

I do worry Nintendo is going to get stuck in BOTW fever and this become their Forza Horizon or Call of Duty, where they'll just keep pumping out games in this Hyrule instead of changing it up like they used to. I can only hope the next Zelda has that semi-linear with open areas like the Ocarina to Twilight run it had. Or maybe I'm just old and this is what the people want.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: UNLIMITED CREATIVITY, FAMILIAR GROUND: Tears of the Kingdom stands strong by introducing revolutionary new mechanics and creative puzzles, but it suffers from leaning too heavily on Breath of the Wild’s foundation while simultaneously raising the price by $10. It is a brilliant expansion of an existing world, but that familiarity comes at a cost. THE EVOLUTION: A BUILDER’S PARADISE: If Breath of the Wild was about exploration, Tears of the Kingdom is about invention. The new "Ultrahand" and "Fuse" mechanics are nothing short of wonderful. Being able to build everything from simple rafts to complex, fire-breathing mechs turns every obstacle into a creative playground. This ingenuity extends to the shrines and world puzzles, which are significantly more polished and satisfying than those in the previous game. The sheer joy of "breaking" a puzzle with a ridiculous contraption is the game’s greatest strength. THE SKY AND THE DEPTHS: While the surface may feel familiar, the addition of the Sky Islands and the massive, eerie Depths adds a much-needed layer of verticality. Descending into the pitch-black Depths for the first time is a haunting, high-stakes experience that balances the bright, airy feel of the Sky. These new locations provide the "wow" factor that keeps the game from feeling like a simple retread. THE BIGGEST CONS: RECYCLED ASSETS AND THE PRICE TAG: However, three major issues hold this back from perfection. First, the surface map is essentially a "Ctrl C + Ctrl V" of the BOTW map. While there are changes, the "déjà vu" is real and can make exploration feel less magical for returning players. Second, the story is surprisingly paper-thin; it lacks the quiet, emotional resonance that made BOTW’s narrative so memorable. Finally, there is the $70 price tag. Charging $10 more for a game that heavily reuses the world and assets of its predecessor is a tough pill to swallow. PERFORMANCE: PUSHING THE LIMITS: Technically, the game is a miracle of optimization for the aging Switch hardware. The fact that the physics engine can track multiple moving parts on a custom-built mech without crashing is impressive. That said, you will see frequent frame drops when using Ultrahand in busy areas, reminding you that this software is screaming for more powerful hardware. (Note: A Switch 2 version does exist, but be aware that it requires a separate purchase.)PROS:Revolutionary building mechanics (Ultrahand/Fuse). Incredible, complex shrine puzzles. Massive new world layers with the Sky and the Depths. CONS:Surface map feels overly recycled from the first game. Paper-thin narrative compared to Breath of the Wild. The $70 entry fee feels steep for a sequel with reused assets. THE FINAL VERDICT: 8/10: Tears of the Kingdom is a mechanical masterpiece that offers some of the best gameplay in the series. However, the recycled world and increased price prevent it from reaching the legendary status of its predecessor. It is an essential play for the "mechs" and the puzzles, but the sense of discovery isn't quite as fresh the second time around.

Building masterfully on Breath of the Wild, it introduces Ultrahand, Fuse, Ascend, and Recall abilities that unleash unprecedented creativity, letting players build vehicles, weapons, and contraptions to traverse skies, surfaces, and depths seamlessly.​This expanded Hyrule—now with sky islands and vast underground realms—brims with mysteries, shrines, and regional phenomena that reward curiosity at every turn. Combat feels dynamic and inventive, puzzles are ingeniously layered, and the narrative delivers emotional highs like the epic Ganondorf showdown, all while respecting player agency above all.​Nintendo's polish shines through: no major bugs, frictionless physics, and hundreds of hours of emergent fun make it a generational masterpiece that redefines adventure games. If Breath was revolutionary, Tears is transcendent—don't miss this legend.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, on the other hand, represents the opposite extreme of Ocarina of Time: instead of perfecting the classic structure, it expands it into an open system where physics, creativity, and experimentation are the true language of design. What's astonishing is that, despite the enormous risk of disrupting its own equilibrium—more freedom, more systems, more potential chaos—the game doesn't fall apart. Instead, it maintains cohesion, purpose, and consistent reward, demonstrating that the series can risk everything and still sustain itself with impressive clarity of vision. The Zelda series could falter when it becomes overly conscious of its own structure—as happens in The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword, where progression feels excessively programmatic and directed—but what's extraordinary is that when it finds the balance between design and intention, between freedom and form, between homage and identity, it doesn't fail. Whether from the classic precision of Twilight Princess or the systemic audacity of Tears of the Kingdom, Zelda demonstrates that it can wander down radically different paths without losing its essence.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
TOTK is not as good as BOTW, but it comes close. The graphics are amazing. My favorite aspects of the game were the hand mechanics and gliding all around Hyrule. The Ultrahand mechanic in particular, was a lot of fun and added creativity to exploration. However, I found myself relying almost entirely on Ultrahand and rarely using abilities like Recall. The game should have encouraged more balanced use of its abilities.

The game offers an enormous amount of content, but much of it feels unnecessary or uninteresting. Some areas of the Depths felt empty and boring to explore, and the same was true for the sky islands. Because the surface world is very similar to BOTW, exploration didn’t feel very surprising this time around. Completing the game also felt very cumbersome and more difficult than BOTW.

In terms of story, the narrative felt stronger than in Breath of the Wild. I enjoyed collecting the Tears much more than the memories in BOTW. Regarding enemies and combat, I personally preferred the Guardians from BOTW over the Constructs. The Fuse system was a fun addition that added diversity and creativity to gameplay. Finally, the music was not memorable, and I missed the more recognizable, classic Zelda musical style.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Breath of the Wild was already an incredible game with so much to do and explore, but I think Tears of the Kingdom improves on it. While people complain that they feel this game just kinda ignores what happened in BOTW, that didn’t really affect my enjoyment of the game since I think the gameplay is better since you can build to make navigation much faster and you’re also introduced to the Sky Islands, (which I will admit are a little underwhelming since most of them are really tiny) and the Depths which I thought was fun to explore and opened for more exploration and I enjoyed getting all the lightroots to get more of the map. The story is this game is I think great and I especially love what they did with Zelda especially when she sacrificed herself to become the Light Dragoon and restore the Master Sword for Link. Now, I will say that the Master Sword is a downgrade in this game because you can’t upgrade the damage and durability like you could in BOTW and the story makes it seem like the Master Sword will be more powerful than ever when it pretty much has the exact same base damage of 30 and runs out of energy kinda quickly. It’s even worse when you have to either fuse things to make the sword do more damage or there’s straight up just better weapons than it. It’s just really disappointing that they nerfed the Master Sword in this game. Anyway, I wanted to talk about the dungeons in this game which I think are much better than the Divine Beasts from BOTW since they actually feel different from each other in terms of design and puzzle solving. The bosses are also more interesting this time around with my favorite being Colgera from the Wind Temple. Final thing I wanna talk is Ganondorf since they absolutely did a fantastic job with him. He just looks so badass and the final fight is so much better than Calamity Ganon from BOTW. I especially love the last phase where he turns into a literal dragon and you ride on top of the Light Dragon to hit his weak spots and it’s just so epic. Oh, I forgot to mention this, but while BOTW had the Champions, this game has Sages and while they’re cool to have, I just don’t like how you have to use most of them by walking up to them and it could get annoying especially when you have multiple out. And there’s also the fact that some of them like Sidon and Mineru I just found to be kinda useless and Riju’s power is pretty much the Shock Arrows from BOTW. My favorite to use was easily Tulin especially when used in the sky since you can get more distance with him which is funny that the wind sage is the most useful just like Revali’s Gale from BOTW. Anyway, I’m gonna wrap this up by saying that TOTK is an improvement over BOTW and I would highly recommend playing this game.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: The Legend of Zelda, Tears of the Kingdom is more than just a sequel, it’s a bold step forward for a game that was already revolutionary. Building on everything Breath of the Wild achieved, it takes familiar ideas and pushes them to incredible new heights, showing that even in a world we thought we knew, there’s still so much to discover.What makes Tears of the Kingdom truly special is how deep and creative it feels. Mechanics like Ultrahand, Fuse, and Ascend turn you from an explorer into a true inventor. Every challenge can be solved in countless ways, limited only by your imagination. The physics system, already amazing in the first game, has been expanded so that experimenting with the world is endlessly rewarding. Whether you’re building complex machines, improvising weapons, or stumbling on surprising interactions, the game constantly encourages you to play in your own way.Technically, the game is impressive, but it’s important to note that on the original Switch, the game sometimes struggles due to hardware limitations. Frame drops, long load times, and occasional stuttering can make parts of the experience frustrating, and the sheer scale of the world doesn’t always feel smooth. However, playing it on the  Switch 2 shows the game at its best: stable, gorgeous, and fully immersive, making it much easier to appreciate the incredible world and systems Nintendo has **** art and sound remain incredible. Hyrule looks and feels timeless, the music and effects add subtle but powerful emotion, and the story is stronger and more refined without ever taking away your freedom to explore. Every moment feels intentional, every adventure personal.Tears of the Kingdom doesn’t just improve on its predecessor, it completely redefines what freedom and creativity in a game can feel like. It’s a landmark achievement, a masterclass in game design, and a reminder of why Nintendo does what it does best. One of the goats

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Este juego tiene muchos problemas.
Historia
Nunca me interesé por los nuevos personajes, especialmente por las mismas cinemáticas: "Secret stone? Demon king?". Odio que Link se haga p****** cuando es evidente que la Zelda que aparece es falsa, el juego pretende que sea una gran revelación cuando no lo es, queda muy mal. Una historia sin consecuencias, pudieron hacer que Zelda recupere su forma original si se superan los 150 santuarios como final verdadero o algo así, no porque sí o por "el poder del amor" supongo. En el momento que decían que es un cambio irreversible dije nah, nintendo tiene miedo y efectivamente, no esperaba nada y aún así decepcionaron, hasta le devolvieron el brazo a Link y todo
Santuarios y puzzles.
Los puzzles son muy triviales, casi todo lo puedes solucionar con un escudo cohete, flecha bomba, una motoneta voladora, etc, no se siente que estés "burlando a los desarolladores" como unos dicen sino como si los santuarios fueran un cubo encajable didáctico dónde cualquier pieza entra en cualquier hueco por estar mal diseñado, tanto que en la segunda vuelta por el juego (incluso en la primera partida) uno se aburre de hacerlos y solo lo hace para completar todo o ni se molesta en hacerlos.
Hablando de santuarios ¿Cuál es la necesidad de poner como 5 tutoriales de santuarios después de la gran isla de los albores? Desde el principio del juego uno aprende como esquivar, usar el arco, etc, ¿por qué volver a enseñarte como hacer un parry en ese santuario que no viste temprano y entraste después de 50 horas de juego? Encima con textos lentos que no se pueden saltar, parece que no supieron como hacer santuarios interesantes y decidieron hacer puros copia y pega para llenar los 150. Por no mencionar que la mayoría de los santuarios son tutoriales para los artefactos zonnan o para gimmicks que nunca vas a volver a usar en el overworld como la pelota que hundes en el agua para que salga expulsada y active un interruptor. Otra gran parte son "bendiciones de Rauru" (santuarios sin puzzles), muchas veces cuando encontraba uno sentía alivio porque los puzzles me parecían trámites o eran tutoriales para usar artefactos zonnan que ya sé cómo funcionan, no es un cumplido a estos santuarios vacíos, es más una crítica a los normales. Muy pocos son interesantes o divertidos como las pruebas de combate, pero honestamente, botw lo hizo mucho mejor en la isla donde te quitan temporalmente tus pertenencias. Debieron ir por el camino de los santuarios del DLC de botw, esos mejoraron muchísimo.
Templos
Los templos nuevos son lo mismo que las bestias divinas pero con "skin de templos tradicionales" y con cosas zonnan en vez de sheikah. Los jefes están ok, no son los mejores de la saga (la reina gibdo y los phantom ganon me gustaron mucho; colgera, el octorok que tira fango y el gohma de roca la verdad no me gustaron sus combates, pero al menos son diferentes).
Sabios y artefactos zonnan.
La IA de las copias de los sabios es horrible, atacan muy lento a los enemigos, se te amontonan cuando estás recogiendo cosas haciendo que los actives por accidente y cuando quieres usar un poder se alejan de ti, por no hablar del golem de Mineru que es lo más incómodo e inútil del juego. Muchos artefactos son incómodos, por ejemplo los escudos fusionados con cañones, si caminas mientras fijas blanco dispara a todos lados menos al objetivo al que estás fijando y si te quedas quieto el enemigo ya está muy pegado a ti (porque oh sorpresa, a pesar de que requiere baterías no puedes decidir cuando disparar y pasa mucho tiempo entre cada disparo) y te explota en la cara. Pudieron añadir botones para disparar o avanzar cuando uses un vehículo, la moto hyliana era mil veces más satisfactoria de usar que los vehículos zonnan, además ¿para que construir tantas cosas complejas con ruedas, luces y cañones incontrolables que hacen poco daño y que gastan mucha energía? si por el mínimo costo de 9 zonnanios (2 ventiladores y 1 manubrio) ya puedes viajar a donde sea, el juego no premia la creatividad sino la eficiencia. 
Overworld. 
El cielo y sobretodo el subsuelo no son interesantes. Las islas son pura copia y pega, con cosas poco interesantes. El subsuelo solo sirve para farmear zonnanios, bombas, flores aturdidoras y hongos exhaladores, lo único que hay es contenido de amiibos reciclados, esquemas yiga o zonnan que nunca vamos a utilizar porque la moto voladora ya lo hace todo y campamentos de enemigos. Todo el subsuelo se ve exactamente igual, no hay variedad de animales o enemigos nuevos, es de lo peor del juego. Hyrule es la mejor zona de las tres pero le afecta mucho que vimos gran parte de él en breath of the wild.
UI. Y el peor punto es la interfaz de usuario es insufrible navegar por esos menús buscando los materiales que quieres
Es divertido el juego, sí (las primeras 20 horas cuando estás experimentando con los objetos y poderes nuevos al menos). No se siente como un DLC de botw pero sí muy repetitivo si jugaste el juego anterior

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom is a phenomenal sequel which fixed majority of the flaws that Breath of the Wild had. I much preferred going through the different Temples compared to the Divine Beasts as they all had their own unique atmosphere and vibe that wasn't able to be created within the Divine Beasts. The side quests within TOTK were also improved upon, by including Addison and helping him put up signs to helping Koroks find their friends (even if it included strapping them to a rocket). Fundamentally the game was better as well, with the abilities significantly improving on those in BOTW. Ultrahand, Recall and Ascend allowed for unlimited freedom on how to solve all the puzzles. Additionally I found TOTK's story to be more intriguing too, as it persuaded me to actually find all the geoglyphs and unlock all the memories. The ability to create your own vehicles also allowed for varied and more effective transportation, however unlike in BOTW I finally figured out how to use the horse properly. Overall, I think The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom is a MUST play game, and the definitive way to play a 'Breath of the Wild' style game on the Nintendo Switch.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
If you want a great adventure, Tears of the Kingdom is your game. This game is absolutely a whole experience, i had the chance to play Breath of the Wild when it came out a few years ago, and it was a masterpiece. I was afraid Tears of the Kingdom didn´t overcome the standard that BOTW created in it´s time, but it truly made it feel like a demo. The amount of creativity, passion and love in this game is seen in every minute detail, I´m still amazed that the development team made this whole game run on a Nintendo Switch. The narrative is not it´s strongest point though, they could´ve done it better in my opinion, but that´s the only "issue" the game might have besides a couple performance problems the game has due to the hardware (this only happening in the Nintendo Switch version). Those two little problems aren´t enough to overshadow the greatness of Tears of the Kingdom.
Finally, I was able to do the 100% of the game, and I can truly tell that it gave me 800 hours of pure fun, adventure and exploration.
If you have a Nintendo Switch, and the opportunity to play The Legend of Zelda, give Tears of the Kingdom the chance, you are not going to regret.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Tears of the Kingdom is a perfect sequel of Breath of the Wild. The game has wonderful combat, clothing, quests, and a bunch of more content around Hyrule. The story is a wonderful experience as Ganondorf is resurrected, and Link must defeat Ganondorf to save Princess Zelda as she's gone right back in time. Link and Zelda have grown closer as it seems they are taking their relations to the next and beyond. The mechanics like the fusion mechanic surely impressed me very including the successor of Magnesis, that being Ultrahand, which really helps the puzzle get done in time. Anyway, this was my full review of The Legend of Zelda Tears of the Kingdom, and if you read this review thank you

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: As a lifelong Zelda fan and with years of reflection after playing this is such a swing and miss. I was so excited for it to fix my gripes with BOTW - the top thing was an improved story and the lack of care Nintendo took in this was shocking. As someone who sorely misses the linear storytelling of the old games, as soon as I had the opportunity to find all the dragon tears I did and what ensued was a jumbled mess of storytelling with the ultimate sin being the discovery of where Zelda is. This all could've been attributed to my desire to have a more story driven experience but what was simply avoidable was that upon discovering this early on all the characters had no change in dialogue. Link knew where Zelda was yet all characters kept asking about her and why she was evil and the typical lore mystery that makes a Zelda game great was ****. This was so egregious I thought surely this was a bug that Nintendo would patch -- BUT IT HASN'T BEEN. Taking what could've been one of the best Zelda games into one I couldn't get myself to beat when getting all the way to Ganon. The complete disregard for the UX of the story baffles me and I long for the day that emulator models fix this narrative flaw. Also one of the top worst gaming experiences ever ensued when I fell for the incredibly long and redundant yiga clan depths  quest. The reward was abysmal and the quest itself was extremely boring. I had assumed this would heal the story in some way but it ultimately had nothing to do with it and again offered info that didn't matter or had already been discovered. I sincerely do not know what Nintendo was doing here. This game broke me and I truly hope the next game is a return to form. I know they didn't plan for DLC but I really wish they had a stripped down version and those who wanted more of the filler could've chose for it with DLC. There was simply no "legend" to this Zelda. And what they did include was self imploding almost immediately.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Peca pelo excesso em algumas coisas, como as profundezas, que apesar de ter relevância na história, é muito cansativo abrir todo o mapa para não ganhar nada em troca e no fim ser uma área que acaba sendo mais desinteressante que a superfície e o céu como áreas para se explorar. Pra ajudar, eu que morro de medo de jogar em áreas escuras, acabou sendo um dos motivos para não ir muito com a cara do jogo assim que o comecei.

A exploração das profundezas acabou me saturando rápido. Mas anos depois voltei agora para o jogo e fiz as pazes com ele e sim, usando cheats para evitar me saturar de novo com algumas mecânicas que não gostava.

O uso da tecnologia zonai apesar de ser criativíssimo e mudar muitas dinâmicas do jogo, puzzles, também uma hora acaba sendo muito chato ter que depender de equipamento, energia e ter de montar algo diferente a cada situação. Apesar de usar muito a criatividade do jogador, também me saturou. Com um cheat de energia infinita, isso se resolveu para mim.

Os puzzles de santuários são muito fracos. Os puzzles da superfície são muito mais interessantes.

Ganha muitos pontos ao incluir uma nova civilização (os zonai) que possuía muita habilidade com tecnologias avançadíssimas e ao avançar no tempo, utilizar de arqueologia, antropologia, escavações etc. para descobrirem o passado de Hyrule.
A história dos sábios que lutaram com Rauru (personagem FODA e gostossíssimo) para pararem Ganon. Mineru também é muito fodona, namoral.
Fora que é muito foda ver os personagens de BOTW crescidos e maiores!
A história de Zelda nesse é bem triste e melhor que o BOTW em que ela só fica choramingando pedindo pro Link a salvá-la, aqui a gente acompanha uma Zelda ativa, se fazendo de mártir por Hyrule.

Muito bom ver novos tipos de inimigos também.

O enredo é muito mais criativo que o primeiro e o final eu achei sensacional com a luta entre ps dragões Zelda e Ganon.

Por ter feito as pazes com ele, vou dar nota 8 e não o favoritar. BOTW foi uma surpresa enorme e o primeiro Zelda jogado e estará para sempre no meu coração.

30/11
Nota 8

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Nintendo correctly decided to evolve the physics-based gameplay of Breath of the Wild, and did so originally as an expansion pack, in lieu of a full sequel.

They then completely **** this idea up by instead making it a full sequel that entirely focused on this one mechanic that turned out to be rubbish anyway, whilst simulatenously giving us a sequel to one of the best games ever made by absolutely pissing all over it- even as far as ignoring that the first game ever happened (a sin already committed with Wind Waker's unskippable 5 minute opening cutscene 20 years prior that pissed on Ocarina of Time and the player's accomplishments).
What is new and present in TOTK is inherently interesting and dare I say fun, but the execution is so massively flawed that whatever magic the game holds is utterly marred by the focus on quantity-over-quality. I loved the first game to absolute pieces, but can't bring myself to ever play TOTK ever again. It's absolutely insane that this game took as much time as the original game despite recycling 70% of it. Easier said than done, but I think they should have focused on it as a sequel first and foremost, with the contraptions mechanic being added to in post-release updates. Downsizing the world and splitting the content equally between Sky, Land, and Underground would have been this game's biggest boon by far, and would have needed as much effort as copy-pasting literally every layer of it, which is pathetically what they did. The 100+ copy-pasted caves were also an abject mistake that I still cannot quite believe they did. For the amount of content and quality it does deliver, it is an astounding game almost beyond measure, but it's neither a game that any previous BOTW player has any business near, nor anyone looking to fully complete beyond the half-arsed story. The contraptions also effectively feel like their own game that were still tacked-on after the fact, and half of it flat-out doesn't work.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Tears of the Kingdom est la suite que Breath of the Wild méritait :
Plus ambitieux, plus créatif, plus généreux. 
On retrouve ce sentiment rare d’aventure totale, où chaque colline, chaque caverne, chaque îlot du ciel cache une histoire ou une idée brillante.

Liberté totale, créativité assumée

L’Ultrahand et les autres pouvoirs ne sont pas juste des gadgets : ils nous donnent une liberté de gameplay que presque aucun autre jeu n’ose offrir. 
Construire, expérimenter, détourner les mécaniques du jeu… On apprend sans cesse de nouvelles façons de jouer. 
Et ce n’est pas juste du fun : le jeu récompense véritablement l’imagination.

Un monde qui vit déjà… et qui évolue

Hyrule n’est pas une copie de BOTW avec du vernis. 
Le monde a changé, de nouvelles zones souterraines immenses et mystérieuses,
les îles célestes qui ajoutent une verticalité totalement folle et des PNJ qui réagissent à ce qui arrive au royaume.
On a l’impression de revisiter un lieu familier, mais en mutation permanente.
Une aventure qui ne s’essouffle presque jamais
L’écriture, les donjons, les boss, la musique : tout est mieux rythmé que dans BOTW. Chaque quête apporte un vrai moment marquant, et même après 100 heures, la sensation de découverte ne faiblit pas.

Verdict

Le jeu n’est pas parfait : visuellement, on sent que la Switch atteint ses limites. 
Mais malgré ça, TOTK offre une expérience d’une richesse et d’une inventivité monumentales. 
C’est le genre de jeu qui rappelle pourquoi on aime jouer : parce qu’on est libre, surpris, émerveillé.

Ma note 9 / 10
Un chef-d’œuvre audacieux et inventif, qui restera gravé longtemps.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Прошёл The legend of Zelda: tears of the kingdom 2023 года на эмуляторе ryujinx на пк. Выпустили очередную Зельду и опять все ей нахуярили девяток на всяких сайтах с оценками. И ведь в новой Зельде 0 графических улучшений по понятным причинам (свитч давно устарел), и карта та же что и в botw пусть и со значительными изменениями. Любая другая контора кроме Нинтендо выпусти она такой копипаст словила бы лютую волну негатива, но только не они, нинтендоёбам вообще на всё похуй, они скушают что угодно вообще. Об этом не принято говорить, но до ботвы каждая новая 3D Зельда преимущественно копия Окарины вплоть до ботвы. Ботва была по сути неким софт ребутом в серии, единственная часть которая отличалась настолько что не была копией предыдущей игры, но видимо теперь каждая часть Зельды будет копией ботвы.  В то же время, в игре очень много изменений, которые в отрыве от всего остального ну очень хороши. Новые механики реально пушка, очень хорошо встраиваются в геймплей и основу игры, головоломки завязанные на физике объектов топ. Боёвка осталась прежней, но на неё тоже влияют новые механики поэтому без претензий, кроме, пожалуй, казуальности, почти любой враг забивается в говно одной кнопкой если есть ресурсы. Сюжет такое же убогое дрочево и пережёвывание дерьма как и любая другая часть Зельды, просто взяли старых персонажей и нахрючили новый сюжет. Любая игра, где вместо диалогов всплывают иконки с текстом идёт нахуй, никаких оправданий этому быть не может это полный позор, даже на пс 2 это было постыдно, а сейчас и подавно. Несмотря на то что я поливаю игру дерьмом, она хорошая, атмосферная, красивая (пусть и не технологичная), местами великолепный геймдизайн, большой открытый мир который можно хрючить до посинения если вы фанат Тодда Говарда, но я убеждён – фанатов нинтендо кормят с лопаты, а они довольны потом что привыкли. Музыку вообще не меняли... Мой вердикт – 6/10. На эмуляторе работает хорошо, но не без проблем.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: A good follow-up, but it can’t quite recreate the impact of Breath of the Wild, which set the bar high. The expanded three-layer map — underground, surface, and sky — adds a clever twist to a world many players already knew well. Immersion remains top-tier, with incredible sound design and environmental detail. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
After so many years in development, the sandbox and creative system that was added.. was not enough to improve on the many issues I had with its prequel. Pretty much everything was perceived as perfect, and nothing was truly improved upon.. what a shame.

From more repetitive and dull tasks.. to the same world being re-used. It doesn't feel like this rethread of a successful product achieved anything worth praising.

When I realized I could create that "one bike" that made traversal obsolete (and horses for the most part), or launch miles into the sky to comb every pixel of the map.. my engagement disappeared. The old saying “players will optimize the fun out ****” remains true, because when something is the best option, why would you want to handicap yourself and waste time doing anything else? Especially when there's so little this glorified-DLC offered.

Everything I disliked about BotW is heightened here, which made the experience even worse as I held all those frustrations from start to finish. Good music, though!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: While I totally understand the lack of interest many will have, as I believe this to be the biggest deviation from traditional Zelda in the series history (even including most spin offs!) I found this to be either the best, or 2nd best entry in the franchise. The game really shines when you engage with it on its level rather then brute forcing simple solutions. The challengesare broad but specific enough for a broad range of player expression, allowing for really creative, rube goldberg like contraptions. Honestly had a blast abusing the quick save to hone in hyper specific, ridiculous “oh my gosh, i believe this is working” type creations work for combat, puzzles and exploration. Like any game, there are faults, however. The biggest is the performance problems, specifically in the intro with ultrahand in the sky islands which i hear the switch 2 version handles well (have not played yet). 2nd, after the 3-4 hour intro portion, the game sags hard on a tired “zelda is evil?!” plot point and a boring cutscene the game forces you to watch 4 times. I also think the ending proves that link really should be talking now, his lack of voice ruins the agency of him and just makes it a game whereZelda is the unplayable protagonist (at least link felt more incorporated doing this in twilight princess, midas story by making him actively manipulated-into-friends)

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
(Gameplay - 9/10):
This game's gameplay is truly unique, and is doing something no other game has done before. The combat is hugely customizable, allowing you to create literally anything. The closest thing that I can relate to this system is Minecraft's redstone. If you like creative gameplay, than this is a must play.

(Story - 3/10):
This is not a story game. But most people that play Zelda games already know this - this game's story is, however, worse than the other Zelda games. If you want to play a Zelda game with a good story, play Majora's Mask.

(Overall): If you have not played Breath of the Wild yet, don't play this game. It will be very overwhelming. This might not seem like a big deal, but the appeal of Breath of the Wild was its simplicity yet huge scale--this game does not have the same satisfying simplicity. This game also takes risks in its new mechanics, which will likely impact the entire industry, but overall, it is still unpolished.

Globalement un plutôt bon jeu. Cependant, il ne parvient pas à atteindre le niveau de son prédécesseur. Entre quêtes secondaires recyclées, map quasiment inchangée en surface, ciel très vide et souterrains paresseux, une impression générale de facilitése dégage de ce jeu. L'histoire ne nous surprend pas car très prévisible, sachant que le jeu vous offrira en permanence la possibilité de vous auto-spoiler avec un système de souvenirs qui marche moins bien que dans Breath of the Wild. Presque tous les sanctuaires peuvent être bypass assez facilement, et il en va de même pour les temples. Il y a aussi de bons points : une bande son magnifique, des cinématiques très bien réalisées et une DA sublime.

Finalement, j'ajouterai que le mieux est l'ennemi du bien. TotK ajoute du contenu dans tous les sens, mais il manque souvent d'utilité (voir le début de ma critique), ou bien est peu pratique à utiliser. Ce qui faisait la beauté de BotW et de son univers, c'était la pureté qui s'en dégageait. Ici, la pureté a disparu, et c'est bien dommage...

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: I like all Zelda games, and this one is no exception. But this one it's a bit difficult to review. Especially when you compare it to the predecessor game. The story is better and the gameplay is fun, but overall it feels almost the same. It's ok to reuse the same engine and world, but much of it is generic and dull. For example, the shrines are essentially identical, just with different assets. And what really annoyed me from the beginning were the constant modal popups when you pick something up, no matter how trivial it was. A simple notification would have been enough, with the option to view more details if needed. It just ends to button mashing to skip everything. Same with the shrines. A clear sign of poor UI/UX design. Some quests are also unnecessarily tedious. Instead of highlighting the location mentioned in the text, the game forces me to carefully read it. I also hope for complete voice acting in the next game. It would enhanced the experience and will work with this dialogue system, which other games have proven it. The worst part of the game are the breakable weapons and other items. And this even faster than in the previous game. And the Master Sword can't even be used to defeat a small mob because it breaks first. I understand the design, but it's just not fun. The Blood Moon event is also frustrating. It interrupts the gameplay and ruin your progress. A better design would have been respawning enemies outside your range without black screen fade. The game feels repetitive with lots of copy-paste content. Most treasure chests contain boring, useless stuff, even the hard to find ones feel unrewarding. The game forces you to heavy grind. Companions are an interesting idea, but in practice they're either in the way or too far to be helpful. I'd rather just have their abilities myself. Also, having to watch the same cutscenes from companions 4-5 times is a drag. There's a feature that highlights cave locations, which is great. But it still shows completed caves, which makes no sense. A lot of stuff just pads the playtime. And while I love spending time in this world, these kinds of issues stack up. At the end of the day, I do enjoy the game. But it carries over too many of the same flaws from its predecessor. I really miss traditional dungeons with meaningful item based progression. I'm confident the strengths of classic Zelda and modern design can be combined. I hope so for the next game. I wish I could give it a higher rating. Maybe a 8 or 9. But despite all the things it does right, the issues just weigh it down.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
"No fun allowed: The video game."

It's a step down from BOTW in every way. Everything about this game is tedious, gimmicky and unsatisfying. The sky adds nothing but more empty space, the underground is a big open bowl that constantly blocks your progress with giant walls, the story and world map are both rehashes of their predecessors, and the entire thing is a derivative asset flip with a first party price tag.

The garry's mod vehicles are gimmicks to the Nth degree, they're slow, awful to control and mandatory for most of the game. Want to build a plane to fly accross the map? Too bad, because the wing part will just vanish for no reason because no fun allowed.

Every single weapon you pick up has to have another weapon or a monster part glued onto it for it to do any damage at all, but of course weapons still break every 5 hits like in BOTW, meaning that you have to stop, drop and glue every 5 seconds to be able to contend with the many many damage sponge enemies.

The story is incredibly dumb even by nintendo standards, the flashbacks are even more annoying to find than the memories, and the sidequests feel like obligations rather than something the devs actually wanted to add. Nothing says "rewarding" like agonizingly making your way through a boring quest for 30 minutes to an hour, only to be rewarded with nothing but 100 rupees. You can get the same amount of money from breaking a rock.

It's nintendo first party sludge for diehard fanboys, plain and simple. Almost $100 for the same game, but worse. Oh, and it still runs like trash as well as the cherry on top.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This game is a bittersweet masterpiece, since while it is truly amazing and certainly a lot of fun, just thinking about how much more mind-blowing this game would have been as the first introduction to the BotW formula makes me feel regretful we didn't see all of these features and ideas in the original. This truly is a sequel which expands upon, improves, and doubles down on every design choice and feature of the original. Breath of the Wild was an incredible game but it mainly succeeded because of its exploration and brilliantly constructed open world. While it had fun combat and puzzle design, and a nice minimalist story which leaned on subtlety and environmental storytelling, these were not the strongest points of the game - they simply were good, while the world and exploration was great. 
Tears of the Kingdom feels like it knew this about its predecessor and revitalised and improved upon every aspect of the original. The combat is better, and there is more variety in moves, abilities, and enemy variety. The movement and traversal options have been expanded to a ludicrous degree. The puzzles and abilities are both vastly superior to the original. The dungeons are more inventive and unique from one another. The story is more elaborate and characters are more memorable. And the final boss is vastly superior to the original. Everything that was good in the first game is better in the second.
The only thing which has not changed as much is the world. Hyrule has had many subtle changes all across its landscape, and structures and settlements have changed dramatically. But it is still functionally the same world from the original. If you have played the oroginal as much as I have, then you know that there simply isnt as much to explore and discover in Hyrule this time around.
The first game had an atmosphere of discovery - sinking into a vast and ruined kingdom to uncover all sorts of fascinating experiences and characters and places. This was the beating heart of the game and the wanderlust of players is what drove them to explore the map.
This game has an atmosphere of rediscovery instead. Rather than exploring a world for the first time, you are revisiting a world that is very familiar to you and finding out everything which has changed over the years. The core of this exploration is more focused on tracking down leads and rumours about what crazy events have taken place all across the world, and investigating them at your own leisure. I do not mean to say that this style of exploration is bad in some way - I was enthralled by it for dozens of hours, writing down all the rumours I had heard from NPCs and all the interesting things I had seen in the distance that I wanted to uncover later. I tracked down all these leads and gradually made so many amazing discoveries. This sort of exploration is incredibly enjoyable and rewarding. BUT - I do prefer BotW's style. While there are some new areas that bring back that BotW feeling, namely exploring the sky islands and the depths, the islands are too few in number to really scratch that itch (I loved all of them, but they don't constitute a brand new map), and the depths lacked the same visual and functional variety as the different provinces in the overworld, making them less enjoyable to explore. It is in this way that I think, having played BotW so much, TotK just does not capture the same essence, rather it goes in a slightly different direction; one I enjoyed, but ultimately not as much as the first. 
But this game is also a bittersweet masterpiece for this exact reason. BotW was already a 10/10, but I cannot imagine how blown away I would have been if I had skipped it and played TotK blind. The entire world of Hyrule AND the Depths AND the Sky islands? I would lose my mind. No game would ever come close, and even if the world isn't as novel after BotW, the variety in this exploration and rediscovery makes the game's pacing so engaging and addictive. You can ride around the overworld for hours, then find a chasm and dive into the Depths, fighting minibosses and enemy camps until you're too burnt out, then ascend to the overworld and take a trip on a dragon to the Sky Islands, soaring around, solving puzzles, collecting fairies and treasure maps, so you can dive back to the depths to find where they lead, and go back to the overworld to ride to the next region. The game has a phenomenal loop of all sorts of incredible experiences.
I am upset a little that this game didn't have a brand new overworld like BotW, but I am by no means disappointed in this game. This game is a victory for Nintendo for proving that you can make a sequel to a boundary-breaking masterpiece without milking all the tried and true mechanics dry. This game surpasses the original in every way, while offering a different sort of exploration that is still equally enjoyable and satisfying. 
It is just in this last detail, that I slightly prefer BotW.

However, as I completed more dungeons, I was left disappointed. The evil Zelda thing was silly, as I knew she went into the past, so it had to be Ganon, but no matter what, every character didn't know Zelda was in the past, which was very unsatisfying. 

I also thought the sequel to BOTW would a co-op game with the tease showcasing Link and Zelda exploring,g only to find out Zelda gets pushed to the side again, and you have to save her again.

The mechanics are tedious too; you had to grind so much to get full batteries, and you couldn't store builds. you had to save it and then rebuild it using a valuable material that you would need to grind.

Additionally, the new heroes' abilities are less rewarding and super tedious than BOTW. I loved collecting the BOTW powers as they were super powerful and easy to access using the D-Pad. Now they all run around, and you have to interact with them mid-combat to activate their abilities which are mediocre at best or useless.

Overall, the game is good, if you enjoyed BOTW and wanted more this is definitely for you just keep in mind you might get annoyed at some changes they made especially to the boss dungeons and heroes abilities.

Review: It pains me so much that this Zelda is not a 10/10... Entirely my personal opinion, but I did not find this one nearly as enjoyable as botw. The cut-and-paste world became redundant, there were not enough different things in it. Also, the dialogue felt lazy and uninspired at times and the story was all over the place (in particular the memories did not work as effectively here as they did in botw). The ending really disappointed me too, like excuse me I thought Zelda could never return to her normal self? But hey lets just sprinkle some rando magic on her and BOOM shes all good again. My issue isn't that she went back to normal, its that the entire process seemed wayyyy too easy and rushed, like they could have given us a little quest at the end, sorta like an epilogue or something, showing Link and Impa figuring out what needs to be done and then Link doing it and getting her back... Can I also just emphasize the lacklustre relationship between Link and Zelda for a sec? I know this is a kids game, but she loves him goddamnit!! That was made official in botw or at least heavily implied, but she barely has anything to say to him when he gets her back?? Not even a hug?? Ughhh I just needed something more here, but catching her in the sky was pretty nice. Onto the good things - the building mechanic was awesome and the dungeons + bosses were a bit better (not you though water temple). Also, the enemy variety was massively improved in this one. I was so glad they brought back normal bombs too (even though I do love the remote ones). Riju my girl! She is such a queen, obsessed with her new design and just loved everything in general about her quest line. Final boss was phenomenal, Ganondorf really blew it out of the park with the epicness and the anxiety I felt when he started destroying my hearts LOL he was not playing around! I really liked how much they put into the game too, I was so overwhelmed with this game at first. Hiding the depths from game trailers was crazyy. I enjoyed exploring them, and the sky too. Also, getting to see familiar characters again made me smile so much. Just a shame that I can't put this game on the same pedestal as botw...I know so many people loved this one though so I still recommend it!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: If I had not played Breath of the Wild, this game would have been a 9 or maybe even 10 out of 10 game. However, I believe that this game, as fun and exciting as it is, does not live up as a "sequel" to its predecessor. This has nothing to do with the game's new mechanics or sandbox-style gameplay, which is every bit as fun, maybe even more so than Breath of the Wild. The wacky Zonai parts allow you to be so creative with building machines, and watching the creative builds people come up with online is so fascinating to me. The new abilities are also a welcome change from Breath of the Wild, with Recall being my absolute favorite to toy around with. The game is as pretty as always, with the Sky Islands being absolutely gorgeous, and the depts being so forboding and mysterious (at least for the first few minutes you're in there), and the music and sound design is the best in the series hands-down. My issues with the game come with the actual content of the game, like the quests, shrines, dungeons, and story, and the way it fits within the continuity of Breath of the Wild. For a game that takes place so far after the events of BOTW that the game describes Hyrule as "healing" over and over again, Tears of the Kingdom hardly changes the status quo. Many locations hardly change enough in the timeframe. I mean, Lurelin Village is overrun by "Pirates" (which is just a bunch of Bokoblins, thanks for getting my hopes up), and end of that questline just returns the village to the exact same way it was at the end of Breath of the Wild. Not to mention, the Shrines of Tears of the Kingdom are far inferior to what they were in Breath of the Wild. With the exception of the Proving Grounds shrines, there are far more tutorial shrines, chest shrines, and shrines that you can BS with a rocket shield. While you may consider navigating Tears of the Kingdom's challenges in your own way as "good game design," the failure of TOTK to incentivize you to engage with it leads me to believe otherwise. If they really wanted you to experiment with building things, then why the hell did they make have of the Zonai materials despawn after a certain amount of time? Truly baffling! The shrines, unfortunately, still all have unvaried interiors, and the new look is, in my opinion, much uglier than that of Breath of the Wild. The new areas to explore, the Depths and the Sky Islands, are absolutely disappointing as well. The Sky Islands are repetitive and mostly empty while the depths are exhausting to explore for more than 10 minutes at a time. Many of the Dungeons of the game aren't any better. With the exception of the Lightning temple (Gerudo Town once again being the standout area of the game), the dungeons provided little challenge, and the boss battle at the end barely set up any challenge at all. I never thought I would miss the samey interior of the Divine Beasts, but at least those puzzles were fun and interesting! I don't WANT to clear the fire temple by building a hoverbike, I want a challenge! Not to mention, the story was unbearable to sit through. Hearing the Sages recite the same speech after each dungeon was absolutely grating, and the time travel shenanigans just wasn't implemented well enough. Ganondorf has zero character motivation to do whatever he's doing in the game, the Zonai of the past do absolutely nothing different with the knowledge that they lost the Imprisoning War, and Zelda's sacrifice by turning into the Light Dragon changed absolutely nothing about the status quo in the end, which begs the question of why the story had to turn out that way at all. Was it just so they didn't have to give us Zelda as a companion like the teasers of the game led us to believe? Instead, we got the Sage abilities, which clutter up the screen, and constantly run away from you whenever you need them the most. I still had an overall positive experience with the game because the Story and Continuity were not the main focus of the game, but by the very virtue of it being set in the same Hyrule was BOTW (and costing 70 dollars) I couldn't help but wish for something far more substantial. Tears of the Kingdom always aims to deliver a spectacle at whatever opportunity it has, and I appreciate what they are trying to go for. It certainly had an impact on me the first time I saw it, but after giving this game some time to sit, you can so easily look past a lot of that illusion to see that the "improvements" it makes to Breath of the Wild are quite shallow. Still more replayable, in my opinion, but it's not as thought out as its predecessor.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: This game is overrated. It's mid at best. Yes, it has its fun moments but its questionable, and outright bad ones bring the game down to the point where the good moments are greatly overshadowed. Let's be honest. The depths ****. It's 80km^2 of the same copy-and-paste biome, fauna, and enemies all over with the occasional, sparsely placed structures like mines that don't really have anything interesting going on. Its design is the pinnacle of bad game design, resulting in a boring, tedious, and monotonous experience and gameplay loop. People saying that the depths are good are crazy, I just don't understand them at all. The same goes for the sky. It's mostly empty with copy-and-paste shrine puzzles. The biggest and most interesting part of the sky is ironically the tutorial island, but it's over quicker than one thinks. It sets the player's expectations on a misleading path, where one thinks they will see other sky islands like it later in the game, but behold, there are no other such places. The rest, again, are just isolated small, mostly copy-paste, islands with similar puzzles. It's so disappointing, considering the sky islands literally were the game's selling point. The ultra-hand mechanics are not thought out either. They allow for massive cheese in basically every puzzle and dungeon. It feels like I was cheesing more than actually doing the puzzles properly, and most puzzles outside of shrines in the game don't even require much interesting use of the ultra-hand mechanics anyway. It's overall just a non-thought-out gimmick. The shrines are terrible too. There are way too many tutorial and blessing shrines, way way too many. And the actual shrines are mostly boring and strange too, with way too much allowance for cheese, again. Back to the sky and depths, their lack of content does NOT help at all the fact that this game basically just copies BOTW's map. They added caves sure, but they're not that interesting considering the vast majority are the same; go in, break some rocks, find a frog, and get out. There are the occasional boss and shrine caves but they don't offer much variation either after you fight the same boss for the 10th time. They all look the same, play the same, and ultimately create again a boring, monotonous experience. What else have they added to the main map? Rocks! Copy and pasted everywhere. How interesting! And that's basically it aside from some minor changes here and there. It's all the same. The fact that the depths and the sky don't offer much intriguing discovery or exploration leads to this game heavily lacking in that aspect. It cannot stand on its own feet and leeches onto BOTW in order to seem "good" (it really isn't). It takes the same engine, map, assets, music, enemies, mechanics, and more and adds half-baked trash on top with just a tiny sprinkle of good. This game was in development for longer than its prequel yet it feels like they barely scratched the surface on making this a good overall stand-alone experience, especially considering that they already had the foundation with the engine, map, and mechanics. It feels more like a poorly made reimagining than an actual sequel, and the fact that you go to the same 4 exact places as in the first game doesn't help either. Don't get me started on the long copy-paste cutscene played 4 times. This game is weak, poorly made, and is overall a bad game by Nintendo. I expected way more from them, especially considering the development time, but here we are I guess And it's frustrating seeing how much praise this game gets when it does NOT deserve it at all, and Nintendo does NOT deserve their enormous earnings from it.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom is an exceptional game, though it closely mirrors its predecessor, Breath of the Wild. However, that’s not necessarily a flaw—why change a formula that was nearly perfect? The world is vast and highly immersive, with a wealth of mechanics that can easily captivate players for hours. I personally recommend, for both TOTK and BOTW, to avoid using online guides. Learning how the game’s intricate systems work on your own adds to the overall experience, and relying on guides can detract from the discovery process.While TOTK introduces some exciting new mechanics and an even more expansive and detailed world, there is one persistent issue that I find puzzling: the lack of a true endgame. Like BOTW, once you complete the main storyline, there's no open-world mode to freely explore or finish side quests. It would be wonderful if the world evolved after completing the final mission, but even without that, simply being able to continue the adventure post-credits would elevate this game to a perfect 10/10. Instead, players are forced to reload their last save before the final mission and avoid completing it to keep the experience going. This aspect significantly dampens the overall enjoyment, as you’re left with two choices: finish the game and lose the motivation to complete side quests, or never finish it at all and focus solely on everything but the main story.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Zelda nunca defrauda pero es que en esta ocasión se han superado. TOTK supone un punto de calidad que está al alcance de muy pocos. La experiencia de juego es indescriptible, cada uno va a tener una y va a desarrollar su historia de una forma diferente. 

El mundo está muchísimo más vivo que en BOTH y se nota en la cantidad de enemigos, la interacción entre ellos, los NPC que te encuentras, ... Además, puede parecer que Hyrule está igual que en su precuela pero no es así, todo ha cambiado y se ve distinta, a pesar de que las ubicaciones son las mismas. 

El sistema de combate es idéntico que en BOTW pero con una variedad de armas y combinaciones de estas con diferentes objetos que no existen horas suficientes para probarlas todas. Esto hace que su gameplay sea diferente cada vez que pruebas una combinación. Además, le da un plus de uso a las armas. 

En general es un juego único, con personalidad que hace que cada vez que quieras avanzar en el juego, te despistes y vayas a hacer otras cosas. Perderse nunca fue tan divertido y TOTK es claramente el juego que marca la diferencia en este aspecto. Es un indispensable si tienes la switch, muy recomendable probar antes la precuela BOTW.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
When this game came out all I saw on twitter and youtube were people talking about how this game was a solid 9/10 game, but not as good as insert game here.
I find it ridiculous that when a game (especially one as good as Totk) Comes out, we find each and every problem we have with it, and gloss over the actually good parts of the game.
"Totk isn't perfect" "Totk a solid 9/10" and "Totk is a missed opportunity"
Gamers please, shut your mouths. Tears of the Kingdom is an incredibly polished and incredible feat of Game design. You can see in Breath of the Wild and now in Totk that Nintendo's focus was to make a fun game. Not to make a 10/10 traditional Zelda, not to beat out the competition, but instead to make a fun video game. "If the games are not fun, why bother" -Reggie.
Here's a news flash. This game is fun, incredibly fun. The Ultra hand ability alone got players to sink hours into it just experimenting with what they could build with it.
But the best part is, is that there are 3 other abilities that are woven perfectly into Tears of the Kingdoms gameplay.
You're stuck in a large underground cave or want to scale a mountain or ledge, but don't want to spend time climbing it? Use Ascend and literally swim through the Terrain.
You accidentally dropped your vehicle or weapon off of the brand-new Sky Islands?
Use Recall, and with an enormous reach to have any object you want just go back to the same position it was in before it dropped.
Do you hate weapon durability and having your weapon break?
Use Fuse to create weapons with the very materials that broke your weapon in the first place. Additionally, use any and every material you have to create many unique arrow types that continue to further the combat.

Yes, Totk may not be perfect, but it's leagues ahead of game design than 90% of AAA games that come out.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The Legend of Zelda Tears of the Kingdoms (TOTK) est un jeu magnifique du point de vue graphique. Le jeu est beau pour la puissance que peut fournir la Switch. La direction artistique du jeu nous a fait encore des merveilles de choix qui peuvent en étonner.
  TOTK se dote également d'une bonne histoire. Au point où j'avais du mal à finir le jeu, de "peur" d'arrêter mon aventure. Le jeu a également des quêtes secondaires qui ne sont pas simplement FedEx avec un peu d'histoire et d'enjeu. Du tutoriel à la fin du jeu, l'histoire est très belle avec un ordre que l'on souhaite.
  Mais des tâches subsistent sur le jeu : pertes de FPS quand trop d'éléments sont affichés ou quand vous allez vite, contrôles difficiles si vous avez une petite manette, un peu de réutilisation et de recyclage par rapport à BOTW (Breath of the wild) et un 100 % qui n'est pas si logique. Cependant, c'est un point personnel qui m'a plus surpris, pour ne pas dire choquer. L'introduction de technologie. La licence de Zelda a été très peu sur ce terrain. Ici, l'introduction a été réussie. Mais le rapport n'est pas là.
  Finalement, l'effet de surprise n'est plus là comme sur BOTW mais pour TOTK, on retrouve tout de même un excellent jeu. Un peu dans l'ombre de son grand frère.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Why is the map here so similar to the original map? It pretty much ruins the exploration. There were not enough sky islands at all... and the depths are just a reskin of the surface, kept very dark so you don't notice how boring and empty it is. the story is genuinely horrible, I've watched SpongeBob episodes with a better plot than this game. and the dungeons in this game are pretty bad, though not as bad as in Breath of the Wild. This game also completely lacks an atmosphere of any kind. it evokes little to no emotion through a majority of the game

The good stuff? I like the enemy variety and combat, and I like the fuse mechanic a lot. Some of the puzzles are pretty decent, and the sand temple almost felt like an actual dungeon with fun stuff in it. almost. 

Ganondorf was a good villain, and his boss sequence is one of the best in the entire Zelda series. That said, this game was a massive, massive disappointment. Nintendo needs to set their next Zelda game in a very different world, with new exploration to be done. And hopefully, it might have a decent story and atmosphere to go along with it. 

I recommend playing this game if you've never played Breathe of the Wild, as then the exploration will feel fresh. Otherwise, play at your own risk

Review: Honestly, everything about this game exceeds BOTW. From quality of life changes to large scale map transformations, it is unlike anything else. BOTW was my second Zelda game I ever played, and I absolutely loved the adventure I had at that game along with the DLC. Now with TOTK, the game turned an already existing world into a fresher and new look, with a reworked surface world, the depths and the sky islands. Even revisiting old areas in BOTW seems to yield a quest of some sorts. And the world isn't the only thing I am praising here, the gameplay mechanics is probably what 50 percent convinced me to get the game.Just the idea of creating mass weapons of destruction, advanced vehicles, new movement ability, and time manipulation, it just amazed me. The amount of freedom you get here is immense. If you just got introduced to the Zelda series and BOTW was your first game. I recommend you try this.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Having played countless masterpieces over the past two decades, I can confidently say that this is the best video game ever made. While it's not entirely perfect, it stands out to me as the pinnacle of gaming for several reasons:

The game’s mechanics - allowing to build virtually anything your imagination can conjure, and the way these creations impact exploration, combat, and puzzles gave me a level of satisfaction that I’ve never experienced before. 

The exploration itself is incredibly rewarding. I found myself unable to leave any area of the depths or sky islands unexplored.

The story is compelling, complemented by a cast of rich, engaging side characters. Even the hundreds of secondary stories are fun and captivating, adding layers of depth to the overall narrative. 

The game’s scale is immense—probably the largest I’ve ever played—and yet, even after 150 hours, I’m far from completing all tasks or losing interest.

The art direction is simply breathtaking, one of the best soundtracks I’ve ever heard and outstanding visuals. I often found myself revisiting villages just to enjoy the music. 

Everything feels meticulously crafted, and the game is polished to perfection, a rarity in today’s gaming landscape.

My only wish is for improved performance. The occasional frame rate drops are hard to ignore, especially when compared to the 60fps 4K standard of most modern games. Despite this, it doesn’t diminish the game’s brilliance.

TOTK will go down in history as probably the best game ever created, and I feel it’s going to retain the throne for a long, long time.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: its still a masterpiece, but its not perfect. To start-the story.Nintendo sort of bragged in the trailers that tears would have a better story-but while still working fine for the game, its not as good as breath of the wilds's. Basically zelda has been captured by ganondorf, and ganondorf makes a fake zelda go around hyrule ruining her good name and causing chaos through misunderstandings. Zelda is actually stuck in the past, though, which replaces the memories. in BOTW, link had amnesia, and you got your memory back through collectables. this worked, cause you typically remember things out of order. The tears? not so much. Theres zero benefit to viewing zeldas journey in the past out of order, and it contributes nothing to the mainplot except its how you get the master sword, which if I remember correctly isn't necessary. The intro of totk is much worse than botw's however. Its the same structure-go to the 4 shrines to get your abilities-but much more linear than the great plateau. when you get your paraglider in botw,you get the feeling of "oh, the training wheels are off" in tears when you leave the great sky island, it feels like "thank f'ing god". the abilities themselves? they're equal to breath of the wild. the tear's abilities are more ambitious, and therefore it was more difficult to curate puzzles for them. So, they're equal. the open world? I feel they change enough to make it just as fun to explore. Maybe a new city would've been nice (and no, the lookout landing area where you first land isn't a city). where I think Tears outdoes botw is the dungeons. Yeah, it just activates 5 thingamajigs again, but the dungeons are larger and more expansive, and they look different visually. the bosses are an improvement too, but I didn't hate the blights or the divine beasts. the abilities you get from the dungeons are helpful at first but later get in the way. I feel like the partner skills would've been more helpful in the little ability wheel- you're telling me they put amiibo there but not tulin? Overall, still really good. another must-play if you like good games, but play botw first if you haven't.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: For the most part it's kind of entertaining but that's it, it's just entertaining. There's so much to do but the stuff that you're actually doing feels kinda superficial. I notice my brain switches off while playing, the same way it does while watching stuff like tiktok or other short form media because all the things you do in this game seem like short bursts of random things to that don't really amount to anything, you don't feel like you're progressing towards an overarching goal like you do in other Zelda games, you're just fulfilling what the game has to offer for the sake of it, for that little bit of dopamine you get after completing a shrine or what ever copy paste things you can find in the world. And the parts of the game that are supposed to progress the story, the dungeons, just feel lazily tacked on. They don't really feel part of the world they're in other than the fire temple and the lightning temple. You don't get that feeling slowly unraveling a dungeon that feels rewarding when you beat it, instead all you have to do it walk up to the terminal things which are marked on your map and that's it. It feels kinda naff. And on top of that the cutscenes after are so lame. I've never seen something so cheesy. It just kinda feels like it doesn't take itself seriously, which is upsetting because that's not what I liked Zelda for when I was younger. It doesn't even feel like a Zelda game, just an open world type thing vaguely trying to disguise itself as a zelda game.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Everything *Breath of the Wild* did fantastically is still present here but not expanded upon. Five years for a glorified DLC and a $70 price tag is insane. They didn't fix any of the issues with *Breath of the Wild*, mainly the dungeons. While the dungeons have been improved upon, they are still weak in the grand scheme of Zelda dungeons.

The world being recycled is fine, I guess. The underworld is cool until you realize they copied the map, inverted the Y-axis, painted it black, spammed annoying enemies around, and added roots. There are good aspects to the depths, like the little built areas that are cool, and the cosmetics have been replaced from paid microtransactions (Amiibos) to in-game drops. The sky is boring and repetitive. Really, the only redeeming factor of this game is the building, which is fantastic, don't get me wrong, but it's just fun factor. The story, dungeons, environments, and bosses are barely different from *Breath of the Wild*. It's an alright game, but *Breath of the Wild* was groundbreaking. A $70 DLC is kind of ridiculous. If you enjoyed *Breath of the Wild*, you will like this, but personally, I'm already tired of the new formula and a game that was originally meant to be a DLC isn't really for me. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Overall, the game truly is great and ambitious. It's a miracle this game runs on the switch considering how intricate the mechanics are and how much the hardware is being pushed to its absolute limits. In most ways in fact, Tears of the Kingdom improves on Breath of the Wild in almost every way. I enjoyed the story more, the problem solving is quite creative, and there's lots of technical quality of life improvements in terms of inventory management, cooking and recipes, balancing, classic dungeon structures with a more directed narrative and focus. There are however some issues. First, my favorite part of Breath of the Wild were the shrines; bite-sized and simple mental exercises that were short and enjoyable. In Tears, the shrines were my most hated and frustrating aspect. They were simply too difficult to figure out on my own I had to look up a guide after an hour of experimenting only to say "oh that's how you do it, yeah I never would've thought to do that". In those moments, I felt like I've been cheated of my time. Especially since you only get 1 blessing of light. The new mechanics and tools in this game are quite genius but how they are implemented can be very awkward to execute. I'll also mention that core aspects of the janky combat and controls remain completely unchanged from Breath of the Wild which is an obvious area of potential improvement. 

Overall however, the game really does succeed in important ways that make it worth experiencing.
