Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Hiya folks, welcome to this week's episode of "way too late reviews", where I'll be reviewing The Legend of Zelda : Tears of the Kingdom, the sequel to the legally distinct 2017 game, Breath of the Wild. There are rocks in the sky now! Seriously though, it does feel different. There are improvements, for sure. New monster types are cool, bokoblins wearing armour is cool, fusing stuff is cool, ultrahand is cool, coolcoolcool. I have some minor gripes about these things, but for the most part, the game builds on BotW with success. But there's a lot of stuff that annoys me. The intro ****. BotW's Great Plateau was a great tutorial section, it gave players a shocking amount of freedom while teaching the basics, and I just don't think the Great Sky Island works nearly as well. The sky islands don't allow that kind of freedom, and it feels restrictive. At some point I was kinda stuck, and figured I should just warp back to a different point to take a different path, but the warp ability is locked until later. Why? It's harder to navigate the islands than the plateau, and BotW has the teleport ability available eariler. Finally, I leave the islands, get back to the ground below, and I got no map. Clearly there's going to be towers, but I don't see them. Sure, Purah will tell me, but I have to spend another 10 minutes walking around talking to people before I get to check it out. Now Purah gives me the paraglider so I can be shot up into the sky from a tower to get the local map info, which is cool. But at the same time, the game doesn't really incentivize the type of exploration that made the first game so fun. The shrines are harder to see, instead of glowing a bright orange they're surrounded by this greenish mist that doesn't pop at all. I used to spend a few minutes at the top of a tower scoping the area for bright spots. Now, I jump into the air and try to pick a destination within a few seconds. Once I've hit one of these targets, I would usually end up teleporting back to the tower to start the cycle over again. I don't have a sensor, I can't see any shrines, I don't have any armour worth mentioning, I'm low on weapons, just going off isn't viable. I never felt like walking aimlessly like I did in BotW. Walking aimlessly sounds bad, but BotW actually made it good. Now, the loop of catapulting high into the sky and paragliding over to a shrine doesn't promote that relaxing, interesting, secret-discovering walking that was central to BotW. And I get it, it can't be the same as in BotW, but this new paradigm of travel rarely produces that feeling of wonder that BotW seemed to be able to dole out with such consistency: seeing a Divine Beast for the first time; catching my first glimpse of a dragon; climbing the Akkala citadel; seeing a goddamn bear. That's a hard act to follow, and I don't want to be disingenuous. But I gotta callz'em like I seez'em, and I kept seeing a game that prevented me from doing what I wanted to do. Where's my shrine sensor? I got to this tower, and it didn't work. Gotta make some porridge before buying stealth armour. A Hyrule-sized map of the Typhlo ruins (the Depths) isn't my idea of fun. Caves almost all feel and look the same. The memories don't force me discover the world like they did in BotW. Spears are OP now with fusion, and 2-handed weapons kinda ****. I don't care about Bubbulfrogs. The sky islands look cool until you've seen the same one five times. Shrine rewards are garbage, I don't want a large battery. Speaking of armour, I'm 50 hours in, where are my upgrades? I had to check a guide to activate a fairy fountain, and I needed to do 4 (FOUR!) quests to see 1 (ONE!) fairy. AND THEN I GET CHARGED TO UPGRADE!? Preposterous! Scandalous! Ignominious! In a game where random exploration should be enjoyable, why would I want to get bogged down with these restrictive quests? Why do I have to do THIS specific Main Quest event to get access to fairies? Why am I being punished for doing them out of order? BotW didn't have this, this, this video game equivalent of c*ckblocking. Why are there so many item types? Why do I need 75 pieces of armour if I only use like 5 different sets? Why can't I just put on a whole set at a time yet? Why does enemy damage seem way out of whack? Why do I need colour-specific enemy drops for upgrade when I have 75 armour parts to upgrade? I haven't seen a red Lynel in about 40 hours, how am I supposed to find its specific parts? Why are enemy horns in the codex but not fangs? Why can't I fuse items to my weapons or shields in the menu? Why can't I scroll through the menu with the right stick anymore? Why do the avatars ****? WHY WHY WHY WHYYYYY I just don't really want to return to it. I'm done with it. It's obviously not a bad game, but ultimately I gotta tell Mari Kondo that BotW sparks joy, and TotK does not.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
As a lover of storytelling in all of its forms, I was expecting a lot more from this, which isn’t that crazy of an expectation considering this was a sequel that already had the map and characters laid down for it, but also one of the longest to produce Zelda games. This review will only contain story, as few people seem to talk about it compared to the gameplay itself.

While BOTW’s story wasn’t groundbreaking, it focused on the somber moments and was a lot more personal to Zelda as a character. It had environmental storytelling that added to the established story, characters that, while not deeply explored, were distinct and memorable, and certain mysteries were created specifically for this world.

The environmental storytelling isn’t even something I can recall in TOTK, the characters you met in BOTW no longer remember you and the new ones they introduce are either completely devoid of anything interesting or resolve their (relatively pointless) character arcs in 2 minutes, and no mysteries from BOTW are answered, with some built upon further and creating more questions.

Most of the memories consist of a couple characters standing around recounting the same boring information over and over, practically only existing so Zelda can have a forced flashback in a later memory. Other cutscenes are quite literally copy and paste for the temples, and the rest of the main quest story is pretending to not know the answer to where Zelda is, which immediately becomes frustrating to watch, only becoming worse the further down the main quest you go and the more memories you get that make it painfully obvious that she’s in a different time.

I will ignore the annoyance I get from just the mention of „zonai” because of the fanbase, and will say that any mystery surrounding them is gone, not because anything was answered or elaborated, but because the Zelda team decided to make them yet another ancient tech society, completely ignoring the aesthetics they created for them in BOTW and the whole „barbaric magic wielders” information they gave us, instead making strange places like thyphlo ruins actually be the work of hylians… for some reason. 

This wouldn’t be that big of a problem if they actually made these different interpretations of zonai interesting, but they only leave 2 characters behind and some vague info of the rest having died off. No insight into how or why, or what their society was like, or what the ‚secret’ stones are, or in what way they’re a secret when multiple characters have them and the main villain knows of their existence and how they work.

Speaking of the villain, after 16 long years since Ganondorf’s last appearance, it’s safe to say he’s gotten worse. No motive, no backstory, no character traits, no screentime. I’m not talking about making him redeemable, i’m talking about making a villain that grabs your attention, and makes you WANT to defeat him for the umpteenth time. But no, none of that here. The closest thing he has to something interesting is killing a woman on screen and turning into a dragon. His plans make no sense (how would moldugas do anything on solid ground to a fortified and raised structure?), and the only reason he succeeds is because the other characters are even dumber than he is (why did the bearer of the triforce of WISDOM think meeting him with the queen alone at night was a good idea???)

Mysteries like the 8th heroine are added onto, but end right as they get interesting, with 0 crumbs scattered in the world for the player to find and come up with their own conclusions. And new mysteries are created with some pretty big implications that aren’t and most likely won’t be explored further, like the game implying that the 3 dragons were once zonai, or that the ancient hero looked… like whatever it looks like, with visual similarities closer to a zonai and ganondorf than link.

Sometimes I rewatch the initial reveal teaser, and wondering what they had in mind when they made it. Ganondorf sported a different design, more reminiscent of his OOT days, murals on the wall depict a battle that never takes place, the outside of the imprisoning chamber has the old zonai designs on it, the dondon was rideable, there were no secret stones… it almost feels like major portions of the story were scrapped, and I think that could explain the disappointment despite the long development time, because I highly doubt all those years went solely to creating the physics engine. This game is not 6 years worth of story in quality nor quantity, and for a lot of people it isn’t in gameplay either.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
If you experience this game without having played any others in the Zelda series, you could be forgiven for saying that this is a satisfying game. However, there is little that this game has on its own merit. It is mostly a copy and paste of its predecessor, Breath of the Wild, with much less charm and ingenuity. This game is a sequel, but only in its blatant reuse of assets and characters from the other game. The gameplay is very clunky and takes several steps backwards from its predecessor in an attempt to add new content. If you want to spend tons of time in menus searching for items, this may be your game. The puzzles are far too easy, and the combat is an absolute drag. The additions of new abilities would make combat more enjoyable, if not for the aforementioned menu clunkiness.
The worst offender is the story. Using one of gaming's most iconic villains turns out to be more of a cash grab, as he provides little to no substance to the game. He turns out to be just a generic powerhungry villain with no development or compelling motivations. The story is told in a way that insults the player by calling you stupid. There are many repeats of npcs telling the player the same story events over and over. Since this is a spoiler free review, I won't go into details, but I could probably sumarize the story in two sentences. In addition, this story is not only disconnected from the canon of the series, but it also insults anyone who thinks it might be connected. As a long time fan of the Zelda series, I saw many points where there was potential for connections to the rest of the series. However, every single one of these ended up being a retcon or a dissatisfyingly oversimplified explanation. In other words, this game rejects previous entries in the series, while using content and ideas from other games as a form of fan service. All of this was done in pursuit of a story that wasn't even compelling, and seemed to just be in place as a filler.

To be fair, I did enjoy some of the creative mechanics of the game. Building vehicles and weapons was fun, but even those unique aspects soured after long enough. As a player, there was little to motivate me to utilize these aspects of gameplay to their fullest potential. I also somewhat enjoyed the addition of the underworld-like area known as the depths, but this also eventually became boring after a couple hours.

In short, this game is a big waste of time. The gameplay loop becomes very repetitive only partway into your playthrough. The story is overly simplified, poorly presented, and does not connect to the greater lore of the series (but to the contrary it demeans and denies the other games, even as a supposed "sequel"). If you are looking to pick this game up, I would encourage you to look at other titles in the series, which deliver better on almost every aspect.

Review: The legend of Zelda: Tears of the kingdom is a great, beautiful and exciting adventure for 100+ hours, the game is really good, and it undoubtedly has many, though not revolutionary, but excellent game design **** comparison with the previous part of the series, this game has more interesting abilities, for the most part being improved abilities from Botw. I even missed 3 or 4 stables, although in the previous part they were points of interest, which it was difficult not to get into. After 60 hours, you begin to realize that the game was deliberately stretched, without offering anything new in return. For comparison, I completed the game in 130 hours, that is, for about 70 hours I was bored playing Zelda. I think that Nintendo should move away from the canons of Botw and Totk in the next part, because this model has already outlived its usefulness.Despite all the disadvantages, I'm betting 87/100 on this game. She is still beautiful, though not without significant flaws.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Ok, hot take considering I rated Breath of the Wild significantly lower. However, Tears of the Kingdom actual tics off most of the boxes. It has actual music this time, you can build stuff, the paraglider is costomizeable. Nintendo really built off of the failure that was Breath of the Wild.

The depths in my opinion was the best place to explore. I'd wager most my time exploring was either in the depths or exploring the improved map. Yes, the map is the same but there is far more places and things to explore this time around. And you have monster hordes you can fight too. As well as different enemy types.

I generally enjoyed exploring the caves as well but this game isn't all sunshine and rainbows.Some issues from before still linger. While Hyrule's society has begun to rebuild the story still suffers from the same memory system that Breath of the Wild used.

Also temples/dungeons are just tailored to look like traditional dungeons while the actual temple/dungeon retains the same activate the terminal concept in Breath of the Wild. I will cut Breath of the Wild some slack with the terminal activating because well we are inside a Divine Beast, a machine.

But here we had the potential for an actual dungeon/temple experience in a modern Zelda game. The bosses were fun but they felt more like rewards for sticking through the borefest that is activating the terminals.

And, of course, another big gripe. There is only ONE save state. Zelda games prior had at least two to three save states. No one wants to restart and lose all that progress just for another letsplay and I can assure you it's annoying to create another switch profile just to replay the game.

Breath of the Wild subjected itself to being a tech demo so Tears of the Kingdom could be something. But even then, Nintendo couldn't find that balance. And now, I fear for the next new Zelda game. Tears of the Kingdom had serious potential, but Nintendo just couldn't unlock that potential to its fullest.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: This game is amazing. The combat is fun and the enemies, the normal ones and the bosses, are very creative. It has epic moments and the final boss fight is perfect in it’s difficulty. The new abilities are fun, especially autobuild and fuse. The dungeons are way more fun than the one it’s prequel had. The controls are perfect and not difficult to master. I like Link’s new look with his long luxurious hair and Zelda’s new look with short hair. The world is massive, you can get lost in the tutorial area alone. When you think you have seen everything, you always stumble on something fun, creative or just awesome. The story is nothing special, but enough for an open world rpg. Something that I personally don’t like is that the characters have little to no personality in this game, except for, weird enough, the main villain Ganondorf and some random npc’s. I know Nintendo wanted to make Link silent so the player feels more connected with him, but this doesn’t work for me at all. I can’t feel connected with a long haired elf guy. And they could have given at least the other characters like Zelda some more personality. This game had everything Breath of the Wild had. Ironically, this makes the game a lot worse. Another thing that makes the game just not perfect is the fact that it looks a lot like it’s prequel Breath of the Wild. Don’t get me wrong, I’ve played both and both are amazing games, but I don’t feel like exploring the whole overworld another time, it’s kind of the same. I know there is another world under Hyrule, the Depths, but this underworld is emptier than my love life. There are also Sky Islands, and these are very fun to explore with lots of extra side quests, but after a while they all look the same. I am very disappointed there isn’t coming a dlc. I think you could add plenty of things to the game, like new armour with references to older games, or just some extra side quests. But if you haven’t played Breath of the Wild, you probably won’t have any issues with it. For that reason, it feels unfair to give this game a lower rating than its prequal, because it is technically a better game. Overall, this game is amazing and a must-buy for everyone, especially for someone who enjoys open world rpg’s (like me). 9,7/10

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I loved Breath of the Wild but this sequel was the most overrated and disappointing game I have ever played. Halfway through I really just wanted the game to end but kept playing and regret it. Maybe you have to be a minecraft type player to enjoy this game and I am not. I found the building system, while technically impressive to be tedious and it's the main selling point. Another selling point, the sky islands are underwhelming. They're just shrine puzzles basically and there's not enough of them. There needs to be some cool lore up there or something. The depths are also uninteresting. There really isn't much to do down there and again there is basically no lore or story there.

The story is bad. Due to the non-linearity of the game, every dungeon repeats the same story beats. It feels like you can play the game for hours and hardly progress. If you find the tears early and know the story it also makes it frustrating because you know what is going on but the characters don't and keep talking about it and Link just stands there not saying he already knows or ever even emote anything. 

The dungeons are a joke. Getting to them was sometimes fun but the dungeon itself and the dungeon boss was usually so easy it felt like a joke. Using the sage abilities is so annoying it makes them useless. 
Combat is ok. Enemies seem like they're able to one hit you too much but since you can pause anytime and eat food it is not too difficult.

Exploration is key to open world games and a big reason why I loved BotW but here it is not good. In BotW I would climb to high points to see shrines and glide to places but in TotK you can just fast travel to a tower which shoots you up in the air and glide to where ever you need to go. Many shrines are hidden in caves which make them harder to find but the result was me just not looking for them as much. The shrine puzzles are usually kind of straight forward because the building system and materials the shrine gives you makes it obvious what you need to build. Rewards for basically doing anything are never good enough.

The fuse ability actually makes weapons breaking worse. In BotW you can just pick up another weapon and start using it. But in TotK weapons are basically useless until you fuse something to it. So you have to go into the menu, select something, drop it on flat ground so it doesn't roll away, equip the weapon, select fuse ability, and finally use fuse. How do people think that is good or fun? There is way too much time spent in menus generally,  whether is eating food or selecting an item to fuse to your arrow among the thousand items you have in the menu. 

The other abilities are ok but I often forgot they even existed unless a shrine required me to use them. 

I don't think the professional critics spent enough time in the game to realize how tedious and repetitive the game is. I genuinely do not understand how this game has such high reviews.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Just how Breath of the Wild set a new standard for exploration, Tears of the Kingdom sets a new standard for freedom to do whatever you want. The devs realized that CHEATING IS FUN, because it makes the player feel like they've done something nobody else could, which is to cheat the system. Nintendo identifies and manages to inject this feeling into the game by giving the player inmense freedom to do things in their own order, and in any way they want: There's never a single way to solve a puzzle.

This thesis, in which the game heavily relies upon, is what makes Tears of the Kingdom FUN.

Still, however, the game keeps the charm of the original BOTW and manages to improve most of its features, like, for example, the durability of weapons.

TOTK doesn't come without its flaws, though. Some are the following:
- Lots of menuing, specially when firing fused arrows
- Lack of sky content outside of a few islands
- Depths feel dull and boring, as not much goes on down there
- That praised feeling of traveling to new locations in BOTW is lost
- Would've been nice to give Link some slightly new moves to make the game stand out and feel more agile.

Overall, it's a solid 9/10 just because of its thesis. Story is ok.
Also just a nitpick but the main theme was SO GOOD yet it was never used in the actual game, where they could've used it in a climactic moment in the story :(

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom is by far one of the best games in the series, of the year 2023. It brings so many new things that its big brother (Breath of the Wild) is a draft next to it.

From a narrative point of view, it's good. Years after Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom follows Link and Zelda exploring a cavern beneath Hyrule Castle where they encounter gloom seeping out causing sickness. They uncover a mural depicting Hyrule's history and awaken a mummy, leading to Link losing his arm and the Master Sword being broken into pieces. They embark on a journey to defeat the Demon King Ganondorf.Link learns of Zelda's fate with help from Mineru, ancient sages, and Dragon's Tears. Zelda was transported to the past by a secret stone. After Ganondorf killed Sonia and became Demon King, Rauru appointed sages to battle him. Zelda underwent draconification to aid Link in defeating Ganondorf, with the help of allies and ancient spirits. Mineru bids farewell as sages vow to protect Hyrule.

From an environmental point of view, it's quite mixed. The kingdom of Hyrule has changed a lot. Strange sky ruins appeared, as chasms formed, leading to the Depths. The Surface has changed a lot with all the ruins that have fallen, and which have changed the typography of the world. The Sky Islands are very good, with good ideas, but it would have been necessary to add at least thirty, even forty more. The Depths are a reverse copy of the Surface, the atmosphere is excellent, but I would have liked to have more side quests (there is only one unfortunately) and main quests (3 out of 22 is not not many (I would have liked to have four more)). TotK lives in the shadow of its big brother: it's unfortunate.

Bestiary side: they have improved a little. The bosses are incredible (special mention to Ganondorf who is very difficult and the best final boss of all Zelda games combined). But where are the Darknuts?

As for the temples, people criticize that it's too short (it's true) and some say that they're not even "temples". But need I remind you of the definition of this term (not to be confused with "dungeon")? According to Wikipedia: "A temple is a place of worship, a building used for spiritual rituals and activities such as prayer and sacrifice. By convention, the specially built places of worship of some religions are commonly called "temple" in English, while those of other religions are not, even though they fulfill very similar functions", whereas a dungeon is "a room or cell in which prisoners are held, especially underground. Dungeons are generally associated with medieval castles, though their association with torture probably derives more from the Renaissance period." In the TotK case, the temples ARE temples. A temple is visited in 25 or 30 minutes, not in 90 minutes! They're a place without many traps and many enemies! The Wind Temple was ok, the Fire Temple is, according to Captain Burgerson, a "cheese factor" (i agree), the Water Temple is underwhelming (but its architecture is beautiful), the Lightning Temple is perfect and the Spirit Temple (with the Construct Factory) is also ok. These temples serve the same purpose: to remember figures of the past (deities). In other Zelda games, dungeons are only used to place enemies in rooms (even if the lore is interesting) and do not focus on deities (some exceptions though).

As for characters, it's good. As for miscellaneous things, it's ok. The shrines in this game are so cool, but the Koroks are very uninteresting.

A 9 out of 10 is excellent: I wish the next Zelda game will be an open-world game with many dungeons or temples like the old ones, but with more variety.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
After more than sixty hours, I'm sad to say that Tears of the Kingdom is an overall disappointment. To be fair, the core gameplay from Breath of the Wild remains strong enough to keep the game engaging and enjoyable. And the two new additions of the Sky and Depths help make the world feel somewhat fresh. 

But ultimately, Tears fails to surpass Breath of the Wild in a few critical ways, most notably the story. The plot of Tears only gets worse the more I think about it, with lazy copy-paste cutscenes, a laughably underdeveloped villain in Ganondorf, and an overall failure to make us care about anything that's happening. The decision to tell Zelda's story through disconnected "memories" only ended up spoiling major moments and robbing the main story of any tension. Link not even smiling when he rescues Zelda was the final slap in the face in a story that is somehow worse than the barebones Breath of the Wild story. Not to mention the totally unexplained disappearence of all Sheikah technology!

Finally, the new building mechanics, while kind of cool, felt overused and forced; there was no reason not to use your horse to ride everywhere unless the game actively made you use the Zonai stuff.

Ultimately, Tears of the Kingdom is a good open world game with some cool setpieces, but in the grand scheme of the storied Zelda franchise, it's sorely lacking. Most importantly, Nintendo needs to hire some better writers, because their flagship action-adventure franchise cannot be having worse storytelling than Mario.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This Is the best single player game I’ve ever played. The moment to moment gameplay is so much fun, the tools at your disposal make traversal extremely entertaining and the game is HUGE. 

Every time you find yourself thinking “I wonder if I can…” the answer is almost always “yes.”

Link’s new abilities are all useful and fun, and they offer up many ways to solve puzzles and interact with the world. The controls are accessible enough for anyone to pick up, while offering enough complexity to be creative and style on enemies during combat.

The difficulty can be whatever you want it to be, at least in the later portions of the game. As you unlock armour upgrades you’ll start to take less damage, and you can do as many shrines as you feel like to get to a power level you’re comfortable with, or go all out and trivialise the difficulty. There is an annoying tendency to get one-shot early into the game though before you’ve progressed Link’s vitality or armour.

The story of TotK is surprisingly strong and I found it to be engaging enough to propel me through the main quest even when every five steps something else caught my eye.

The music on offer here is also great, although mostly there to provide ambience. Sound design is equally good, though I’m not a huge fan of some oft repeated cues (opening map, picking up items). 

Minor nitpicks such as clunky cooking or high enemy damage early in the game are absolutely dwarfed by the sheer joy I experienced just about every moment playing this game. 

My first play-through of TotK took 215 hours to roll credits, and I had so much fun I ran it back straight away, clocking in another 150 hours.

Should you buy a Switch just to play this game? Yes. Yes you should.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Tears of the Kingdom is Breath of the Wild again at its core. It reuses the same overworld, the same music (with some new ones), characters, the concepts of shrines, koroks, everything. Weapon degradation is still a thing, though Fuse sort of makes weapons more durable, in over 100 hours of gameplay I never felt that. 

But the main attractions are the sandboxing in-game powers of Ultrahand and Fuse.

They are technically very impressive, and they work near perfectly on an aging Nintendo Switch system. For those who love the creative and experimental aspect, these are phenomenal. 

However if you don't, Ultrahand and Fuse can prove to be tedious and punishing to use. Very rarely in the game do you actually need to use them to its full potential, and in the overworld and puzzle solving in shrines and dungeons, the solutions to them are often incredibly easy and frankly boring. 

Though it's possible to be very creative in making a contraption with Ultrahand to go through an obstacle for ex., what's the purpose of doing all that when there's no reward for doing so?

As for the rest of the game, while it has more enemies, more things to do with the welcome addition of caves, sky islands and the depths, the game inherits make of the same issues as Breath of the Wild, in the way that so many of its content are copy and pasted all over the map.

The depth are especially a huge disappointment. At first, I was blown away by the sheer size, mystery and darkness. That is until you explore the thing and realise there's very little to do and it always has the same biome. The rewards for being there are either cosmetic or Yiga Schematics which is only interesting if you love Ultrahand.

It's a very monotonous game and if you played the first 15 hours, you've basically seen what the entire has to offer.

The main story has an advantage over BotW in that it has a mystery and intrigue, while it was very barebones in the previous. The problem is that these mysteries cannot be sustained in a game as open-ended as this.

The dragon's tears side quest reuses the same "memories" system as BotW. The problem is that the story told through them is fundamentally linear. It is truly absurd that the game lets you even see them out of order, and ruin the story that way.

It is also disappointing that once again the most interesting cutscenes and story beats are in the "Dragon's Tears" which have happened 10000 years ago, creating a major disconnect. You only experience the story passively, which creates a lack of urgency. 

And what do you get in the present-day story as Link? The same thing as BotW where you complete 4 dungeons in any order. But the mysteries around them are all caused by a fake Zelda, in which the inhabitants aren't aware. It's obvious from the start that she's an imposter, so having the characters surprised everytime imposter Zelda does something bad is pretty stupid. 

And then there's probably the laziest, most embarrassing thing the Zelda team has done in its history. At the end of each dungeon, you get cutscene with a faceless, nameless sage explaining the events of the "Imprisoning War"… FOUR TIMES. There are no variations in its presentation, there's nothing NEW being told regarding the story or the lore. There's no justification for these, they could have done different cutscenes pertaining to what dungeons you've done, but no, they went for the laziest implementation possible.

We'll end with dungeons. For fans of dungeons in older Zelda games, prepare to be disappointed. While they're superficially better than in BotW due to them having different themes, the use of the "4/5 terminals in any order" bogs them down.

In older Zelda games, dungeons were traversed in a linear or semi-linear way, constrained maze-like rooms with puzzles that were interconnected. Completing a puzzle meant that bit-by-bit you were figuring out accessing more and more of the dungeon. Traversing the dungeon WAS the puzzle. 

You unfortunately do not get that experience with TotK's dungeons, this is mainly due to its insistence on player freedom. It means the game designers cannot funnel you in a specific navigational puzzle or encounters since it has to assume every terminal you visit might be the first one, which makes traversing between terminals trivial.

Overall, it is still a competently made video game that is phenomenal for those with a experimental sandbox-based mindset. The game was released with no majors bugs or glitches at launch. That can only be praised. The ending sequence with Link successfully grabbing Zelda is a big highlight and the character designs are top-notch.

But the flaws of the new open-world Zelda formula are becoming more and more apparent, and they will not be welcome when the next 3D zelda game releases in 4-6 years.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
For Tears of the Kingdom, my experience playing through the game has been bad.  I have nothing against TotK using the same map as BotW but with 2 added landscape to explore, the sky and depths.  Exploring the world of TotK seems rewarding at first, but it starts getting old too fast and the only reward is just seeing the sites.  You still have to find hundreds of Korok seeds to expand your weapon, bows, and shields inventories to functional levels.  There are physical dungeons, but they don't hold the charm as the traditional Zelda games achieved.

The most important factors of any game is the content and how you play in it.  The content is more quantity than quality.  The gameplay feels good if you have plenty of resources to burn through.  Finding great weapons is a bit more difficult in TotK than BotW due to new mechanics from the Zonai technology.  To incentivize using the fusion mechanic, weapons have lower durability than they had in BotW.  As long as you have decent fusion material, you can make "decent" weapons, but for me, that fusion material pool is used for too much, and this led to terrible experiences with combat. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Points positifs :
- Le jeu est fourni, il est difficile de s'ennuyer.
- L'histoire est prenante, voire touchante. Pour une fois, les quatres élus sont vivant. Les gens nous connaissent (et pas que les vieux zoras).
- Les nombreux pouvoirs permettent de libérer sa créativité de toutes les manières, et les nombreuses solutions aux énigmes nous font nous sentir plus malins que le jeu.
- Un tas de nouveaux plats, de nouvelles tenues, de nouveaux ingrédients, de nouvelles fonctionnalités.
- Une véritable amélioration, des détails qui font toute la différence.
- La plupart de PNJ sont retravaillés. Alors qu'on avait jusque là que trois âges (enfant, adulte, personne âgée), un quatrième a fait son apparition (adolescent).

Points négatifs :
- Un jeu beaucoup trop bazar. On est submergés par des quêtes, des grottes, des puits, des korogus et des monstres.
- Un total oubli du jeu précédent. Toute la technologie archéonique a disparu, les château d'Hyrule a perdu toute sa saveur. Pas de nouveaux secrets sur les vestiges anciens.
- La nouvelle technologie magique n'est pas belle. Du vert brillant, de la "glue", une batterie...? Et surtout, la technologie magique ne semble pas exister dans l'histoire. Dans Botw, l'histoire était centrée sur les gardiens, les sheikas, les créatures divines. Là, hormis Ganondorf et sa magie, on n'entend jamais les personnages s'en sortir grâce à la technologie, qui est pourtant le centre du jeu.
- Pas d'ajouts. Pas de nouveaux peuples, de nouveaux villages, alors que la taille de la map a triplé ! À croire que les développeurs n'ont créé ces nouveaux lieux que pour "stocker" du matériel...

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Este juego, puesto simplemente, es el mejor juego que jugué en mi vida. Las habilidades que se presentan podrían ser, cada una, revolucionarias e increíbles por sí solas. Pero no, acá están las 4 juntas. Ya a nivel mecánico, este juego es una locura nunca antes vista. La forma en la que se puede manipular todo el entorno, y a su vez usar las diversas habilidades a la ves para hacer lo que te dé la gana es una genialidad. Por ejemplo (muy simple), quiero llegar a un lugar alto, entonces agarro una tabla de madera, la alzo, luego la dejo caer y retrocedo el tiempo para infiltrarme. Por más tonto que parezca, esto es una completa locura solo a nivel jugable si no que en programación. Y para agregar más, se agregaron las islas en el cielo, un subsuelo igual de grande que el mapa original, y una red cientos de cuevas y cientos de pozos en el mapa original. Las físicas, a su vez, complementan a las habilidades y el mapa, siendo extremadamente detalladas y retroactivas. Hay tantas cosas para decir sobre este juego, pero intenté resumirlo en un párrafo. Simplemente alucinante en todos los aspectos (incluso la música y la dirección de arte por dios!), y uno de los mejores, sino el mejor juego de la historia. 15/10

Review: Basically, it's Breath of the Wild, but a lot better. There's so much more to do in TotK. Two brand new areas to explore, on top of the original map being made a new experience again. The side quests are more fun as well. Combat has quality of life improvements. The hand abilities are a lot better than BotW's shekiah slate powers. Ultrahand lets me mess around in all kinds of new ways, like driving across large stretches of land, and kill monsters in new ways. Fuse fixed the weapon durability problem. There is one weakness in gameplay: the sage abilities are more gimmicky and less practical (exception being the wind one). The story is an improvement over BotW (mainly due to the tear memories, rather than Link's own quest) but still a bit lacking. The dungeons are decent, with proper elemental themes returning, as well as unique bosses (rather than the boring Blight Ganons in BotW). The finale is pure greatness, and Ganondorf has had his best showing to date.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Since the release of BOTW, we never thought it could be beaten, never mind matched. However, Tears Of The Kingdom undoubtedly improves on virtually every single aspect of the game, from the core gameplay its self, to minor details within the game, truly defining it as the greatest game OF ALL TIME. 

Firstly, Tears of the Kingdom drastically improves upon the dungeons seem within Breath Of The Wild. Although the divine beasts were very good, they felt repetitive, and each one felt like a slight reskin of the other. However, in Tears Of The Kingdom we see a more traditional and unique style to the temples, each fitting their respective areas. The lightning temple, a prime example of how great the temples are, feels much more like a traditional dungeon with rooms throughout the dungeon connecting to each other to form a sensational sequence of puzzles to finish the temple. Furthermore, the journey to the temple itself is sensational, truly setting up the marvel of the temple to come. To further improve upon BOTW, the bosses are drastically improved. The fights are thrilling, entertaining and truly enhance the dungeon further. They are completely unique which makes it feel all the more special. 

Secondly, the new abilities introduced truly enhance the gaming experience. Firstly, fuse is essential to fixing the durability problem. Instead of looking for the weapons themselves, fuse allows us to create our own weapons which mean that we are focused upon the materials not the weapons. Ascend allows us to efficiently ascend through ceilings, hills, caves in order to reach another place, almost like revali’s gale. Recall is just out-right amazing. And ultra hand completely revolutionises Tears Of The Kingdom. It allows us to create and tackle the game in what ever way we want, eradication the linear aspect to any puzzle and the game in general. It brings the players imagination to life and truly changes the gameplay experience, making it better than ever. 

Thirdly, the story of TOTK is more in-depth and meaningful than before. Characters like Zelda are more developed and truly feel essential to the plot. It is all a mystery at first, and engages the reader as we slowly unveil the mystery. And, of course, the introduction of Ganondorf is genius, adding a deceitful, thrilling and powerful antagonist to the plot and giving us the greatest Zelda boss fight ever, and the greatest cinematic ending to a game in history. 

Finally, the introduction of the sky Islands and The Depths eradicate the emptiness of breath of the Wild and give us a more jam packed Hyrule. Everywhere you go, there is always a new puzzle, challenge or mystery to the game, perfecting the open world genre. 

Tears Of The Kingdom doesn’t revolutionise open world gaming, but perfects it and improves upon one the greatest games of all time. It is truly a masterpiece and a must get for any player of any console.

If you were questioning wether you needed to play the prequel before this, the answer is NO most definitely not, go straight to TOTK and never look back!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This is as close to a 10/10 as a game can get with this level of scale and adventure.

I have a lot of flaws with this game. There's too much dialogue, the UI ****, the sky islands are barren, the cutscenes for the dungeons are boring, etc. etc. etc. But all these flaws completely fail to ruin my experience with the game. 

This game gave me an emotion that no other game could have given me. I don't want to do a spoiler review but I can write so much about it. Some of my favorite moments in not only Zelda but gaming history, come from this game and it took me 150 hours to finally decide to fight Ganon. And the ending was... simply fantastic.

Maybe I'm biased or my love for the franchise blinds me to its flaws, but I have not had this much fun with a game since Mario Odyssey nor Celeste.

I don't want to write more. Just know, there are critiques one could give the game, but the highest of highs remain here and I wouldn't trade this experience for anything.

I wondered before what Breath of the Wild was missing when I played that game. It wasn't the weaker abilities; it wasn't the lackluster ending; it wasn't the empty Hyrule. It was one thing: a heart. The charisma and wit of Ocarina of Time, Majora's Mask, Wind Waker, Twilight Princess, and Skyward Sword were missing in Breath of the Wild. This game has it.

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom... has it all. If they just tweaked a few more things and I'd give this a perfect rating

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Tears of the Kingdom is such a massive improvement from Breath of the Wild. I was not impressed with the move from "classic" Zelda to BoTW, but ToTK is truly a fantastic game. In many ways it is the game BoTW should have been.

I almost see BoTW as a sort of beta version of ToTK. It is as if the creation of the open world and game mechanics took so much time and resources that the developers did not have time to actually fill the world with content or a story. With ToTK I feel like the mechanics and open world concept was already developed, so now they were able to focus solely on filling the world with content and a richer storyline. 

ToTK is a true pleasure to play. It is a great game with lots of fun and so much to explore.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Esse jogo é talvez o melhor que já joguei e já vi na vida, com um mundo imenso e uma história maravilhosa, Zelda totk é a mistura perfeita de um jogo mundo aberto e linear. Zelda totk é uma melhora em todos o sentidos quanto ao botw, agora com a adição das profundezas e das ilhas no céu, o poder de exploração e a sensação de descobrimento está ainda maior, sem falar que o mapa principal (a superfície) não é exatamente igual a do jogo anterior, mesmo que em teoria fosse o mesmo. Além da exploração, a resolução de problemas e das shrines estão bem melhores, podendo ter diversas soluções para apenas um problema, e muitas vezes necessitando muita criatividade para passar por eles. E por último mas não menos importante, a história de Tears of the Kingdom está espetacular e muito mais imersiva do que nunca, com trechos emocionantes, de deixar qualquer um na ponta da cadeira. Claro que esse jogo não é perfeito, algumas críticas que tenho quanto a ele é de que se repete alguns erros de seu antecessor, não o suficiente para estragar sua jogatina mas ainda assim são meio chatinhos, os problemas mais graves que encontrei são quanto a performance do jogo, onde muitas vezes o fps cai ou para renderizar o mapa e alguns lugares o jogo tem telas de loading maiores do que o ideal, onde muitas vezes me vi pegando o celular enquanto carrega, algo que com certeza não é bom, outro ponto negativo são as profundezas, eu particularmente gostei bastante de explorar, porém preciso admitir que pode sim ser repetitivo e um problema para a maioria das pessoas. No geral The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom é um jogo espetacular e uma obra de arte, e definitivamente um dos melhores jogos de todos os tempos, como disse antes, não é perfeito, mas não acho que suas imperfeições impactam de forma muito negativa a experiência do jogador, e mesmo com esses problemas não muda a grandiosidade deste jogo incrível, e com certeza um jogo que todos que gostam de mundo aberto e uma história fenomenal devem jogar algum dia.

Dungeons are improved but still not at the level of classic Zelda titles. Though I loved Totk it disappointed me in a few ways. I believe using the same map was a mistake. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Decent open world game that gives the player basically total freedom.
Basically the player explores the view and explores/finds stuff that can be ordered into several categories. Some of these things are more fun, other less so.

Pros
-Some really fun "activities" in the world, including
--Caves
--Sky Islands
--Some side quests
--Interesting locations and their associated mysteries
--Quirky characters
-World is beautiful
-Main quest is fun

Cons
-Several aspects of the game feel like a chore
--Korok Seeds
--Helping the guy with the signs
--(Many) shrines
-Light on story
-Most of the things one does in the game feel meaningless. Yes, some activities are intrinsically fun, but they don't lead to some overall progression. Exceptions that feel meaningful are: New outfits, the few story/lore drops, and uncovering the map
-Recipe/cooking system adds an unnecessary (and unfun) level of complexity
-Ultrahand feels very fiddly and unfun to use

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Good and playable,but nothing special. immortals fenyx rising was more fun than this.
A huge world with nothing interesting going on, there is no fun in exploring. All the Chests you get, have useless stuff in them, just another batch of bow/sword/shield... put them to the 50 other ones in your inventory. Having to walk to my next destination scared me more than Ganondorf and his lackeys and you know whats worse? now you get the same empty useless world in the sky and in the depths.
The Whole game felt like a chore to play. Just finished it at around 65h, not gonna continue or play the sidequests.

Pro:
- Crafting variety is huge, some ppl will love to build machines etc. (not me)
- gameplay is nice, swordplay and bow etc. is great
-love the coloring of the game
- interesting characters including both mcs and villain

con:
- cant call your horse from more than 20 meters. not gonna buy any dlc for that tbh, nintendo has to learn to build in quality of life features (they are probably scared that it would cut the playtime short if you were on horseback all the time)
- weapon durability
- weapons overall,  mastersword is probably the biggest joke ever.
the only good weapons in the game are either limited or have big debuffs... is that supposed to be fun?
- tedious sidequests, like unlocking the fairies for equipment enchancment (they should beat the guy up who came up with that idea)
- equipment enchancement costs too much, 4x upgradeable, costs 10, 50, 200, 500, so760 just for 1 piece + rare materials (so selling them is not an option, they should also beat up that guy, but is probably the same dude), 2280 rupees for just 1 set of clothing to max and there are above 15 or so sets.
- farming money/rupees is almost impossible and goes too slow, quests reward you max with 300, the gems are way to scarce and are needed for upgrading or weapon buff
- shrines are harder to find compared to botw, wasnt fun to look for them, not gonna open a gameguide for that
- depths are just pure suffering. cant see more than 5 meters ahead, gloom everywhere and mobs that either put gloom on you or oneshot you... the whole idea is nice but the realization is so bad.
- Dragontear quests should be fixed, so that you get the videos in order, mine were all over the place. so i was confused till i stopped playing and watched the whole video in order on youtube. that way i could spoil myself and also have atleast some clue what was going on
- damage scaling is very bad. i was hitting like a truck with my 70+ dmg weapon but still couldnt scratch the silver class monsters, burned many good weapons on some random mobs
- the game is trying too hard to be mysterious .. i dont want to explore everything, give me a clear line, show me where i have to go, where i can find the caves etc., the world is too big and everything looks similar so i dont wanna go to most of those places and explore them

i enjoyed the game but it had moments where i absolutely hated it.
i am glad that i played it, but i will def not preorder the next zelda title thankts to this game

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: It irons out almost all of BotW's weaknesses. GOOD: - Gigantic open world with lots of secrets and unique caves. - A comprehensible story with an epic climax, albeit very predictable. - GANONDORF IS BACK! The final battle is epic, but simple. This is probably the way to pick up casuals and veterans alike. - The skills! Weaponfuse as well as building vehicles is great! Crafting weapons in particular is great fun. There aren't too many special fusions in the end, but it solves the problem that BotW still had. Battles are motivating. You are well rewarded and make noticeable progress without a level system. AVERAGE: - Timeback Skill - is very helpful, but also necessary in places to rewind the far-flying parts that didn't land where you physically expected them to. - Bosses - they're still not as good as they were in previous Zelda instalments, but better than the Ganon fights in BotW. Not good: - Enemy Variation. BotW already had few enemies, but TotK simply has too few enemies for a game in 2023. Only a handful of new ones have been added. I would have liked more creative enemies here, especially because of Weaponfuse. - Dungeons. Some say that the great dungeons of the good Zelda days have returned. I can't confirm that. The 4 story dungeons are even worse than the Divine Beasts. The fire and water temples in particular are just areas stuck together with no depth. The worst dungeons Zelda has ever had. - Sky Islands: Of all things, the main focus of the marketing is the weakest area in the entire game. It's more a question of how you get up there. Once you're up there, one of three copy-paste patterns awaits the player. Boring. On top of that, there is a pathetic variety of enemies up here. There are really only the small robots and maybe the occasional flying enemy. - Underground. Provides strong kicks for the first 3 hours. Then it becomes just as trivially boring as the Sky Islands. Absolutly NO GO: - There's nothing worse for an open world than copying the world from the previous instalment and barely reworking it. There are caves, which are the best innovation on the surface. Everything else in the familiar open world is a bitter disappointment. Exploration is no fun. Worse still: where there was nothing in BotW, there is often nothing to be found in TotK either. So the open world degenerates even more into an Ubisoft junk world. TLDR: A potentiel masterpiece that fails due to its open world formula and doesn't make the most of its cool game design ideas.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
While the game functions fine technically, I don't have much else positive to say. TotK is everything BotW was not, it's unrewarding, grindy, immersion-breaking, poorly written, trend-chasing, un-interactive, and, frankly, stupid. 

The core gameplay loop of exploration doesn't work without a world designed for that exploration, that the player has not experienced and does not fully understand. That was BotW innovation. TotK fails to understand this on a fundamental level to such a degree that we might even start to think BotW was a fluke. 

Beyond that, TotK's new mechanics actually negatively impact BotW's other major innovation: world interaction. Because, you no longer have to think about the terrain when you can just Ascend past it all or build a flying machine to bypass it all. It's kind of amazing how little they considered BotW when making this game.

Then, there's the story, which tries to pretend all other Zelda games never existed. BotW included, despite being a sequel. Never seen anything like it before, but it's awful.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Many people have their own criticisms of this game - the reused map, the weird storytelling, the weapon durability, the objectively empty depths, and objectively repetitive sky islands, which soured the gameplay experience for some. 

However, dropping into Hyrule for the first time in 6 years, what you are met by, are a plethora of questions - What happened to Zelda? What happened to the 4 races of hyrule? What changed? As you explore the surface of Hyrule, you never run out of questions to ask. The depths, and the sky islands, nurture this constant sense of curiosity, drawing your eyes to them, perhaps not acting as second and third maps, but rather like additional locations on the original map, fueling your imagination and curiosity. While the rewards at the end of the trail these questions lead you on may not necessarily be the best or most useful, what is fulfilling is the journey, the act of travelling, the anticipation, and the discovery along the way itself. Along with the constant discovery and exploration, there were some of the highest highlights along the way. This game is the king of setting the mood. The sounds, the atmosphere, and the visuals of the Lightning Temple, Wind Temple and Fire Temple set the mood in the best way possible, getting you ready to take on the puzzles, enemies and bosses.

This game nails the *feeling* of exploration, wonder, and curiosity, enhanced by the gorgeous artstyle and mood setting. This, is what sets this game apart, and this is what makes this game a 10/10 for me, despite all its other shortcomings.

Review: Tears of the Kingdom's biggest crime is the same as its predecessor: a huge emphasis on exploration but a saddening lack of meaningful discovery. Make no mistake that this is basically a copy/paste of the same framework as Breath of the Wild, but with one major difference that enhances the experience to another level: Link's new arm abilities. They can manipulate where (and even when) objects are to solve puzzles as well as jumping through ceilings as a brilliant display of vertical traversal. It's a great game, and everyone who loved Breath of the Wild will no doubt love this one as well. But for me personally, I can only play a little at a time before its open world design starts exhausts me more than it should.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: One of the most flawed games ever made, and yet, one of the greatest ever made. Is it Breath of the Wild again? Pretty much. However, do I consider that a flaw? Absolutely not. Tears of the Kingdom is Breath of the Wild but better in almost every way. Breath of the Wild was already one of the greatest games ever made, and if this game is just that but improved and on a bigger scale with a brand new mechanic that completely re-invents the wheel, then what's not to love? The game has its flaws not because it isn't like Ocarina of Time in how it does its dungeons or story structure, instead I think ToTK's approach to dungeons are extremely valid and well-made, but it has its flaws due to some repetition in its world and poor writing in its story. Aside from that, Tears of the Kingdom is the best open world game we've seen to date.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: This was the single greatest gaming experience I have ever had. The opening sequence immediately captured me and left me wanting more. once we gained full control, learning the new mechanics of the game was absolutely delightful. ultrahand especially was the most fun i've ever had learning. The moment the great sky island is finished, the game allows you complete freedom to explore and do whatever you wish. I loved visiting locations that were present in Breath Of the Wild and seeing how the developers changed it. My love for exploration also made traveling the depths one of the most fun parts of the game. there were a ton of mines where i dug up zonaite to upgrade my batteries and every now and then, my exploration would be rewarded with a side quest, or a neat piece of armor that referenced the older zelda games. I smiled from ear to ear upon finding my first piece of the twilight princess set. And the temples for the sages were all so much fun to play through. Especially the wind temple. The atmosphere, music, and dungeon puzzles in that dungeon made me realize that this game was everything I wanted it to be. It's also insane how you can try almost anything with ultrahand and things just work. I don't know how the hell the zelda team pulled off making a game like this work for the switch in just 6 years. the parallels the drew between Zelda and Ganondorf as determined individuals willing to sacrifice everything for their goal, as well as the connection between king Rauru's ideal of what it means to be a king compared to Ganondorf's were executed masterfully. This game was an emotional roller coaster.  Absolutely my favorite game of all time and a must play for anyone who calls themselves a gamer. Not to throw shade at any of the fantastic games that are nominated for GOTY 2023 but after playing them all it feels absolutely impossible that any game other than tears of the kingdom wins. Excellent work Hidemaro Fujibayashi and the rest of your team.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Tears of the kingdom is one of the best games not only from Nintendo, but also in general, its mechanics such as ultra-hand or combination, are fun and easy to understand, which makes it unique, its open world despite being the same, it still feels fresh Thanks to the new sanctuaries, caves and the representation of the underground, the only thing that is not very good at all are the celestial islands, these are few, small and become repetitive, from then on it has a Quite a broad and fun exploration for which you don't know where to start.

Its story seemed somewhat simple and not very elaborate to me, it was what I had the most expectations for, the best part of the story is Zelda's sacrifice to repair the master sword for more than 10,000 years by becoming a dragon, the idea of ​​memories is not bad, it's just that it is not well captured because they were able to put an order to the memories and make them last longer, I also lack context for certain things such as a representation of the underground, how the zonnan became extinct (not counting rauru and mineru), these if we see his **** ending is excellent, it feels epic and magical, even though all the bosses are easy, the dialogues and scenes never cease to amaze, such as Ganondorf, the battle against the black dragon is beautiful, the soundtrack is wonderful and as it is In the Zelda saga, burying the master sword in the dragon to destroy the tear that started it all, making Ganondorf powerful. Breath of the Wild had a sad ending due to the death of the champions but in Tears of the Kingdom despite the death of Mineru's spirit, the post-credits scene conveys joy and peace, defeating Ganondorf, his draconic form and saving to Zelda saving her from the fall and making her Hylian again.

In conclusion, Tears of the Kingdom surpassed its predecessor in many aspects, making it a totally unique open-world video game.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom

The new areas and building on the old map is awesome, but occasionally some areas feel empty. The machine building and weapon crafting is fun as well, but the controls feel a little clunky. There's a tad bit too much when it comes to shrines and collectables, but those quests are mostly skipable if you don't want to do them  The item durability is less of an issue this time around, which was appreciated! I will say the story is amazing from start to finish. If you love Zelda, and if you adored BotW, this is a must play.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: A monumental follow up to The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. Nintendo has put even more effort into creating the Sandox experience, with unbelievable mechanics that beg the question of how they managed to create this game on the Nintendo Switch. The world's size and richness have nearly tripled, and the gameplay of the basic map has also been significantly altered. The player can navigate to a substantial number of sky islands and a massive subterranean area without encountering any loading screens. In conclusion, Nintendo has succeeded in producing a game that both matched and surpassed its expectations.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
En clair The Legend of Zelda : Tears of the Kingdom est un excellent jeu avec un travail de fou sur des éléments comme les pouvoirs qui offre tellement de possibilité que les développeurs ont prévu/laissé. Mais tout en réussissant à ce qu’il ne soient pas destructeur de l’expérience en cassant totalement le jeu. Un jeu qui vient corriger quelques soucis de son prédécesseur notamment sur les temples et leurs boss qui possède plus d’identité. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Simply put- the best game ever made. It’s so good that its flaws become irrelevant. Exploration and creativity have never been better applied to a video game. It takes everything BOTW was and tops it. 

Ultrahand is the greatest gaming mechanic ever made. It adds an unprecedented level of creativity and interactivity. There’s nothing more fun or engaging than designing a machine, device, or item to accomplish or reach something. It along with fuse lead the list that adds up to the best set of abilities Zelda has ever had. 

It’s almost inconceivable that arguably the most massive open world game ever made was pulled off on such obsolete hardware with so little compromises. The graphics are somehow immersive and fantastic as a result of Nintendo’s doctorate in cartoon worlds and knowing what makes graphics look good and bad. With that said, I’d still love to see what Nintendo could do with identical hardware to PS5 and Series X. 

I spent over 700 hours on this game because I didn’t want it to end and because there’s that much to do in it. 

My only real complaints are that the coordinates should’ve had a movable reticle that shows it’s locations rather than yours, the hero’s quest tracker was too short and should’ve been limitless, that the game could have had a more organized and extensive tracking of true 100% completion and central hub featuring several hundred categories (you can add hundreds of hours to a game by simply creating more to complete), the lack of a meter that shows a weapon’s or shield’s degradation, and the main dungeons should’ve been self contained and lengthier. All that said, as I noted above it’s so good it makes these complaints completely irrelevant. 

At the end of the day, like BOTW it’s as good as gaming gets and further proof Nintendo is untouchable when it comes to game design. I just hate that there’s such an extensive wait in between titles. If only gaming had the same delivery time as TV shows. Imagine a world where we get one Zelda per year or every other year.

Review: I really wanted to love TOTK. While the game is wonderful and nostalgic on its own, I cannot shake the feeling of general disappointment. The incredible draw and magic of BOTW lies in a world undiscovered, the melancholic yet absolutely liberating feeling that you're one with the wild, seeing what's beyond every hill, lake, cliffside, spark in the distance. TOTK doesn't have that feeling anymore because the main map has already been explored in the previous game, and both the sky islands and the depths are not real worlds with complex biomes, objectives, and stories for you to want to explore. They're just filler environments, stretched for the sake of expanding the worlds. They're not that rewarding or exciting to discover as a whole. The memory aspect also doesn't fit with TOTK, and the story line falls under the same formula as BOTW, which does not work in the context of TOTK. Although the weapons, combat, runes, gameplay elements are new and exciting and innovative, the core meat of the game (story, world exploring), are just not enough to make this game great. In summary, TOTK doesn't capture the magic and awe that BOTW has in its open world concept , doesn't have elements from previous zelda games that make up for it (story is weak, dungeons are weaker), and the innovative aspects of the game (building, interesting runes), are just not nearly enough to make this game a truly spectacular standalone zelda game.

Better side quests, better visuals, better abilities, better story, better shrines, better enemy variety, a better world, and more content to sink your teeth into if you're a completionist. However, two things hold the game back. The first one is the UI, which is extremely clunky when doing things like fighting alongside sages or attaching items to your bow. The second major issue is that the game is on the Nintendo Switch. I love the Switch, but it can barely handle this game and its innovative mechanics. Frame drops are the norm and not being able to experience this game in 4k 60fps means part of the world's beauty is lost. Despite that though, the new mechanics alone could warrant buying the game since they are unbelievably fun to mess around with for hours.

Review:
The Legend Of Zelda Tears of the Kingdom SIGNIFICANTLY improves all aspects of the previous entry and continues to bring what made BOTW a great game with it’s story mechanics and voice acting. However in this entry with the nearly 7 year old system that is powering the game, the mechanics sometimes struggle to truly live up to modern day games. It’s quite unreasonable the charge that Nintendo is offering for the game. What this game really delivers on in the other hand no pun intended is ultra hand, this new ability can stick almost anything together. Players have created such monstrosity’s like mechs to cars. This is an unusual mechanic to this series however the way it’s used and the endless possibilities are truly what make this game shine including a world that has tripled.

VERDICT: The Legend of Zelda Tears of The Kingdom is full of fun surprises in a familiar place. The game is full of tech issues, however with the addition of Ultrahand brings a whole new light to this game.
Due to the Nintendo consoles lack of performance the game remains a last gen experience that may not be suitable for most gamers, Nintendo Switch Fans will find this possibly the greatest Switch Game of All Time.

7.5/10 Great!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Review in Portuguese.
Tears of the Kingdom parece viver à sombra do seu predecessor, trazendo inovações que, embora interessantes, não justificam completamente o preço integral do jogo. Entre as novidades, os novos poderes e a mecânica de construção são os pontos altos, sendo implementados de maneira criativa e eficaz. No entanto, outras adições deixam a desejar. 
O novo mapa, chamado Depths, é notavelmente vazio e repetitivo, dando a impressão de ter sido incluído apenas para justificar a existência de uma nova área no jogo. As ilhas no céu também são escassas e, em grande parte, se assemelham umas às outras, o que diminui a sensação de variedade e exploração. 
A trama é envolvente, mas não traz nada de realmente inovador, seguindo uma estrutura de missões semelhante ao jogo anterior. Para um título desse porte, esperava-se uma abordagem mais inovadora e cativante.
Em relação aos gráficos, o jogo mantém o belo estilo de arte do seu antecessor, mas, em algumas ocasiões, parece até pior, o que é decepcionante, especialmente considerando que o jogo foi lançado para o Nintendo Switch. A escolha de um console limitado pela própria Nintendo não justifica totalmente esse retrocesso visual.
A trilha sonora é um ponto forte, com composições fantásticas e emocionantes, embora uma parte significativa delas seja reaproveitada do jogo anterior. 
Em resumo, Tears of the Kingdom é um jogo competente, mas é difícil ignorar a falta de inovação em muitos aspectos. É decepcionante ver um título tão esperado reciclar elementos sem trazer melhorias significativas. Ainda assim, ele oferece uma experiência sólida para os fãs da série, mesmo que deixe a sensação de que poderia ter sido muito mais do que é.

Zelda TOTK superou minhas expectativas e se tornou o melhor jogo que eu ja joguei na vida. Todas as criticas envolvendo o BOTW ficam extremamente irrelevantes quando se trata de TOTK. As sky islands, o underground, a exploração da superfície, a utilização de tudo que está em sua volta para solucionar as dificuldades de exploração... tudo está extremamente bem feito e bem planejado. Os novos poderes: ultra hand, fuse, ascend, recall... TODOS são incríveis. Tudo em Zelda TOTK é incrível, surpreendente, completo, magnífico, e, acima de tudo, MONUMENTAL. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
It's a great, fun and beautiful sandbox action game, but I long for the days when Nintendo valued story and lore. I think there's been a Mario-fication of the Zelda series and the developers have even stated that the story isn't critical to Zelda games, but I'd argue that the story is what has always driven interest in it. Look at any Zelda fan forum or site and they're overflowing with analyses of the story and the lore.

TOTK's gameplay is undoubtedly great, but I found the main story once again left a lot to be desired. I found much more joy in the side quests (like Lurelin village) and general exploration. My advice is to avoid the main story as much as possible and explore the game. The end of the game felt rushed and like an afterthought, unlike the beginning, so don't hurry to the end.

Are we ever going to have instruments and great music in Zelda games again? I sure hope so. TOTK is a wonderful game, and it sounds like it's the formula that Nintendo is going to use going forward, but I pray for a better story and music in the next one. I don't know how Nintendo can look at the success of Elden Ring, a brand new IP, and keep saying that story isn't important for the Zelda series.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Yes, they reused BOTW map, but they changed, added so much to it: underworld, sky islands, and tons of caves (filled with materials). The new mechanisms (fuse, zonai builds) adds so much variety in the way to handle battles and at times exploration. Along with the new items' usage, these new features overall extends greatly over BOTW the number of methods at disposal to solve problems. Creativity runs wild thanks to Zonai builds allowing for almost unlimited possibilities. As a result, some shrines can be solved in multiple ways. The fantastic physics unique to this game will be talked about years and years after. You might surprise yourself when trying to build a cutomized machine, not knowing if your machine is built properly and is working as intended. You get sometimes this "Aha" moment when you find out it actually works or how it should work. Then you go wild testing and destroying any moving living things (no I didn't say Koroks, though I could...).

The final boss fight might be one of the most memorable fighting moments I have ever witnessed.

On the downside, the sky islands are sometimes a bit empty and there are repeat locations in the depth (e.g., Yiga hideout and monster mining camp) but there are also tons of good surprises in the skies (dungeons, starview, zonaite forge) and in the depth (bosses, coliseums, labyrinths, spirits, abandoned mines, all the areas surrounding fire temple).

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
People are going too soft on this game since it got review-bombed with 10s at the start and they're probably afraid of offending people. It's not just - "Im too old for this!" (Thats an excuse to calm the internet). As a 26-year-old, I can still enjoy many other games with more intensive puzzle mechanics/building. A game where I have to watch a youtube video to make every contraption I need to make is a bad game. I get absolutely no reward for tediously gluing parts together for hours so to complete this slog I just ended up climbing and using stamina potions just like the last game. Call me an idiot, but I don't have time to keep failing, and failing just to save another Korok and get two pieces of poop. I've been a Zelda fan for decades and played and enjoyed every title thus far (even BOTW! Though I enjoyed it less than many others). TOTK is "fun" in the sense that sometimes I feel like I get to do something interesting, but lets face it - for the most part this game is a puzzle/engineering sim THEMED with Zelda. And if you dont like spending hours upon hours doing literal work for minor rewards, this game isn't for you. We watched people playing it online - tons of videos with robots shooting lasers from their nether regions and thought haha! That looks fun. But the strangest thing happened. My partner and I get the game, played for an afternoon, and then moved on with our lives. Then I went to plug in my Wii and play Twilight Princess again ;) When the hype clears and your depression over the world's events has its upturn - which game do you return to? Probably not TOTK.
Also where's this metacritic score coming from? 96? Really? That is hilarious. Nice job lining your pockets with Nintendo money.

Review: If you compare TOTK to BOTW, then yes TOTK beats BOTW overall. But TOTK feels like a very solid expansion pack of the previous game. Exploration has been ramped up, story expanded in a very satisfying way and core gameplay loop remains the same. Biggest milestone is the new feature of utilizing your surroundings to merge weapons and create various tools for transport and destruction. A fantastic addition to the general gameplay. And exploring the various levels was a blast. While the game definitely amazed me, it lacked for me the same WOW factor I experienced with BOTW. In some sense its suffering from its own previous success. I hope they continue with this format of Zelda games, but if they do so completely different map.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: This game is a milestone for the Zelda franchise as a whole, as it builds on the environment already established in Breath of the Wild, but also incorporates elements of older Zelda games within it. Tears of the Kindgom’s story is also unbelievable in its own right. Although it retains the same format of storytelling from Breath of the Wild, that being explaining the narrative through events that occur in the past, it subverted my expectations with its intriguing ideas. Furthermore, the gameplay is outstanding, for it allows the player to make the game as creative and fun as they want it to be. Instead of making a set of rules that the player must follow to accomplish tasks, they said, “Here,  YOU figure out YOU want to solve this problem.” Overall, Tears of the Kingdom fixes most of Breath of the Wild’s problems, and outshines it in many ways. I strongly recommend this game if you haven’t played it already.
