Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
When the first trailer for Tears of the Kingdom (TotK) dropped, I wasn't too keen on buying the game because of Breath of the Wild (BotW). Despite all the praise BotW received, I struggled to finish the game. I only made the effort to finish BotW because at some point TotK convinced me it might be a fun game. I finished BotW months before the release of TotK, despite having purchased it at launch.

The difference between the two is night and day. TotK is NOT glorified DLC. Those who claim it is DLC are clearly lying about having played the game. It is a highly fun and addictive game.

Pros:

The game is seamless. You can find the highest sky mountain and glide into the deepest chasm without any loading screens. That is impressive when you consider it's all on the Switch.

The game is visually stunning. While it's doesn't have the graphics of something like FF16, it's watercolor art style feels just right. I play this game on an 80" 4k tv and I don't mind the look of it.

The way the story is delivered has some issues, but the story is touching. Zelda is not just damsel in distress like in previous games. She plays a major role in helping you defeat the Demon King.

Ultrahand is the bread and butter of this game. It has limits but there's a lot you can do with it. It all depends on how creative you are. Some of the fusions look wacky, but they are fun to play with.

Cons:

It does have some frame rate drops. This game really does push the Switch to its limits, but for what this game does, it is truly impressive how much it gets away with. The drops aren't too frequent to ruin the experience. The only moment I remember seeing a frame rate dropping was when I jumped off a sky platform chasing a fire-dragon that was going into a chasm. I glid alongside the dragon until it reached the depths then landed on it. It was just a moment the game stuttered.

There are some narrative issues. I don't think this is a spoiler, but the narrative revolves around you finding Zelda. If you've grown up with the series, you know that's a staple of the franchise.

I encountered Impa early on, and she sent me on a quest to find all the tears. I have an obsession with unlocking the world map in these open world game before starting the story. It usually results in me reaching max level before I even start the campaign.

Finding all the tears reveals what happened to Zelda, yet Link still runs around pretending he doesn't know. It's funny but it's still a glazing narrative issue.

This is minor. In my exploration I also stumbled across the Master Sword without receiving the quest from the Deku tree since I couldn't find the entrance to the Lost Woods. The entrance alluded me until my brother said, "Why do you climb everything." Then my it clicked in my BotW brain.

I just feel certain reveals could have been held off until certain criteria were met. I know it would complicate the game for some players, but it could have held the narrative a little better.

All the champions have the same cutscenes. These moments could have been used to expand the narrative.

This game is almost flawless, but since I can't give it a 9.5, it takes the whole 10.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
To say that I'm disappointed would be a gross understatement.

To clarify, The Legend of Zelda is my favourite series in gaming and has never failed to impress, move and floor me with every one of the games.

This is the very first time I've felt let down. And it hurts. I so desperately want to agree with all of the rave reviews, but I just can't.

To me, Tears of the Kingdom is effectively a repurposed Breath of the Wild.

- There are no fundamental differences with the way this game looks plays or feels. The combat mechanics are untouched and play exactly as they did in BotW (flurry rush and bullet time galore). The fusion mechanic makes the weapons look cooler and adds more longevity to even the weakest of base weapons... but I struggle to care beyond aesthetics when the combat encounters are the exact same mechanically against opponents that are also largely the exact same ones from BotW.

- The new mechanics are fun to muck around with, particularly "Ascend", however the whole "Ultrahand" vehicle building gimmick never really stuck for me. I only ever engaged with it as a matter of convenience in the overworld, and while the shrine puzzles were mostly well designed, it all felt a bit samey after a while. I understand that this is preference, but when this is the foundation of new mechanics that the game is built around in the stead of actual puzzles akin to the classic titles that made them as fun as they are... I don't see it as a worthy successor.

- The dungeons themselves are an improvement over the Divine Beasts - however still follow that same formula of do the thing five times then fight the boss. Also, here are the five places you need to go to marked on your map from the get go. It's all so watered down. Half the fun of the old dungeons was navigating, now that's all done for you! At least we've got actual bosses now good god, the Ganon Blights were dismal in BotW.

- The story is bad. It's a bad story. Not necessarily because of the content, but certainly because of the structure and how it's conveyed to the player. There is absolutely no agency whatsoever as soon as the intro to the game is over. They just do the memory thing again, except this time they aren't even Link's memories and he therefore has no role in the story whatsoever. It's a story that has already happened that the main character isn't involved in that barely affects the game's actual proceedings??? How are we supposed to care? It's so clear that NIntendo didn't want to sacrifice the freedom and wanted to have it both ways, which has resulted in one of the most poorly delivered stories I've ever seen with no weight whatsoever. This is helped in no part thanks to Link's complete lack of characterisation. He is as stiff as he ever was in BotW but at least in the game it was somewhat justifiable as he was a soldier with amnesia. They even had an in game explanation for it. You'd think after years of peace with Zelda he'd have dropped the act just a little. It makes it so embarrassing when scenes are supposed to have weight and he's just standing there looking like he's fresh out of a lobotomy procedure. Agonising to watch. I know he's always been somewhat of a blank slate but come on!

- Ganondorf, as a result, is a total wasted opportunity. He is hardly in the game at all. Could they not have sacrificed just a smidge of the freedom to provide a sense of stakes, weight and agency to this game?! We already got boundless freedom in BotW, reign it in a bit!

- The sky and depths definitely exist. They both harbour some great main story stuff, but the remainder of both is just lacklustre. Sky has a load of islands to discover but they all amount to the same thing of just super simple shrine puzzles and then a Rauru's Blessing. The dephs are even worse. A great big giant pit of the same biome strecthed across the enitre map with a whole ton of copy paste enemies and armour from the amiibos. On that note, there is barely any new armour, which is hugely dissapoiting.

- I don't know some of the new bosses are cool, but there aren't nearly enough. The caves on the surface are cool for a while but most look and play the same. There are barely any new enemy types, hardly matters though because the mechanics are the exact same and aren't conducive to engaging combat. The Map is the same, they've revamped it with different enemy base layouts and way more of them but who cares when it's just the same assets from BotW but more abundant?

I'm being harsh I know. This isn't a bad game, just one that's disappointed me greatly especially considering the development time. I have had enough of this formula, this franchise needs at least some amount of linearity to work!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Zelda TotK is a direct sequel to Breath of the Wild. It uses the same map of Hyrule, but changes so many areas, adds caves, adds Sky Islands and a completely new 3rd aspect that was not shown before. It is an absolute massive game and one of the best open worlds ever created.

The exploration and adventure aspect of the game is its biggest strength. The new abilities, especially the building function via Ultra Hand, gives you one of the best sandbox experiences ever. There are almost no limits to what you can do and the physics in the game are something I have never seen before.

It also tackles some of the issues BotW had: The world is way more dense, the new temples are much more fun than the Divine Beasts – even though they still dont reach the highest hights of older Zelda game dungeons. Weapon durability is still in the game, however due to the fuse ability it feels way less tedious. Its actually fun to create new weapon combinations. The story overall is stronger than in BotW, with some great story telling, however its still very surface level – but it still has some emotional peaks.

One of the weakest aspects that hasnt changed at all from BotW is the combat itself. It still feels clunky, very little options and no new tricks here. Overall, an amazing game, an amazing entry in the Zelda series and one of the must pure fun games I played in the last years.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
After 150 hours, it's time to write a review. This game made me smile from the first day I played it to the day when I defeated Ganondorf, which was yesterday. At first, I thought it was nothing much different from BotW aside from the new abilities... but man I was I wrong.

But first, the cons. The story was a bit weak at first but gets better. I wish they changed how the armors looked even a little bit because most of them are exactly what they looked like in BotW. I was also hoping for more variations with the korok challenges. It is the same Hyrule from BotW... but tbf, the sky islands, depths, caves and wells added a lot more places to explore and discover. And with the overworld monsters, I was expecting more of a challenge.

The more hours I spent, the more different gameplay opportunities open up. Fiddling with zonai devices and fuse is funny as it is rewarding. Ascend is a god-sent ability that is very satisfying to use. The puzzles, places, bosses, and even the HUD is curated for a unique gaming experience which is what I personally think Zelda games do best. Not to mention there are several ways to solve a singular problem. I am a trial and error type of guy so it resonated with me very well.

I mentioned that the story is a bit weak in the beginning but it got better and better especially in the final sequences of the main quest. I recommend getting the tears in order as it will provide you a more coherent story-telling experience!

I love this game to the point that after 150 hours I wish there was more content even though I've only completed about 2/3 of the sidequests and about 90% of the shrines. I'll certainly keep playing and wait for the DLC (no official announcement yet but I hope there is a DLC). If that DLC didn't come after I 100% the game quests and shrines, I am considering another playthrough.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I enjoyed the previous opus but was still frustrated with some of its aspects (endurance, climbing, breakable weapons) and was sceptical about Nintendo being able to do better via a sequel. And well, what a masterpiece there, every single aspect I was frustrated about has been reworked/twisted. The building mechanics is fun, the world manages to bring you to explore it and it's rewardind (remiding me of Elden Ring by the way).
Graphics are what they are due to hardware limitations but I met not one single bug and it globally runs smooth.
The story I thought at first was less intense than BOTW proves itself to be a least on the same heights at last. The world is coherent, musics are neat and well designed/ timed.
The only "cons" may be the main story bosses which are way too easy and not much of a challenge compared to BOTW's ones.
This one of the rare game which left me with somewhat of a feeling of emptiness after the ending and that is a sign of greatness for me.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Most disappointing game ever. BOTW is one of the greatest games of all time and this is a lazy soulless clone of it. New skies and depths have nothing fun to do might as well not be in the game at all. Same monsters, koroks, lame sidequests and shrine puzzles from BOTW copy pasted everywhere. The main quest is slightly improved divine beasts (they still ****). Bosses are a total joke. Story is awful makes no sense, awful character design and cringe cutscenes. Not just the map, literally EVERYTHING is copied over from BOTW and the story plays out exactly the same. How am I not supposed to feel like I'm just replaying an inferior BOTW ripoff? If you play Zelda to make logic gates and helicopters then I guess this is your game but if you're anyone else with a brain this game is a complete failure. I am still dumbfounded that Nintendo created this embarrassment. Even more dumbfounded that everyone is giving it a 10??? I will never understand...

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I have spent about two hundred hours on this game and while I think it is decent, it is one of the weakest in the series.

There is a lot to do, but most of it is just the same thing over and over again. This game is all about quantity over quality. Most quests and tasks just feel like busy work; it would probably take me another two hundred hours to try and 100% this game. I would rather have half the amount of stuff to do and instead have significant improvements to the quality of life functions and gameplay mechanics, along with a better story.

There has been almost no improvements to the gameplay and quality of life from BotW. The game has better frame rate and only experienced slowdown minimally. Of course, most areas are pretty devoid of anything and the new large area feels empty and soulless. I hated that after spending what must have been 60+ hours completely exploring the new area I was given a lame participation trophy instead of something useful or interesting.

Sure, they added some new land and areas to explore but it gets very repetitive quickly. They add some new clothing but you get so tired of having to change back and forth that you really start to wonder why there is no way to save a couple clothing sets and quick change between them. And while it is nice finding a unique weapon, knowing it will break is always depressing - and I sure wish the Master Sword was stronger in this game. I can barely kill two Moblins with it before it breaks. The only time it actually felt like the Master Sword is during the final battle where the sword can't break. After that fight, I never want to see items breaking in a Zelda game ever again.

I did enjoy the boss battles but thought there was not enough variation as you end up fighting the same large bosses over and over. I  enjoyed the new outfits but hated changing every five seconds. I also disliked how many items you needed to upgrade the clothing. I don’t want to spend hours farming the same thing over and over again.

The game does have some cool battles, events, and scenery, and I really did enjoy the final boss fight, but that doesn't excuse the tediousness, repetition, and the lack of gameplay and quality of life Improvements. I also wish the story was more consistent with the first game.

It is really frustrating how they seem to change parts of the lore around from BotW and almost never reference or have anyone try to connect what is happening in TotK to what happened in the Breath of the Wild. While there are interesting parts to the story, it is difficult to feel the same sense of emotion and connection as in the first game. The story does feel inferior  and 90% of the interesting characters and stuff that is here, well they were already here from BotW.

Tears of the Kingdom is not a bad game per-say, it’s ok and fine for a time sink if you have nothing better to do. I really think they should have had the sequel take place outside of Hyrule or have a Dark-World variation like in A Link to the Past to help break up the monotony. Don’t go in thinking you are getting some great improvement over Breath of the Wild. I actually think the game is a downgrade.

There is tons of new things to make the game feel fresh but the underlying systems and gameplay are the same. Go kill 4 bosses, do bunch of shrines, explore similar world as in BOTW but with few changes and once again collect something like 1000 korok seeds without ability to track them without using a third party app . The underground level is an copy pasted wasteland that is just annoying to explorer and there is so few sky islands that I do not get how they even made that a selling point. You will hear people saying the game is 2 or 3 times bigger then BOTW but in reality its maybe like 1.2 - 1.5 times bigger. If it was not for the whole construction mechanics this game would not be even consider to be innovative in any way. Its a shame that the same devs that have shaken up the gaming market with BOTW decided to go the same route as the rest (UBISOFT 2.0) and just create another copy pasted game.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This game... In my opinion, it really is one of the greatest games I've ever played.  This is my opinion, I really respect any opinion and any criticism of this game, but this game, it just fills all the criteria that make a game as good as perfect for me.  I'm having so much fun exploring every layer of this game, I've already put 90 hours into this game and I'm probably not even halfway through the game.  There is so much to explore. I enjoy it so much. You can explore the world of the game more freely than ever and it's just unbelievable how great the game is. Probably the most impressive thing about this game in my opinion is just that you are trying to solve a problem with the new mechanics of the Game or you just have an idea in your head trying to implement it and you just know that it will work because in this game everything just works.. everything works together so naturally.  It's just amazing how smoth the game features blend in together.  If you really liked breath of the wild as a game, how it worked and the exploring of the world, then I promise you will love tears of the kingdom just as much, if not more. And if you're worried that the map will feel too similar to breath of the wild, then I can tell you from my experienced, for me it was like playing a whole new game no matter what layer of the map I was on, whether it was Sky Island or on Hyrule itself.
In conclusion, I can say that I enjoyed the game like no other game before. Everyone has to know for themselves what kind of game they enjoy the most but I can really recommend this game to anyone who really liked breath of the wild. In manny places you can already get the Game for about 40-50 $/€ wich in my opinion is a great Deal :)

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I have been a gamer for a long time, but I have to admit that I lost interest in playing games for many years. I felt like most games were repetitive, boring, or too easy. I was looking for something that would challenge me, surprise me, and immerse me in a rich and beautiful world. That's when I decided to try the new Zelda game on the Nintendo Switch.

I was blown away by how amazing this game is. It is not just a game, it is an experience. The graphics are stunning, the music is captivating, the gameplay is smooth and intuitive, and the story is engaging and emotional. The game gives you so much freedom to explore, discover, and create your own adventure. You can climb mountains, glide through the air, ride horses, cook meals, solve puzzles, fight enemies, and more. The game never gets boring or predictable, because there is always something new to see or do.

The game also has a lot of depth and replay value. There are many secrets to uncover, side quests to complete, weapons to collect, shrines to activate, and bosses to defeat. The game adapts to your play style and skill level, so you can always find a challenge that suits you. You can also customize your character's appearance, equipment, and abilities to fit your preferences.

The new Zelda game is the best game I have ever played. It rekindled my love for single player RPGs and made me feel like a kid again. It is a masterpiece that deserves all the praise and awards it has received. If you have a Nintendo Switch, you owe it to yourself to play this game. Trust me, you will not regret it.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
After very much enjoying – but not exactly falling in love with – Breath of the Wild, I was admittedly pretty sceptical in the run up to Tears of the Kingdom. Sure, that third trailer was awesome, but to me at least, it still appeared too similar to its 2017 predecessor and I didn’t think it would grab me like more traditional Zelda’s titles such as The Wind Waker and A Link Between Worlds did in the past. However, after more than 200 hours of exhilarating gameplay, I can comfortably state that this game is the easiest 10/10 I’ll ever give.

From the opening few hours in Sky Isles tutorial area, I was utterly hooked and didn’t once stop to dip into a single other game across Switch, PS5 and Series X until I’d finished what is, for me, an unadulterated masterpiece and the very peak of Nintendo’s creative vision. On and off, it took me six whole years to put 125 hours into Breath of the Wild, but it took me less than six weeks to reach the same milestone in Tears of the Kingdom. The Switch is definitely showing its age these days, but somehow, TOTK manages to look absolutely stunning on both a 65” 4K living room TV and the systems own OLED screen in handheld mode. Yes, the frame rate does occasionally dip below 30 frames-per-second, but after a couple hours I stopped even noticing it. Seriously, if you’re still on the fence, do yourself a favour and jump off right now and pick this game up. I highly doubt you’ll regret it for even the merest moment.

Tears of the Kingdom is without question my game of the year so far and, as far as I’m concerned, the greatest video game ever made. Yes, it really is ‘that’ good. Seriously, just give the game a chance, and you’ll probably feel just as strongly about it as I do.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
What a huge disappointment. Obviously, like everybody after playing BOTW, which was really nice (with its own flaws, some big some small), I was pretty excited about the sequel. Instead we got BOTW again with some extra stuff, that was not interesting or fun at all.

First of all the extra maps, skies and depths, are a chore (besides the very first island when you begin the game). The depths look ALL the same and there is almost nothing to do there. Very boring. If you have found 2-3 Yiga clan places in the depths, its like you have seen all of them, cause they are the same. They even give you the same 2 rewards, the yiga scheme and one of these zonai things. Such a lazy job by the devs. The same counts for the mines btw. The same with the skies, almost nothing interesting to do besides moving the crystal to a shrine. Everything super repetitive and gets a chore pretty quick.

If you have discovered 2-3 caves in the main map, it is as if you have seen already all the caves of the game cause they are the same. If you got 5-6 korok seeds, its like you have gotten/seen all of them, cause they are pretty much all the same. The wells? All the same. Very repetitive and extremely boring. The bosses are supereasy, all of them. Horse is not needed cause you can fly everywhere through the towers. The story is super lame and not interesting at all. NPCs are super repetitive, every NPC saying the same stuff all the time. Another thing: Zeldas character is not likable at all (Link.. I am waiting for you... grrrr super cringe and they should change that whiny voice actor as well asap). The main map? Exactly (!!) the same as BOTW with some extra stuff added on top of it in very few places so it doesnt appear at first glance exactly the same, even though it is. There isnt this nice wonder of exploration, you already know everything, its like playing BOTW again, which is a big no-no cause I spent already hours and hours exploring that place. Why should I do it again? I really wanted to stop playing a few times and uninstall the game but I was not giving my hopes up, hoping that something good will eventually happen ..to no avail.

Weapons break again after 5-6 hits the most, so it is not worth doing any missions or whatever hands you a weapon. The new powers are.. well.. average. The ultrahand gets tedious pretty quick. Even if you have the patience to build a flying machine.. it breaks again after half a minute or so in the air lol I mean, the game is laughable. Then you have the sign-guy here and there, having to do again the same and the same.

This game would only be worth playing (maybe..) if there has never been BOTW. But since BOTW exists, just play BOTW, which is obviously a much better game (in case you have never played any of these 2 games). The enemies? The same as BOTW, minus the guardians, plus a couple of new ones in the skies (these robots) and these gloom hands that grab you. I dont understand how Nintendo had the nerve to release such a piece of sh.. honestly. They should be ashamed of themselves and, like many said, sell it as a BOTW DLC for 20-30$ the most. Such a super lazy job. I couldnt wait to finish it to not have to touch it again. Ignore all these 10s you see, these are fanatic fanboys under the age of 18 that would give it a 10 regardless of its content, without even having ever played it. What a huge disappointment and rip-off by Nintendo. Six years for that, Nintendo? right..

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Este juego fue capaz de crear perfeccionar a su precuela agregándole 2 nuevos y extensos mapas en los cuales hay montones de secretos. Su sistema de pelea no es innovador, pero la fusión hace que puedas crear armas para cada tipo de monstruo. Hyrule está hecho de modo que si buscas algo, probablemente te topes con más secretos llenos de diversión. Los santuarios no son puzzles demasiado extensos pero te pueden complicar más de uno y sus templos son tremendamente divertidos. Finalmente, sus mecánicas son increíbles: con la ultramano puedes crear construcciones y mover cualquier tipo de cosas; con el retroceso puedes hacer retroceder la trayectoria de los objetos hasta su punto original, con la combinación puedes combinar armas con cosas o con más armas y con la infiltración puedes atravesar objetos arriba de ti. En resumen: 10/10 y GOTY.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: O jogo é incrível, Vaz tudo que seu antecessor fez, e sinceramente a maioria das coisas melhor, indico esse jogo pra 2 tipos de jogadores, fãs da franquia, e quem não jogou Zelda BOTW, já que mesmo melhorando tudo, é visível que a estrutura é a mesma, mesmo sistema de 4 masmorras, ir lá e livrar tribo x de um problema causado pela volta de ganon, existe problemas de performance e as texturas ficam borradas em alguns momentos do jogo, uma reclamação pra fazer são os sábios, já que a mecânica deles é bem quebrada, você constantemente ativa-os sem querer, colocar o mesmo botão pra ativar todos, não foi uma escolha tão inteligente e deveria ser melhorado futuramente, porem oque há de bom no jogo ? É totalmente livre, deixa você explorar do jeito que quiser, apesar das masmorras terem repetido o anterior, foram melhoradas, tendo visuais completamente diferentes, chefões totalmente diferentes, porem a resolução dos problemas são extremamente simples, já as side Quest, são muito divertidas e te dão boas recompensas, não terminei o jogo ainda, tenho 250 horas, e fiz aproximadamente 50%, amei cada segundo, os problemas nesse jogo são visíveis, e devem sim ser coitados, porem existe diversos pontos positivos, como por exemplo, a falta de loading ao descer do céu, ou descer para as profundezas, tocando no assunto, os céus e as profundezas foram adicionados, e fazem a exploração ser muito mais interessante, tem adições na superfície, além de diversos novos inimigos, como o horroblim, gleock, grande bokoblim, entre outros, as mecânicas desse jogo, são incríveis, o fuse, a ultrahand e o acend, fazem com que sua imaginação flua, e te dá diversas maneiras de resolver problemas, falando em resolução de problemas, os santuários, apesar de serem parecidos com o anterior, me pareceu uma maneira de incentivar o jogador a ser criativo, já que há diversas maneiras de resolvê-los graças as novas habilidades, você pode pensar que fez errado, mas não existe certo ou errado nesse jogo, sua criatividade diz oque fazer, e você faz, simplesmente maravilhoso, a história ficou muito mais interessante, e o final é emocionante a ponto de fazer qualquer casca grossa chorar que nem um bebê, esse jogo, faz o seu antecessor parecer uma versão beta, ou só um gostinho do que viria pela frente, já que esse jogo, faz com que você seja mais livre do que nunca, porem, mesmo com diversas melhorias, não poderia dar 10, ao menos, não com os problemas que citei, os gráficos não são tão importantes pra mim, mas a queda de FPS pode quebrar a imersão em alguns momentos, além de ser bem perceptível ao usar o ultrahand ou entrar em algum lugar muito pesado, mas mesmo sendo um problema grave, devo dar os parabéns a Nintendo por conseguir rodar esse jogo em um console tão ultrapassado. Minha conclusão é que, jogue, se você gostou do anterior este vai te deixar abismado, o jeito que tudo aqui é expandido, e simplesmente maravilhoso, o final é lindo o começo é lindo tudo aqui é lindo, pra quem realmente gosta de explorar, este jogo é um prato cheio, personagens incríveis, história melhorada, chefões visualmente impecáveis, e o jeito que esse jogo faz com que a experiência seja única pra cada pessoa, é simplesmente um jogo que facilmente entra na lista de melhores jogos já feitos, pelo menos essa é minha opinião!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Una gran juego de mundo abierto y con gran personalidad. Pero una pésima secuela que no aclara la historia de Breath of the Wild y añade un popurri de ideas incongruentes que no aportan nada al universo de Hyrule, por el motivo  de que la trama es superficial y sin alma.

LO MALO

- Una historia fragmentada que carece de profundidad y desarrollo de personajes.

- La dificultad es casi inexistente, siendo su único desafío los enfrentamientos con los Gleoks o los primeros momentos por el subsuelo.

- El cielo que era su principal punto fuerte, es solo una anécdota por su escases de retos, desafíos y lugares interesantes para visitar.

- Agujeros de guion que descolocan si vienes de Breath of the Wild, donde se reescriben y se olvidan eventos anteriores.

- El rol de los sabios junto a su jugabilidad que no aportan nada a la trama y suelen bugearse o hay que perseguirlos por el mapa para poder activar su habilidad, convirtiéndolos en una molestia que es recomendable deshabilitar (Salvo Tureli).

- Determinadas mecánicas como el farmeo de dragones por piezas y cada 10 minutos aprox, solo para obtener un objeto por aparición.

- A ratos la pantalla se queda colgada o se ralentiza inesperadamente debido al exceso de partículas o efectos ambientales.

- Misiones secundarias anecdóticas y carentes de desarrollo personajes. Salvo pequeñas excepciones que utilizan las mecánicas y al menos divierten..

- El cringe que da la sobredosis de gemidos que suelen emitir los NPCs.

- Combate final sencillo y el cierre de la trama bastante cliché con  el "poder del amor" que arruina el momento del sacrificio, estropeando con ello el desarrollo de cierto personaje.

A pesar de todo lo malo, el juego es bastante solido y entretenido como experimento de mundo abierto. La mecánica de subsuelo aporta bastante la experiencia, junto a la inclusión de trajes amiibos ,como contenido gratuito, en misiones secundarias. Así mismo, el personaje de Kabalit  que opera como tutorial de mecánicas, dando un aire fresco tras cada encuentro  y por ultimo el uso de habilidades de Link que son mas intuitivas e inmersivas en la experiencia, permitiendo acomodar el juego al gusto del jugador.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Funny enough, my biggest gripe is that the stable owners and Great Fairies need to quit repeating themselves. They are so long winded XD bhaha. Yes, I am aware I can’t turn my horse well at full speed, thanks. Yes, I am aware upgrading an outfit twice may unlock an enhancement, thanks. Noted. For the 1,000th time. It’d be great if maybe they repeated their tips two or three times tops, then quit after that point.

The game is nearly a masterpiece to me.

We’re a sandbox generation, so building contraptions was fun to encounter in a Zelda game, but soon enough there are plenty of portals and towers unlocked for fast traveling between the three layers of the world that the feature isn’t used as much in mid to late game. (Fine with me, tbh, it got too time consuming to build all the time).

So those Koroks that need to be reunited with their friends? I think maybe 3 or 4 got reunited the first couple days. After that, they’ve been completely ignored. Poor neglected Koroks. LOL. Just too many of them.

The sky islands and the underground are incredible experiences at first, but they are big and basically empty. I play about 8 hours a week now, and find myself visiting them for quick sessions of grinding as nothing entices me to stick around long. I replayed BOTW many times over the years, but with how ToTK is such a huge game, I don’t see how I’ll care to restart it from the beginning. Maybe that’s why I’m taking my time with all the side quests, knowing this might be my only time through LOL.

The storyline is more complex, layered, and interactive than BOTW. Rather than the townspeople hunkering in the towns afraid and needing saving from pockets of monsters, they are a bigger part of the story, trying to “help” solve what is going on. There are all sorts of researchers about, and monster fighting teams, etc. You even get to fight alongside the Gerudo army. The personalization of NPC’s really helped TotK excel over BOTW.

I might be rare that I like the breakable weapons lol. Upgradeable outfits compensate for having weaker weapons (maybe even over-compensate). Just plan to take the time to make a couple outfits really strong before you progress too far, then you can take on toughter monsters and use their parts to fuse better weapons.

The only thing I find strange is that I have no desire actually beat the game. I’ve watched videos and it seems like a frustrating, arduous task anyways. In BOTW, Zelda (and others) constantly urge Link to rush and help, but the story in TotK is more about the unraveling of mysteries, and is less urgent feeling.

Although I liked building Link’s house, it also looks like an IKEA project. LOL

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom es un juego muy esperado y ha recibido críticas muy positivas. Es una secuela directa de Breath of the Wild y se basa en lo que hizo Breath of the Wild anteriormente, refinando los sistemas del primer juego. El juego es tan amplio como profundo y algo que justifica cómodamente la espera de seis años. Es el juego de Zelda más narrativo1. El juego sigue siendo un caótico patio de recreo físico, pero es uno que es de alguna manera más amigable y en otros aspectos incluso más castigador que su predecesor.

IGN lo describe como una secuela notable que de alguna manera eleva aún más el listón hacia las nubes2. Este sandbox es más grande, más rico y de alguna manera aún más ambicioso, con nuevos sistemas creativos como la construcción de vehículos, la elaboración ridícula de armas y un mapa renovado de Hyrule con una cantidad vertiginosa de profundidad que profundiza aún más la exploración intoxicante que hizo que el original fuera tan cautivador. Breath of the Wild se sintió lejos de estar inacabado pero, inconcebiblemente, Tears of the Kingdom ha logrado hacerlo sentir como un primer borrador

En Metacritic, el juego tiene una puntuación Metascore de 96, lo que indica aclamación universal basada en 140 críticas. TheGamer lo llama una obra maestra que no solo iguala lo que vino antes, sino que hace todo lo posible para superarlo1.

En resumen, The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom ha sido muy bien recibido por la crítica y parece ser una adición emocionante a la franquicia.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
TotK is a bit of a let down all things considered. As a complete package I find the game to be alright the pros and cons tend to even out for me. If you enjoyed BotW you'll likely enjoy TotK as its no secret the games are very similar.

To get the biggest negative out of the way I feel that the combat is a real let down. I wasn't expecting a dramatic change from BotW but it feels like there was no adjustment to how quickly weapons break. The fusion mechanic is alright it just feels to me like an added step in getting weapons that can actually manage to hurt monsters. Both of these factors made me almost always avoid combat whenever possible. To finish off the subject of combat, by the end of the game having more HP felt like more of a problem than anything else. I'm unsure if this is how the game actually works so maybe I'm wrong but the more HP I had the stronger variants monsters were around Hyrule. I spent more than half the game at 5 hearts and it wasn't until I upgraded my HP that I started to encounter more powerful enemies. I always felt like I could die in 3-5 hits no matter how much HP I had.

Another major problem I have is the story. Not so much as to what happens in the games story but that again all the good parts of the games story happen before the events the player gets to personally experience. While this happens a lot in the Zelda series I feel like almost every game has moments outside of the final battle where a pivotal event takes place. There really is no such event in this game. Outside of the final battle I would argue there is no story development that takes place in this game. You again find memories of the past and help the four races solve an issue with their home which awakens them as a sage to help you in the final battle. Those moments aren't bad and the problems the four races face in this game were interesting its just everything felt disjointed.

The dungeons overall were better than BotW but in the end they were a bit of a letdown. The airship was the first I went to and I had a very good time with it I found it to be a great experience from getting to the dungeon until defeating the boss. The other three dungeons I cant say the same for once I found out they were all the same thing I tended to not enjoy them. That being said the pyramid was interesting to navigate in my opinion and the worst one by far is the Zora dungeon. You can basically skip doing anything in that dungeon if you try.

So what would I say is positive about this game? The exploration obviously. Overall the world is fun to explore. It is fun to find shrines, while the shrines aren't amazing they're still fun to do. Overall the best shrines I would say are the ones that have an overworld puzzle to get into the shrine rather than a puzzle inside the shrine. Doing side quests, exploring the world, riding horses or building cards no matter how you choose to go through the overworld its fun. The sky islands are lacking in my opinion but still interesting. The underground unfortunately is a letdown. I did find all the light roots but there's really not much of anything else to do down there aside from the Master Koga questline and the fifth dungeon. There are no shrines in the depths and that's a little sad. You can go the whole game without ever going into the depths aside from the story dungeons. That realistically leaves 90% of the depths empty at least the sky is physically 90% empty and every bit of land you can go to in the sky has something to do. Regardless of that though exploration makes this game fun. Traveling through Hyrule finding shrines, quests, caves, and even the occasional Korok (I cant emphasize occasional enough as looking for more than that is insane.)

To quickly address the new abilities replacing the old slate mechanics. I thought they were okay overall. Ultrahand is most used and I'm not gonna talk about performance its the switch if your not happy with the performance I don't know what to say we've known the switch is underpowered since 2017. Building things to solve puzzles or vehicles  is neat. It wasn't for me though and I actively tried to solve puzzles without it or travel without it. Ascend is the best ability hands down. I already mentioned fusion and I never used blueprints really.

Overall I'd say I enjoyed the game but it still deserves a six to me. Exploration alone can't save this game. I'm glad people enjoy it and say it's their favorite game but its just not mine. I hope that future Zelda games build from here as it feels like they didn't build from BotW. Adding more world and then not utilizing it. Adding another story you only get to watch rather than experience. It's a letdown. All that being said I enjoyed it and many others will hopefully more than I do.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
BOTW is the greatest game ever made. Every village, every side quest, every unexpected twist and turn was a delight: an incredible voyage of discovery, and those discoveries were thrilling. TOTK has none of that. I'm 40 hours in and haven't experienced a single moment that was unexpected or new. All the enemies, all the insects, even all the sound effects are the same as BOTW, except the maps are emptier and the quests are sparser.

Oh look, it's Hestu. Oh look, it's Kilton. Oh look, Tarry Town. Again.

This is not a new game. This is not a sequel. This is an expansion pack. Five years for this? I feel cheated.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I can't believe I am giving a Zelda game such a low rating but this game has cemented the fact that Zelda as we know it is dead.

This game is a complete chore, grinding for material to create stuff to grind for more materials just to repeat the same thing over and over. Want to upgrade your inventory then grind, want to get new weapons then grind just bear in mind that you will break your useless weapons to get equally useless ones, of course you also have the Ubisoft towers, a staple in chore-like open world titles such as this and the Assassin's Creed franchise.

There are no dungeons, exploration is not rewarding, not only are you exploring the same map but you are doing it for pointless loot too. God I miss key items and dungeons, remember how cool it was to open that chest not knowing what you'll find inside. Remember how cool it was to go into the overworld now with the key item to open new avenues for exploring. Back then the overworld was a big puzzle itself, in this title the puzzle are contained in another grinding mechanic known as shrines.

There is no story, no epic, no lore, no side quests, no memorable characters. It's just a bunch of mechanics and gimmicks, Zelda is dead and we killed it. This game whatever you want to call, but it is not a Zelda title.

I gave away this Zelda and don't plan to buy another BoTW like title, I'm not interested in Open World Zelda, if you like grinding and gimmicky mechanics this game is for you. If you like Zelda then it isn't.

Zelda was the only game that got me into buying a Nintendo console, but I guess not anymore. You lost a fan Nintendo, it's sad to see what Zelda has become. I hope 2D titles survive and don't get destroyed too.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom is an impressive game even on Nintendo's six-year-old console. While the performance may have issues ‌and combat can get a little repetitive, it is no match for the amount of content that is filled in the game. With side quests that will take you across all the maps, you will always have something to do. In addition to the amazing story that is lifted even further up by the extraordinary voice acting, and memorable music, Tears of the Kingdom’s story will be one that people will look back at as a classic. Not to mention, the unique gameplay mechanics, such as fuse and ultrahand to help each player have an experience that is specifically unique to them. With so much to do in this game, the seventy-dollar price tag is definitely worth it and is a must for the Nintendo Switch. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Final Update: After 105 hours, finished the game. The depths are an afterthought, you just need to do enough there to gain batteries and complete a couple of quests and the rest is pointless. The story is also an afterthought: let's be clear, there is no path to the story which can be summed up as: intro cinematics, getting your companions, expanding your stash and unlocking regions, defeating bad guy, end cinematics *** credits *** more end cinematics. The number of main quests is actually extremely small, and the number of side quests is actually mostly fillers, barely more. The game is made to make you grind and watch the load screen to get a couple of items to be strong enough to defeat the bad guy at the end. Many times in the quest there are either issues with translations, or plain logic. As mentioned it's not a true open world as there is no story progression through your exploration of the map. FPS drop throughout the game is truly unbearable and the hindrance of your companions is also unbelievable annoying. It is said that repetition is the key to comedy, well this game is the plain demonstration: what a joke.

Update: played the game for 60+ hours, it’s empty, grindy, and repetitive to give a semblance of depth to this game. It’s a very empty and soul-less game. The stuttering and fps drop is really annoying, same as the cut scenes (if you’ve seen the cutscene for a shrine once, twice or three times, you just end up mashing the controller’s buttons). Thank god there are duplication bugs to help getting food and coins rapidly, because this game is worst than a chore. It’s bad enough that I start to root for the antagonist… it’s really not an action or rpg game, barely a Minecraft clone with unnecessarily idiotic puzzles).

I don't get the hype: the game is ugly, stutters, lags (controler or joycon response is... slow), and the world is empty with inconsistent use of voice acting.

Game mechanics are incredibly poor (doing a simple 360 takes 4 seconds, looking around to 'solve' the puzzles is equally enragingly long), no possibility to tune any game parameter or remap anything, it's worse than a PC game designed in the early 2000 and it's not refreshing to see pixelated shadows.

The use of some kind of cell shading to mask the low capacity of the console as well as using supersaturated textures with a mix low polygon models with high quality particles makes the game appear even weirder.

I've tried playing this game but every 5 minutes I quit since it's really just not that good and it's not even trying to be good nor modern in any sense of the term: it's like playing a game of watching the paint dry using one hand and wondering why this kind of stupid controller setup is.

I get it, people like to play games that basically play themselves, do not require any kind of character development, skills, or involvements so they just enjoy watching pretty colors playing in front of their eyes but I think there is a limit to that kind of mindlessness. Even games like the sims 1 have more depth!

Another theory for those justifying the time it takes to pass the "tutorial" section is the sunk cost fallacy: a self justification not to face the fact they wasted money and time. As such they need to self justify, and justify to the eyes of others, having wasted their time.

Interesting fact, just checked and most of the new 10/10 scores are from users with zero other rating or review. In this case, I'd look at the 4000+ positive reviews as being highly suspicious. Maybe 10% of genuine positive and the rest being bots or paid fake accounts.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
There is a common criticism that 'If you didn't like Breath of the Wild, you won't like Tears of the Kingdom'. That's one that I would have to disagree with-- The game definitely feels more open-ended and easier to get through the world and explore more. My only real criticisms are that while there is a much bigger story, you don't really get to be a part of it. You watch it happen, and feel a bit of a background character in the grand scheme of things. Lots of really great characters, but you don't do much with them. Alongside that, The Sky Islands are very much sent into the background and for a really visually appealing and interesting idea, there isn't very much with it.

Besides all of that, the game play and experience is exceptional. The presentation of everything feels sincere and is a very comfortable game to play. Much of the core game play elements from Breath of the Wild are still here, like Shrines, Breakable Weapons, and Non-Linear story elements. Those still have their same flaws as they did in Breath of the Wild, although they have had improvements where the majority of complaints originated.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom is more The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild.  It really is as simple as that.

However, The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom does everything that The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild does well so much better than The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild.  So much so does Tears of the Kingdom do everything Breath of the Wild does better, that Breath of the Wild has become completely obsolete -- there is simply no reason for anyone to ever go back and play The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild.  If you never played Breath of the Wild, just skip it; Tears of the Kingdom does everything Breath of the Wild does, but so much better.

Though, if you *have* played Breath of the Wild, and have no desire to play it again, Tears of the Kingdom is very much the same game again.  And while it does everything Breath of the Wild does, but better, it also doesn't fix any of Breath of the Wild's biggest problems -- such as weapon degradation, its frustrating and unintuitive combat system, and the fact that you can't really do much in the game when it storms.

You get thrown into a new location in the depths after you fought Demon King's allies in the castle. And instead of going after him, we're just going to build some funny robot. It makes no sense. I did not enjoy this last part in the slightest, the puzzles were nothing but frustrating. But the final boss however is sooo good. If it wasn't for these 2 problems, this would have probably been my favourite game, but unfortunately giving it a higher score just didn't feel right for me.

If you liked Breath of the Wild you definitely will like Tears of the Kingdom. It's just more of it. It drags on but every other aspect of it is just perfection.

MIDDLE OF THE GAME: 4/10
It is the same game as BOTW. Same places. The sky islands are not nearly as compelling as they seem at the beginning. The sounds effects, animations, music, and themes of each area are literally copy and pasted. The only really fun part of the game other than exploration was the leadup to the Wind Temple. The shrines get boring as hell. I was skipping them after I got the stamina wheel up a bit. It is the same game.

MORE CONS: The vehicles in the depths sometimes don't even work (tire traction, too many hills for vehicles to roll, wing vehicles dont last long, etc... it felt like a CHORE.

END: 9/10
The ending sequences and boss fights are imaginative and emotional. Maybe one of the best endings of a zelda game. However, it does not compensate for the drab and dull midgame, which is essentially a DLC of BOTW.

Conclusion: If you don't play this game, you won't really miss out on a ton, unless you like building and seeing which devices do what. I found the devices and builds served little utility throughout the game. You can survive with the same combat as BOTW... which, was already really basic. None of the bosses were that tough if you spent a decent amount of time in BOTW, which we all have.

The dungeons were still clunky and no better than BOTW. Let's all move on. BOTW had a good run.

The game is still fun, it just feels stale.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
As an avid and long-time fan of The Legend of Zelda series, I have eagerly played nearly every title, which is why I find it disheartening to say that "The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom" (TOTK) marks a significant downturn for the franchise. While its predecessor, "Breath of the Wild," introduced a departure from the established formula, TOTK continues down this path with even more gimmicks, diminished depth, and an underwhelming story.
Nintendo's decision to take one of their most cherished series and turn it into a cash-grabbing scheme aimed at the lowest common denominator is truly appalling. TOTK entices players with superfluous physics mechanics, an abundance of lifeless non-playable characters, and a world that feels artificial and devoid of substance. In stark contrast, the 1998 release of "Ocarina of Time" on a modest 64 MB cartridge managed to deliver an unparalleled gaming experience despite the technological limitations of its time.
For those of us fortunate enough to have experienced "Ocarina of Time" during its prime, we were introduced to a vibrant Hyrule brimming with life. It was an adventure that transcended mere gameplay; it felt like an immersive journey that captivated our senses and emotions. Regrettably, TOTK falls short in every aspect. It lacks depth, fails to introduce memorable characters, offers an underwhelming narrative, and possesses a soundtrack that fails to evoke any genuine praise.
However, credit must be given where it is due. TOTK does replicate the visual design of "Breath of the Wild," a somewhat noteworthy achievement. Additionally, the introduction of new building mechanics adds a refreshing element to the gameplay, although these alone are insufficient to redeem the overall decline that the series has experienced. While the Lighting Temple holds some nostalgic value, it, along with the other temples, merely serves as replacements for the Divine Beasts from "Breath of the Wild."
One of the significant grievances I have with TOTK is its complete departure from the fantasy realm into the realm of science fiction. The Legend of Zelda has always been a fantasy series of the highest caliber, with a few entries incorporating subtle sci-fi elements. However, TOTK abandons the series' fantasy roots entirely, transforming it into just another generic sci-fi game. This departure raises questions—why not equip Link with a spaceship and a blaster, completely disregarding the enchantment of Hyrule? After all, the vast galaxy beckons, and why confine ourselves to the barren sky islands and depths when we can expand the breadth of the game at the expense of its depth, venturing into outer space?
My point is simple: everything that endeared The Legend of Zelda to us old-school gamers, has been stripped away. A captivating story? Nowhere to be found. Memorable characters? Sadly lacking. A musical score that enraptures players with its beauty, breathing life into every scene and landscape, fostering an emotional connection with the game world? Forget about it! The list of disappointments goes on and on.
In the hopes that this downward spiral ceases with TOTK, I implore all those enthralled by the game's allure to reconsider their perspective. It is our responsibility as gamers to maintain the integrity and quality of games, collectively recognizing the importance of preserving the very essence of what made The Legend of Zelda series so cherished. Let us not succumb to drinking the Kool-Aid but instead seek to rekindle the magic that once enchanted our hearts.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom

vedere annunciato il seguito diretto di botw ambientato nella stessa mappa era una scelta doppiamente rischiosa, che avrebbe potuto facilmente portare ad un senso di già visto, e di poca voglia di esplorare nuovamente quel mondo, ma totk non è un semplice dlc che aggiunge due isolette volanti e qualche potere nuovo.
anche in questo capitolo il senso di libertà è pressoché infinito e anzi amplificato da tutte le nuove potenzialità.
cancellare completamente i vecchi poteri per metterne di nuovi, è stata una scelta tanto azzardata quanto **** prima i poteri risultavano quasi limitati alla precisa situazione, ora ci daranno ancora più libertà per interagire con il mondo di gioco e permetterci di fare quello che vogliamo.
se prima potevamo prendere gli oggetti di metallo, ora possiamo prendere ogni singolo oggetto, e collegarlo con altri oggetti per creare veicoli e tante altre cose.
se prima ci si rompeva un'arma ora la possiamo collegare con un'altra per farle durare di più e creare tante variabili diverse potendole collegare anche con tutti i vari consumabili, se prima i bastoni o le alabarde erano un po inutili, ora potendole trasformare in quello che vogliamo risultano le armi più interessanti di tutte.
parlando di scoperta dei nuovi poteri, quello che mi ha fatto più volte dire: ah ma io posso fare questo. è il potere di poter attraversare i soffitti, tanto difficile da implementare nel game design tanto bello riuscire a risolvere enigmi passando sotto essi.
ma quello che è davvero più incredibile di tutti è quello che manda indietro nel tempo gli oggetti.
si switch ha in memoria la posizione di tutti gli oggetti che si spostano nel gioco, e manda indietro solo quello che selezioniamo.
a tutti questi nuovi poteri si aggiunge anche una piacevole cosa introdotta con il dlc di botw, dove il gioco terrà traccia di tutte le strade che percorreremo durante il gioco, aiutando molto a capire quali parti delle mappa dobbiamo ancora visitare.
se è vero che totk continua a non raggiungere la qualità dei vecchi dungeon, quanto visto in questo capitolo però eclissa completamente quelli di botw.
caratterizzandoli meglio come stile, mettendo delle meccaniche uniche che sbloccheremo grazie alle abilità del compagno che ci aiuterà nel dungeon di turno. e infine mettendo dei boss unici, che non puntano sulla difficoltà della sfida ma che continuano a farci scoprire come usare il nuovo potere imparato.
i sacrari invece in parte serviranno a farci imparare i nuovi poteri, essendo a tutti gli effetti dei tutorial, e alcuni potranno essere completati ancor prima di entrarci, dato che la vera sfida sarà riuscire ad entrare.
in generale comunque li ho trovati più divertenti da trovare e completare, permettendoci appunto di sperimentare al massimo tutti i nuovi poteri, è vero che risultano un po più semplici, ma preferendo quello che posso fare con i nuovi poteri era inevitabile preferire questi nuovi sacrari.
anche le missioni secondarie le ho trovate meno inutili da fare rispetto a quelle che avevo fatto in botw, e anche qui il merito è tutto dato alla sperimentazione dei poteri nuovi.
dato che si baseranno in parte sulla costruzione di mezzi, o magari sulla costruzione di strutture per sostenere dei cartelli messi sempre di più in luoghi improbabili, e da delle forme sempre meno semplici da sostenere.
e anche per quanto riguarda la trama del passato mi trovo a preferire quanto visto in questo capitolo, sia perchè è meno complessa da trovare. sia perchè non racconta una storia tanto lontana, o perlomeno la storia è ambientata lontana, ma è molto più interessante per quello che sta accadendo nel presente. senza entrare nel dettaglio è complesso da spiegare.
senza contare le diverse parti sotterranee, creando a tutti gli effetti una seconda hyrule sotterranea tutta da scoprire.
ma non è finita qui, non si sono limitati a creare tre zone diverse, ognuna di queste tre zone è tematizzata da un tipo di gameplay/esplorazione differente, obbligandoci ad agire in maniera differente in base a dove ci troviamo.
se la parte a terra è quella più simile a botw, una volta andati in cielo dovremo imparare a spostarci tra un'isola e l'altra, e risolvere le tipologie di enigmi che ci verranno proposti, che sono differenti da quelli visti a terra.
mentre una volta andati sotto terra, ci sposteremo in un ambiente completamente buio, pieno di miasma dove non potremo camminarci sopra, e se le prime zone non saranno difficilissime essendo pianeggianti, in altre zone avremo ben altri problemi per capire come arrivare in determinati punti.
questa alternanza di situazioni, oltre a rendere il titolo vastissimo e pieno di cose da fare, porterà ad avere un titolo basato su tre dimensioni differenti.
totk prende botw e lo migliora pressoché ogni singolo aspetto, elevandolo a tal punto da diventare uno dei migliori giochi mai fatti.
voto 100

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Breath of the Wild but ten times better. Map feels fresh and story is amazing. Side quests are amazing and the exploration feels incredible as they have added sky islands and a whole Hyrule below the surface. Ultrahand, fuse, ascend, and rewind are all amazing. Especially ultrahand as your can create your own devices to aid you in battle, help you go places, etc. Fuse allows you to make many combos in weapons, such as adding a mushroom to a stick, which made it bouncy. Ascend and rewind are straightforward, Ascend can allow you to teleport up on higher surfaces, which makes exploring a lot easier and less frustrating at some points. Rewind is kind of like stasis in Breath of the Wild, but instead of freezing time, it rewinds time. Tears of the Kingdom allows for limitless creativity and problem-solving. Every NPC feels real which makes the world feel alive. Every village in the game has a new thing to it (Rito Village has a snowstorm, Lurelin Village has been taken over by pirates.) The four dungeons in the game have been upgraded and are alot better than Breath of the Wild's divine beasts. The game is also a lot harder than Breath of the Wild, though once you play for a while and upgrade weapons and armor, it gets easier. The soundtrack is also amazing, it really hits the spot. Tears of the Kingdom is one of the greatest games ever made.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
TL;DR It's good. Most likely you won't regret playing it, especially if you haven't played Breath of the wild yet. The critic is exaggerating it (it wouldn't deserve a 10), but it's definitely a high quality video game with a lot of care put into it.
On the "full price DLC" debate: it does, in fact, feel like DLC, but there is so much content that it's well worth its price. In fact, most DLC would be overpriced compared to this game.
However, I wouldn't recommend buying a Nintendo Switch exclusively for Tears of the Kingdom, or any single videogame, really.

PROS
-Some of the best environmental puzzle solving around which encourages yout creativity and rewards unintended solutions
-A highly-acclaimed physics system that manages to surprise you after years of playing
-A LOT of content (and it's mostly good)
-It's really cinematic at times (especially the music, the dungeons, the bosses and the skydiving sections)

CONS
-The story is weak and incoherent
-Outdated graphics and performance dips in some situations (the day one patch helps, install it)

YOU DECIDE
-Not only the main map, but all the formulas (shrines, memories, 4 main dungeons) from the previous game are brought over
-There is a lot of building to be done and it can get goofy

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Nintendo did it again. Sort of.

To save you some time, if you liked Breath of the Wild, you'll like Tears of the Kingdom as well. If you didn't, nothing will change your mind.

It's all here. Engaging exploration, cute visuals, lots of surprises, crazy breakable weapons, shrines, great OST, koroks, creepy enemies, cool towers, funny writing, a nice story and endless gameplay possibilities.

Only now you have some pretty new and impressive things to keep things fresh. Ascend is probably one of my favorite mechanics ever in a game, ultrahand is godsend, endlessly attaching things to your items never gets old and rewinding is pretty useful and creative. I'm not a "puzzle" guy and I thought these new things weren't going to stick the landing with me, but I was definitely wrong. It all works very well.

There are also two new maps. The sky islands and the depths. I absolutely loved everything in the sky, especially how well they were implemented to the story. It's astonishing. The depths were pretty fun and ominous at first, but became annoying and repetitive after a while.

TOTK is definitely remarkable, with plenty of things to catch you off guard, from the story to gameplay. The ending nearly brought me to tears, with some of the best "cinematic" moments and battles I've experienced in this franchise. It is, without a doubt, an excellent sequel to BOTW. A good one, with few flaws to point at.

Yet, one major feeling slowly crawled inside me on my 180h playthrough.

The sense of novelty kinda vanishes. Don't get me wrong, a game isn't supposed to throw new and shocking things at you at all times! But that overwhelming feeling I had when I played BOTW faded after 80h in. I felt like I was pretty much done with it after experiencing nearly everything new that the game had to offer. But there were MANY other things to do and explore. Felt like I was playing BOTW again and, although I LOVE that game, its replay factor might be its weakest aspect.

That's really the only thing I have to complain about it. Or the biggest thing, in a way. A few problems from the previous entry are still here (like how they handle the story and the infinite shrine hunting) and the new "friend abilities" don't hold a candle to the likes of Revali's Gale or Mipha's Grace. But this might just be me nitpicking at this point, to be honest.

Tears of the Kingdom is a fantastic game and there's A LOT to talk about it. But, for now, I'll just repeat what I said before: if you're like me, and you loved BOTW, pick this one up NOW. If you didn't, it might not change your mind.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Tears of the Kingdom podría haber sido un juego más ambicioso.

Totk desvela los grandes misterios de su predecesor contando una poética historia de sacrifico tras la fundación del Reino de Hyrule, y desvela los misterios detrás del Cataclismo y del entonces gran misterio de los Zonai.
Ahora, Hyrule se ha vuelto un mundo más interactivo gracias a la implementación de las nuevas mecánicas y la introducción de los artilugios Zonnan, que han logrado permitirle a la comunidad jugar de formas inimaginables.

Pero aunque he disfrutado de cada implementación, con +120 de horas invertidas, siento que 6 años de desarrollo ha sido demasiado tiempo para la poca innovación que Nintendo ha trabajado en esta continuación del Botw.

En primer lugar, aunque la historia es muy cautivadora, tristemente su narrativa es simple y deja mucho que desear. Los acontecimientos importantes se cuentan por medio de recuerdos que puedes recolectar opcionalmente, y al final de cada misión principal te cuentan la misma historia hasta que llegas al desenlace en el Castillo de Hyrule. Aquí no hay cavidad para la sorpresa, ya que la historia en sí es muy intuitiva desde el principio, lo que provoca también que no se produzca mucha empatía con algunos personajes debido a la falta de interacción real.

Luego, a parte de algunas alteraciones significativas en las regiones donde toman lugar la historia principal, todo lo demás sigue siendo exactamente lo mismo, lo que provoca que se pierde la gracia por explorar.
No hay que olvidar que este Hyrule fue diseñado para Botw. Cada camino, colina, o paso, estaba pensado para conducir al jugador a un punto estratégico del juego, e incluso el mismo terreno se planificó para contar los acontecimiento del Cataclismo (Todo ello redactado en "Creando a un Héroe"); por lo que al mover las cosas de sus sitio muchas rutas pierden su propósito.

Después están las Islas Celeste y el Sub-suelo. Aunque ahora tenemos nuevos niveles de exploración, estos espacios se sienten vacíos y parecen que no tengan un autentico papel en la historia.
El subsuelo, por ejemplo, no es más que un Hyrule invertido con los mismos diseños de minas repartidos por todo mapa, y con el único cometido de ser una fuente de extracción de Zonanio.
Y con las Islas Celeste ocurre lo mismo, mas allá de la Gran Isla de los Albores y Las Islas del Trueno, casi todas las demás islas parecen carecer de importancia.

Y finalmente está su extraña armonía con Botw. Aunque es comprensible su familiaridad con el juego, ya que Totk en sí es una continuación del mismo, el inconveniente reside en que al reciclar las mismas mecánicas solo ha logrado que se pierda bastante el concepto de "Nueva Experiencia"; tanto su jugabilidad, progreso, experiencia, y la forma de contar la historia, siguen el mismo patrón.
Pero también se ve bastante descompensado tras la eliminación inexplicable de todos los componentes que definieron a Botw, como las Torres Sheika, Los Guardianes, o las Bestias Divinas. En ningún momento se te explica el porqué ya no están presentes en el mundo, simplemente han sido borrados del juego; como una forma por parte de Nintendo de decir que "este es un juego diferente en un mundo diferente" (Es triste entrar el Santuario de la Vida y ver que lo han sustituido por una cueva).

Personalmente, me hubiera gustado haber sido más partícipe de los acontecimientos del juego, y no haberme sentido como un mero espectador. Aunque Zelda se enfoca en el gameplay, sus juegos más modernos han tratado de involucrar al jugador en la historia, tanto mental como emocionalmente, pero como en Totk se enfocan más en los acontecimientos del pasado lejano, hace sentir como si Link no fuera más que un extra en la historia; e incluso se percibe como si tratasen de involucrarle de forma forzada.

No digo que Totk no sea un buen juego. Desde que lo comienzas, hasta que lo terminas, se puede sentir la dedicación por parte del equipo de Nintendo. Pero creo que debido a las grandes expectativas procedentes del gran juego que fue Botw, Nintendo se debió de sentir eclipsado para intentar crear una experiencia mejor, por lo que optaron por ir a lo seguro y volver a utilizar la misma fórmula.

Sólo espero que de aquí a 6 años, en el próximo lanzamiento de Zelda, si es que ocurre, podamos volver a ver otro juego igual de ambicioso, en donde vuelven a experimentar y reinventar lo que fue la saga por más de 35 años.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
《王国之泪》作为一部续作来说，它显然是出色的，它具有比前作更为有趣的战斗系统，添加了可供玩家发挥创造力的建造系统，将地面的内容拓展到了天空与地底，并利用“通天术”“鸟望塔”等全新设计来使玩家在天地之间穿梭自如，当你同步推进天空、地面与地底的进度时，你绝对会收获更加充满激情的游戏体验，全新的怪物和奖励设计令大多数战斗不再得不偿失，即使是《塞尔达》系列一贯并不出色的剧情也在《王国之泪》中通过讲述一个穿越一万年时空的故事的“龙之泪”来进行了补充。相比于《旷野之息》中玩家不可避免的孤独感，任天堂几乎用尽全力在《王国之泪》中设计了各种各样与伙伴并肩作战的桥段，使得每个玩家在海拉鲁大陆上的探险不再寂寞。通过佐那乌装置与滑翔伞的移动，整个游戏的移动进度会比前作更为流畅，即便如此《王国之泪》的游戏流程长度依然能达到前作的两倍甚至三倍，毕竟相比于《旷野之息》的地表，《王国之泪》多了地底与天空整整两个维度。《王国之泪》同时还具备了更加令人震撼的音乐与大型战斗设计，在风之神殿中与急冻盖拉的战斗可以说是整个游戏最为震撼的一幕，从顶着暴风雪逐步向天空突进到突破云层时一览无余，从急冻盖拉苏醒时bgm响起到与其战斗时大开大合的移动和攻击，无一不展现了任天堂对于演出节奏的精确把握。“究极手”“扭转乾坤”等极为强大的功能也能在为玩家提供发挥想象力的空间的同时又很少出现致命性的bug。
然而这并不意味着《王国之泪》在游戏史上的地位就能够超过《旷野之息》，首先《王国之泪》整个游戏本身的框架就是建立在前作之上的，从角色设计到游戏逻辑无一不利用了前作已经完善的基础，它更大的创新是在于同样地形却天差地别的体验，实际上在神庙与四神殿之类的解密设计上该作是完全不如前作的，有别于《旷野之息》天衣无缝的四神兽，《王国之泪》中四神殿的设计更像是割裂感十分明显的复制粘贴。《王国之泪》修改的四贤者设计也比前作要令人难堪，因为在乘坐载具移动或是拾取物品时，贤者们总是靠近并占用你的A键导致出现失误，而在战斗中需要贤者的帮助时又不得不去寻找甚至追赶贤者们。从世界大小来看似乎是多了天空与地底两个维度，而实际体验上则是空岛并没有太多内容，地下也几乎都是相似的宝藏与战斗，在两者之中的移动也几乎全部要依靠“究极手”制造的佐那乌装置来飞行，并没有给予玩家充分的选择来进行移动。
游戏在Nintendo Switch上的表现似乎也只是差强人意，720p的画质与不那么稳定的30fps帧率对于部分注重画质的人是灾难性的，尽管对我来说可以接受但是部分情况下的掉帧确实是影响了游戏体验。
不过总的来说该游戏绝对是一个十分好玩的游戏，《王国之泪》在难度上可以说是老少皆宜，游戏性上适合喜欢解密、战斗、创造等各种内容的玩家，100个小时仅仅只是游戏流程的一半左右，极为丰富的内容绝对能让每一个用心体验的玩家感受到其中的乐趣。
感谢任天堂为我们带来继《旷野之息》之后的又一部难以释手的佳作。

Review:
I did not expect to love this game as much as I do. There's just so much goodness to explore and do. The world doesn't feel stitched together as many open world games do. Many open world games struggle to fill the world with content without everything feeling bland. Tears of the Kingdom does not run into that problem. The Ultrahand adds so many options that a challenge can be overcome with 1000s of solutions. It's the perfect sandbox that allows for player expression.

The only reason I don't give this a 10/10 is because of the hardware limitations (framerate, resolution) and some pacing issues with dialog and cutscenes. E.g., when completing a shrine, let us just skip the entire thing vs. skip cutscene, wait for item prompt, accept, skip cutscene.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Given the way most AAA franchises are treated by studios, with routine and uninspired follow-ons or remakes (looking at you Assassin's Creed), this is a triumph from Nintendo. If you think this is a $70 DLC, or just two DLCs put together due to the sheer size of the world, then I just don't know what you expect out of a video game.

If you didn't like BotW, you won't like this. It has a much bolder storyline with some added creativity that feels like a (close) return to form of the narrative-driven Zelda that I missed in BotW. The world is still an open world, which means most of the side quests are still scattered in pockets – stables, villages, etc. But that was also the remarkable thing about BotW: you really could just go anywhere and they've retained that. But they've added some linearity to how you should progress, which I quite liked.

The main mechanical difference is the relationship between monster parts, materials, weapon breakability, and rupees with the new Fuse ability. Feels a lot more balanced vs. the hundreds of Bokoblin fangs you could gather in BotW only to be able to use them in...elixirs? A much needed upgrade.

Main complaints which I overlook for the sheer imagination and scale of this game:
- Performance is extremely laggy in some areas. And that's with the internal witchcraft Nintendo already has to make this game seamless as possible.
- The added collectibles. I felt like the orbs and Koroks were enough in BotW. Here, they've added even more and it's what most AAA franchises do to make the game "interesting" after you've beaten the main storyline.
- The scattered armor sets. I felt like BotW rewarded you for exploring the world, whereas TotK requires you to. Good armor you could purchase, special armor was findable. The sheer size of the world requires many more hours to really find the good armor than probably should be required.

Many other aspects of BotW were improved: more linear main dungeons, a harder final boss fight, the ability to revisit main dungeon areas, and again, can we talk about that story?

TL;DR – it makes BotW look uninspired and simple, which is just saying this should be Game of the Year.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Just about the perfect sequel. Whereas Breath of the Wild was a game about the joys of exploration and discovery, this is a game about the joys of creation and ingenuity. Whereas Breath of the Wild was about finding and climbing the mountain, this game is about flying up the mountain in a space shuttle, blowing up the mountain, and using it as parts for an unheard-of death machine. (metaphorically, of course.) Where Breath of the Wild let you choose where to go and when to do it, this game lets you choose how to go and what to do. It manages to add amazing new areas, along with somehow making the old ones feel new again. It manages to be both an outstanding vessel for your creativity and a fantastic open-world RPG. Every new mechanic works beautifully. Everything is well thought out. While the moment-to-moment writing and dialogue isn't as on point as in Breath of the Wild, this is a small blemish in an otherwise nearly perfect game. The overarching story writing makes up for it as well. The physics and creativity the game allows are breathtaking. The score/soundtrack is fantastic. The game feels very different to Breath of the Wild, but not in a way that is better or worse. Just... different. Some parts bring joy. Some fear. Some amazement. And almost always, they are absolutely incredible. They managed to make a sequel that is equal to Breath of the Wild. A truly *ahem* breathtaking experience.
10/10
