Review:
The Legend of Zelda Tears of the kingdom was a game worth waiting for. The surface was completely redone with little aspects staying the same. The skies are amazing! Just every part of them is great. The puzzles, the NPCs and the lore as well. The Depths are amazing as well. When I first discovered them, I was truly amazed. It just keeps on going.

Another thing I want to mention is the variety of enemies in this game. In BotW, you had your classic Bokoblins, Moblins, Lizalfos and Lynels with a few others. Now we have redeads, Like Likes, many types of constructs, underground variants, even the classical enemies have horn variants. There is so much.

Finally, I want to mention the exploration. In BotW, you were like "Oh, look, a cool mountain!" and you can go there. In TotK, you have just so much around you. You get a main quest but you get sidetracked 15 times before you actually arrive to the location. Imaging you want to go to Rito Village, you hop on your horse and off you go. In front of you is a Malice hole. Then you find an NPC with a quest and suddenly when you finally get back on track a rock falls from the sky waiting for you to recall it.  Just so so much concentrated in this truly immensely massive game. Worth the wait.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Nintendo's lazyness is big on this one. A forced agressive FSR 1.0 profile that drops the resolution from 900P to 780P 20 FPS in busy scenes, giving you a blurry mess and shifting resolution to crazy visuals that are unbelievably jarring.

The game suffers from every Breath of the wild 's flaws, that were criticized LONG after the game was out to avoid being in trouble with nintendo, this game suffers the same barrage of fanboyism on day one, but little by little everyone that has played enough of this game see what everyone with a sound mind see :

The same boring map as Botw, you rediscover absolutely nothing, it is even boring to have to redo all the same map, they couldn't think of any new mechanics too forcing you to accomplish 120 shrines on the main map and 32 in the sky. Not to even talk of the reused korok system . what is even more outrageous is the divine beast tier easy 5 sages dungeons. Not a single one was difficult, at all, the ambiance of BOTW was darker and felt like there was also much more at stake then this disney ified, cheap "sequel", the issue here is to sell this as a new game, it is not, it reuses 90% of all the known assets, animations, ennemies, there is maybe only 4 new ennemies in the whole game. one of them crawl on the roof of caves, one of them is a tree, another one is a pool of bloody hands trying to catch you, and the last one is a 3 headed dragon, THAT's IT !!! the rest of the game has every same reused ennemies from botw.

Even memories storytelling system is as janky and badly managed as BOTW with 11 tears, so, 11 memories to find and you can find them, again, one of the biggest flaws of BOTW repeated the exact same way, in an anachronous, desynched manner, forcing you to rewatch all of them in a chronological order because we didn't feel like guiding the game with quests that make sense story telling wise at nintendo, profiting from the nature of the open world to get lazy AGAIN.

There is also a lot of cut content from the trailers we saw, and they will obviously be made into dlc's, when we saw link in a special environment on the back of a huge animal, that is nowhere to be find in the current game, if you release a trailer for the game and cut content that was advertised as is before launch, i call it false advertisement. The trailer also gave the promise of a darker, more interesting game then botw dungeon wise, and nintendo saying the dungeons will not be divine beast like but have more of a regional feel to them and not do the same thing again. Guess what... These dungeons are as bad and as SHORT and easy as divine beast, even a toddler can finish one in under 20 minutes, and the bosses are way way way too easy too. leaving absolutely not much of a memorable moment , any taste in the mouth as they are done way too fast and give you absolutely no challenge.

I played BOTW again from start to finish (over a hundred hours) before playing this game. Prior to the release, my fear was that the game will feel too similar and I will already be tired of the gameplay by the time I boot it up. Impressively, the developers has managed to make Hyrule unfamiliar and expand it to stupefying heights. This game is sooooooo huge!!! So much content, so many things to do, so much destruction. Tip to new players: You need to read, you need to talk to NPCs and you need to be perceptive of clues. Go out and get wild.

I never imagined my love for BOTW will be topped by the sequel who uses the same engine, artsyle, and main map. But TOTK managed to give that same sense of wonder I felt when I first played BOTW.

THIS GAME IS FANTASTIC!!! I’m honestly disappointed in some of these reviews, this game is so vast I’ve barely scratched the surface it feels with about 15 hours! I love exploring with building cars, planes, boats, and whatever dumb things I come up with. There are THREE whole layers to the map, and with NO LOADING SCREEN it’s feels fresh and new while exploring hyrule once more. I don’t think I could get tired of the games, if I start to feel bored? Don’t worry I can do lots of quests and challenges or maybe I want to build some funny monstrosity, YOU CAN DO THAT IN THIS GAME! I don’t regret the $70 price tag AT ALL. It’s not a $70 dlc, you can’t change my mind. There is a ton of new content and story that captivates you and keeps you playing. Nintendo outdid themselves and I’m excited for new titles of the future. THIS HAS TO BE GAME OF THE YEAR, no, GAME OF THE DECADE! 11/10 fantastic! :)
P.S. I super disappointed in those who gave terrible reviews, half them are crying about their 50 hour, tedious dungeons not being there, and the others think it’s a dlc because of reused assets. Some people are also complaining about frame drops or no 4k which is dumb, the game looks really good (especially on oled switch), you can expect frame drops on the first couple months of release. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I loved Breath of the Wild.  While it is a great game, it's not perfect, and Nintendo really had an opportunity to improve upon the foundation laid out by BOTW with a direct sequel...instead they chose to play it completely safe and rerelease BOTW as TOTK.  I call this game "Copy/Paste - Find and Replace".  Here are just a few examples:

1. The music is almost completely copy pasted throughout the entire game; I think I noticed 5 new themes while playing.
2. Ascend rune is just Revali's Gale but now it goes through solid matter.
3. The time rune no longer freezes time but moves time backwards slowly.
4. You wake up in a shrine with zero powers.
5. You start on the “Great” area and can’t leave until you gain your 4 base powers.
6. Zelda is missing for some reason.
7. Zelda's Memories are now called Dragon’s Tears.
8. You have to complete Zonai Shrines instead of Sheikah Shrines to open up warp points.
9. You have to find all the same armor sets.
10. You go to each race's region to beat a themed dungeon.
11. You have to collect stupid Korok seeds.
12. Weapons are very very fragile (possibly more so than BOTW).
13. You gather the four Champions to help you fight Ganon.
14. You have to remove “Corruption” within each race’s region.
15. You have to complete a dungeon in each race’s region.
16. Sheikah Towers are now Skyview Towers.

The only new gameplay aspect in this entire game is the fusing/crafting system, which is so needlessly finnicky and restrictive as to deter me wanting to use it.  I hope you like building long planks as a ramp or bridge, because that’s largely all you do.  Sure, you can build vehicles to your heart’s content, but you have a limited “energy” meter that drains within 5-10 seconds meaning you cannot actually USE any of those vehicles for any meaningful length of time.  How do you upgrade your energy meter?  Grinding.  Lots of grinding.  I’m sorry, but I don’t want to grind for 20-30 hours just to improve a **** battery.  I want to enjoy a Zelda game, not play an MMO.

Another thing that bothers me is that all of the shrines are stupidly easy.  There wasn’t a single one that even /remotely/ used the new mechanics in interesting ways.  Nintendo is so proud of its new crafting system that solving a puzzle often times, you guessed it, means you build a ramp or a bridge to cross a gap.  Whoopdie damn do.

The temples are seriously the worst in the series.  They are all THE SAME TEMPLE, with variations on “how many buttons do I need to press”?  You just wander around until you find a button, then you press it.  Do this a few times, fight the boss.  Temple over.  There are no puzzles, no items, no thought.  It’s just so incredibly lazy, and I don’t know why they designed them this way.

And why is Zelda relegated to not being a character in this game?  In BOTW she was very sympathetic, compelling, and well written.  In this one they make her disappear and then she doesn’t have any character change or growth throughout the entire game.  She’s there to be a magical mcguffin, and it’s just sad.  I wanted her to play a larger role, help Link alongside him this time around, maybe even contribute to gameplay.  Nope.  Go sit on the sideline and do nothing, Zelda.  You aren’t important.

I criticize this game because I know Nintendo is capable of more, and quite frankly this game is just creatively empty to me.  Same map, same gameplay, same exact story, same beats…and apparently it took them over 6 years to make.  I keep asking myself, how is that possible?  I don’t have an answer.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I'd like to discuss some important points about Tears of the Kingdom that I think the reviews were lacking to clearly explain, and it is necessary to clarify the flaws in advanced to set up players expectations.

Float islands: while the trailers and the marketing massively showed the air lands, it is just the tutorial of the game and you are gonna finish it in 2 hours. There are some small floating island through the game, but they are not so big or interesting.

Map: the map of the game where you are gonna play 80 to 90% of the game is exactly the same. You are gonna spending uncountable hours looking for new korok seeds and new shrines at random places. I do feel a little disappointed here, cause I was expecting more of the floating islands or some significantly change in the original map. But not, you are gonna play the same game twice, but with a new story. There are a new place that I will not mention here (to let people discover while playing), but it unfortunately is not so interesting.

Story: the story is brand new and captivating. Every location shows the passage of time and people remember you when you approach. You will most of the time, follow the story buy a way like the memories in Breath of the Wild, finding places and seeing a scene.

New powers: here is where I think Nintendo spent most of the time developing the game. The new powers, in special the Ultra Hand, let players use the game as an amazing sandbox. You can craft unimaginable things and solve problems in creative ways.

Overall, I think this game would be great if Breath of the Wild didn't exist, but it does. Tears of the Kingdom felt to me like a copycat trying to monetize through the success of its predecessor. This game is worthy playing if you give some years between Breath and it, ir order to forget most of the map. I can not imagine other franchise to imitate so hard its predecessor, using the same map, and critically being so acclaimed by media. Sometime I think reviewers are afraid of Nintendo stopping sending game to them if they give bad reviews.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom - A Riveting Sequel Expanding the Breath of the Wild Universe

Rating: 9/10

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom takes players on an exhilarating journey set in the vast and immersive world of Hyrule, expanding upon the events of its predecessor, Breath of the Wild. This highly anticipated sequel introduces a captivating storyline filled with mystery, ancient ruins, and the struggle against the encroaching "Gloom."

The game begins as Link and Zelda delve into a secret passage beneath Hyrule Castle, driven by the enigmatic phenomenon known as the Gloom. Unearthing Zonai ruins, the duo discovers murals depicting a great war against the Demon King and the revelation that the Zonai may hold the key to understanding the origins of the royal family.

As the adventure unfolds, Link and Zelda encounter a mummy bound by Gloom, wielding dark power. A fateful encounter leads to Link's transformation, his arm replaced by a powerful disembodied limb. Joined by the guidance of the ghostly figure Rauru, Link embarks on a quest to restore his strength, reunite with Zelda, and save Hyrule from impending peril.

The gameplay in Tears of the Kingdom remains faithful to its predecessor, building upon the open-world exploration and dynamic combat mechanics that made Breath of the Wild a beloved title. Additionally, new gameplay elements such as rail grinding, mechanical transport, and the ability to fuse objects with weapons add depth and variety to the experience. The inclusion of Recall, Fuse, Ultrahand, and Ascend runes further expands Link's arsenal and strategic options.

The development of Tears of the Kingdom has been a highly anticipated process. The decision to create a direct sequel stemmed from the desire to revisit the vast landscape of Breath of the Wild while introducing fresh narratives and gameplay mechanics. The game showcases meticulous attention to detail, with stunning visuals and a richly crafted world that seamlessly blends familiar locations with new discoveries.

The announcement and subsequent trailers for Tears of the Kingdom generated immense excitement among fans. The continuation of the Breath of the Wild universe, coupled with the promise of an engrossing story and new gameplay elements, has captivated players worldwide.

Although some details remain undisclosed, such as the possibility of playing as Princess Zelda or multiplayer functionality, the anticipation surrounding Tears of the Kingdom is undeniable. Fans eagerly await the release, eager to embark on another legendary adventure within the beloved world of Hyrule.

There’s one thing many can dislike, which is the graphics and performance. It’s running on a Switch, you can’t ask them to magically make it more capable of better graphics. There are some fps drops using the abilities, when you are fighting enemies or making big fires, but it not that it is unplayable. Personally to me it looks great, the art style helps the game to not look that bad considering the resolution it runs at. Most realistic-looking old games age really bad compared to the current ones with similar style, that won’t happen to TotK, just like it didn’t happen to Wind Waker and Skyward Sword. With a file size of only 16 gigabytes, they managed to make a better game than the ones that are a hundred gigabytes. For those points that I mentioned, and more (being a Zelda fan makes it more special to me), The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom deserve a perfect score of 10/10.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The least someone could say of Breath of the Wild is that it was a risky shot at a new Zelda engine which landed in many ways and missed in others. Tears of the Kingdom is a perfection of that risky engine with a polished sheen that (necessarily) outshines its brilliant predecessor in nearly every capacity. Odds are, if you played Breath of the Wild and enjoyed the adventure but had some qualms about it, Tears of the Kingdom addresses your misgivings innovatively and delivers more than is asked for. It has unique puzzle-solving mechanics, a gorgeous art direction, a fantastic soundtrack, and an enormous map that manages to stay thoroughly engaging despite its size.

A central idea behind Breath of the Wild was that you, the player, have the freedom to avoid anything you don't personally find fun. If the game offers you something that doesn't tickle your fancy, it is almost certainly completely optional. Tears of the Kingdom also believes this philosophy and provides hundreds of hours of content for you to decide what it is you find fun and to jump all the way into that. Fan of exploration? This is your game. Prefer side quests? Plenty of those too. Rather spend your time fighting enemies? Combat is diverse, satisfying, and engaging. Want to enjoy a story that rewards fans of the series? It has that too. Pretty much anything you could ask for in a video game can be found in Tears of the Kingdom without looking too far.

There are essentially 3 types of people who won't like this game: people who don't enjoy games with an encumbrance of freedom, classic Zelda fans who want the series to return to its roots, and people who find its admittedly unorthodox control scheme too tedious to adjust to. If you are one of these people, you probably will still find lots to enjoy during a playthrough, but you'll see the reviews and think it is undeserving of its inordinately high praise. To that end, I think an objective viewer of this game's merits would come to the same conclusion many of us have which is that Tears of the Kingdom delivers extreme quality despite personal preferences.

It's worth mentioning that whether the game is worth $70 or required its full 6-year development time is irrelevant in terms of reviewing its quality. As a finished piece of art isolated from outside considerations, this game is as good as it gets.

Sure the world is good but that's because it's BoTW world completely reused and BoTW world was good to begin with. I understand it's a sequel but the reuse of assests is crazy. If you don't like building stuff literally every 5 minutes to get everywhere this game isn't for you. 2. If you hate being in menus more then actually playing this game isn't for you. 3. If you're a classic zelda fan that's itching for classic dungeons you can spend hours in trying to figure them out this game isn't for you (slightly larger unique looking divine beast is about all we got). 3. If you hated the weapon breaking in botw this is even worse because it both has weapon breaking which wasted enough time but now you have to waste even more time to "fuse" stuff to weapons just to be effective at battle. ---- the world is great, the exploring is great, just like botw but the rest of it I'd lacking and really does feel like DLC.  BoTW was a great one time departure from the Zelda franchise but many of us are ready for a real Zelda game not a Zelda skinned open world game. Not saying the next Zelda can't be open world but it actually needs to have Zelda gameplay in it... dungeons, items you actually need to work for, meaningful weapon and gear upgrades (that don't break),  a higher sense of fantasy.  The Zelda formula is timeless and has proven itself over and over again, I'm not against change but I am against upended an entire franchise people love for something "new" and completely forgoing homage to the past.

Congratulations to Nintendo and to all the gamers and developers, regardless of the platform, we should all be proud of achieving this level of narrative, game mechanics, game scale and uniqueness in experience as part of the human technical, philosophical and artistical way of expression. This game, together with some other great games, is a reason to be proud as gamers and as humans, this is not a competition, we as a race are every year pushing our boundaries in many areas with original works such as this one. Embarking on a Boundless Journey: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom takes players on an awe-inspiring adventure through the beloved world of Hyrule. Building upon the foundation set by its predecessor, Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom introduces captivating gameplay features and an expansive world to explore. Tears of the Kingdom invites players into a realm of boundless possibilities, offering expanded gameplay and a sense of exploration without limits. Drawing from a modified version of Hyrule, the game presents a wealth of new challenges, quests, and hidden secrets. Players are encouraged to embark on a thrilling journey through diverse environments, ranging from sky islands to intricate caves and the mysterious Depths. Each location presents a distinct atmosphere and a plethora of captivating encounters, ensuring that the exploration of Hyrule remains a captivating and mesmerizing experience from start to finish.

Unleashing Creativity with Engaging Gameplay Features:
Tears of the Kingdom introduces a host of engaging gameplay features that empower players to unleash their creativity within the game world. Through the integration of Zonai devices and the innovative Ultrahand ability, players are granted a sandbox-like experience that allows for experimentation and invention. These mechanics enable players to combine various objects, construct unique structures, and push the boundaries of the game's physics. The freedom to create and interact with the environment adds depth and interactivity to the gameplay, fostering a sense of wonder and endless possibilities.

Alongside the exhilarating gameplay, Tears of the Kingdom presents immersive quests and memorable characters that bring the world of Hyrule to life. The game weaves a compelling narrative, propelling players forward as they unravel the mysteries and challenges that await them. From the charming allies to the formidable foes, the characters of Tears of the Kingdom add depth and emotional resonance to the journey, creating a truly immersive experience.

Conclusion:
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom invites players to embark on a boundless journey through a modified version of the beloved world of Hyrule. With its expanded gameplay mechanics, diverse environments, and immersive quests, Tears of the Kingdom offers an unforgettable adventure that pushes the boundaries of what can be achieved within the Zelda universe. By providing the freedom to explore, create, and engage with the world, Tears of the Kingdom celebrates the spirit of adventure and discovery that defines the Zelda franchise. Whether you are a long-time fan or new to the series, Tears of the Kingdom is a testament to the enduring magic of Hyrule and a must-play experience for Zelda enthusiasts and gamers alike.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
El juego es espactularmente perfecto, es una obra maestra en todos ámbitos y un juego muy disfutable en mecánicas, cinemáticas e historias.
Uno pensaba que era imposible mejorar lo insuperable como Breath of the Wild, pero el hecho de continuar y mejorar la trama es simplemente espectacular.
El juego tiene de todo lo que busques, tiene una historia y trama profunda y oscura en la que se basa el juego, pero el juego al ser no lineal puedes completarlo e ir lo desarrollando de distintas maneras para al final llegar al mismo final. Por no contar con una manera en específica de jugarlo el juego es inmenso no solo en posibilidades sino que también en la manera de vivir lo y de entenderlo.
El juego no solo tiene un mapa gigante lleno de detalles hasta en el más mínimo árbol, si no que cuantas con otros 2 mapas, el de los cielos y de las islas celestes donde investigas los secretos de los Zonnan y el del subsuelo de donde vienen los monstruos y el villano de la historia.
El juego tiene una dificultad relativamente alta pero al aprender como usar las habilidades y mecánicas del juego se pueden usar para afrontar la dificultad.
El juego no se vuelve repetitivo debido a sus detalles, misiones secundarias y la búsqueda de items como todos los ropajes y la semillas kologs, pero que tu puedes ignorar si solo quieres enfocarte en la historia. Puedes irte chetando poco a poco para enfrentarte después de muchas horas a las mazmorras o puedes ir al empezar el juego y valerte de tus habilidades (y aprovecharte de bugs)

El único punto endeble del juego es su calidad gráfica, que pese a ser de una consola de bajo rendimiento, el juego cuenta con muy buenos gráficos y una cantidad considerable de fps, pero en Nintedo Switch (en su mayoría modo portatil) también se pueden sufrir bajas de frames y a mi me pasaron algunos errores de renderizado.

El juego es una obra maestra y no se siente para nada como un DLC del botw, tu lo puedes jugar sin conocer nada de Zelda o habiendo jugando todos los juegos y lo vas a disfrutar igual.
En lo personal siento que el juego marca esta historia como una especie de reboot o nueva Li a temporal a la historia de Zelda así que no siento que sea tan necesario saber el lore, pero aún así recomiendo jugar primero Breath of The Wild y sus dlc, segundo Age of Calamity y por último Tears of The Kingdom.

El juego es perfecto y sin duda lo puedo considerar como uno de los mejores juegos que he jugado en mi vida, y solo lo pondría después de minecraft porque tiene un valor sentimental en mi vida.

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom 10/10

Review:
I honestly love almost everything about Tears of The Kingdom. As a super hyped up sequel to one of the best games released ever, it is obviously very hard to meet everyone's expectation with it. And I would say that TOTK outdone BOTW in almost every aspect (the new mechanics they introduced), that I had to stop myself from playing it after a 10 hour session with TOTK cuz the new mechanics and the refurbished Hyrule are just so damn fun to explore and play with.

The reason why I think it's a 9/10 though is that I think the story of TOTK is probably the weakest part of the game. It's not essentially a terrible story, like for example the opening of the game is one of the most exciting hook to a story I've ever witnessed in the entire gaming franchise, but I just think that when it comes to what BOTW offered story wise, the story of TOTK in the later part lacks the kind of emotional tug to me the way BOTW did.

Obviously, what made BOTW amazing is definitely not about the story, and TOTK is absolutely a better version of BOTW when it comes to the game-play aspect. But I'd have to say that the story of TOTK made me not as submerged and emotionally connected to the game as i did with BOTW. But if you're here for the gameplay, TOTK is definitely a must-play and 10/10 when it comes to game mechanics.

The attention to detail in Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom is commendable. From the tiniest environmental interactions to the subtle nods to the series' history, it is clear that every aspect of the game has been crafted with love and care. This level of dedication is what elevates it to perfection.

In conclusion, Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom is a triumph of game design, storytelling, and artistry. It is a rare gem that captures the imagination and leaves a lasting impression. With its stunning visuals, immersive gameplay, and emotionally resonant narrative, this game transcends the medium and stands as a testament to the power of video games as an art form. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
i had a weird feeling about this sequel. While the trailers at first teased interesting twists in the story, game structure/progression & some aspects of the world, I just wondered how they were gonna refresh a game with essentially the same map, enemies & combat, without entering in redundancy & shallowness.

And after putting the hours on this game, I can confirm that this weird feeling developed to disappointment, as much as I wanted to love the game.

For starters, if you didn't like BOTW, you probably won't like TOTK, and that's a huge let down for people who wanted something different, considering the years of development.

Exploring the world hasn't changed that much, the feel is quite similar, & while the sky islands & the underground provide new areas for traveling, there isn't something really refreshing, & the reward for exploration feels unbalanced. You are just gonna find some shrines, some enemies (lots of recycling) or some weapon that you probably won't use, or be excited about. Nothing too transcendental.

The story is there, but the open world shenanigans & the structure of the game progression makes it feel like it is far in the background in your gameplay experience, a problem that BOTW had.

I had some hopes for the dungeons, & some leakers where claiming wild takes about them, but in reality, they are glorified divine beasts with little to zero difficulty. The lead ups where a bit more interesting though.

The new abilities have their charm, but if you are not interested (like lots of people) in distracting yourself with infinite builds & fuses that don't provide any substance or meaning to your quest, you probably going to find it tedious & useless quickly. And there are TOO many options with various weapons anyway, so you won't find something really challenging that makes the difference in effectiveness.

This is without even mentioning the graphics & performance issues that i think they are just unacceptable for any major franchise/major game development. Dips in fps  & aged graphics.

So here we are, with more questions than answers,

Why is this game getting 10s almost everywhere, with no objective review in sight?
Why is everyone assuming that an infinite sandbox & open world "experience" automatically gives a game a greatness status?
What happened to the mystic & sense of transcendence that made past Zeldas so great?

The thing is, this is a game that is perfect for streamers & people that make memes, because the potential of making jokes & crazy situations is very much there. But it seriously lacks the feel of something transcendental, of the experience of being a hero on a mission, a magical journey with high stakes & immersive places. The customization options are amazing, but they should not be the main point of the game, since i am not interested in minecraft zelda edition.

Still, there are many moments of charm & there are many opportunities to express yourself & enjoy the ride. But in no way this is a perfect game.

Reviewers & fans have to take a step back & really analyze this game better, because we are sending Nintendo the wrong message & there's a huge room for improvement.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This is the greatest game I've ever had the pleasure to play. It's as if it were MADE for me!!! That's because I'm a life-long gamer, and this game was MADE for those that love GAMES!

Firstly, the presentation is out of this world, beyond anything I've seen on the Switch before. The visuals, music... Everything in the game-world comes together beautifully. Despite the limited horsepower of the Switch (which is a handheld console running 2015 hardware), the presentation as a whole (during gameplay) comes together in a way that's above even the latest and greatest from other developers with VASTLY more powerful hardware. The world is wonderfully simulated to an impressive level of detail and due to this, feels alive. Only titles from the likes of Rockstar such as Red Dead Redemption gives this simulated world a run for its money imo. Standing on a sky island in the long billowing grass, rich with wildlife, and seeing the vast land below, clouds rolling over, is just breathtaking. The grand sense of scale is like nothing I've seen in an open world game before. It's as if every feature of the landscape is calling out to you, calling out that a fantastical adventure lies ahead.

The Story & Cutscenes are greatly improved over the previous title 'Breath of the Wild', much to my delight. They've pretty much been improved in all areas, direction, graphical fidelity, animation quality, story telling & frequency.

The game feels completely refreshed over BOTW (despite people that haven't played it calling it BOTW 1.5), it instantly cements itself as a brand new adventure... The land of Hyrule returns from the last game but it has changed dramatically, there's a whole new world in the sky, new enemies, new shrines, new abilities (all of which are crazy creative, to a shocking degree, and feel AWESOME to use). NEW EVERYTHING. The only thing that remains from BOTW is the graphical style (but now there is more variety to the themes), some features of the landscape of the land below (as it takes place in the same setting), and some of the core gameplay features that worked in BOTW, although most of those have received QOL improvements or other changes/overhauls.

The abilities... My word, the Nintendo devs must have been on some hard hallucinogenics to come up with the new abilities in Link's arsenal. They are incredibly creative and offer gameplay opportunities that I've not experienced in any other game, such as the ability to be CREATIVE yourself. The puzzles in the game can be solved in a ludicrous number of ways, and coming up with your own silly ways to solve them is extremely fun & rewarding. The abilties in the previous game did feel somewhat 'restricted' as if the devs were scared to give the player 'too much power'. This game completely fixes this complaint, the new abilities are beyond whacky and give so much power to the player but still without being overpowered.

Toga Link with his long hair is also just FABULOUS. Love the new look.

My only real negative so far would be that It can drop to 20fps at worst when using the ability 'ultrahand' or displaying very graphically intensive scenes but that hasn't affected my experience much, most of the time any action is going on it's a locked 30fps, and the input lag remains constant, which is actually a great ACHIEVEMENT on the Switch with this game. Anyone that says otherwise is quite uneducated and ignorant on the topic of game optimisation & hardware. It's very playable and when you play it, you melt into the experience, not giving a single hoot for the resolution or FPS. This is a very well-optimised game for the Switch and should be lauded as such.

The game works on DAY 1, no bugginess & no 'we'll fix it later' from Nintendo. Just a solid release that works great. Almost unheard of in today's industry. If any game deserves the new inflated prices of videogames, it's this one. Nintendo still know how to deliver a great game.

I will add finally that if you truly HATED the gameplay in BOTW, this game might not change that or be your cup of tea, although a lot of complaints that people had for BOTW have been rectified, so if you thought BOTW was a 7/10, this game could be a 10 for you.

Even if the game isn't your cup of tea, you'd have to be pretty dull to not see or appreciate the effort and expert game design throughout that the devs have delivered. It's a work of art, as has been every mainline Zelda game since Ocarina of Time in 1998. Any user score below 7 is from a blatant salty troll (that probably hasn't even got the game), ignore them.

I'd give this game an 11/10 if I could, it's one of the best games I've ever played. I wonder what Nintendo have in store for the next Zelda? The mind boggles. To top this they'll have to pull out all the stops once again.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: I really do not understand what anyone sees in this game or breath of the wild. From the standpoint of being a Zelda game the only thing that makes these 2 new games in the series a Zelda game is the name and the presence of the characters Link and Zelda. As far as feeling like a Zelda game in gameplay or atmosphere it does not. From an audio design perspective, Zelda games had classic music and soundtracks that many of us remember to this day. This game and BOTW are completely unforgettable from a soundtrack standpoint. Much of this game feels tedious and pointless, from the stamina meter to the paper mache weapons, to the unnecessary time sink that is cooking. This game and BOTW both feel like someone wanted to create a video game version of that stupid Nintendo Labo crap. Botw and this game should have been a new franchise and then Nintendo could have focused on making an actual Zelda game that would be true to what that series actually has been.  I haven’t even touched on the underpowered nature of the Switch, but when you’ve gotten used to playing modern consoles where nearly all games run at 60fps, 1440p or 4K with HDR it is PAINFUL to try and play a game that runs at 30fps (at best) with muted colors and jaggies everywhere from lack of resolution. This game and BOTW are EXTREMELY overrated and I personally expect better from the Nintendo I once loved. I literally hate this game and what Nintendo has done to another series that I once loved. Nintendo, do better, Nintendo fanboys, expect better. It’s time to wake up!

Es el juego más completo que exista, el mundo por si solo te invito a adentrarte en cada uno de los rincones que hay.
La historia es perfecta, emotiva, cautivadora; continua a la perfección con lo que su antecesor había dejado.

Los templos aunque sencillos superficialmente, son desafiantes e entretenidos, perfecto para llevar al jugador a adentrarse más en esta historia.
Por último las mecanicas, me han parecido perfectas, no hay mucho que decir puesto a qué son básicas, pero esto no quita el hecho de que brinden muchas oportunidades creativas al jugador para explotarlas a lo largo de todo Hyrule.

Es el juego perfecto, una verdadera leyenda

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Nintendo has absolutely sent the bar into orbit with this one. The gameplay designers have brains AND balls to do what Tears of the Kingdom does from. From a mechanics perspective (and speaking as a seasoned game developer myself) TOTK does what no other company on the scale of Nintendo has been willing to do: dream big, take massive risks, and execute BRILLIANTLY. The scope of what is possible with the mechanics provided to the player via object manipulation and unique traits of those objects is nothing short of awe-striking.  So awe-striking that it overshadows the veritable cornucopia of systemics and mechanics already introduced in the previous title, Breath of The Wild.  We will be seeing players finding new things to do and love in this game for many, many years to come. Beyond the meat of what makes this game unique, Tears of the Kingdom builds on what made breath of the wild great, leaving nothing behind.  There are a wealth of "verbs" (things you can do) that is rivaled only by the games that borrowed directly from the first title. While other games follow the overwhelming status quo of combat being a primary (or only) way the player can really interact with the world, Tears of the Kingdom, like it's predecessor allows and encourages the player to experiment against the question "what if I could _____?" And the answer is virtually always YES. Game developers better be paying attention to this one. Tears of the Kingdom is an absolute masterclass in gameplay and systemic design.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
El Juego es una locura en más de un aspecto, a pesar de ser un juego para una consola híbrida de hace 6 años todo lo que hacía bien su antecesor (Breath of the wild) en esta secuela se ve llevado a su máxima expresión al grado de incluso superar todo.

Una secuela directa que cambia tantisimas cosas que realmente se convierte en un juego totalmente nuevo y ajeno al anterior, algo similar a lo ocurrido con "Ocarina of time y Majora's Mask).

Tears of the kingdom es una propuesta revolucionaria que no tiene miedo a competir contra gráficos fotorealistas o consolas súper potentes ya que tanto su sistema de mecánicas, su mundo tan rico y lleno de vida, su banda Sonora excelente y su apartado de artistico, crean un mundo único que te sumergirá de lleno desde el segundo uno.

Tras 70 horas de juego aún se siente que no has visto ni una pequeña parte de todo lo que te ofrece el juego y la historia es exelente.

No obstante no puedo decir que el juego sea perfecto aunque para mi lo sea, se tiene que ser objetivo al dar una reseña y su punto más débil y en mi opinión es el único error que tiene es la potencia de la consola, a pesar de eso Nintendo junto al equipo de Monolithsoft hicieron un trabajo excepcional, el juego corre igual que su predecesor a 900p/30fps en modo dock y 720p/30fps en modo portátil, sin embargo el juego está súper pulido y los fotogramas son totalmente estables salvo momentos muy puntuales donde llegan a bajar hasta 20fps,
También la implementación del FSR de AMD el juego luce de maravilla.

Conclusiones: Nintendo siempre hace un trabajo de admiración con Zelda, es una genialidad lo que logran y que siempre su franquicia rompedora e innovadora ha sido Zelda, Tears of the kingdom provocó en nosotros una inseguridad pero superó cada adversidad trayendonos algo único e inolvidable, es un juego imprescindible y me atrevo a afirmar que el nuevo mejor juego de la historia.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Tears of the Kingdom takes the concepts laid out by Breath of the Wild and brings them to a fine polish.

The map has been altered slightly and events have shifted enough to properly reflect the passage of time. Despite the surface layer having the same base geography, the new additions of landmarks and the completely different mechanics change the nature of traversing the world entirely. I know where various specific places are on the map, but getting to them isn't the same as it was. It is a whole different challenge, one that I relish. The addition of various caves around the map is a nice little distraction. There were some incredible surprises inside some of them, and a few that caused me genuine terror I wasn't ready for.

The sky layer is definitely the place where the dev team tested all of the new mechanics behind Link's new abilities. The variety of little puzzles and interactions you can find there are surprising. it is very much reminiscent of the outer lying sky islands of Skyward Sword, but there is far more to do in this game than in that one. There are clearly places you are intended to reach later on in the game, but given enough time and effort, you can reach them at just about any point in the game. I encountered one specific place where there was an enemy that ended me a number of times before I was able to run away. Were I better player I may have stood a chance, though.

The Depths layer offers an experience I haven't encountered before in a Zelda game. It is a challenge to just survive there. I spent a good hour during one session traversing the underground and barely uncovered a fraction of the map, yet the number of things I found to do and enemies to fight caught me off guard, and I was trying to avoid most of them. There are things that will jump out at you from any corner available down there, even from the ground beneath your feet. I also met a face I wasn't expecting down there, but was very glad to see again.

The dungeons of this game are leagues ahead of those found in Breath of the Wild. The challenges offered by them force you to think about what you're doing. Some solutions where fairly straight forward in hindsight, but coming to those conclusions in the first place was a delight. The bosses are given a spectacular presentation, and offer just the right level of challenge. I felt good after completing them.

This game is not perfect. While I haven't encountered any graphical or framerate issues, and don't think I've encountered any bugs, there is a certain tedium to equipment management that is less enjoyable.

Having said that, I do enjoy finding new pieces of things to attach to other tools I've collected to create new and interesting tools. There's one specific item dropped by a specific type of world boss that I've already taken a liking to and regularly go back to obtain for my weapons. You are also still required to have a great variety of tools on you at any given time if you want to be thorough in your exploration. I've discovered a number of tools already that are a must have for exploring certain sections of the map.

The new mechanics of this game are a genuine joy to experiment with. I've been thoroughly enjoying testing the limits of what the abilities can do. There are a number of things that can be done in this game which were simply not possible or were otherwise too complex for those like myself to do in the previous title, but the new mechanics have brought forth numerous new possibilities for interaction with the engine. There are some times when I find myself missing the powers of the prior game, but those times are few and far between, and that does not detract from the experience.

If you enjoyed Breath of the Wild, you will enjoy this game. If you haven't played Breath of the Wild, I highly encourage you to do so before picking this game up. The experience is not the same.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I had the honor to receive (certainly by mistake), the game in advance. This game is in the perfect continuity of its predecessor, although it has kept some defects. Let's start with the latter.
One of the main flaws that I decided to mention for this review is the dungeons. This is a point where I expected an evolution from Nintendo with a new way of conceiving them. In spite of these expectations from me and also from the players, I still find them too close to what was done in Breath of the Wild, that is to say structures with 4 or 5 points to activate in order to reach the boss. In the previous Zelda games, each dungeon varied and was solved in a different way, which brought a great originality to each of them. Here, the only nice thing about the dungeons is the environment that varies each time and the theme of each of them, involving in this the bosses for which Nintendo has made an effort. In short, Nintendo didn't put as much effort into the construction of the dungeons as one would expect, and the way of solving them would be different from BOTW.
Other minor technical flaws including slowdowns (probably because I only had access to 1.0.0 during my session) are present and will require a patch but did not spoil my gaming experience.
As for the qualities of this Zelda, as usual in the games of this series, Nintedo has provided us with a game of very high quality, putting even its predecessor at the rank of prototype despite the revolution it brought. The narration is much better with an excellent scenario. On this point, Nintendo has listened very well to the players. I was also satisfied with the soundtrack, with the reworking of some of the themes you could hear in BOTW.  The construction system is very well integrated in the game and is well brought in the story (a whole tutorial area is dedicated to the mastery of it), the new powers are also excellent. Nintendo has, on this point, kept the best of BOTW to make something much more advanced, which gives a gameplay that can vary to the extreme.

In short, Zelda Tears of the Kingdom is a game that I recommend to those who are looking for an excellent game that pushes its concept to the end. I could talk about many other qualities but not all of them come to mind as I write.

Review:

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Primero que nada, crecí con los Juegos de Zelda, para mi son los mejores que haya jugado pero por hoy ya no pienso lo mismo, tengo más de 35 años y tengo obligaciones obligatorias como todos, recalco esto pues quiero ser lo mas objetivo posible. El juego de Tears of the Kingdom Tiene una historia floja, nada de que sorprenderse, hay mejores en la tv. Sus santuarios son un poquito innovadores pero tenían que ser así por las nuevas mecánicas del brazo. Son tantas que aburren. La mecánica de armar esta bien, me gusto pero ya después aburre andar ayudando aún NPC con sus rótulos, honestamente esto me aburrió. Las semillas Kolog son cansadas, es tediosas, depender de esto en el 2023 para ampliar tu alforja ya es aburridisimo, honestamente esto de las semillas Kolog no era necesario y es lo que hace a este juego un copia y pega del Breath Of The Wild. Cambio el mapa y que bueno que lo hizo pero nada innovador. Lo que más odio es que las armas se rompan, algunas veces estaba en una batalla con algún jefe y cuando se rompían, me rompía la experiencia y luego el juego me obligaba a pensar en que arma apoyarme y cuando ya no tenía mejores y eso es frustrante, las armas que tenia ya ni daño le hacían. Faltaron Dungeons hechos y derechos, esos que tenían plantas altas con puertas cerradas con llaves y lugares con difícil acceso. Ítem legendarios con un arco único y cosas así que solo encontrábamos en Dungeons, faltaron jefes y sub jefes en los Dungeons pero como no están los Dungeons entonces me río mejor. El juego en gráficos me pareció hermoso, no tuve problemas con ellos pues también soy consciente del poder de la portátil. Los templos son repetitivos, activar 4 o 5 interruptores para luego pasar al jefe final y fin del templo, todo aquí es casi igual a su precuela. La verdad Tear of the Kingdom me pareció mucho corta y pega, ya parecía fifa en muchas cosas. El juego lo terminé sin hacer muchos santuarios, misiones de nps (aburridas para mi) no complete mi alforja, no quise buscar trajes para completarlos y aun así le invertí 100 al juego, de donde saqué fuerzas a mis más de 35 años de edad? Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Despite its majestic predecessor, The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom left much to be desired. The game suffers from a discordant universe, where the integration of monsters and technological artifacts creates an incongruous atmosphere that detracts from the immersive experience expected from the franchise. The narrative is lackluster, with underdeveloped side characters lacking charisma and a storyline that fails to inspire.

Furthermore, the bosses, previously a highlight, now seem increasingly generic, lacking the originality and intrigue that characterized earlier installments. The game's saving grace is its customizability of builds and environment interaction, which offers some creative gameplay dynamics, but this is not enough to offset the other weaknesses.

The open-world format, a trend in gaming, here feels generic and lacks the unique touch that would differentiate it from countless other open-world games. In essence, Tears of the Kingdom feels like a missed opportunity, a game that took the right risks with its predecessor only to fall back on safer, less inspiring choices, resulting in an experience that is far from the revolutionary gaming experience that was Breath of the Wild.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Tears of the Kingdom accomplishes an impressive feat- following up on, and convincingly improving on- a formula perfected by its predecessor. In an impressive showcase, Tears of the Kingdom offers an expansive new take on the legacy Breath of the Wild left behind— offering new experiences, thousands of new interactions, insane player creativity, and an expansive world that effectively doubles the scope of the prequel.

To call Tears of the Kingdom a masterclass in presentation and creative design would be a massive understatement. The game improves on many aspects of the Breath of the Wild formula, and offers an unforgettable story and experience that will surely be beloved for years.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The legend of zelda tears of the kingdom é um daqueles jogos onde vc joga e entende que jogos podem ser mais que jogos, esse sentimento está em quase todos os jogos da franquia ,mas qual a diferença dele para os outros jogos da franquia ,ou melhor o seu antecessor breath of the wild ? Tears é uma expansão de botw é realmente uma sequencia ,então se vc quer algo de diferente do botw então o jogo não é para vc ,o jogo continua tendo shrines , o mesmo metodo de contar historia e a mecanica de combate com algumas implementações novas ,porem um dos maiores diferenciais desse jogo pro seu antecessor é os poderes novos que vira o jogador novo e os jogadores antigos da serie de cabeça pra baixo, nunca se foi tão divertido e bem implementado suas mecanicas com um mundo como esse jogo é, esse jogo te desafiar a pensar de maneira criativa usando as ferramentas que ele te dá e de forma diferente de botw, onde agora o processo de montar seu veiculo ou bigiganga pra te divertir pra camba ao se sentir um genio.
Mas é só isso ? então não, tears corrige todos os problemas de botw ,poucos inimigos ? não mais ,mundo vazio ? não  mais.
Mas o mapa é o mesmo ? sim , porem não parece nada ,o mapa foi modificado de um jeito que vc sabe que está em um lugar antigo de botw quando vê um ponto forte de referencia, mas se olhar tudo ao seu redor esta diferente e com coisas diferentes para fazer. Alem que ha novidades que acresentam o mapa tanto para cima ,quanto para baixo.
A novidade em relação a itens ? sim , o jogo tá recheado de itens novos e que te dá colecionaveis novos e moedas de trocas novas para incresentar mais progressão para suas novas ferramentas.
E a performance ? No switch ela tá muito boa ,o fps cai um pouco ao usar a mecanica de construção quando sua criação tem muitos objetos , mas não é algo que incomode, na verdade o mais impressionante é quando vc sobe para os ceus ou desce e desce para mapas mais abaixo e não há loading ou até quedas ao transitar entre os 3 niveis diferentes de mapa , A Nintedo fez bruxaria pra otimizar isso.
No geral temos um jogo que faz com que Zelda breath of wild pareça um beta ,ele melhora tudo e incresenta coisas ainda melhores, definitivamente não há nada melhor do que esse jogo dentro desse genero e não tem nenhum jogo que chega perto de fazer oque ele faz.
Se vc tem um switch ou pc gamer vá jogar ,fassa esse favor pra si mesmo.
(observação dessa vez eu pensei que teria um jogo 100 no metacritc ,mas como a vida não é justa não foi dessa vez.)

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: It is an awesome game, I am so far only on the first dungeon, but it is a vast improvement on Breath of the Wild, and that is one of the best games that was ever made. For example, it sort of added crafting mechanics, which players have always been asking for in Botw. It also made the return of traditional more themed dungeons, this makes it a lot more fun, I also quite enjoyed getting to use the champions decedents, and I was positively surprised at how useful they were, like it wasn't just there for the decor, it was actually fighting, and the ability that I got to use so far was very helpful. Finally, I really like the 4 abilities that I have unlocked so far (recall, ascend, fuse, and ultrahand), they are a ton of fun to play with, and it adds a creative aspect to the game. Furthermore, combining all four abilities makes it incredibly good, especially for traversing the land, which, contrary to what some people may want you to believe, was vastly expended, with a vast underground, and a lot of sky traversal. In conclusion, it is an awesome game, and it is totally worth the price!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Masterfully crafted videogame. BOTW was already an amazing game, but they’ve made TOTK a lot better. It feels fresh (because of the new abilities, the sky islands, dungeons, new shrines, and the underground). It feels like BOTW, but so much has changed that I see it as a return to a land that fills us with nostalgia, but improving on every aspect that made us love it. I understand that it’s a similar formula to BOTW, and if people didn’t click with the 2017 title, they believe they might not click with this one. Still, for me, those individuals should try TOTK because it combines the formula for BOTW but brings back elements from classic Zeldas they have wished for. This game isn’t anything less than a 10. I get we all have different tastes, but having different tastes does not warrant giving an masterfully crafted game a low score. It’s a 10/10 and I understand if people say it’s the best game of all times; because it probably is. -Justin

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
It's a good game, a good expansion on the things BOTW do so well at. I would not call it a DLC though as the world and puzzles got revamped. It definitely delivers on what it promised, a decent open world Zelda(puzzle) game. Integrated with fun side quests and plenty of spaces to explore. Brand new customized building mechanics all give returning players a good refresh on what made the game good in 2018.

At the same time it also carries most of the negatives form its predecessor. Soulless openworld, lack of incentives to explore, combat starts fun but parry is op, rewards are either breakable common gear or stamina and HP from temples, monster variety is just as terrible, story is almost non existent, music is questionable...

If you were awed by BOTW, you would be awed by this game. But if you weren't convinced by BOTW or if you are like me who never finished the game despite multiples tries. You will definitely question what does make this game fun.

If you liked BOTW you will like this one. Its basically BOTW 2.0, mostly same map, music seems similar to. Runs terrible on my rather old switch and is looked to 30fps (which is -1 point from me)

But like many other sequels it didnt really adress the problems of the first game:

Combat still pretty clunky and boring, midway through the game you can use your builds to cheese most enemies
Cooking is still stupid
Weapon durabillity still exists and ruins the flow of combat

Its new fusion system is fun, but its clunky as well, what should be a 5 second mechanic in the inventory turns into a nightmare as you have to: Open the inventory -> Drop the item you want to fuse your weapon with -> select the power -> select the item and then chose the weapon to fuse

All in all this game is basically BOTW 1.5, it is not enough new to justify a new game in my opinion  but it was also more than what you would usually put into an DLC
In the end its basically if you liked BOTW you like this game cause its almost the same, if you didnt like BOTW you wont like this game.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Tears of the Kingdom improves on the main issues of Breath of the Wild: 1) A large world, but lacking content, 2) a lack of an engaging story driving player actions, 3) puzzles based around very specific powers.

Tears of the Kingdom is massive, adding the sky islands, the depths, and many cave systems. It kicks off with a playable cinematic that sets up the basic plot of the story and leaves the player set to figure out what happened. While most of the story is still in memories, the scenes themselves are more engaging and reveal a wild plot element. The story is furthered by the dungeons and boss battles, which are both more engaging and diverse. The themed dungeons are still non-linear, unlike the classic Zelda dungeons, but the lead up to them has the dungeons themselves are much more involved than the divine beasts. Finally, the three abilities are vastly more simple in their premise, but allow a plethora of solutions and shortcuts ensuring for a unique experience.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Tears of the Kingdom is a wholesome, mostly enjoyable adventure game. But six years of development should've resulted in more innovation and refinement. TOTK feels like a sidegrade or reshuffle of its predecessor (BOTW), not a true sequel.

TOTK carries most of BOTW's strengths but also some of its flaws. Korrok seeds instead of unique rewards, simplistic combat and story, usage of menus interrupting the gameplay flow, breakable equipment that lacks progression, these issues still persist.

As for new features, the sky islands are an afterthought aside from the tutorial area, fusing does not fix breakable weapons, and the Ultrahand feature absolutely wrecks the framerate. Manipulating the game through crafting contraptions is the best new addition, but it feels more like a cool novelty than something well slotted into the core gameplay.

Disappointingly, these games continue to be held back by their hardware - playing TOTK would undoubtedly be a better experience on any of the outdated Switch's competitor machines, just like with the previous game.

Despite these issues, Tears of the Kindgom is a good game that I would recommend to those who seek a mellow but magical adventure. (If you're someone who seeks a gritty or fast-paced experience, look elsewhere.)

If you observe Tears of the Kingdom in total isolation, it's a good game. As someone who played BOTW and waited six years for a sequel, I cannot help but feel short-changed, as if Nintendo started resting on their laurels after BotW's universal acclaim.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
If you liked Breath of the Wild, then you'll like this, as it's more of the same. If you didn't, like me, then you'll probably dislike this even more.

The days of old Zelda game design philosophy are gone. I have to accept that, but I don't have to like it. Rather than creating interesting puzzles for players to solve, we just create our own solutions. Sounds great on paper until you realize how shallow the system really is. Materials right next to a bottomless pit. Gee, I wonder what I'm supposed to do. It's so brain-dead simple, I'm genuinely amazed at how many people consider this the "next level" of adventure games.

Rather than address the complaints of weapon durability (one of the stupidest mechanics of any video game), Nintendo double down and force you to use its "fuse" system to "fix" the problem yourself. Now only it's worse since fusing requires you to pause the action to do it. Bomb arrows? Going to need to pause every single time you craft one, taking you out of the experience each time. Horizon Zero Dawn and Days Gone solved this problem by having a radial wheel that only slowed down the action to craft, rather than stopping it, but Nintendo think they know what's best.

Cooking in BOTW was easily broken by using hearty ingredients, and if you knew where they spawned, then great, because you now have a steady supply of meals that remove the entire point of experimentation, rendering the entire system moot. Instead of making this more interesting by adding in a sort of tolerance system where meals become less effective over time until you make something else, they left it the exact same. You also need to pause the game to heal again, which is just... lovely.

General combat has been completely unchanged from BOTW. Flurry rush, an easily abused mechanic, is no different, even the animations are the same as well!

Perhaps the worst thing about all of this is how people give Nintendo a pass with a 30 FPS target, but expect other triple A developers to have a stable 60 FPS, showing how two faced a lot of the gaming industry really is.

Honestly, Nintendo should be held to a higher standard going forward, and despite this game obviously selling millions of copies, I think it just shows how little a developer can change and people will simply accept it because of name alone. But when Ubisoft does it, people drag them through the mud for not changing enough.

The new mechanics are great and unique, the possibilities for creativity are almost endless. One can tell that the developers have put a lot of love and heart into every detail. The new world is amazing and makes you want to explore it further, especially with the new abilities which make the old ones look boring. What's not boring is the new, changed Hyrule. It's based on the old map (with many changes), but that's just the "ground level Hyrule". Without spoiling too much... there are new areas, and they're BIG and full of things new to explore.

If this game didn't meet your expectations, that's on you. But you can't deny that the game was made with care and passion. The way I like to play games, I already see myself putting an unholy amount of time into this gem.

Thank you, Nintendo

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Oh boy, where do I begin?

I've had this game pre-ordered since February, and I have to say I had never been so excited for a video game in my life. I can safely say that Tears of the Kingdom is living up to the hype. It takes everything that worked in Breath of the Wild and adds it to what could, perhaps, be considered a more traditional Zelda story and structure.

Shrines are still here, which I love. In the last game, they were a great way to test your puzzle-solving abilities, as well as practice using the Sheikah Slate abilities you had in the previous game. That ethos is continued in Tears of the Kingdom, but the puzzles have had to be altered slightly to accommodate the new Zonai abilities we have due to Link's very snazzy right arm.

I also love how you can basically build anything out of anything with Link's new Ultrahand ability. It allows for some really creative ways to solve puzzles in the world in general as well as shrines, and for you to get creative when trying to find your way around. Ultrahand definitely has to be my favourite ability, just for the sheer number of possibilities it unlocks.

One final thing: the soundtrack in this game is incredible, as Breath of the Wild's was. It feels more dynamic than it's predecessor's, but it really works. Breath of the Wild took place in a post-apocalyptic Hyrule, while this same Hyrule has attempted to heal from the Calamity of the last game, and has been dealt a major blow. Certainly in the one major story quest I'm doing at the moment, the music seems more urgent, like there is an immediate threat to the world.

All in all, I absolutely love this game, and I personally think it overshadows Breath of the Wild. In years to come, Tears of the Kingdom will be regarded as one of the best games of its era, and an indication that Nintendo fully knows what they're doing with the Zelda series now. Have to give it a 10

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of The Kingdom took everything about its predecessor and flipped it on its head. Everything from the music, to the game play mechanics have been increased ten fold. If you like your hand being held for the entirety ****, this game is not for you. Links four main abilities some would call gimmicky, but I would call them a unique set of powers that allow the players to traverse the expanded world of Hyrule however they imagine. Although you no longer have the champions abilities from The Legend of Zelda: Breath of The Wild, you’re still given all the tools necessary to complete any challenge thrown your way. That’s what makes this game so amazing. You have to go out of your way to reap what you sow. There is no other way around it. This game is very rewarding for your hard work. When it came to building vehicles, it was a bit clunky at first but the more you practice the more you get the hang of it. The frame rate in this game can drop at times, but it’s so amusing it’s forgivable. The story through memories was a bit of a let down I must say. I was really hoping they’d deviate from its previous title in order to keep things fresh. I would say the same about its tutorial, seeing as you start with obtaining Link’s 4 abilities through shrines. Although it’s the same engine, map, mechanics, and characters, it’s approach to the overall open world story telling was a bit too similar to Breath of The Wild. These are the only small complaints I had of the game as I was too distracted by having a jolly good time. The Legend of Zelda: Tears of The Kingdom took the foundation of Breath of The Wild and built upon it. That’s what makes a direct sequel work really well in my opinion. Keeping things similar enough but not too close is a hard line to walk and I think the developers did a fantastic job at towing it. Overall the game is rewarding despite its small similarities from its previous title and will keep you thinking hard the entire way.

In terms of visuals, there aren't significant differences compared to the previous installment, but the overall graphics are more rich and diverse, providing a delightful visual experience. However, this enhancement comes at the cost of slightly strained frame rates, and there may be occasional drops in FPS in certain scenes, which is a somewhat regrettable aspect.

The free synthesis system is a major highlight of this game, offering players a diverse and engaging gameplay experience. Through synthesis, you can greatly enhance your character's abilities and skills, not only increasing the game's replayability but also providing players with more strategic choices.

The world map design in the game is highly appealing, filled with a sense of mystery and exploration. Players can't resist the desire to explore every corner, and the design that encourages active exploration brings immense joy.

The story is relatively simple and straightforward, without overly intricate and complex plotlines. This design makes the game easy to understand and get into, without burdening players with excessive complexity. It is believed that this simplicity will not be a concern for most players.

Overall, through its rich visuals, enjoyable free synthesis system, captivating world map, and straightforward storytelling, this game creates a delightful and worth-exploring gaming world for players.

Muchos se preguntan porque a Nintendo no se le critica por este aspecto, un ligero apunte: Si Playstation es criticada por ejemplo por Forspoken tanto en gráficos como en rendimiento general es PORQUE PS5 DA PARA MUCHO MÁS, si Xbox SeriesX se critica por ejemplo Redfall por sus gráficos simples y sus 30 FPS, es porque Xbox Series X DA PARA MUCHO MÁS, y cuando en PC un juego sale mal optimizado incluso para una RTX4090 es porque esta mal optimizado, igual que los citados de arriba, pero en Switch nadie se espera gráficos, nadie espera 60FPS ( menos aún en un mundo abierto ) por ende, a sabiendas que la maquina en 2017 ya salió tecnológicamente desfasada si el juego no tiene mas gráficos no es achacable al juego SINO A LA MAQUINA.

En definitiva, si te gusta Zelda, cómpralo, si te gustó BOTW es te encantara mil veces más, y si no lo hizo BOTW te aseguro que este si lo hará.

It is fun for like 30 minutes then just becomes boring then you ride it out cause you want to believe that it gets better but it truly just never does. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
720p 20fps Are you kidding me?

The game I was so eagerly anticipating turned out to be a major letdown due to its poor optimization. Despite my excitement and high hopes, the game's lowly 720p resolution and stuttering 20 frames per second left me feeling extremely angry and frustrated.

I was constantly plagued by lag spikes, choppy animations, and sluggish controls, which made even basic gameplay actions feel like a chore. Every time I tried to immerse myself in the game's world, I was pulled back to reality by the constant interruptions and slowdowns.

It was especially infuriating to know that these issues could have been easily avoided with better optimization. It was clear that the developers had neglected this aspect of the game in favor of flashy graphics and other superficial features. They had failed to prioritize the smooth and enjoyable gameplay experience that gamers like me crave.

I couldn't help but feel a sense of betrayal and disappointment as I played through the game. All my excitement and anticipation had been for nothing, and I was left with a subpar gaming experience that barely resembled what I had been promised.

As I navigated through the poorly optimized world, I couldn't help but wonder how much better the game could have been if the developers had put in more effort. It was clear that they had squandered a great opportunity to create something truly special, instead settling for a half-baked product that was barely functional.

All in all, the game's poor optimization left me feeling incredibly angry and let down. It's a shame that such a promising title was ruined by such a simple and avoidable flaw. Until the developers can address these issues and deliver the polished, optimized experience that gamers like me demand, I won't be wasting any more of my time or money on their games.

Greater Variety

Cons

Puzzling / Dungeons
Music
More Linear
Safe

TOTK improved upon monster variety. It’s much easier to switch items, the quests are passable, and the characters feel more likeable. Most importantly, the story in TOTK can go toe to toe with any other Zelda. The map feels significantly different from before, so I can confidently say it doesn’t feel “rehashed”.

That said, this is BOTW. Even the tutorial is scarily close to BOTW. I’ve never been big on the futuristic theme. I can see why Nintendo’s given BOTW so much love considering its sales, but I think part of BOTW’s success was it’s fresh breath into the franchise, not the structure of the game. In other words, I don’t want 100+ hour long Zelda games. Especially considering how many of those hours are spent walking from place to place.

Fusing is a large portion of the game. It’s helpful because it gives every item in your inventory a purpose. It’s somewhat annoying because most of the time, ALL of your items become ugly.

I’m worried that Zelda is starting to lose its identity. The puzzles were heavily, heavily reliant on Ultrahand. It needed more materials to work with to allow a more diverse experience. Puzzles in TOTK revolve around machines. It didn’t feel like Zelda, and worse, it wasn’t satisfying to complete a puzzle—it was sweet relief I could stop using Ultrahand. Puzzling in TOTK feels much more linear than BOTW. Yes, linear. Machines are meant to be built one way to work. And that made shrines feel like an absolute drag.

Of all the changes in the game, I feel like the music changed the least. I’m used to having beautiful Zelda music each game, but BOTW and TOTK have not delivered. The music was empty in BOTW, but the Sky Islands theme is nothing short of AWFUL. A good chunk of the score I can look you in the eye and say anybody, and I mean anybody, could write it.

I don’t play Zelda to build modern technology. I play Zelda to play epic one on ones with exciting music, progress through a story, and complete dungeons. That’s what OOT was designed for in the first place. Link’s a knight, not an engineer. I like fast paced, satisfying puzzling that tests Link’s reflexes and skill. Not running around the map. Not taking thirty minutes as you fiddle around with Ultrahand to progress through three phases of a single shrine.

It’s like TOTK was forced with the worst of two worlds. It avoided the influence of old school Zelda, and it couldn’t provide too much variety to work with since the open world game is already hard to design.

All in all, I didn’t mind the “go here” “go there” attitude that TOTK developed to extend simple tasks like unlocking the Sky Towers. I’m satisfied with the BOTW formula, but it should place a much larger emphasis on puzzles. Not big lengthy physics puzzles, a simple chain of commands to get Link from A to D in five minutes. Time will tell whether vehicles in Zelda will be popular, but for me on a personal level, they’re a bust.

Review:
Tear of the Kingdom is another great game from the Zelda Franchise.

Already have more than 10+ hours in the game and barely scratch the whole map of ToTK, puzzles in shrines are quite unique compared to the first one, some of them will require you to think outside the box using the Rune (Botw)/ DIY game mech they include in the game which is fun for the most part (excluding the clunky controls such as rotating the object).

The combat is pretty much the same nothing has changed, they gave you the ability to fuse weapons to another object making the weapon more durable or stronger which is very helpful.

The main problem I have with TotK is, though flying islands scattered at the skies of Hyrule, Hyrule itself was the same map as Botw with a change of landscape prior to the events at the start of TotK, You need to repeat the same thing you've done from Botw in order to reveal the whole area in your map you need to go to towers (different method this time) and scan the whole area via flying up the skies to reveal the area which is pretty much the same and a hassle imo since it was the same map we explore from Botw, Clunky controls when you're in the Rune/DIY mode rotating an object will literally piss you off while this mech is fun it'll test your patience with the clunky rotational controls.
Performance as expected it's a switch game a 30 fps with frame drops in certain areas, and graphics is the same as Botw.

Overall the game is fun with some few problems still exists from Botw.

Overall

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This game is amazing if you liked BOTW, which is what you want in a direct sequel. All it does is improve on what BOTW was. Now that said, it's not like it can't stand on it's own. There was a lot of concern of the map being too much of the same. I, too, shared this. After playing for about 30 hours I can say for sure that's not the case. We get the old map with some additions, and the sky islands like we saw in the trailers. (Don't read further if you consider a location to be a spoiler) The thing that truly changes the map is the depths. It as as big as the first game's map, and is is completely different. Honestly they could have had the depths as the only map in the game (So long as they added towns to it, which I haven't found in it so far, but I have found a shop), and less people would've complained compared to now. The fact this was never talked about in the marketing is kinda crazy to me.

The fuse mechanic and Ultrahand are truly amazing. I don't want to talk about them too much, as I feel the joy of  thinking "Will this work?" and finding out it does is too great. What I will say is that the fuse mechanic can be used for traversal, not just combat. This is a mistake I've seen some people make. Thinking Ultrahand is for traversal, while fuse is for combat, when in actuality you can use both for both.
